questions.title: How much does it cost to apply for a patent?
questions.text:
The two main costs involved in a patent application would be the official filing fees and your patent agent's fees (if you engage one).
The total cost varies from case to case depending on the approach you take and the complexity of the case. A list of the official fees can be found here.

questions.title: How do I contact EMA?
questions.text: Please visit our website for EMA’s contact details.

questions.title: Can I get the HPV vaccination and any other vaccination at the same time?
questions.text:
If you have recently received the COVID-19 vaccine (e.g. in the last 14 days), you can still receive the HPV vaccine. An interval of at least 14 days before or after the COVID-19 vaccine is encouraged, but is not strictly necessary.
Please consult your doctor for the latest guidelines.

questions.title: Can MediSave be used for the co-payment after subsidy for vaccinations?
questions.text:
Those eligible for subsidised vaccination may also use their MediSave to cover the out-of-pocket expense at CHAS GP clinics and polyclinics.
Please check with your preferred clinic if the clinic is able to process the remaining co-payment via MediSave. If they do, please check with them on your eligibility to pay via MediSave.

questions.title: If I do not have enough in my MediSave, and I am not able to pay the remaining co-payment, are there other ways to receive the vaccination?
questions.text:
At CHAS GP clinics, these nationally recommended vaccinations are fully subsidised for those who hold the Public Assistance card.
Patients who go to the polyclinics for their vaccination(s) and have financial difficulties in paying for their bills can approach the social worker at polyclinics to enquire for assistance.

questions.title: What are some common side-effects of the flu vaccine?
questions.text:
Some people may feel faint after the vaccination.
Sit for 15 minutes to avoid fainting.
Soreness, redness, or swelling at the injection site, slight headache, body aches or tiredness; fever of more than 38'C is not common.
- These side effects usually go away on its own within 2 to 3 days
- You may take Paracetamol to help to relieve the pain or fever

questions.title: What precautions should I follow before receiving the flu vaccine?
questions.text:
Inform your healthcare professional if:
- You are allergic to this vaccine or any of the other ingredients of this vaccine
- You have a history of Guillain-Barr Syndrome (a rare nerve condition)
- You are pregnant or breastfeeding

questions.title: What precautions should I follow before receiving the HPV vaccine?
questions.text:
Consult your doctor to find out if a vaccination is suitable for you if:
You are pregnant or planning to become pregnant
You are not feeling well and having a fever
You are allergic to this vaccine or any of the other ingredients of the HPV vaccine
You are taking any other medications

questions.title: What precautions should I follow before receiving the pneumococcal vaccine?
questions.text:
Inform your healthcare professional if:
You are allergic to this vaccine or any of the other ingredients of this vaccine
You have a history of Guillain-Barré syndrome (a rare nerve condition)
You are pregnant or breastfeeding

questions.title: Where can I find the full list of CHAS GPs that offer subsidised vaccinations?
questions.text:
The full list of CHAS GPs can be found (here) .
Before heading down, please call the clinic to check if they offer the specific vaccine you’re looking for, as vaccine availability may vary.
Enrolment on the Health Appointment System (HAS) is voluntary for clinics. However, you can still use HAS to book an appointment online at an available CHAS GP clinic without needing to call the clinic directly.

questions.title: Who should receive the HPV vaccination?
questions.text: In Singapore, according to the National Childhood Immunisation Schedule (NCIS) and National Adult Immunisation Schedule (NAIS), HPV vaccination is recommended for females aged 9 to 26 years.

questions.title: What are the infection prevention control measures to minimise transmission at home?
questions.text:
You may wish to observe the following guidelines while recovering at home to minimise risk of transmission:
1. Take appropriate infection prevention control measures during your recovery at home. Should you reside with a vulnerable household member, preventive measures such as wearing a mask and not sharing a room with other household members should be taken to mitigate infection spread. Alternatively, consider other accommodation arrangements, if possible.
2. Practise good personal hygiene by washing your hands regularly with soap and water.
3. You may wish to monitor your oxygen saturation using an oximeter and temperature if unwell.

questions.title: I was tested positive. Can I recover at home with other household members?
questions.text: Yes. You can recover at home with other household members who are well. Do take precautionary measures to minimise the risk of transmission.

questions.title: Why do I have to be quarantined?
questions.text: You are under quarantine as you were identified as a close contact of a mpox case. The prevailing definition of a “close contact” means that you were in close proximity to an mpox case during his/her infectious period for a significant period of time.

questions.title: Why do I have to be isolated?
questions.text: Isolation is necessary to limit the spread of the virus in the community.

questions.title: Are pets allowed at my home while I am under isolation order?
questions.text:
Pets are allowed to remain at home during your isolation period. However, as a precaution, you may wish to minimise direct contact with them as animals can be infected.
When possible, delegate pet care to other household members and keep pets away from personal items, beddings, and clothing, etc.
Good hygiene should be practised, including thorough handwashing after handling pets. Veterinary attention should be promptly sought for animals that are unwell.

questions.title: What is an MOH-designated Isolation Facility? Who is it managed by?
questions.text:
An MOH-designated Isolation Facility is a facility set up for persons under quarantine due to risk of exposure to infectious diseases of concern, including mpox.
Currently, there is one designated facility which is managed by a managing agent contracted by the Ministry of Health (MOH). If required, MOH can activate other isolation facilities located at various locations in Singapore.

questions.title: Where can I find the latest local updates on the mpox situation?
questions.text: For information on the local situation, please refer to CDA’s website: Weekly Infectious Diseases Bulletin 2025 | Communicable Diseases Agency

questions.title: What should I do if I suspect I might have been infected with mpox?
questions.text: You should see a doctor immediately and inform him/her of your recent exposure and/or travel history. Your doctor will assess your condition accordingly.

questions.title: What is mpox?
questions.text:
Mpox is a disease caused by the monkeypox virus (MPXV). The virus is part of the same family as the virus that causes smallpox. Mpox is not related to chickenpox.
Mpoxis endemic in parts of Central (Clade I) and West Africa (Clade II). It is a zoonotic disease, meaning it can spread from animals to humans. The virus has been found in animals including squirrels, Gambian poached rats, dormice, different species of monkeys and others.

questions.title: What is an Isolation Order (IO) or a Quarantine Order (QO)?
questions.text: An Isolation Order (IO) or a Quarantine Order (QO) is a legal order issued under the Infectious Diseases Act 1976. It may be issued to a person who is suspected or confirmed to be a case or an at-risk individual (e.g. exposed contacts) of an infectious disease. The IO or QO is necessary to limit the spread of the virus in the community.

questions.title: What if I refuse medical examination and/or to be isolated / quarantined?
questions.text:
A person who fails to comply with an Isolation Order (IO) or a Quarantine Order (QO) issued to him/her under the Infectious Diseases Act 1976, or who refuses to cooperate with Health Officers carrying out their duties under the Act, commits an offence and may be arrested without warrant.
The penalty for a first offence is a fine of not exceeding $10,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months or both. For a second or subsequent offence, the penalty is a fine not exceeding $20,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or both.

questions.title: What do I do if I feel unwell while I am isolating at home?
questions.text:
You may contact MOH through the hotline number provided to you in your Isolation Order.
Should you experience the following: shortness of breath/breathlessness, chest pain or chest pressure, changes in your mental state, or any unusual symptoms with your nerves, headache or any neck stiffness, you should call 995 immediately for an ambulance. You are to inform the 995 operator that you are an mpox patient.

questions.title: What happens if I am unable to self-isolate at home?
questions.text: While self-isolation at home is the default option, we understand this may not be possible for everyone. If you cannot isolate at home, you will need to make alternative arrangements such as staying with relatives or friends who can provide a separate room.

questions.title: My doctor suspects I have mpox. What happens if I am tested positive?
questions.text: If confirmed positive for mpox, you will be isolated and managed clinically in a hospital setting or at home depending on the clinical assessment.

questions.title: My doctor suspects I have mpox. What happens if I am tested negative?
questions.text: If you are tested negative, you are not required to isolate.

questions.title: What happens during my recovery period?
questions.text: For those who qualify for recovery at home or at government isolation facility, you will receive regular telemedical consultations to assess your state of recovery. You may also be conveyed to NCID for additional reviews where necessary.

questions.title: My doctor suspects I have mpox. What happens after I have been tested?
questions.text: Depending on clinical assessment, you will either be isolated in a hospital setting or home.

questions.title: When does my quarantine end?
questions.text: Your quarantine period ends at 12 noon on the last date indicated in your Quarantine Order, or when you receive a Revocation Order, whichever is earlier.

questions.title: I received a call from CDA notifying me of contact tracing. How do I verify if this is not a scam call?
questions.text: To verify the authenticity of calls from CDA, call CDA Hotline 6461 5340 to verify the authenticity of the CDA number and full name of the caller.

questions.title: I have been in recent contact with someone who was issued a Quarantine Order (QO). What should I do?
questions.text:
Monitor your health and seek medical consultation should you be unwell; informing the doctor that you have been in contact with an individual that is serving quarantine.
Please refer to https://www.cda.gov.sg/public/diseases/mpox for more information.

questions.title: I have been informed by CDA that I was in close contact with a confirmed mpox (Clade I) case and need to be quarantined. What should I do?
questions.text: If you have been informed that you had close contact with a confirmed mpox case and will be placed on quarantine, please return to your place of residence immediately and isolate yourself from the rest of your household. MOH will contact you with further details and arrangements for your quarantine.

questions.title: If I am unemployed and on Quarantine Order (QO), who can I go to for social and financial assistance?
questions.text: Please contact MOH at the contact number listed in the Quarantine Order (QO) for assistance.

questions.title: If I am unemployed and on Isolation Order (IO), who can I go to for social and financial assistance?
questions.text: Please contact an MOH Officer at the helpline number furnished in your isolation order.

questions.title: How will my test result be made known to me?
questions.text: The attending physician and/or MOH will inform you of the test result, i.e., whether you are tested positive or negative for the virus.

questions.title: How will I know if I have recovered from mpox?
questions.text: You will be assessed by a doctor who will advise you on your condition and recovery.

questions.title: How long will it take for me to be conveyed to a quarantine facility?
questions.text:
You will typically be conveyed on the same day you are first informed by MOH of your quarantine status and duration.
Please self-isolate while waiting for quarantine instructions and conveyance from MOH.

questions.title: How long is the recovery period?
questions.text: Mpox patients usually recover within two to four weeks, although serious illness and complications may occur especially in vulnerable persons (e.g., young children, pregnant women or immunocompromised individuals).

questions.title: How long does it take for my test result to be available?
questions.text: It typically takes up to 24 hours for your test results. If retesting or additional testing is required, the process will take longer.

questions.title: How is mpox spread?
questions.text:
Mpox can spread through physical contact with infected individuals, skin lesions and body fluids, contaminated materials and environments, or exposure to respiratory secretions. The virus can also spread from animals to humans, e.g., through bite or scratch from an infected animal, bush meat preparation, or direct contact with the blood, body fluids, or skin or mucosal lesions of infected animals.
Please refer to CDA’s website https://www.cda.gov.sg/public/diseases/mpoxfor more information on mpox.

questions.title: If I am under Quarantine Order (QO), do I have to pay for medical assessment and quarantine for mpox?
questions.text: Costs related to medical assessment and quarantine for the mpox will be borne by the Government of Singapore.

questions.title: Does MOH/CDA publish an update to the list of countries affected by mpox?
questions.text: MOH/CDA does not maintain an updated list of countries affected by mpox. Please refer to WHO’s website for the latest update on the global situation for mpox.

questions.title: Can vaccination protect oneself against mpox entirely?
questions.text:
The MVA-BN (JYNNEOS) vaccine is estimated to provide over 80% protection against mpox, although current data remains limited in concluding the level and duration of protection conferred by vaccination.
Individuals are therefore advised to continue adhering to the recommended precautions against the disease, such as avoiding high-risk sexual activities and practising good personal hygiene.

questions.title: Can I quarantine together with my family member(s) / travel companion(s)?
questions.text: For public health reasons, a Person-Under-Quarantine (PUQ) must be isolated in a separate room from anyone not under quarantine orders, including family members and travel companions.

questions.title: Can I get vaccinated against mpox in Singapore?
questions.text:
The MVA-BN (JYNNEOS), a third-generation smallpox vaccine, is currently available in Singapore as Post Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) for persons who have been identified to be close contacts of confirmed mpox cases.
In line with international recommendations, mass population-wide vaccination is currently not recommended as a preventive strategy for mpox, as the risk to the general public remains low with disease transmission predominantly via close physical or prolonged contact. Members of the public are advised to take the recommended precautionary measures such as avoiding high-risk sexual activities and practising good personal hygiene.

questions.title: I have been informed by MOH/CDA that I was in close contact with a confirmed mpox case. Where will I be quarantined?
questions.text: If you are required to quarantine for mpox, you will serve your quarantine at an MOH-designated Isolation Facility.

questions.title: At the end of the isolation / quarantine period, will transport be provided for me to return home?
questions.text: You will be required to arrange your own transport to your place of residence after completion of the isolation / quarantine period.

questions.title: Are meals provided at the MOH-designated Isolation Facility? I have specific dietary needs.
questions.text:
Yes, meals are provided at the MOH-designated Isolation Facility.
If you have specific dietary needs, please inform the MOH Duty Officer or the facility’s Duty Manager as soon as possible to facilitate the necessary arrangements. Where the facility is unable to cater to your specific dietary needs due to late requests, you may make alternative meal arrangements (e.g. contactless food delivery from family or friends, or delivery services) at your own expense.

questions.title: I am a Pregnant patient. What should I do if I become unwell?
questions.text:
Pregnant women are at higher risk of severe illness from COVID-19.
You are advised to recover under the care of your doctors. Monitor yourself, and if you develop fever, cough or difficulty in breathing, or severe, prolonged or worsening ARI symptoms, you should seek medical attention early.
If your gestational age is 28 weeks or greater, you are advised to seek medical attention.

questions.title: I am a patient ≥ 60 years old. What should I do if I become unwell?
questions.text: Medically vulnerable persons (i.e. elderly persons aged 65 years and above and those with chronic medical conditions) are at greater risk of severe disease or complications when infected with COVID-19. If you develop ARI symptoms, or have severe, prolonged or worsening ARI symptoms, you should consult your doctor for medical management.

questions.title: Why is mask-wearing still required for higher-risk healthcare settings and residential care settings?
questions.text:
MOH has retained the practice of mask-wearing for higher-risk healthcare and community care settings, including inpatient wards, emergency departments and residential care facilities. These are settings where vulnerable persons, including the elderly and immunocompromised, may need to access services, and where the risk of infection is compounded by large crowds and prolonged close contact with others who might be infected.
Hence, to protect the vulnerable persons receiving care and the healthcare staff delivering care services at these premises, mask wearing will continue to be required at these settings.

questions.title: What is the treatment for COVID-19?
questions.text:
COVID-19 is generally managed with supportive treatment, depending on the patient’s clinical condition and symptoms.
Treatment and drugs for COVID-19 are available for infected cases with severe disease or persons who are at high-risk of severe COVID-19.

questions.title: What is the COVID-19 General Advisory?
questions.text:
Persons with mild acute respiratory infections symptoms, including those infected with COVID-19, should stay at home until their symptoms resolve. If there is a need to go out while symptomatic, they should exercise social responsibility by minimising social interactions, wearing a mask, and avoiding crowded places or meeting medically vulnerable persons.
Medically vulnerable persons such as seniors and those with chronic medical conditions, as well as persons with severe, prolonged, or worsening symptoms, should see a doctor.

questions.title: I may have been exposed to COVID-19 but I have a COVID-19 vaccination appointment soon. Can I still go get the vaccination?
questions.text:
If you are well and asymptomatic, you may proceed with your COVID-19 vaccination appointment.
If you have any further concerns, you may check with the vaccine provider.

questions.title: I have received a call from MOH. How do I verify if that is true?
questions.text:
To verify the authenticity of calls from MOH, you may wish to:
1. Take down the MOH number and full name of the caller who dialled your number.
2. Call MOH General Line 6325 9220 to verify the authenticity of the above information.
3. Please note that at all times, MOH will not ask for your financial details. MOH will also not ask you to collect documents from MOH, unless your company has an existing business with MOH.

questions.title: How does COVID-19 spread?
questions.text: COVID-19 is primarily transmitted through inhalation of infectious respiratory particles when an infected person coughs or sneezes. It can also be transmitted via contact with contaminated surfaces such as when a person touches these contaminated surfaces and then touches their eyes, nose or mouth.

questions.title: Do I have to pay for the ART and consultation? How much does it cost?
questions.text:
From 1 Apr 2023, there will no longer be extra subsidies at polyclinics for the testing (ARTs and PCRs) and treatment of all respiratory infections.
Singaporeans will continue to enjoy prevailing subsidies under the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) at CHAS General Practitioner clinics. At polyclinics, prevailing polyclinic subsidies will apply.

questions.title: I am well but I had tested positive for COVID-19. What should I do?
questions.text:
While there are no legal requirements for COVID-19-positive individuals to isolate, you are strongly encouraged to exercise personal and social responsibility to reduce transmission risks. In particular, persons who test positive for COVID-19 should:
· Stay away from work, school, or public places until their symptoms have fully resolved. If there is a need to go out while symptomatic, they should minimise social interactions, wear a mask, avoid crowded places and meeting medically vulnerable persons such as seniors or immunocompromised patients.
· Practise good hygiene, such as frequent handwashing and covering their mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing.

questions.title: Is the RSV (Respiratory Synctial Virus) vaccine available in Singapore?
questions.text:
There are two types of RSV vaccines available locally. The RSV vaccines are approved for prevention of lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) for certain groups of people.
If you are keen to receive the vaccine, do consult your doctor who will be able to recommend the type of RSV vaccine which is suitable for you.

questions.title: How does tuberculosis (TB) Spread?
questions.text:
TB is typically spread through prolonged exposure (days to weeks, rather than minutes to hours) to an individual with active TB disease.
When a patient with active TB disease coughs, TB bacteria is released into the air and may be inhaled by those around – prolonged exposure can result in acquiring TB infection.
A person cannot get TB from sharing cups, eating utensils, and food. TB is also not spread through shaking someone’s hand, kissing, or touching bed linens or toilet seats.

questions.title: Why can't I find my Healthier SG clinic of choice? What do I do if my existing General Practitioner (GP) is not a Healthier SG clinic?
questions.text:
For Healthier SG, residents can enrol only with a clinic that is participating in Healthier SG. GP clinics that are not Healthier SG will not be available for selection.
As you will need to enrol with a Healthier SG GP clinic to access Healthier SG benefits, you are strongly encouraged to choose from the list of Healthier SG clinics in HealthHub.
You may continue to visit non-Healthier SG clinics even after your enrolment. However, Healthier SG benefits will not be applicable at clinics that you are not enrolled with, so you would only be able to enjoy the existing schemes such as CHAS and MediSave.
If your current GP is not on Healthier SG, you could also encourage your GP to onboard Healthier SG.

questions.title: Who do I contact should I need to amend my appointments for referrals?
questions.text: Please inform the clinic you were referred to that you would like to change your appointment. If you are unsure of the clinic you were referred to, please contact your enrolled Healthier SG GP clinic for clarification.

questions.title: What is the difference between this donation and Mosque Building and Mendaki Fund (MBMF)?
questions.text:
Mosque Building dan Mendaki Fund (MBMF) which is deducted from every Muslim employees’ monthly salary goes towards paying for the cost of constructing new mosque buildings and the upgrading of older mosques.
All operational costs, such as manpower and utility bills still depend large on donations from congregants. This portal aims fulfil that throughout online donations. All your donations will be channeled to the local mosques to meet their operational needs.

questions.title: What are the benefits of paying my Zakat by Giro?
questions.text:
1. It is cashless and convenient.
2. You can better manage and plan for your long-term assets.

questions.title: Religious Guidance Regarding the COVID-19 Vaccination
questions.text:
The Muslim community is recommended to take the COVID-19 vaccination as it is a basic necessity to protect ourselves and also those around us. The past religious edicts of MUIS regarding medicine and vaccination have addressed the concerns regarding ingredients that are used.
Thus far, the production process of the COVID-19 vaccine and its ingredients are not in conflict with our past religious edicts. In fact, the processes that are involved to produce the COVID-19 vaccination are not against any principles and values of the Islamic Shariah.
OFFICE OF THE MUFTI, 13 DEC 2020

questions.title: How much is the current contribution rate to Mosque Building and Mendaki Fund (MBMF)?
questions.text:
You may visit the link below for the current contribution rate to MBMF:
https://www.muis.gov.sg/mosque/Mosque-Infrastructure/About-MBMF/Employer-Information

questions.title: Does a Muslim-owned eating establishment require Halal certification from Muis?
questions.text:
In general, halal certification is voluntary in Singapore. Owners of eating establishments, Muslims and non-Muslims alike, are advised to obtain MUIS Halal certification as this provides an independent testimony and assurance that the food they serve is halal.
However, we do not penalise Muslim-owned companies should they make halal claims about their operations, as it is their religious responsibility to ensure so.

questions.title: What if I do not have a Singpass account?
questions.text: You can register for a Singpass account on the Singpass website (https://www.singpass.gov.sg). Alternatively, you may visit a Singpass counter for assistance. You can locate the nearest Singpass counter at https://go.gov.sg/singpass-counters.

questions.title: Can I receive another (non-COVID-19) vaccine at the same time as COVID-19 vaccine? How long do I have to wait before getting other vaccines?
questions.text: The vaccines can be administered together with other non-COVID-19 vaccines across all ages.

questions.title: Where can I find out more about the COVID-19 vaccines?
questions.text: Learn more about COVID-19 vaccines by visiting the MOH website.

questions.title: What should I take note of on vaccination day?
questions.text:
Wear short sleeved or clothes where the sleeves can be rolled up.
Bring your ID (NRIC/FIN/Student Pass/Birth Certificate).
Male vaccinees aged 12 – 29 years who are receiving any dose of Moderna/Spikevax, Pfizer-BioNTech/Comirnaty or Novavax/Nuvaxovid COVID-19 vaccines should refrain from participating in strenuous physical activities for one week after vaccination.

questions.title: Where is the Healthier SG Enrolment Station nearest to me? How can I check if my GP / polyclinic is participating in Healthier SG?
questions.text: You may check for your nearest Healthier SG Enrolment Station and the list of participating clinics at https://gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg . Simply enter your postal code or name of clinic to search.

questions.title: Can I get tested for COVID-19 at GP clinics?
questions.text:
Testing for COVID-19 is available at some GP clinics.
You are encouraged to contact the GP clinic before visiting. Your GP will ask about your symptoms and medical history and evaluate your condition.
If needed, your GP will administer the appropriate COVID-19 test at the clinic and these services are chargeable. If not, your GP may refer you to another location where swab testing is available. Self-testing with ART kits is also an option.

questions.title: How can I pay the Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) using my CPF?
questions.text:
As Stamp Duty is payable within 14 days from the date of purchase, you will need to:
Pay Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) in cash first.
Subsequently obtain reimbursement from your CPF account.
Drawing upon CPF savings to pay Stamp Duty is under CPF's purview. For further clarification, please contact CPF Board.

questions.title: What if I do not have enough funds to pay Stamp Duty, can Stamp Duty be deferred or paid by instalments?
questions.text: There are no instalment options available for Stamp Duty. Penalties will be imposed on late and non-payment of stamp duties.

questions.title: How can I get more information about the CDC Vouchers Scheme?
questions.text: Please visit the CDC website https://vouchers.cdc.gov.sg
topics: CDC Vouchers (Merchants) / About CDC Vouchers Scheme

questions.title: How do I check whether my deceased next-of-kin made a CPF nomination?
questions.text: Please refer to this FAQ by the Central Provident Fund Board for more information on CPFB processes with regards to CPF Nomination.

questions.title: How to check the deceased's insurance policy?
questions.text:
Each insurance provider may have their own processes with regards to the release of information related to a deceased policyholder.
You can check with the insurance company on the necessary documentation needed such as a death certificate and proof of your relationship to the deceased, to establish your legitimacy in seeking this information.

questions.title: Can I nominate my family members who are not a Singaporean/ Permanent Resident as my CPF Nominees?
questions.text: CPF members can nominate any person in their nominations, including those who are non-Singaporeans / Permanent Residents.

questions.title: If a person nominates the religion organization under their CPF nomination, will CPF inform the organization?
questions.text:
Nominations are confidential. CPFB will not disclose your nomination details to anyone, including your nominee(s).
This will only be done when you pass away. You are encouraged to keep your nominees informed yourself, should you wish for them to know of the CPF Nomination.

questions.title: How do I report death that occurred overseas?
questions.text:
If a Singapore citizen or permanent resident had passed on overseas, you should register the death and get a death certificate from the foreign authorities in the country where the person had passed on. You can then report the death to ICA with the foreign death certificate to update ICA's records.
Please refer to the ICA website for more information on Report Death that Occurred Overseas.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: How do I book/ change/ cancel my appointment in MyICA?
questions.text: You will be prompted to make an appointment in 'Applications' if required. If you have booked an appointment, you will see your upcoming appointment in 'Notifications'. You can click on the notification to view instructions on how to make changes to the appointment. Alternatively, you can book, change or cancel an appointment in 'e-Services', under 'e-Appointment'.

questions.title: How do I print or save the acknowledgement page?
questions.text: Once payment is successful, you will be brought back to an acknowledgement page. You can use the "Print" or "Save as PDF" function on the web browser to print or save a copy of the acknowledgement page.

questions.title: What should I do if I encounter error messages when submitting my extension of stay application?
Who are the authorised visa agents?
questions.text: You are advised to liaise directly with the nearest Singapore Overseas Mission for information of their authorised visa agents, if any. For locations of the Singapore overseas missions, please visit the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' website under "Overseas Missions".

questions.title: What are the PWM wage requirements for part-time employees who are paid on a monthly basis?
questions.text:
For retail and food services PWMs, and Occupational PWs, you can refer to the respective pages for the applicable PWM hourly wage for part-time work.
For the other Sectoral PWMs,

questions.title: If I'm not eligible for re-employment, can I still get Employment Assistance Payment (EAP)?
questions.text:
No, your employer is not obligated to offer you re-employment or an Employment Assistance Payment (EAP) if you are not eligible. Check if you are eligible for re-employment.
However, your employer should inform you at least 3 months before retirement so you have time to look for a new job. Employers are also encouraged to help employees who aren't eligible for re-employment, such as services like career coaching.

questions.title: Is the Employment Assistance Payment (EAP) taxable or subject to CPF contributions?
questions.text: No, the Employment Assistance Payment (EAP) isn't considered income, and is not taxable or liable for CPF contributions.

questions.title: Why do I need to pay CPF and tax for my workers who are on light duty medical leave?
questions.text:
When an employee is on light duty, they are required to report to work unless they are excused by their employer.
As an employer, you must pay their normal wages, which are not reimbursed by the work injury insurer. As these are the actual wages paid by the employer, both employer and employee have to contribute CPF under the CPF Act.
topics: Workplace safety and health / Work injury compensation

questions.title: Which web browsers are supported?
questions.text: Opera 19, Internet Explorer 10, Chrome 33, Firefox 14, Safari 5 or later versions are supported. Please ensure that your browser is updated for a better experience in navigating MySkillsFuture.

questions.title: Can I access MySkillsFuture on my mobile device?
questions.text: Yes, it is a mobile-friendly website designed for easy reading and navigation.

questions.title: Does MediShield Life cover hospice care?
questions.text: Yes, MediShield Life covers the Inpatient Hospice Palliative Care Service (IHPCS) at inpatient hospices and community hospitals. Please refer to the latest limits here
topics: MediShield Life / Benefits Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Can I submit the MediShield Life claim directly to the Central Provident Fund Board after I have settled the bill at the medical institution?
questions.text:
All MediShield Life claims must be e-filed by medical institutions to ensure accountability and efficiency in claims processing, due to the high volume of claims involved. The Central Provident Fund Board does not accept claims submitted by patients.
The medical institution will seek your authorisation to submit your claim for you. If a payout is due, it will be made directly to the medical institution to offset your bill.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Will the claim details on the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements be changed if the hospital adjusts my bill size?
questions.text: Yes, the online statements will take into account any adjustments made to the hospital bills, if the hospital has informed the Central Provident Fund Board about the change before the date of enquiry.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: What are the claim details that can be viewed from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text:
Claim details will be reflected on the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements whenever there is a MediSave deduction and/ or MediShield Life payout.
You will also be able to view the claim details for MediShield Life claims, even if the claimable amounts are below the deductible.
If you are covered under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), you will be able to view the claim details for claims under the MediShield Life component of your IP on the ’Summary of Healthcare Payment’ page. IPs comprise two components – the MediShield Life component administered by the Central Provident Fund Board, and the additional private insurance component administered by private IP insurers. You will have to contact your private insurer if you want to find out more about the total claim computation under your IP.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Why am I unable to view claim details of my hospitalisation from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text:
Claim details displayed online are accurate as at the date of enquiry. They will be reflected only after the medical institution submits your claim and the MediSave and/or MediShield Life claim is processed.
Please note that the medical institution can only submit your claim after the medical bill has been finalised. Claim details of your hospitalisation will only be available after your MediSave and/or MediShield Life claim is processed.
You can check the status of your MediShield Life claim via 'My Activities' after you log onto "my cpf Online Services" with your SingPass.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Will I be informed of how much I have claimed to date from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text: You will be able to view the total amount that you have claimed for the current policy year, as at the date of enquiry.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: I am an existing ElderShield insured. If I am eligible for ElderShield claims, should I claim from ElderShield or join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you are unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living (i.e. have developed severe disability), and is an ElderShield insured, you should apply to claim under ElderShield so that you can receive your monthly claim payouts in a timely manner.
You will not be eligible for CareShield Life if you have developed severe disability.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Will I have to pay extra premiums if I join CareShield Life with pre-existing medical conditions?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1979 or earlier and have pre-existing medical conditions, you can choose to join CareShield Life if you do not develop severe disability. You will not need to pay additional premiums for pre-existing medical conditions.
You may wish to refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Should I opt out of ElderShield if I would like to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
There is no need to opt out of ElderShield. Your existing ElderShield cover will be upgraded to CareShield Life and the premiums paid for ElderShield will be taken into account.
Simply access the Application to join CareShield Life e-Service using your Singpass and we will notify you on the outcome of your upgrade.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Will ElderShield 300/400 insureds receive subsidies or an incentive as well since there were no incentives in 2002/2007 when ElderShield 300 and 400 were introduced respectively?
questions.text: CareShield Life premium subsidies and incentives will be extended to Singaporeans (including those on ElderShield 300/400 today) if they join CareShield Life, as these are intended to support the increased benefits under CareShield Life and ensure that CareShield Life premiums remain affordable.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I have opted out from ElderShield. Can I join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
You can join CareShield Life if you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1979 or earlier and do not have severe disability.
If you wish to join CareShield Life, you may access the Application to join CareShield Life e-Service and log in using your Singpass to complete the application. Some applicants may need to undergo a disability assessment. You will be informed if a disability assessment is required.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. If I paid ESH300/400 premiums previously but my policy lapsed due to non-payment of premiums, how will my CareShield Life premiums be affected?
questions.text:
As your ElderShield 300/400 policies have lapsed, you are no longer covered under ElderShield 300/400. Your premiums for CareShield Life will be based on the premiums for an uninsured individual.
Those who need assistance with their premium payment after subsidies and incentives will receive Additional Premium Support, and no one who joins CareShield Life will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. If I currently have severe disability but subsequently recover, can I join CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you have recovered from your severe disability, you can choose to join CareShield Life. You may be required to go for a disability assessment to determine your eligibility.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: If I was previously claiming from ElderShield, but have recovered from my severe disability, can I join CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you previously claimed from ElderShield but have since recovered, you can choose to join CareShield Life. You may have to go for a disability assessment.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Will I receive any premium subsidies as an ElderShield 300/400 insured if I upgrade to CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you are an ElderShield insured, you can receive CareShield Life premium subsidies if you upgrade to CareShield Life. CareShield Life is a new scheme, and these subsidies will ensure that the premiums remain affordable even as the new scheme offers better protection and benefits.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: If I am currently on ElderShield 300/400 and choose to upgrade to CareShield Life, can I opt out or downgrade back to ElderShield 300/400 subsequently?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born between 1970 and 1979, you will be automatically enrolled in CareShield Life from 1 December 2021, if you are currently covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme and do not develop severe disability at the point of auto-enrolment. You can opt out of CareShield Life by 31 December 2023 if you do not wish to join the scheme and you will automatically be placed back onto your ElderShield 400 scheme.
Those who are not auto-enrolled can choose to join CareShield Life. If you are an ElderShield insured in this group, you will have a 60-day free-look period from the commencement of your CareShield Life coverage, for you to consider your decision. If you choose to opt out, you will be given a full premium refund and automatically be placed back onto your original ElderShield 300/400 scheme.
You will not be able to opt out from the scheme after the applicable opt-out/free-look periods.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Should I upgrade to/join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
The Government encourages Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1979 or earlier without severe disability to consider joining CareShield Life for basic lifetime financial protection for long-term care. CareShield Life provides monthly cash payout in the event of severe disability, for as long as you are unable to do three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).
The Government also provides support to help make premiums affordable.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: If I have finished claiming my ElderShield 300/400 payouts, can I still join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
You can choose to join CareShield Life but you may be required to undergo a disability assessment. You will not be eligible to join CareShield Life if you are unable to do three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).
However, you can tap on Government subsidies and various Government assistance schemes such as Home Caregiving Grant and ElderFund, and MediSave Care to complement your personal savings and family support, in meeting your long-term care needs. Government assistance schemes such as the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund can also help defray the cost of consumables and assistive devices.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: The current ElderShield scheme has a maximum entry age of 64 years old. Can I join CareShield Life if I am older?
questions.text:
There is no maximum entry age for CareShield Life.
However, as premiums increase with age, you are advised to use the Premium Checker using your Singpass to check your personalised premium payable before applying to join CareShield Life.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier and did not qualify to join ElderShield previously. Am I eligible to join CareShield Life now?
questions.text: You can choose to join CareShield Life if you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1979 or earlier and do not have severe disability. Some applicants may need to undergo a disability assessment. You will be informed if a disability assessment is required.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Can I join both CareShield Life and ElderShield to get double the protection?
questions.text:
You will not be able to be on both CareShield Life and ElderShield.
However, upgrading to CareShield Life will not affect your ElderShield Supplement plan if you already have one. If you are currently covered under ElderShield, you can upgrade to CareShield Life for higher and lifetime payouts. Your ElderShield coverage will be terminated upon joining CareShield Life. For more coverage, you can also purchase Supplement plans from private insurers.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier, and am not enrolled in ElderShield. Am I eligible for CareShield Life?
questions.text: You can join CareShield Life if you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1979 or earlier and do not develop severe disability.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: What will happen to my current ElderShield and Supplement plans after CareShield Life is launched?
questions.text:
The launch of CareShield life will not affect your existing ElderShield and supplement plans.
However, you are encouraged to consider upgrading your ElderShield to CareShield Life if you do not have severe disability. If you choose to upgrade to CareShield Life, the ElderShield premiums that you have paid will be taken into account when computing your CareShield Life premiums, resulting in lower CareShield Life premiums.
The Supplements will also work with CareShield Life cover and do not need to be terminated.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Do I need to back pay premiums from age 30 to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
ElderShield premiums that ElderShield insureds have paid will be taken into account when computing their CareShield Life premiums. Insureds do not need to back pay for CareShield Life coverage starting from 30; they will only be paying for coverage going forward.
However, CareShield Life's annual premiums for older insureds will still be higher than those of younger insureds, as they have less years to spread their premium payment over.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Why is the Government auto-enrolling ElderShield 400 insureds who are born between 1970 to 1979 to CareShield Life?
questions.text: It was to make it more convenient for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents to join CareShield Life. If you were auto-enrolled and do not wish to join the scheme, you can opt out by accessing the Opt-out of CareShield Life e-Service and log in using Singpass to complete the application by 31 December 2023.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Will I be able to join or upgrade to CareShield Life?
questions.text:
You can join or upgrade to CareShield Life if you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1979 or earlier and do not have severe disability.
If you join and are covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2024, you will receive Participation Incentives to help to offset your premiums for 10 years. You will be eligible for Participation Incentives of up to $4,000 ($400/year) if you join by 31 December 2023, and up to $3,000 ($300/year) if you join between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024.
For more information on the types of premium support available, you may refer to this page. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Do I have to undergo a disability assessment before joining CareShield Life?
questions.text: You may be required to undergo a disability assessment prior to joining CareShield Life. Should you be required to attend a disability assessment, you will receive a letter with instructions on how to do so.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I do not have a CPF account. Can I still join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you do not have a CPF account, you will still be invited to join the scheme. You can make your first premium payment via the following methods:
(1) Opening a CPF account by making a top-up to your MediSave Account
(2) A family member* can apply to take over as your premium payer using his/her MediSave savings. To do so, he/she may visit the Change Premium Payer e-Service and log in using his/her own Singpass to complete the “Change Premium Payer” transaction.
*Family member refers to the Insured's spouse, parents, children, siblings or grandchildren.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. If I join CareShield Life, will I get premium rebates?
questions.text:
An independent council has been set up to regularly review and recommend premium and payout adjustments for CareShield Life, in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework.
Should the amount of claims be lower than expected, the council could recommend adjustments to future payouts and premiums (e.g. to reduce the rate of premium increases, or even lower the premiums). Conversely, if the amount of claims is higher than expected, the council could recommend adjustments (e.g. increase the rate of premium increases) to make the scheme more sustainable. A premium rebate is one possible mechanism within this framework.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I have submitted my application to join CareShield Life and received a letter to attend a disability review. How do I go about it?
questions.text:
Please contact an MOH-accredited assessor to schedule your disability review. Your letter will include instructions on how to attend a disability assessment.
If you need further assistance, please contact AIC at 1800 650 6060 or submit an enquiry via “My Correspondences” at https://efinance.aic.sg with your Singpass Login.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I have already paid for ElderShield premiums for this year. Will I get any refund if I apply to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
The ElderShield premiums will be refunded if you join CareShield Life and your CareShield Life commencement date is in the same year as your ElderShield policy renewal.
For example, if you paid ElderShield Premiums in September 2021 (for your ElderShield policy renewal in 2021), and later joined CareShield Life in December 2021, the ElderShield premiums you have paid in September 2021 will be refunded to you.
The refund of ElderShield premiums (if any) will take place upon collection of the first CareShield Life premium.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I have applied to join CareShield Life online. Where do I check for my application status?
questions.text: You may view the status of your application via the My Transactions e-Service (Singpass login is required).
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I have applied to join CareShield Life online. When would I be informed of my application outcome?
questions.text:
We will notify you on the outcome in approximately seven working days if your application has been approved, unsuccessful or pending assessment. You will be notified via the e-mail address that you have registered with a government agency (e.g. Singpass). If there is no e-mail address registered, an SMS will be sent instead.
A letter will only be sent out if both e-mail address and mobile number are unavailable.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I do not have Singpass. Can I apply to join CareShield Life via a hardcopy form?
questions.text:
Please apply for Singpass via the Singpass website. Alternatively you may contact the Singpass Helpdesk at support@singpass.gov.sg or 65 6643 0555.
Thereafter, you can apply to join CareShield Life with your Singpass
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I have applied for CareShield Life and my application has been approved. When will my premiums be deducted?
questions.text: Your CareShield Life premium will be automatically deducted from your or your payer’s MediSave within two months from your policy start date. Please ensure you have sufficient funds in your MediSave for CareShield Life premium payment.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I have applied for CareShield Life and my application has been approved. Why is the coverage status reflected as ‘Waiting for Cover’ on My Policy e-Service?
questions.text:
Coverage status will be reflected as 'Active' only after successful premium deduction (about two months from your approved date).
However, please be assured that you will still be eligible for claims while your coverage status is 'Waiting for Cover'.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I have applied for CareShield Life and my application has been approved. Why does it not show up on the Healthcare dashboard – “Long-term care insurance” section?
questions.text:
The information will be displayed after successful premium deduction.
Nevertheless, please be assured that once your application has been approved, that would be your policy start date and you will be eligible to claim if the onset of severe disability falls on or after that date.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: My CareShield Life coverage status on the My Policy e-Service is reflected as ‘Waiting for Cover’. Will I be able to claim from CareShield Life?
questions.text:
As your CareShield Life application has been approved, you will be eligible to claim if the onset of severe disability falls on or after your CareShield Life policy start date. This applies even if the premiums have not been deducted.
Should you wish to claim from CareShield Life, you can submit your application via the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS) Application Portal using your Singpass.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Why are Government subsidies provided for CareShield Life and not for ElderShield?
questions.text:
Government subsidies are provided for CareShield Life as it is a mandatory scheme for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or after, unlike ElderShield which is optional.
While CareShield Life is also optional for those born before 1979, they would not be able to cancel their CareShield Life cover after the 60-days free-look period. Premium subsidies are provided to help the lower- to middle-income pay their CareShield Life premiums. On the other hand, ElderShield policyholders have the option to opt out or cancel their policy anytime.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Why is my participation incentive $0?
questions.text: Participation Incentive is only extended to Singapore Citizens (SCs). However, both SCs and Permanent Residents (PRs) will be entitled to Government subsidies, if you are from a lower- to middle-income household. PRs enjoy half the applicable subsidies that SCs enjoy.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I have applied to opt out of CareShield Life as I belong to the optional group (i.e. born in 1979 or earlier) and the cover is still within my free-look period. When will my application be approved?
questions.text:
Your application to opt out of CareShield Life will be processed after one working day. You will receive a notification once your application has been processed.
You may view the status of your application via My Transactions e-Service (Singpass login is required).
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I was born in 1979 or earlier and would like to opt out of CareShield Life. When will the premiums be refunded to my MediSave if I opt out?
questions.text:
You will not be able to opt out from CareShield Life after the applicable opt-out/free-look period. If you choose to opt out of CareShield Life within the applicable opt-out/free-look period, you will be given a full premium refund after one working day. If you were covered by ElderShield prior to your enrolment into CareShield Life, you will be automatically placed back onto your original ElderShield scheme.
You may view the refund made to your MediSave via Transaction History at cpf.gov.sg (Singpass login is required).
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Can I sign up for CareShield Life on behalf of my parent/spouse/sibling?
questions.text:
Your family member’s Singpass will be required to sign up for CareShield Life.
You can guide your family member to use his/her Singpass to apply for CareShield Life by accessing cpf.gov.sg/CSLeServices > Application to join CareShield Life e-Service. Some applicants may need to undergo a disability assessment. Your family member will be informed by Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) if a disability assessment is required, after his/her application.
If they are facing difficulties you can accompany them to the Community Clubs/Centres or CPF Service Centres to sign up.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Will I receive the Participation Incentives of up to $4,000 as long as I apply to join by 31 December 2023?
questions.text:
It depends on whether you will be required to undergo a disability assessment as part of the underwriting process.
If you are not required to undergo a disability assessment by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and apply to join CareShield Life using our eService by 31 December 2023, you will be eligible for Participation Incentives of up to $4,000.
If you are required to undergo a disability assessment by AIC and attend your disability assessment after 31 December 2023, you will not be eligible for the Participation Incentives of up to $4,000 as your application will only be approved as per your disability assessment date.
Therefore, you are encouraged to apply to join CareShield Life early if you are planning to do so.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I have previously joined and opted out from CareShield Life. Will I still be eligible for Participation Incentives of up to $4,000 if I join CareShield Life by 31 December 2023?
questions.text: You will be eligible for Participation Incentives of up to $4,000 even if you have previously opted out, as long as you are a Singaporean Citizen who joins and are covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2023.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Why is there a need to start CareShield Life earlier at age 30?
questions.text:
Starting CareShield Life at age 30 allows a longer period for premiums payment to be spread over. A longer duration of premium payment allows insureds to spread premium payment over more years, so as to reduce annual premiums payable. Consequently, insureds will benefit from additional years of coverage starting from age 30.
By the age of 30, most Singaporeans would have started working and many would have worked for a few years. It is also a good time to start planning for their long-term care needs. They would have started contributing to their MediSave, and should be able to cover their CareShield Life premiums without out-of-pocket expenses.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: I am born in 1990 or later, when will I be notified of my CareShield Life cover?
questions.text: If you are born after 1990, you will receive a CareShield Life welcome package about two months before your 30th birthday.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: I am going to be 29 years old when CareShield Life is launched. If I have severe disability, will I be able to join the scheme earlier?
questions.text:
Under CareShield Life, premiums paid by insureds are designed to be risk-pooled within their own generation and used to cover their claims in the event of severe disability.
As there is no risk pool for your cohort when the scheme is launched, your cohort will be covered under CareShield Life when you turn 30 years old, even if you have developed severe disability.
You may refer to Government support schemes specifically for younger Singaporeans who have developed disability and their caregivers (age 65 and below) on the SG Enable's website or speak to SG Enable at 1800-8585-885.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: Why are Singaporeans not covered by CareShield Life from birth?
questions.text:
The priority of CareShield Life is to provide protection against severe disability during old age, when Singaporeans are most likely to need long-term care.
There are various support schemes for families who need support for their loved ones who are younger than the starting age (of 30) for CareShield Life but have developed severe disability, e.g. subsidies for early intervention programmes under the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), and subsidies for therapy services at KK Hospital and the National University Hospital.
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare can provide further assistance to Singaporeans who are unable to pay for their care even after Government subsidies and other means of support.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later and am terminally ill but do not develop severe disability. Can I be exempted from CareShield Life?
questions.text:
As CareShield Life is universal for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later, there are no exemptions. As long as you are covered under CareShield Life, you can still receive monthly payouts in the event of severe disability.
The Government will support Singaporeans who are unable to afford their premiums, so that no one will lose their coverage due to financial difficulties.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later, and I have pre-existing severe disabilities or medical conditions. Do I need to pay additional CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
All Singaporean Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later, including those with pre-existing severe disabilities, will be able to enjoy benefits under CareShield Life, regardless of your ability to pay premiums. As such, you will not have to pay additional CareShield Life premiums.
As part of collective responsibility, those with pre-existing severe disabilities should contribute one premium to join the scheme. The payment amount is less than the first monthly CareShield Life payout you will receive. Upon joining the scheme, you will continue to receive monthly payouts for as long as you are unable to do three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).
The Government will provide means-tested premium subsidies, and Additional Premium Support to help those who are still unable to afford premiums even after subsidies. Claims will be paid out as long as insureds meet the claims criteria.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later. Why should I pay for the inclusion of those with pre-existing disabilities into CareShield Life?
questions.text: Including those with pre-existing severe disabilities will strengthen collective responsibility and is fundamental to the inclusive and caring society Singaporeans seek to build. Less than 0.1% of Singaporeans aged 30 to 40 are estimated to have pre-existing severe disability. Hence, the cost of covering those with pre-existing severe disability amongst those born in 1980 or later does not have a significant impact on premiums.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later and I have pre-existing severe disabilities. Will I need to pay premiums for CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1980 or later, you will be able to enjoy protection under CareShield Life, regardless of your ability to pay premiums, even if you have pre-existing disabilities.
As part of collective responsibility, those with pre-existing disabilities should contribute one premium payment to join the scheme. The payment amount is less than the first monthly CareShield Life payout you will receive. Upon joining the scheme, you will continue to receive monthly payouts for as long as you are unable to do three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).
The Government will provide means-tested premium subsidies, and Additional Premium Support to help those who are still unable to afford premiums even after subsidies. Claims will be paid out as long as insureds meet the claims criteria.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: If I reside overseas, can I suspend my premium payment for CareShield Life?
questions.text: CareShield Life will provide monthly cash payouts in the event of severe disability. Today, overseas Singaporeans are able to file ElderShield claims from abroad and receive payouts to support their care costs wherever they may be. This applies even for those who have permanently relocated abroad. This will continue to apply for CareShield Life. Hence, premium payments for overseas Singaporeans cannot be suspended.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: If I have already bought private insurance plans for disability, will there be duplicative coverage when I join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
There are different private insurance plans on the market. Most cover total and permanent disability or are meant to insure against loss of income when an individual develops disability and is unable to work. As such, private insurance plans typically cease coverage between ages 60 to 70 when most insureds retire. CareShield Life, however, provides lifetime coverage and ensures that an individual will receive coverage even if the individual develops severe disability in their later years.
In addition, unlike private insurance products which cease coverage if insureds are unable to pay the premiums, under CareShield Life, coverage will not cease if an individual is unable to pay premiums due to financial difficulties. The Government will provide premium subsidies and additional premium support.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later and have developed severe disability. Can I still benefit from CareShield Life?
questions.text: CareShield Life will cover all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later, including those who have pre-existing medical conditions or severe disability. You will be able to benefit from CareShield Life after you are enrolled into CareShield Life on 1 October 2020 or when you turn 30 years old, whichever is later.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later. When can I join CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you are born in 1980 and after, you will be automatically covered by CareShield Life on 1 October 2020 or when you turn 30.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: How can I find out if I am covered under CareShield Life?
questions.text: You can log in to My Policy using your Singpass to find out if you are covered under CareShield Life.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: What happens to an insured’s CareShield Life policy when he/she passes away?
questions.text: An insured’s CareShield Life policy will be terminated when he/she passes away. Any premiums paid will refunded to the premium payer’s MediSave if the insured passes away within the first 60 days of the first policy year. No premium refund will be made thereafter.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: Who should I contact if I have enquiries relating to CareShield Life?
questions.text: For CareShield Life matters, you may contact us at Write to us or 1800 222 3399/+65 6222 3399 (overseas) from Monday to Friday, 8.00 am to 5.30 pm
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later, when will I be notified of my CareShield Life cover?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1980 or later, you will be automatically covered under CareShield Life on 1 October 2020, or when you turn 30, whichever is later.
If you are born between 1980 and 1990 (i.e. aged 30 to 40 in 2020), you will receive a CareShield Life welcome package informing you of your CareShield Life cover, by 2 September 2020 or up to two months before your 30th birthday, whichever is later. If you are born after 1990 (i.e. aged below 30 in 2020), you will receive a CareShield Life welcome package before you reach age 30.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: What happens to an insured’s CareShield Life policy when he/she is no longer a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident?
questions.text: The insured’s CareShield Life policy will be automatically terminated and any premiums paid will be refunded to the premium payer’s MediSave if it is within the first 60 days of the first policy year. No premium refund will be made thereafter.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later, who can be covered under CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you are born in 1980 or later, you will be automatically covered under CareShield Life from 1 October 2020, or when you turn 30, whichever is later.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: When do I have to pay for my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text: Your CareShield Life premium is payable annually. The premium payable will be automatically deducted from your or your premium payer’s MediSave within one month from your policy anniversary. You can refer to the My Policy e-Service to check if you have any premiums payable.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: What will be the rate of premium and payout increment for CareShield Life?
questions.text:
The rate of premium and payout increases for CareShield Life will have to be reviewed regularly based on actuarial principles, taking into account factors like changes in claims experience and longevity. This is important to keep the fund sustainable.
An independent council has been set up to regularly review these trends and advise the Government on premium and payout adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework. Actual future premiums and monthly payouts will vary depending on the regular adjustments.
To give Singaporeans greater certainty in the first five years, payouts and premiums* will each increase by 2% per year.
*2% increase of premiums per year excludes GST.

questions.title: How was the starting payout of $600 per month for CareShield Life decided?
questions.text:
Long-term care costs vary depending on one’s care needs and arrangements. How one finances these costs also vary, depending on one’s financial resources.
In deciding the enhanced payouts, the ElderShield Review Committee took into account the basic long-term care costs for a range of services and settings, other sources of long-term care funding, such as Government subsidies and assistance schemes, community support, personal savings, family support and Government-funded safety nets e.g. MediFund or ComCare; as well as the need to balance benefits and premium affordability. As part of the overall enhancements to long-term care financing, CareShield Life will provide better protection and assurance to Singaporeans for their basic long-term care needs.
If you wish to have additional coverage, you may consider supplementing your basic CareShield Life insurance with Supplements from the private insurers.

questions.title: Why do CareShield Life payouts stop increasing once insureds stop paying premiums e.g. when they make a claim or turn 67?
questions.text:
CareShield Life payout increases will need to be supported by premium adjustments, to keep the scheme sustainable. Those who wish to have payouts that increase for life may opt to purchase Supplements. Insurers may also wish to take note of CareShield Life features when designing Supplements.
CareShield Life payouts should also not be seen in isolation, but complement existing Government subsidies, Government assistance schemes, community support, personal savings and family support, to better assist Singaporeans with their basic long-term care costs. They can also make monthly cash withdrawals of up to $200 from their and/or their spouse’s MediSave Account(s) under MediSave Care.
For Singaporeans who are unable to pay for their care even after Government subsidies, CareShield Life payouts and personal savings, there are Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare which can provide further assistance.

questions.title: As a pensioner, can I receive any special benefits under CareShield Life?
questions.text: There are no special benefits for pensioners under CareShield Life. Participation in CareShield Life is optional for you, and you can join CareShield Life if you do not develop severe disability. If you are interested in CareShield Life, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass for information on your personalised premiums and premium support.

questions.title: CareShield Life is still targeted at those with severe disability i.e. unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living. Why was this retained?
questions.text:
CareShield Life is targeted at severe disability, so that premiums can be kept affordable for all insureds.
If you are a Singaporean with mild or moderate disabilities, and need long-term care, you can tap on means-tested Government subsidies for long-term care services, as well as other Government assistance schemes (e.g. the Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund) to complement your personal savings and family support.
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund/ComCare can also help you pay for these long-term care costs, should you be unable to afford long-term care services.
If you wish to cover yourself for less severe disabilities, you can consider purchasing Supplements from the private insurers.

questions.title: Why not allow insureds to choose from different CareShield Life plans depending on their ability to pay?
questions.text:
CareShield Life is intended to provide better protection for basic long-term care needs, when payouts are taken together with other long-term care financing sources.
If you wish to have additional coverage beyond what CareShield Life provides, you can consider purchasing Supplements from private insurers.

questions.title: Why can’t CareShield Life automatically reimburse long-term care costs like MediShield Life does for hospital bills?
questions.text:
