The deductions are done after the auction date (i.e. the date where the allotment of your T-bills purchase has been finalised) but before the issue date of the T-bills.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I purchase a regular premium insurance policy under CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: With effect from 1 January 2001, CPF savings cannot be used for new regular premium insurance policies. Only Single Premium or Recurring Single Premium insurance policy is allowed under CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account and CPF Investment Scheme-Special Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I continue to use my Ordinary Account savings to service my regular premium insurance bought before 1 January 2001, even if my balance falls below $20,000?
questions.text: You can continue to service the future premiums using your Ordinary Account savings, even if your balance falls below $20,000. This applies to you even after age 55 as long as you have set aside the Full Retirement Sum or the Basic Retirement Sum with sufficient property charge/pledge in the Retirement Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How will the restriction on investments for the first $20,000 in Ordinary Account and the first $40,000 in Special Account affect me?
questions.text:
The first $60,000 of your combined CPF accounts earns an extra 1% interest. To enable members to earn extra interest, only monies in excess of $20,000 in your Ordinary Account (OA) and $40,000 in your Special Account (SA) can be invested.
However, you can continue to service your agent bank fees and regular premium insurance policies (excludes recurring single premium insurance policies or regular savings plans for unit trusts) even if your OA balance falls below $20,000.
If you have already made investments using your OA or SA balances, you are not required to sell these investments.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What are the options available to me if I foresee that I do not have sufficient CPF to continue paying the instalments on my regular premium insurance policy?
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: If I have an existing regular premium insurance policy bought using cash, can I continue to service the future premiums using CPF under the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA)?
questions.text: With effect from 1 January 2001, CPF savings cannot be used for new regular premium insurance policies, regardless of whether the policies are converted from cash or newly bought from insurance companies.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: If I have terminated my insurance policy bought using CPF, can I reinstate the policy and pay the outstanding premiums and future premiums using CPF?
questions.text: You need to liaise with your insurance company on the reinstatement of the policy. Upon reinstatement, you may pay the outstanding and future premiums using CPF. However, no CPF can be used to pay any outstanding interest owing to the insurance company.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I invest in Fixed Deposit in foreign currency under the CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: Foreign currency Fixed Deposits are not included under the CPF Investment Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Is there a minimum interest rate for CPF Investment Scheme Fixed Deposit (FD) that FD Banks must offer?
questions.text: With effect from 1 May 2007, Fixed Deposit (FD) Banks must offer a minimum effective interest rate that is at least the prevailing CPF interest rate for new placements or roll over of any CPF Investment Scheme FDs. In this way, members will not be worse off than leaving their monies in the CPF Accounts.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I use CPF savings to place Fixed Deposits under the CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: You can use your CPF savings to place Fixed Deposits (FD) with any of the four Fixed Deposit Banks (DBS, Maybank, OCBC and UOB) under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS). However, none of the FD banks are currently offering FD products under CPFIS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: I have forgotten my CPF Investment Account Number. How can I go about checking this?
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I transfer my CPF Investment Account under CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account from one agent bank to another? If so, must I sell my investments first?
questions.text: You may transfer your CPF Investment Account from one agent bank to another. You need not sell your investments, except for your investment in gold bought from your agent bank (excluding gold Exchange Traded Funds). All your investments and cash balances will be transferred along with your CPF Investment Account. To transfer your CPF Investment Account, you need to apply at the bank which you intend to transfer your account to.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I accept gifts and/or rebates from my service providers when investing under CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: All gifts and/or rebates arising from investing under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) must be converted to cash and refunded back to your CPF Ordinary and Special Accounts respectively. You are not allowed to receive gifts and/or rebates direct from your service provider as this will result in a leakage of CPF funds. Alternatively, you may also receive rebates in the form of additional units of investments under the CPFIS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What is Wrap fee?
questions.text:
Wrap fee is an ongoing fee charged by a financial adviser to an investor, for providing bundled investment services, including advisory, brokerage and administrative. The fee is usually charged as a percentage on the market value of assets under management of the financial adviser.
Wrap fee is consumptive and erodes returns on investment funds. As CPF monies are meant for retirement and to prevent our members from paying excessive wrap fees, CPF Board has capped wrap fees at 0.4% per annum with effect from 1 October 2020. This is in line with the Board's continuing efforts to lower the cost of investment for our members.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What should I do if my wrap account currently charges me a wrap fee of more than 0.4% per annum?
questions.text: With effect from 1 October 2020, your wrap fee payable will be capped at 0.4% per annum. You should contact your financial adviser or Investment Administrators if you continue to pay more than the capped rate after 1 October 2020.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What type of investor will be affected by the wrap fee cap?
questions.text: The wrap fee cap will affect CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) investors who have wrap accounts with any of the 4 CPFIS-included Investment Administrators.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How will this wrap fee cap affect my investments?
questions.text: Wrap fee is typically paid by redemption of units in your CPF-funded unit trust investment. With effect from 1 October 2020, you should not be paying more than 0.4% per annum in wrap fee from your CPF-funded investment.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: I have invested in a company using CPF. How can I get the latest financial statement or annual report of this company, if the company has been delisted? And what should I do if the company does not respond to my request?
questions.text: You may approach the company for the financial statement or annual report directly. You can mail your request to their office address through registered post. The office addresses of companies can be found on ACRA's BizFile portal. If you do not hear back from the company, please approach your agent bank who will follow up with ACRA.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: I have transferred money from Investment Account back into my CPF Ordinary Account. When does the CPF interest computation start?
questions.text: When you transfer money from your Investment Account to your Ordinary Account (OA), you will start to earn CPF interest on the transferred amount from the following month, after the amount is credited to your OA.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Do I need to pay accrued interest if I used my CPF savings for CPF investments?
questions.text: You do not need to pay back the accrued interest on the CPF savings used for your CPF investments.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will my CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) investments be sold or liquidated when I apply to withdraw my CPFIS investments upon meeting CPF withdrawal conditions?
questions.text: Applying to withdraw your CPFIS investments will not result in liquidation of your investment holdings. If your withdrawal application is approved, your agent bank and/or product providers will contact you on the transfer of your investments to you.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How can I find out my own profit/loss on CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: You may refer to the portfolio statement sent to you by your agent bank or your product provider. If you have sold your investments, the difference between the cost and sale proceeds is your profit/loss. If you have not sold your investments, the difference between the cost and market value is your profit/loss.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What happens if I make a loss on my investments? Do I have to make good the loss?
questions.text: You need not make good your investment loss. However losses will reduce your retirement nest egg.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I withdraw my investment profits?
questions.text: Profits made from investments under the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account and/or CPF Investment Scheme-Special Account are not withdrawable as the purpose of investing is to grow your savings for retirement. However, the profits can be used for other CPF schemes, subject to the terms and conditions of these schemes.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Are my investment profits, interest earned from investments and dividends received taxable?
questions.text: Your investment profits, interest earned from investments and dividends are not taxable under the CPF Investment Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What does the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) Total Profits/Losses statistic measure?
questions.text: The CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) Total Profits/Losses statistic provides a complete representation of the investors total portfolio performance. It takes into account not only the realised profits or losses of investments that were sold, but also the unrealised profits or losses of investments that members held during the reporting period.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How is members' investment performance in the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA)?
questions.text: Please refer to the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) Profits/Losses Report if you wish to view members' investment performance in the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA).
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Where can I find a copy of the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) Profits/Losses Report?
questions.text: Please refer to the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) Profits/Losses Report.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What constitutes "offences" under the CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: Manipulating investment transactions so that a member may siphon his CPF savings in cash thereby withdrawing the savings prematurely, is an offence under CPF Investment Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How are manipulative investment transactions detected?
questions.text: CPF Board continually monitors the trend of various CPF Investment Scheme transactions. The Singapore Exchange also monitors irregularities in share transactions. Transactions that look suspicious are referred to the Commercial Affairs Department for investigation.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will I be charged if my friend conducts manipulative share trading using my CPF and trading accounts (given by me previously) without my knowing?
questions.text: This will depend on the outcome of investigations. However, you should always protect your password and not allow other people to transact in your name without your knowledge or your approval.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will I run the risk of unknowingly breaching CPF laws while trading or investing under the CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: As long as your intention is to invest for the medium to long term, and you did not siphon out any CPF savings by receiving cash for your investment transactions whether through manipulated transaction prices or cash rebates, it is unlikely that you will breach the CPF laws for manipulative transactions.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will I receive any notifications after the transfer of my investments from my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme to CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text:
You will receive a letter from your agent bank, informing you of the details of the investments being transferred from your Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Investment Account to your CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) Investment Account. You will also receive a letter from National University of Singapore after the transfer.
You can also view your Special Account (SA) investment holdings (combination of ASPFAIS-SA and CPFIS-SA) in your SA portfolio statement anytime using your Singpass via my cpf digital services.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: After the merger of Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) and CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS), will the transfer be reflected in any of my CPFIS statements?
questions.text: The transfer will be reflected through the change to the net amount withdrawn. Your net amount withdrawn under the Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme - Ordinary Account (ASPFAIS-OA) will be merged with your net amount withdrawn under the CPF Investment Scheme - Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA). A footnote will be permanently shown in your "CPFIS Stock & Gold Limits Computation" statement, informing you of the amount transferred from your ASPFAIS-OA. For your investments made under Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme -Special Account (ASPFAIS-SA), they will be transferred to your CPF Investment Scheme - Special Account (CPFIS-SA). You are able to view your combined investment holdings in your SA portfolio statement.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What will happen to my stock & gold investment limits arising from the merger of Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme and CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: Your Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme stock & gold investment limits will be merged with your CPF Investment Scheme stock & gold investment limits.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Arising from the merger of Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme and CPF Investment Scheme, do I need to inform my broker or any of the product providers of my new CPF Investment Account number?
questions.text:
Your agent bank will inform the respective product providers, except stockbrokers, of your new Investment Account number. Agent banks would not be able to inform the stockbrokers on your behalf because agent banks do not know which stockbrokers you have trading accounts with.
You will need to inform all your stockbrokers about your new CPF Investment Scheme Investment Account number. If your stockbrokers use the outdated investment account number, your CPF trades will fail and you will need to settle your trades using cash.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: After the transfer of my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme investments to CPF Investment Scheme, what will happen to the sale proceeds if I subsequently sell those investments?
questions.text: All the sale proceeds will be refunded to your CPF Accounts. You can subsequently withdraw the monies subject to CPF withdrawal rules.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will all my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V Insurance Policies be transferred to CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: All your Part V insurance policies will be transferred to your CPF Investment Scheme Investment Account with the agent bank.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Why do I need to open a CPF Investment Scheme Investment Account now to 'hold' my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Investment?
questions.text: The Academic Staff Provident Fund (ASPF) Part V Scheme does not fall under the purview of the ASPF Investment Scheme. Under the ASPF Part V Scheme, the policies were bought under the name of National University Singapore (NUS). NUS had been paying the premiums directly to the insurance companies, after deducting the monies from members' ASPF Ordinary Accounts, without going through the agent banks. As the CPF Board does not have such a scheme, Part V insurance policies have to be transferred to the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) instead. Under the CPFIS-OA, you need to have a CPFIS Investment Account to hold your investments, including the transferred Part V insurance policies.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I use my CPF monies to service the premiums of my Part V Insurance Policy under Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS)?
questions.text: You can use your CPF monies in your Ordinary Account to service the future premiums of your policies (including endowment, whole life or rider policies, and regular premium policies).
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I take a policy loan on my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policy?
questions.text: Policy loans are not allowed for Part V insurance policies under the CPF Investment Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I pledge my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policy?
questions.text: Pledging of Part V insurance policies is not allowed under the CPF Investment Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can my insurance policy continue to run on Automatic Premium Loan (APL) and/or Extended Term Insurance (ETI) after the transfer to CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: Automatic Premium Loan and Extended Term Insurance are allowed to continue after the transfer of your Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policy to CPF Investment Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How may I repay the Automatic Premium Loan (APL) of my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policy?
questions.text: You may repay the Automatic Premium Loan (APL) by paying cash to the insurance company directly. The cash balance in your CPF Investment Scheme Investment Account cannot be used to repay the APL.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I change the life insured under my Part V insurance policy under Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS)?
questions.text: The life insured must be the CPF member whose CPF savings are used to pay premiums.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I nominate beneficiaries to the proceeds of my Part V insurance policy under Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS)?
questions.text:
You may nominate beneficiaries as long as:
No legal or equitable trust, including but not limited to statutory trusts under any written law, is created over the Part V insurance policy; and
Your insurer allows you to do so.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What is an Investment-Linked Insurance Policy (ILP)?
questions.text:
Under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS), you can invest in various Investment-Linked Insurance Policies (ILPs).
An ILP is made up of an insurance component coupled with an investment fund managed by a professional fund manager. Insurers usually set up two or more sub-funds for each ILP with differing investment objectives to suit the risk appetite of different types of policyholders. These underlying ILP sub-funds are similar to unit trusts. The allocation of premiums across these sub-funds may be fixed by the insurer or decided by the policyholder, depending on the structure of the ILP.
The advantage of an ILP is that it effectively combines investments in a unit trust with purchase of insurance coverage. This is also its disadvantage. An investor might prefer a more flexible combination of insurance coverage and unit trust investment that is not offered by any of the ILPs included under the CPFIS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How will I know whether I am ready to invest?
questions.text:
Once you have an understanding of the amount of risk you are comfortable with and of your investment time horizon, you are ready to make some investment decisions. The CPF Board has classified unit trusts, Investment-Linked Insurance Policies (ILPs) and Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) permitted under CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) into the Risk Classification System.
There is a wide range of investments available under the CPFIS to help you achieve your investment objectives and goals. The Risk Classification System is intended to help you determine which of these may be most appropriate for your investment circumstances.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What are the CPF schemes that contribute towards asset enhancement?
questions.text:
The CPF Investment Scheme and the Special Discounted Shares Scheme contribute towards asset enhancement.
You can refer to the Frequently Asked Questions for more details on the schemes.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What are the criteria for inclusion of Property Fund under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)?
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What are the criteria for inclusion of Fixed Deposit Banks under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)?
questions.text:
In considering the inclusion of Fixed Deposit Banks under CPF Investment Scheme, the Board uses the following criteria:
The bank must be locally incorporated with minimum capital funds of S$1.5 billion and good credit rating; or
The bank must be a subsidiary of a locally-incorporated bank which meets the criteria at (i). The bank must continue to be a subsidiary of the locally-incorporated bank; or
If the bank is a foreign bank, it must be accorded the Qualifying Full Bank privileges.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What are the reasons for the Board selecting these new criteria for new funds which wants to be included under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)?
questions.text: The new criteria cover issues that the Board is most concerned with, such as quality, consistency of performance relative to peer group and investment costs.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What proportion of funds applying for admission into CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) has been successful? What is the target under the revised criteria?
questions.text:
Fund managers would generally assess the quality of their funds using the published CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) evaluation criteria before applying for inclusion under CPFIS. Thus far, funds within the top 50 percentile in their global peer group1 have been successful in their application for admission into CPFIS, and the majority of funds that have applied for admission into CPFIS have been admitted.
New funds will need to meet a higher criterion - i.e. they must be among the top 25 percentile of funds. Going forward, we do not expect a significant change in the success rate of application as managers would continue to assess the quality of their funds against the CPFIS evaluation criteria before application.
1 This refers to comparison of funds of similar asset class/strategy on a world-wide basis.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will the funds that have already submitted their applications for inclusion under CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) be affected by the revised criteria?
questions.text: The revised criteria will only apply to fund applications received by the Board from 1 February 2006 onwards.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What is an expense ratio?
questions.text: The expense ratio refers to the ongoing costs of operating a fund by fund managers/insurers expressed as a percentage of the fund's average net assets. Operating costs include investment management fees, trustee fees, and audit fees, etc.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Why is CPF Board reducing the Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps?
questions.text: Reducing the Total Expense Ratio caps is part of CPF Board's continuous efforts to lower the cost of investing under the CPF Investment Scheme. This would help enhance returns, hence enable CPF members who have invested in the fund to accumulate their retirement savings faster.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will there still be a range of funds for CPF investors to choose from?
questions.text: The lowering of the Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps would not have significant impact on the choices of investment under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS). The Board will work with industry players towards complying with the new TER caps, to give CPF members continued choice in terms of the range of funds available under the CPFIS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How are the new Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps determined?
questions.text: The new Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps are determined based on the FY2012 median TERs (for the relevant risk categories) of CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) List A funds, and taking into account industry feedback. Median TERs were also used in 2008 when CPF Board first implemented TER caps for funds under the CPFIS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Is the 3 years track record for new funds applied at the fund level or based on the experience of Fund Management Companies?
questions.text:
The preference for a 3 year performance track record is generally applied at the fund level. Fund managers should preferably show a minimum track record so that they can be better assessed on their ability whether they are able to give consistently good performance against the benchmark for the specific fund they manage.
In the case of indexed funds or Exchange Traded Funds, the 3 year track record is applied differently. The focus will be on the fund management company's technology or systems and processes that they have established to perform the rebalancing functions to track indexes closely1 and their ability to consistently maintain a low cost structure for the index funds they have under management.
1Low tracking error
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How does CPF Board currently assess whether funds admitted are still suitable to remain in CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)?
questions.text: When determining if a product is suitable to be under CPF Investment Scheme, the emphasis so far has been on past performance and the competency of its investment professionals. Re-evaluation will be required for Fund Management Companies/Funds that have undergone material changes in the organisational structure, fund structure or management team.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will the new admission criteria be applied to existing funds under CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: The new criteria will apply to existing funds from 1 January 2011. To help members make better informed investment decisions, the Board will, in due course, step up its member education efforts and also avail relevant information on the performance and expense ratios of existing funds.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What can members do if the funds in which they have already invested do not meet the new standards set by the Board following re-evaluation?
questions.text: Members who have already invested in such funds can continue to remain invested in the funds, or consider switching to other funds or selling out of the funds if the funds no longer meet their investment objective.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What are trailer fees?
questions.text:
Trailer fees are fees payable to distributors (including financial advisors) who sell the fund to the investors. The trailer fees are generally paid out from a fund’s annual management fees (which is part of the total expense ratio1) by the fund manager or product provider to distributors. As such, trailer fees are not additional cost to end investors.
1The expense ratio refers to the ongoing costs of operating a fund by fund managers/insurers expressed as a percentage of the fund's average net assets. Operating costs include investment management fees, trustee fees, and audit fees, etc.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How is CPF Board enhancing the disclosure of trailer fees?
questions.text:
Currently, fund managers pay trailer fees to their distributors who sell their funds to investors. Fund Managers disclose the trailer fees range in their products’ sales documents which distributors (including financial advisors) generally relied upon when selling their products to investors. Such trailer fees range could be too wide to be meaningful to investors. As such, more trailer fees information i.e. the median would be more useful to investors.
From 1 October 2022, Fund Management Companies (FMCs), Insurers, Investment Administrators (IAs), financial advisors and insurance agents are required to disclose trailer fees information (i.e. range and median) in their CPFIS products’ sales documents in order to help CPF investors make informed decision on their investment purchase.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How would I benefit from the enhanced disclosure of trailer fees?
questions.text: You would be able to understand how much trailer fees that your insurance agents and financial advisors receive. The trailer fees information would be presented to you in the sales documents e.g. the funds’ Product Highlight Sheet, prospectus, Policy Illustration for Investment-linked Products (ILPs), subscription forms by your financial advisors.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Do all CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)-included Unit Trusts/ILP sub-funds charge trailer fees?
questions.text: Trailer fees is subjected to the business agreements between product providers and their distributors (including financial advisors). Some funds may not have trailer fees payable to distributors.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Do I need to pay additional fees due to trailer fees disclosure by my product/service providers? Is there any action required of me (as a CPFIS investor)?
questions.text: You do not need to pay any additional fees. No action is required from you (as a CPFIS investor) given that trailer fees are paid by the fund manager or product provider to distributors.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Who can I approach if I want to know more on the trailer fees of the CPF Investment Scheme products?
questions.text: You can approach your product/service provider or financial advisors for more information on trailer fees.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How will this harmonisation affect the funds included under CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: All CPF Investment Scheme funds that have not met the stricter admission criteria and that wish to be able to take in new CPF monies from 1 January 2011 need to be re-evaluated.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How will the re-evaluation affect the funds that I am holding under the CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: Re-evaluation will not affect the funds that you are holding. However if by December 2010, the funds which you are holding do not meet the stricter criteria, or if your Fund Management Company (FMC) / insurer chooses not to have the funds re-evaluated, you will not be able to purchase more units of such funds with your CPF monies.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Is it compulsory to keep switching funds under the CPF Investment Scheme if the funds which I am holding do not meet the stricter criteria?
questions.text: You can opt to hold on to your existing funds without switching.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: If I hold a fund under the CPF Investment Scheme that does not meet the stricter criteria, when must I exercise the switching option?
questions.text:
Funds that are unable to meet the stricter criteria can only take in new CPF monies till December 2010, and you will be given up till 30 June 2011 to exercise the switching option.
In addition, a fund may decide to cease taking in new CPF monies earlier. If this happens, you have to exercise the switching option within the timeframe stipulated by the Fund Management Company/insurer in its communication letter to you.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How will I know whether the funds that I am holding under the CPF Investment Scheme do not meet the stricter criteria by December 2010?
questions.text: If the funds do not meet the stricter criteria by December 2010, the respective Fund Management Company(FMC)/insurer will be required to inform their CPF clients in writing, and to offer their clients three options, by December 2010.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What should I do if the funds that I am holding under the CPF Investment Scheme do not meet the stricter criteria by December 2010?
questions.text: You will be given options by the Fund Management Companies (FMCs) or insurers to hold, redeem or switch your units, for free, into other CPF Investment Scheme funds that are eligible to take in new CPF monies from 1 January 2011. If you decide to switch funds, please consider whether the new funds match your investment objective and risk profile (PDF, 0.2MB).
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What is Special Discounted Shares Scheme?
questions.text: The Special Discounted Share Scheme is part of the Government's asset enhancement programme to make Singapore a share-owning society, thus giving Singaporeans a greater stake in the country.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Where can I find more information about discounted Singtel shares?
questions.text: You can refer to the Singtel website for more information on Singtel shares.

questions.title: Why are my current discounted Singtel shareholdings different from the quantity I purchased in 1993 and/or 1996 even though I did not sell the shares?
questions.text:
Singtel performed capital reductions on 1 September 2004 and 1 September 2006.
In the 2004 capital reduction, Singtel cancelled 1 in every 14 of its shares, with the resultant shareholding rounded-up to the nearest 10 shares, where applicable. Singtel then reimbursed you S$2.36 for each cancelled share.
In the 2006 capital reduction, Singtel cancelled 1 in every 20 of its shares, with the resultant shareholding rounded-up to the nearest 10 shares, where applicable. Singtel reimbursed you $2.74 for each cancelled share.
Both reimbursements were credited into your CPF Ordinary Account. You were then informed, in writing, of the capital reductions in September 2004 and September 2006.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Why are my discounted Singtel shares not reflected in my Central Depository (CDP) statement?
questions.text: Your discounted Singtel shares are held by the Board on your behalf. Your discounted Singtel shares would therefore be reflected in your CPF Statement of Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How would I know if I would make a gain or loss if I were to sell my discounted Singtel shares now?
questions.text: For sale of discounted Singtel shares, you can use the weighted average cost (WAC) method to determine whether you would make a gain or loss.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What are the dividends rates declared by Singtel for the discounted Singtel shares to-date?
questions.text: You may refer to Singtel website or our dividend table for rates declared by Singtel.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Are the dividends received from the discounted Singtel shares subject to tax?
questions.text: Dividends received from your discounted Singtel shares are not taxable.

questions.title: Can I transfer my discounted Singtel shares to another person?
questions.text: Your discounted Singtel shares can only be transferred into a Central Depository Pte Ltd (CDP) securities account under your name after you have set aside the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in your Retirement Account at age 55.

questions.text: To obtain an application form to transfer your discounted Singtel shares for division of matrimonial assets, please write to us.

questions.title: Who is a self-employed person?
questions.text:
A self-employed person (SEP) is someone who performs work for others under a contract for service.
If you earn an income by buying and selling goods or from providing professional or personal services, you’re an SEP. Examples of SEPs include hawkers, taxi drivers, freelancers, sole proprietors or a partner in a partnership.
Visit the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) website to read more on the definition of an SEP.

questions.title: How can I make my MediSave contributions?
questions.text: You can request an instalment plan or make contributions to your outstanding MediSave payable using the Manage your MediSave payable form using your Singpass.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: My mobile number is already registered to my bank account on PayNow. Can the Government credit my Government cash benefits to me via PayNow-Mobile instead of via PayNow-NRIC?
questions.text:
We can only credit your Government cash benefits to you via your PayNow-NRIC-linked bank account. NRIC is an unchanged proxy issued by the Government, compared to mobile numbers which may be easily changed. To ensure that the money is credited to the correct recipient’s bank account, only NRIC will be accepted as the proxy for Government benefits via PayNow.
Eligible seniors who have linked their NRIC to PayNow, with a PayNow-GIRO-participating bank will receive the benefits in this bank account.

questions.title: What should I do if my facial recognition at the ATM with GovCash functions is unsuccessful?
questions.text: If you are unable to verify your identity via Singpass Face Verification at the ATM despite repeated tries, you may visit a NEW ATM located at selected OCBC branches (refer to OCBC website for latest list of NEW ATMs) during the branch operating hours, and OCBC's Digital Ambassadors will be available to assist you.

questions.title: How do I know if the merchants allow me to make purchases using my GovCash?
questions.text: You can only make purchases using GovCash at merchants that accept PayNow/NETS QR code using the LifeSG app. You can look out for the PayNow/NETS logo on the SG QR label that is displayed by the merchants.

questions.title: Can I cancel the payment after I have confirmed the payment utilising my GovCash on the LifeSG mobile app?
questions.text: No, your GovCash balance will be deducted upon successful payment.

questions.title: What is CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
The CPF Lifelong Income For The Elderly (CPF LIFE) is a national longevity insurance annuity scheme that insures you against running out of your retirement savings, by providing you with a monthly payout no matter how long you live.
Unlike investment products which are meant to grow our wealth, insurance products, like CPF LIFE, help to protect us against life's uncertainties.
With CPF LIFE, you can have peace of mind knowing that you will have a steady stream of lifelong income to support your retirement needs. This way, you can enjoy your golden years without having to worry about financial uncertainties, no matter what age you live to.

questions.title: Why do I need CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
Nobody can predict how long anyone will actually live. Therefore, planning how much of your retirement savings to use for living expenses is a dilemma – Spend too much and you might not have enough if you live longer than you thought; spend too little and you might deprive yourself from fully enjoying your hard-earned savings.
With increasing advances in technology and healthcare, you are likely to live longer than your grandparents’ or parents’ generation. Therefore, you cannot predict how long you will live by looking at how long your parents or grandparents live. Otherwise, you may underestimate your lifespan and find your savings depleted with many more years to live when you are no longer able to work.
With CPF LIFE, you do not need to worry about being caught in such a situation but have the assurance of having a steady stream of income, no matter what age you live to.

questions.title: Can I be exempted from CPF LIFE?
questions.text: If you are automatically included under CPF LIFE, you cannot be exempted from CPF LIFE unless you have a pension or commercial annuity that pays the same or higher monthly payout as CPF LIFE. For more information, please refer to the conditions for withdrawing your retirement savings.

questions.title: Why is the increase in CPF LIFE Escalating Plan payouts fixed at 2% per year and not matched to actual inflation rate?
questions.text:
CPF LIFE Escalating Plan payouts are not specifically matched to actual inflation in each year so that the increase in payouts is predictable and stable.
By fixing the increase at 2% per year, CPF LIFE can provide some protection against inflation while keeping premiums at a more affordable level. Additionally, the 2% increase is meant to be a conservative estimate of the average inflation rate over time, which can vary from year to year.

questions.title: What are CPF LIFE premiums invested in and are the investments safe?
questions.text: CPF LIFE premiums are invested in Special Singapore Government Securities (SSGS), which are safe instruments because they are issued and guaranteed by the Government, and shielded from financial market fluctuations.

questions.title: Does my CPF LIFE premium continue to earn interest?
questions.text: Yes, your CPF LIFE premium will continue to earn CPF interest rates with the floor rate of 4%, and up to 2% extra interest on the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances. The interest earned is factored into your monthly payouts and you receive a higher payout from the start.

questions.title: What happens to the CPF interest earned on my CPF LIFE premium?
questions.text: Your CPF LIFE premium will continue to earn CPF interest rates, which is factored into your monthly payouts to increase the amount you receive, compared to if there were no interests earned. These payouts continue for life, even after your initial premium is exhausted, ensuring lifelong financial security in retirement.

questions.title: What is the breakeven point for my CPF LIFE plan i.e. the age when my CPF LIFE premium is fully depleted, and should it matter?
questions.text:
Unlike investment products where we would aim to maximise returns, CPF LIFE is a national longevity insurance annuity product that aims to protect us against the possibility of having nothing to live on when our retirement savings are used up. As we cannot predict how long we will live, it is not relevant to consider the age when our CPF LIFE premium is fully depleted.
If you pass away before your CPF LIFE premium is depleted, your beneficiaries will always get back any remaining CPF LIFE premium that you have put into your plan.

questions.title: I turned 55 before 2016 and joined CPF LIFE at 55. Will the premium deducted for CPF LIFE continue to earn interest?
questions.text: Yes, regardless of the age that you join CPF LIFE, the amount deducted from your Retirement Account savings for the CPF LIFE premium continues to earn CPF interest rates with the floor rate of 4% and up to 2% extra interest on the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances. The interest earned is factored into your monthly payouts, allowing you to receive higher lifelong payouts compared to other annuities offered in the market.

questions.title: How much Retirement Account savings do I need for my desired CPF LIFE monthly payout?
questions.text: You can easily use the Monthly payout estimator to estimate the amount of Retirement Account savings you need, based on your desired monthly payout and choice of payout start age.

questions.title: What is the latest age to join CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
If you are not automatically included in CPF LIFE, the latest age to join CPF LIFE is one month before you turn 80.
If you are automatically included in CPF LIFE, find out when you have to choose your CPF LIFE plan.

questions.title: What happens to my Retirement Account savings when I join CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
It is dependent on the CPF LIFE plan you choose. If you opt for the Escalating or Standard Plan, all your Retirement Account (RA) savings will be used as your CPF LIFE premium.
If you opt for the Basic Plan, about 80-90% of your RA savings will be directly used to provide payouts until age 90. The remaining 10-20% will be deducted as your CPF LIFE premium when you join CPF LIFE and used to provide payouts from age 90 for the rest of your life. As less is used for your CPF LIFE premium, the monthly payout will be lower compared to the Standard Plan. The Basic plan payouts will also decrease correspondingly as your balances are withdrawn over time to provide you with monthly payouts and earn less extra interest*.
* The extra interest is earned on the first $60,000 of your CPF balances and is used to increase your payouts.

questions.title: When can I start receiving my CPF LIFE payouts?
questions.text:
You can choose to start receiving your CPF LIFE payouts anytime between the ages of 65 and 70 using our Plan my monthly payouts service. Consider starting later as your monthly payout will increase by up to 7% for each year that you defer starting.
CPF Board will send you a notification three months before your 65th birthday to explain your options and guide you in choosing your CPF LIFE plan. Your payouts will automatically start when you turn 70 if you have not instructed CPF Board regarding your payouts by then.

questions.title: Is there an age limit for existing CPF LIFE members to increase their CPF LIFE premium?
questions.text: Existing CPF LIFE members can increase their CPF LIFE premium at any age which will help to increase their CPF LIFE monthly payouts.

questions.title: Can I defer the start of my CPF LIFE monthly payouts beyond 70?
questions.text:
The purpose of CPF savings is to provide members with monthly payouts in their retirement. Hence, you will have to start your CPF LIFE monthly payouts, including any Additional Monthly Payouts (AMP), latest by age 70.
We understand that some members think of their savings in CPF as an investment to enjoy the interest rates. If you have no immediate need for the payouts, you can consider investing them outside the CPF system. Do note that investing outside of CPF carries a certain level of risk and requires careful consideration.

questions.title: How will changes to my Retirement Account affect my CPF LIFE monthly payouts?
questions.text:
Changes to your Retirement Account (RA) can affect your monthly payouts. This is because your RA savings is one of the factors in determining your CPF LIFE payouts.
Outflow from your RA, such as lump sum withdrawals will reduce your CPF LIFE monthly payouts.
On the other hand, inflows to your RA (such as top-ups or refunds from selling your property or investments) will be automatically used to increase your CPF LIFE premium and monthly payouts, provided they are sufficient to increase your monthly payouts by at least $10*.
*This is to avoid small and non-meaningful increase in payouts for members.
Please note that the actual revision may take up to two months, and we will notify you on the changes in your monthly payouts.

questions.title: I am currently receiving Additional Monthly Payout (AMP). Will my AMP be converted to higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts automatically?
questions.text:
You will continue to receive Additional Monthly Payout (AMP) from your Retirement Account (RA). The AMP is not part of CPF LIFE and will cease when your RA balances are depleted. To avoid a sudden decrease in your overall monthly income when your AMP ends, you may consider using your available balances in your RA to increase your CPF LIFE premium and boost your lifelong monthly payout. To do this, please submit your request via FormSG.
Starting from November 2021, any new Retirement Account inflows will automatically be used to increase your CPF LIFE premium. This will allow you to receive higher monthly payouts for life, providing you with greater financial security during your retirement years.

questions.title: Can I request a higher CPF LIFE monthly payout based on my current Retirement Account balance?
questions.text:
If there are no new inflows into your Retirement Account (RA), we are unable to increase your CPF LIFE monthly payout. This is because CPF LIFE payouts are determined by an independent actuarial consultant based on various factors, including your RA savings used to join CPF LIFE.
Find out how changes to your RA can affect your monthly payouts

questions.title: When can I start my monthly payouts if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
You have the flexibility to decide when to start your monthly payouts, anytime from 65 to 70.
Note: If you are born before 1958, you are past your payout eligibility age and can choose to start your payouts anytime.

questions.title: I am reaching age 65. How do I start my monthly payouts?
questions.text:
We will send you a notification three months before your 65th birthday, to guide you to explore your monthly payouts options and submit your instructions through the Plan my monthly payouts service.
If you do not submit any instructions on your payouts by 70, your monthly payouts will automatically start in the month of your 70th birthday.

questions.title: I am unsure whether to start my monthly payouts now. How can I find out how much monthly payouts I can receive?
questions.text:
You may use the Plan my monthly payouts service to find out more about your monthly payout details, provide your payout instructions and confirm your bank account details.
The Plan my monthly payouts service is available to you three months before you reach 65.
With this service, you can find out your estimated monthly payouts when you:
start at 65 or defer to a later age
join CPF LIFE and/or
use more of your CPF savings to increase your monthly payouts.

questions.title: Can I opt out of receiving CPF monthly payouts and withdraw all my retirement savings?
questions.text: Yes, you can opt out of receiving CPF monthly payouts and withdraw your retirement savings in full if you have other sources of lifelong income. Alternatively, you can consider enjoying lifelong payouts under CPF LIFE, in addition to your other sources of retirement income.

questions.title: Can I defer my monthly payouts beyond 70 if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
You will not be able to defer your monthly payouts beyond 70. The purpose of your retirement savings is to provide you with a stream of retirement income.
If you have no immediate need for the payouts, you can consider investing them outside the CPF system. Do note that investing outside of CPF carries a certain level of risk and requires careful consideration.

questions.title: How much monthly payout will I receive if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
If you've reached age 65, you can check your monthly payout in your Retirement dashboard.
If you’ve not reached age 65, we will notify you three months before your 65th birthday regarding your options on your monthly payout and the decisions that you need to make.
Do note that if you are born in 1958 or after, you may be automatically included in CPF LIFE, which provides lifelong monthly payouts.

questions.title: I am not on CPF LIFE. How will my monthly payouts be adjusted if there are changes to my retirement savings?
questions.text: We will review your payouts monthly to take into account the changes to your retirement savings. Generally, topping up your Retirement Account will increase your monthly payouts. Your payouts will be revised in the following month after the inflows or outflows are made to your retirement savings. However, if your remaining payout duration is short, the top-up will extend your payout duration instead so that your Retirement Account can continue to provide you with monthly payouts during your retirement.

questions.title: How long does it take to process my application to start my monthly payouts?
questions.text:
Our normal processing time for applications to start monthly payouts from retirement savings is three days to two weeks*.
* Your application may take up to two weeks to process if you have submitted multiple payout decisions via the Plan my monthly payouts service.
Monthly payouts will start at 65 or within one month (whichever is later) after your instruction is processed.

questions.title: Can I choose how much I want to withdraw from my retirement savings if I have an alternative pension/annuity?
questions.text: The amount that can be withdrawn from your retirement savings will depend on the monthly payout you are receiving from your pension/annuity. You can withdraw your retirement savings in full if the pension/ annuity monthly payout is more than the minimum monthly payout.

questions.title: Why can't I withdraw my top-ups from my retirement savings if I have an alternative pension/annuity?
questions.text:
Top-ups to your retirement savings are meant to build up your retirement savings and boost your retirement payouts. Hence, they cannot be withdrawn as cash in a lump sum or used for other purposes.
In addition to earning risk-free interest rates on your top-ups, you might have also benefited from tax relief. Allowing withdrawals of the top-ups would defeat the purpose of the scheme and the incentives given.

questions.title: Can I still make top-ups or receive top-ups to my retirement savings if I have withdrawn my savings using my pension/annuity?
questions.text: No, you cannot top up or receive top-ups to your retirement savings if you have already withdrawn your retirement savings using your pension/annuity. However, you can top up your retirement savings if you choose to join CPF LIFE.

questions.title: What happens if I surrender my pension/annuity after I have withdrawn my savings?
questions.text:
If you surrender your pension/annuity after you have withdrawn your retirement savings, the surrender value of your pension/annuity, up to your Full Retirement Sum with accrued interest, will be refunded to your Retirement Account. Any excess amount will be refunded to you in cash.
It's important to note that you will not be able to use your annuity to obtain a loan. This is because we need to ensure that we can refund the surrender value when you surrender your annuity.

questions.title: What happens to my CPF LIFE plan if my application to withdraw all my retirement savings using my pension/annuity is approved?
questions.text:
If your application to withdraw all your retirement savings using a pension or annuity is approved, your CPF LIFE plan will be terminated. Any remaining CPF LIFE premium balance1 will be refunded to your Retirement Account (RA) and disbursed to you. You can view your remaining CPF LIFE premium balance via your retirement dashboard under monthly payouts section.
1The remaining CPF LIFE premium balance is the amount deducted from your RA when you joined CPF LIFE, minus the total payouts you received under the plan before its termination.

questions.title: When can I apply to withdraw my retirement savings if I have a pension/annuity?
questions.text:
You can apply for withdrawal of your CPF retirement savings if you have a pension/annuity, as long as you are:
i. 55 or above; and
ii. currently receiving lifelong monthly payouts from your pension/annuity.

questions.title: How will I receive my retirement savings if my application to withdraw my retirement savings using my pension/annuity is approved?
questions.text: If your application to withdraw your retirement savings using your pension/annuity is approved, your retirement savings will be paid to your bank account provided under your Account settings.

questions.title: How can I check the status of my application to withdraw my retirement savings using my pension/annuity?
questions.text: If your application to withdraw your retirement savings using your pension/annuity is approved, you will receive a withdrawal advice by mail after we have processed the payment to your bank account. Alternatively, you can also check the status of your application by logging on to cpf.gov.sg.

questions.title: How long does it take to process my application to withdraw my retirement savings using my pension/annuity?
questions.text: Your application will be processed within one month after we receive all the required information and documents. The retirement savings will then be paid to your registered bank account.

questions.title: Why should I consider monetising my property?
questions.text: You can consider this option if your property can be an additional source of retirement income. It is an option to consider if your CPF and personal savings are not enough to provide you with your desired monthly payouts in retirement. Find out more about the different ways you could monetise your property. You may use HDB’s Enquire Housing Monetisation Options e-Service to check your eligible Housing Monetisation options.

questions.title: I live in a private property. Are there ways for me to monetise my property without selling my home?
questions.text:
You can consider speaking with your financial institution or advisor on the available products in the market that allow you to monetise your private property to supplement your retirement income while ageing in place.
As with all important financial decision, it is important to understand the nature of the product and assess your own risk tolerance and retirement needs/preferences before deciding if the monetisation option is suitable for you.
Alternatively, you can consider renting out a spare bedroom, or your entire property if you have an alternative accommodation. This can provide you with an additional source of retirement income.

questions.title: Can I withdraw my CPF savings before I turn 55?
questions.text: You can apply to withdraw your CPF savings earlier if you have a medical condition that reduces your life expectancy or causes you to be permanently unfit for work or lack mental capacity permanently.

questions.title: Why do I need to own a property before I can withdraw part of my Retirement Account savings?
questions.text:
If you do not own a property*, it's important to consider rental costs when planning for your retirement. This means you may need to set aside more savings for higher monthly payouts to cover these living expenses.
On the other hand, if you own a property*, you need not worry about rental costs in retirement. In addition, you would also have the option to generate extra retirement income by monetising your property. This is why members who own property* can choose to set aside their Full Retirement Sum (FRS) with a mixture of property (up to half the FRS) and cash and withdraw part of their Retirement Account savings down to their Basic Retirement Sum^ if they have other immediate retirement cash needs.
*The property must be in Singapore and lasts you until at least age 95.
^ Excluding, generally, interest earned, government grants and top-ups made under the Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme.

questions.title: Can I choose to set aside my Full Retirement Sum with a mixture of property and cash, and withdraw part of my Retirement Account savings if I own a foreign property?
questions.text: No, you are not able to withdraw part of your Retirement Account savings if you own a foreign property. To secure the refund of your CPF savings when your property is sold or transferred in the future, your property must be located in Singapore.

questions.title: Can I make a partial withdrawal of my CPF savings?
questions.text:
Yes, you can withdraw your savings partially and leave the remaining in your CPF accounts to earn risk-free interest rates* of up to 6% per annum. Your withdrawable savings can be withdrawn any time later, whenever you need them.
If you decide to withdraw a partial amount, your savings will be paid from your CPF accounts in the following order:
1. Retirement Account (if applicable)
2. Ordinary Account
*Based on the current 4% interest rate floor on Retirement Account monies.

questions.title: How often can I withdraw from my CPF savings?
questions.text:
There is no limit to the number of withdrawals you can make, as long as you are eligible and have withdrawable savings.
You can view your Retirement dashboard to check your eligibility and the amount you can withdraw.

questions.title: I am currently using my CPF savings to service my housing loan. Can I continue to use my withdrawable CPF savings for housing payments?
questions.text:
Yes, you can use your Ordinary Account savings, including any withdrawable amounts, to pay for your housing loan.
You can view your Home ownership dashboard to check the savings you can use for your housing payments under the "Amount allowed for this property" section. This will give you a clear idea of how much more you can use before reaching the usage limits.
While you use your CPF savings for housing, it is also important to consider the impact on your retirement savings and ensure that you have enough for your retirement needs.

questions.title: Why is the interest earned on Retirement Account not withdrawable?
questions.text: The interest earned on Retirement Account savings is meant to build up your retirement savings and increase your monthly retirement payouts. Hence, it is not withdrawable in a lump sum.

questions.title: How can I check my withdrawable amount?
questions.text: You can check the amount you can withdraw by logging in to your Retirement dashboard.

questions.title: How do I check if my property lease is able to last me until I am 95?
questions.text: You can check the remaining lease of your HDB property via the Housing and Development Board (HDB) website, or the Singapore Land Authority (SLA) website for private property.

questions.title: Do I earn interest for the balances in my CPF accounts up to the date of my withdrawal?
questions.text:
You will earn interest for the withdrawable amount up to the month before your withdrawal.
The interest earned will be credited into your CPF account at the beginning of each year and can be withdrawn from then on.
Find out how your CPF interest is calculated.

questions.title: How can I check my withdrawal transactions?
questions.text: You can view your latest withdrawal by logging in to your Retirement dashboard. If you want to view your earlier withdrawals, you can find them in your transaction history.

questions.title: Why is my co-owner allowed to withdraw part of his Retirement Account savings while I am not allowed to do so?
questions.text:
In households where the property does not last all co-owners until age 95, only the co-owner(s) who are covered by the lease until age 95 can choose to set aside their Full Retirement Sum (FRS) with a mixture of property (up to half the FRS) and cash, and hence withdraw their Retirement Account savings down to their Basic Retirement Sum*.
* Excluding, generally, interest earned, government grants and top-ups made under the Retirement Sum Topping-up Scheme.
Find out more about the importance of having a property lease that lasts until you are 95 years old.

questions.title: Do I need to pay taxes for the amount I withdraw from my CPF accounts?
questions.text:
No, CPF savings withdrawn are not taxable.
However, please note that if you have any unpaid taxes or MediShield Life/CareShield Life premiums, we may recover the unpaid amount from the CPF savings you are withdrawing.
This is done to ensure that everyone fulfils their tax obligations and has sufficient coverage under MediShield Life/CareShield Life.

questions.title: If my property is co-owned, does my co-owner need to be present at CPF Service Centre when I am making the property pledging withdrawal?
questions.text: Yes, all co-owners must be present at the Service Centre. Our customer service officers will assist the co-owners in submitting the co-owner consent form during the visit.

questions.title: What are the benefits of receiving my CPF savings via PayNow?
questions.text: With PayNow, you can generally receive your CPF savings in your NRIC-linked bank account almost instantly. It is also hassle-free as you do not need to provide bank account details or supporting documents for us to verify your bank account.

questions.title: How long will it take for me to receive my CPF savings via PayNow?
questions.text: If your application is successful, you will generally receive the payment in your NRIC-linked bank account almost instantly.

questions.title: Can I submit more than one application a day to withdraw my CPF savings via PayNow?
questions.text: Yes, you can submit more than one application a day to withdraw your savings via PayNow, as long as you have withdrawable CPF savings.

questions.title: Will I be notified when my CPF savings have been paid to me via PayNow?
questions.text:
Yes. With PayNow, you will be notified when your CPF savings have been paid to you.
If you have registered an email address under “My Notifications”, you will receive an email when the status of your online application is updated.
If you do not have a registered email with us, but have a mobile number in our record, you will receive an SMS notification.
You can also check the status of your application under "Activities".
In addition, if you have opted to receive SMS alerts with your bank, you will receive an SMS notification on your mobile number registered with your bank when the payment is made to your PayNow registered NRIC-linked bank account.

questions.title: How long will it take for the withdrawal amount to be refunded to my CPF account if the PayNow transaction was unsuccessful?
questions.text: The amount will be returned to your CPF account generally within two working days.

questions.title: Can I withdraw my savings earlier if I am sick?
questions.text:
Yes, you can withdraw your CPF savings earlier if you are certified by an accredited doctor to meet any of the following medical conditions:
Reduced life expectancy
Due to illness, your life expectancy has been severely reduced.
Permanently unfit for work
You are permanently unfit for any form of employment.
Permanently lack mental capacity
As defined in the Mental Capacity Act, you permanently lack the mental capacity to make decisions.

questions.title: Who is considered an accredited doctor?
questions.text:
An accredited doctor is a doctor from public hospital, polyclinic, or a specialist.
If the doctor who has certified your medical condition is not an accredited doctor, we will require an independent assessment from our panel of doctors.

questions.title: Can someone make a withdrawal on a member's behalf when the member loses mental capacity permanently?
questions.text:
Yes, the donee appointed by the member under the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) to make decisions on the member’s CPF matters, can apply to withdraw the member’s CPF savings.
To learn more about the LPA, please visit the Office of the Public Guardian's website.
You can also find out more about: What if my next-of-kin did not make a Lasting Power of Attorney?

questions.title: How much can I withdraw under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme?
questions.text:
Under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme, you can withdraw a lump sum of $5,000* or more, depending on the extent of your reduced life expectancy as certified by an accredited doctor.
You may also need to keep a reduced retirement sum in your Retirement Account from which you will receive regular monthly payouts.
*The amount you can withdraw depends on your available CPF balances, excluding top-ups made under the Retirement Sum Topping-up Scheme, government grants and your MediSave Account savings.

questions.title: If I have withdrawn under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme, can I continue to use my Ordinary Account savings to service my housing loan?
questions.text: Yes, you can continue to use your Ordinary Account savings to service your housing loan, subject to existing housing rules, even if you have withdrawn under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme.

questions.title: What happens to my CPF LIFE plan if I am approved to withdraw under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme?
questions.text:
If you are approved to withdraw your retirement savings under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme, you can decide whether to:
(i) terminate your CPF LIFE plan and receive a refund of the premium balance (if applicable); or
(ii) keep your CPF LIFE plan and receive monthly payouts for as long as you live.

questions.title: When do I need to submit the documents to support my application for withdrawal under the Reduced Life Expectancy Scheme?
questions.text:
The medical institution that you approach for completion of the Medical Assessment Report must submit the completed report to CPF Board within 90 days of your application. Please note that completed report submitted through other means, including by you, may not be accepted and will delay the processing of your application. Do allow six to eight weeks for medical institutions to submit the form upon your request.
Please note that your application will be cancelled if we do not receive the completed report from the medical institution by the given deadline.

questions.title: If I am eligible to receive monthly payouts under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme, when will the monthly payouts be paid to me?
questions.text: The monthly payouts of all members are deducted on the 2nd of the month, and the crediting of the monthly payouts to members’ bank accounts will depend on the bank's processing time. You will receive the monthly payouts in your bank account generally by the 4th working day of the month. You will generally receive your payouts earlier if your bank supports Fast And Secure Transfer (FAST).

questions.title: How do I check the status of my application under the Reduced Life Expectancy Scheme?
questions.text: To check the status of your application under the Reduced Life Expectancy Scheme, you can login to CPF website, click on ‘my CPF’, followed by ‘Activities’.

questions.title: What is the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text:
The Silver Support (SS) Scheme is part of a wider suite of schemes (e.g. healthcare subsidies, GST voucher) that the Government has put in place to give seniors greater assurance in retirement.
It provides a quarterly cash supplement to seniors who had low incomes during their working years and now have little or no family support and resources in their retirement. The Government reviews the Scheme periodically to ensure that it continues to target seniors with less means.
Seniors who qualify for SS will automatically receive their cash supplement. No application is required.
To check your eligibility status or submit an enquiry, log in to e-services.

questions.title: Do I need to apply for the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text:
There is no need to apply for the Silver Support (SS) Scheme.
CPF Board will automatically review your eligibility for the SS Scheme every year. Eligible seniors will automatically receive SS every quarter.
Seniors who qualify will receive a notification from CPF Board in December of the preceding year.

questions.title: Can Permanent Residents qualify for the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text: Only Singapore Citizens are eligible for the Silver Support Scheme.

questions.title: I am a Pioneer Generation / Merdeka Generation member. Will I automatically qualify for the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text:
Pioneer and Merdeka Generation members do not automatically qualify for the Silver Support (SS) Scheme.
The SS Scheme is targeted at seniors who had low incomes during their working years and now have little or no family support and resources in their retirement.
The Pioneer Generation (PG) and Merdeka Generation (MG) Packages are one-off schemes to honour PG and MG seniors for their contributions in the early years of Singapore's nation-building.
PG and MG members will be means-tested for SS like all other seniors aged 65 and above, and those who meet the eligibility criteria will receive SS.

questions.title: I am a ComCare Long Term Assistance (previously known as Public Assistance) recipient who is receiving Silver Support. Can I qualify for higher Silver Support?
questions.text:
Seniors aged 65 and above on the ComCare Long Term Assistance (LTA) Scheme will automatically qualify for the Silver Support (SS) Scheme and receive a flat amount of $430 per quarter, regardless of their HDB flat type.
The SS supplements the assistance that ComCare LTA beneficiaries receive, which includes monthly cash assistance to cover the recipient's daily living expenses, assistance with their medical bills at public healthcare institutions, and free or highly subsidised social services such as home help or Active Ageing Centres funded by the government.

questions.title: How can I receive SMS notifications on my Silver Support Payments?
questions.text:
We will send SMS notifications on Silver Support (SS) payments to the mobile number that you have registered with CPF Board.
To receive SMS notifications on your SS payments, you may update your mobile number via my cpf digital services – Account settings with your Singpass.

questions.title: Why are my total CPF contributions used as a reflection of my lifetime wages in the assessment of eligibility of the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text: We look at the senior’s total CPF contributions by the age of 55 to assess his/her eligibility for the Silver Support Scheme, as this is indicative of the incomes that seniors earned during their working years. This refers to the sum of contributions to the Ordinary Account (OA) and Special Account (SA), as well as any CPF savings that had been withdrawn for housing, investment and education.

questions.title: Why is the age cut-off for total CPF contributions set at 55 for the assessment of eligibility for the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text: We have set the cut-off age at 55 for the assessment of eligibility for the Silver Support Scheme to provide a meaningful comparison across cohorts, which experience different sets of CPF withdrawal rules and wage adjustments after age 55.

questions.title: Why is the threshold for total CPF contributions set at $140,000 to be eligible for the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text:
An eligibility criterion of $140,000 set for the Silver Support Scheme would include seniors who were earning lower wages through their working lives, and those who did not work due to reasons such as care-giving responsibilities and medical conditions.
The total CPF contributions threshold was increased from $70,000 to $140,000 in 2021 to strengthen support for seniors with lesser means. The Government will review the criteria from time to time, to ensure that the Silver Support Scheme is targeted at seniors with less means, while ensuring the scheme remains fiscally sustainable.

questions.title: How can I check how much total CPF contributions I have at age 55 for assessing my eligibility for the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text:
Only Singaporean seniors aged 65 and above will be assessed for eligibility for the Silver Support (SS) Scheme.
You may request to find out your total CPF contributions (TCC) used for the SS Scheme by writing in to us.

questions.title: Who should be considered as a member of my household for the computation of my household income used for assessing my eligibility for the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text:
Only family members related by blood, marriage and/or legal adoption (e.g. spouse, parents, children, grandparents, grandchildren, siblings, uncles, aunts, cousins and in-laws) and who live at the same residence are considered members of your household for the computation of your household income used for assessing your eligibility for the Silver Support (SS) Scheme.
Domestic helpers, unrelated tenants, godparents and friends living at the same address are not considered members of your household. Family members not living at your address are not considered members of your household.
If there are recent household changes that you want us to take into account to reassess your SS eligibility, please write to us and we will work with the Household Means Eligibility System (HOMES) to have your household means tested.

questions.title: What is HOMES?
