questions.text: The Household Means Eligibility System (HOMES) is a Government system supporting public schemes, including the Silver Support Scheme, in their conduct of means-tests as part of their assessment in determining the level of assistance for them.

questions.title: How do you determine my housing type when assessing my eligibility for the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text: Your housing type is based on your address as registered in your NRIC.

questions.title: Why is a senior not eligible for the Silver Support Scheme if he and/or his spouse together own a 5-room or larger HDB flat, private property or multiple properties?
questions.text:
The type of home owned is an indicator of the senior’s resources. Those who own a 5-room or larger HDB flat, private property or multiple properties are more likely to have more resources and access to additional retirement income. They would be less likely to require assistance through the Silver Support (SS) Scheme.
There are other schemes to help seniors cope with daily expenses, finance their healthcare needs and increase their retirement savings. Even if you do not qualify for the SS, you can still benefit from many of these schemes.
Those who need additional support can turn to other forms of assistance such as ComCare and MediFund. They may wish to approach a nearby Social Service Office for assistance.

questions.title: Will the Silver Support Scheme cover seniors living in residential facilities (e.g. Nursing Homes/ Welfare Homes/ Home for the Aged and Adult Disability Home)?
questions.text:
Seniors aged 65 and above, including those living in residential facilities that provide long-term care, will be assessed for the Silver Support (SS) Scheme. Seniors whose NRIC address reflects one of these facilities will receive SS if they meet all the other eligibility criteria. Seniors whose NRIC address does not reflect one of these facilities will receive SS based on the housing type of their NRIC address, if they meet all the other eligibility criteria.
Log in to e-services to check your eligibility status or contact us if you have any queries.

questions.title: Where can I find the list of the Board's panel of law firms?
questions.text: You can refer to the list of law firms appointed by the Board (PDF, 0.1MB) to find a firm to handle legal matters relating to your property.

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings for renovation and repairs of my property?
questions.text:
CPF savings cannot be used for renovation, improvement or repair work for your property.
If you are planning to renovate or repair your property, you will need to use your own cash savings to cover the costs. It is important to plan your finances accordingly and ensure you have enough cash savings to cover these expenses.

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to pay the seller's stamp duty when I sell my property?
questions.text:
CPF savings cannot be used to pay your seller's stamp duty. The seller's stamp duty will have to be paid with cash.
It is important to plan your finances accordingly and ensure that you have enough cash savings to cover the seller's stamp duty and other related costs when purchasing a property.

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to purchase a short-lease 2-room Flexi Flat?
questions.text: You must first set aside your Basic Retirement Sum in your CPF accounts before you can use any excess Ordinary Account savings to purchase a short-lease-2-room Flexi Flat. This ensures that you have a monthly income to support a basic standard of living during your retirement.

questions.title: What is the Memorandum of Mortgage?
questions.text: The Memorandum of Mortgage (PDF, 77KB) sets out the priority arrangement between the Board and the bank in respect of the refund of proceeds arising from a disposal of the property where the mortgagee bank has the first charge. The Memorandum of Mortgage has been registered with Singapore Land Authority (SLA) under the registration number: IA/991901M.

questions.title: Does the Board impose a penalty for unsuccessful housing deductions?
questions.text: The Board does not impose a penalty for unsuccessful housing deductions.

questions.title: Can the Board automatically deduct the monthly instalment shortfall for my property from my co-owner's CPF account?
questions.text:
No, we are not authorised to automatically deduct the monthly instalment shortfall from your co-owner's CPF account for your property. All property owners will need to communicate and agree on how to co-pay the monthly instalments.
Each co-owner will then need to submit their own application to instruct the use of their CPF savings for the property.

questions.title: I have used cash to pay for my housing monthly instalment shortfall. Can I apply to pay with my CPF savings, and get a cash refund from my financier?
questions.text:
Yes, you can apply to use your CPF savings to pay the monthly instalment shortfall. However, your financier must agree to refund you in cash. Please check with your financier to confirm they will provide a cash refund before submitting your CPF application.
Getting a cash refund from your financier is not guaranteed and depends on their approval. We strongly recommend checking with your financier first to confirm whether they can refund the cash payment before you proceed with your CPF application.
This will help ensure you understand their refund policy and avoid any potential complications with your application.

questions.title: How can I check my outstanding housing loan?
questions.text:
You can check your outstanding housing loan through the following methods:
If you have an HDB loan:
Online
Visit HDB's website and log in with your Singpass
Navigate to: e-Services > Servicing your HDB Housing Loan > View Housing Loan and Financial Information
In-person at HDB Branch
Book an appointment via the e-Appointment system before visiting
If you have a bank loan:
You can check with your bank on your outstanding loan.

questions.title: Is there any deadline for me to pay for the monthly instalment shortfall for my property?
questions.text:
You should pay off your monthly instalment shortfall as soon as possible to avoid penalty fees from your financier. We recommend checking with your financier directly to confirm any specific deadline for payment.
Late or non-payment of instalments can result in additional fees and charges, so it is best to stay on top of your payments to avoid any unnecessary financial burden.

questions.title: Can I use my Special Account savings to pay my housing loan?
questions.text:
No, you cannot use your Special Account savings to pay your housing loan, as these funds are specifically reserved for retirement purposes.
You can only use your Ordinary Account savings for housing-related payments including:
Down payments
Monthly instalments
Legal fees
If you need assistance with your housing loan:
For HDB loan: You can approach HDB on the financial assistance measures that would work best for your situation.
For bank loan: You can approach your financier on the financial options that are available to you.

questions.title: If I did not use my CPF savings for my property, do I have to top up my Retirement Account upon sale of my property?
questions.text: No, you do not have to top up your Retirement Account as you have never used your CPF savings for the property purchase.

questions.title: Do I need to refund my ex-spouse's CPF account if I take over the property?
questions.text:
Yes, when you take over full ownership of a property from your ex-spouse, you will generally need to refund their CPF account. This refund includes the principal amount your ex-spouse used for the property and any accrued interest, and any amount that your ex-spouse has pledged to make up their retirement sum.
However, the Court has the discretion to order a property transfer without requiring the full CPF refund to be made to your ex-spouse's account.
If you later sell the property, you will need to refund to your CPF account with the total of:
Your own principal withdrawn for the property, accrued interest on that amount and any amount you pledged to make up your retirement sum; and
Your ex-spouse’s principal withdrawn for the property, accrued interest on that amount and any amount your ex-spouse pledged to make up their retirement sum.

questions.title: What do I need to do before I sell or transfer my property?
questions.text:
Before selling or transferring your property, you must complete certain steps that vary depending on your property type.
If you own an HDB flat
You will need to check with HDB to confirm your eligibility to sell or transfer your flat. After receiving HDB’s consent, either HDB or your lawyer (if you have one) will liaise with the Board to determine any amount, that must be refunded to your CPF account. For more information on the resale process, please visit HDB’s website.
If you own a private property
You will need to instruct your lawyer to obtain consent from the Board before proceeding with the sale you sell or transfer your property.
These preliminary steps ensure compliance with all regulatory requirements before your property transaction can proceed.

questions.title: I am buying an HDB flat and selling my existing flat at the same time. Can I apply for a contra facility?
questions.text: If you want to use the refund from selling your current HDB flat to buy a new flat, you can check with HDB to see if you are eligible for a contra facility. This lets you use the refund to offset the purchase price of your new flat.

questions.title: What is Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
Home Protection Scheme (HPS) is a mortgage-reducing insurance that protects you and your loved ones from the risk of losing your HDB flat in the event of unforeseen circumstances like death, terminal illness, or total permanent disability.
HPS is designed to ensure that your loved ones can continue to live in the flat without worrying about the financial burden from any unforeseen circumstances. It insures members up to the age of 65 or until the housing loans are paid up, whichever is earlier. As a member, you will be covered until the age of 65 or until your housing loans are fully paid off, whichever comes first.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I apply to be insured under Home Protection Scheme if I do not have any outstanding housing loan?
questions.text: The Home Protection Scheme (HPS) benefits are used to pay off the outstanding housing loan in the event of a claim. If you have not taken any housing loan to buy your HDB flat, HPS is not applicable to you.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Where can I purchase fire insurance for my HDB flat?
questions.text: If you are looking to purchase fire insurance for your HDB flat, you can reach out to the Housing and Development Board (HDB) for assistance. They will be able to provide you with more information on the process and requirements.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: My co-owner and I each applied for 50% Home Protection Scheme (HPS) coverage. What should I do if my co-owner's HPS cover is rejected due to health reasons?
questions.text: If your co-owner's Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover is rejected due to health reasons, you are encouraged to increase your HPS share of cover to 100% of the outstanding housing loan. This will ensure that the total outstanding loan is fully covered by HPS. However, please note that any increase in HPS cover is subject to approval and you being in good health. It is important to ensure that your home loan is adequately covered by HPS.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If I did not apply to use my CPF savings when buying my HDB flat, can I apply to be covered under the Home Protection Scheme and use my CPF savings for monthly housing instalments now?
questions.text:
Since this is the first time that you are using your CPF savings for your HDB flat, we will need you to provide further information and documents related to your housing loan, such as details of your financier and outstanding housing loan amount.
You will need to submit an application to request to use your CPF savings for your monthly housing instalment and apply for an Home Protection Scheme cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How do I apply to be insured under the Home Protection Scheme after I obtained Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency again?
questions.text: You may re-apply for a Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover online, using your Singpass, if your previous HPS cover has ceased and you are the owner of an HDB flat with an outstanding housing loan. Your eligibility for HPS coverage is subject to approval and your current health condition.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why do I need to declare my health condition when I apply for my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
You must declare your health condition fully and truthfully when you apply for your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover because that is how the mortgage protection insurance works. Your eligibility for an HPS cover is subject to approval and you being in good health.
This is in line with the industry practice where applicants have to truthfully declare their health conditions and may need to attend a medical examination.
Any HPS cover issued based on false/misleading information could be voided at any time, and any insurance claim would be denied. In such a situation, any premiums paid will also not be refunded. To avoid this, members need to declare fully and truthfully their health conditions when applying for HPS.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What if I do not declare my health condition when I apply for a Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text: It is important to declare your health condition fully and truthfully when applying for a Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover. Failing to do so will result in your HPS cover being voided at any time and any claim being denied. In such cases, any premiums paid will not be refunded to you.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Do I need to declare information regarding my health condition when I am not sure if the information is relevant for my Home Protection Scheme cover application?
questions.text:
If you are unsure about the relevance of the information, you are advised to still disclose it so that we can assess your eligibility for a Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover.
You will not receive any claims or any refund of paid premiums if an HPS cover was issued based on false/misleading information given or if you were not in good health before the cover commenced.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Am I still eligible for Home Protection Scheme if I have a serious medical condition?
questions.text:
To determine your eligibility for a Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover, we will need to assess your medical condition(s).
You will need to submit an application and we will inform you of your application outcome in due course. Generally, members who are currently receiving treatment for serious medical conditions such as cancer, stroke, kidney failure, etc., are not eligible for HPS.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen if I am not eligible for a Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
If you have a serious pre-existing medical condition and are not eligible for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover, you can still use your CPF savings to pay your monthly housing instalment.
If you were previously covered under HPS, you may be eligible to port your previous HPS cover to your new property.
Find out how you can qualify for porting your previous HPS cover:
How do I qualify for the porting of my previous Home Protection Scheme cover to my new property?
You may also consider applying for insurance coverage from private insurers.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How do I qualify for the porting of my previous Home Protection Scheme cover to my new property?
questions.text:
If you have purchased a new flat and sold your previous flat, you may be eligible to port your previous Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover to your new property. To qualify for this, you must meet the following conditions:
your previous HPS cover* was terminated due to the sale of your previous flat after purchasing a new flat, and
you are not eligible for a new HPS cover at standard premium rates for the new flat due to your current health condition.
*You must not have had any serious pre-existing health condition that was not disclosed to us when you applied for your previous HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If I am eligible for the porting of my Home Protection Scheme cover, what is the sum assured that I am insured for and the period of cover?
questions.text:
If you are eligible for porting your previous Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover, we will issue you a new cover based on the lower of:
the remaining sum assured of your previous HPS cover or the outstanding loan for your new flat, and
the remaining cover period of your previous HPS cover or the new cover period for the new flat.
The same terms and conditions for your previous HPS cover will continue to apply to your new HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I apply to port my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover to my new flat, instead of applying for a HPS cover?
questions.text: We can only consider porting the previous Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover for members who are not eligible for a new HPS cover. Therefore, you must apply for a new HPS cover first.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Do I need to update CPF Board of my new health condition which developed after my Home Protection Scheme cover has been issued to me?
questions.text:
If you have developed a new health condition after your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover has been issued, you do not need to inform CPF Board.
You are only required to declare your health condition at the point of your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) application. However, if there is a change in the state of your health before the HPS cover is issued, you must inform CPF Board immediately.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Do I need to declare my health when I apply to adjust my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
A new health declaration is required if you are adjusting your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) coverage upwards due to an increase in loan repayment period, loan quantum or share of cover. If you are not eligible for the additional coverage, you can continue to be insured under your existing cover*.
*You must not have had any serious pre-existing health condition that was not disclosed to us when you applied for your previous HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: After I submit my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) application, do I need to declare my newly developed health condition before the HPS cover is issued to me?
questions.text:
You must write to us immediately if there is a change in the state of your health before the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover is issued to you. Please include details of your health condition and a copy of your medical report, if any.
We will assess your eligibility for an HPS cover based on the additional health information declared.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What should I do if I have omitted to declare certain health condition in my Home Protection Scheme application?
questions.text:
Please write to us to declare any health condition which you have omitted in your earlier Home Protection Scheme (HPS) application. Your declaration should include details of your health condition and a copy of your medical report, if any.
We will assess your eligibility for an HPS cover based on the additional health information declared.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: I would like to submit a medical report to support my Home Protection Scheme application. What is the information required in the medical report?
questions.text:
You may submit a medical report to support your Home Protection Scheme application, at your own cost. Your report must be up-to-date from a medical institution in Singapore and include the following information:
Diagnosis and diagnosis date
Reason(s) of hospitalisation, if any
Details of treatment(s)
Date(s) and details of surgery, if any
Details of complications, if any, and treatment rendered
Current condition and treatment(s)
Investigation test results
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What are the alternatives available if I am not eligible for a Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text: If you are not eligible for a Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover due to serious medical condition, you may wish to consider applying for insurance coverage from private insurers.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why am I required to attend a medical examination for my Home Protection Scheme application?
questions.text:
Your eligibility for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover is subject to approval and you being in good health. To assess your eligibility for HPS cover, we may arrange a medical examination for you and/or request a copy of the medical report on your health condition.
You will be notified by CPF Board if you are scheduled for an HPS medical examination. You may check or reschedule your appointment online via e-Medical Appointment Service.
Find out more:
Can I provide my own medical report instead of attending the Home Protection Scheme medical examination?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen if I missed my appointment for Home Protection Scheme medical examination?
questions.text:
If you have missed your appointment for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) medical examination, the Board may not be able to assess your eligibility and process your application. The Board will notify you on the outcome of your HPS application.
If you are not eventually issued an HPS cover and would like to be reconsidered for coverage under the scheme, you can submit a new HPS application using your Singpass.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What tests am I required to undergo for the Home Protection Scheme medical examination?
questions.text:
The medical tests required for the Home Protection Scheme medical examination depend on your health condition.
Generally, the medical examination includes the following:
General checks with height, weight, visual acuity, blood pressure readings and pulse rate
Lipid profile
Fasting blood glucose
Urinalysis
Find out more:
Do I have to pay for the Home Protection Scheme medical examination?
What do I need to prepare for the Home Protection Scheme medical examination?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How long does the Home Protection Scheme medical examination take?
questions.text: The entire Home Protection Scheme medical examination process generally takes up to 2 hours, excluding the time needed for registration.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Do I have to pay for the Home Protection Scheme medical examination?
questions.text:
The cost of the initial Home Protection Scheme medical examination will be borne by the Board.
However, if you wish to conduct any subsequent tests, examinations or obtain second opinions, the cost of such investigations would have to be borne by you. You can choose to proceed with subsequent tests at the same clinic or any other clinic of your choice.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Will I be given a medical certificate for my Home Protection Scheme medical examination?
questions.text: The Board’s panel clinics, which conduct the Home Protection Scheme medical examination, will not issue a medical certificate for the medical examination. However, you can ask the clinic to issue a time chit as evidence of your attendance and duration at the clinic.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: When will my Home Protection Scheme cover start?
questions.text:
Your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will start when all the following conditions are met:
You have obtained legal ownership of the flat i.e. legal documents are signed and keys are collected.
You have executed the loan document with HDB or the approved mortgagee and are legally responsible for the loan.
You have declared your health and have been accepted for cover under HPS.
You have paid the HPS premium. Deduction of the premium from your Ordinary Account will take place generally within two weeks from the legal ownership date of your flat.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How will I be kept informed on my Home Protection Scheme cover details?
questions.text:
We will send you a Home Protection Scheme (HPS) certificate generally within one to two weeks after your HPS cover has commenced and you have paid the premium.
The HPS certificate will include information such as the amount you are insured for, your share of the cover, the policy start and end dates, the address of your insured flat, and your annual premium.
You can also view your HPS coverage status under “Protection against losing your home” via the Home ownership dashboard.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How long will I be insured under Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text: You will be insured under Home Protection Scheme for the term of your loan or up to age 65, whichever is earlier.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What if I lose my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) certificate containing my HPS cover details?
questions.text:
You would not need to provide the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) certificate as a supporting document for any purpose, including making a claim under HPS. You can view your HPS coverage information under “Protection against losing your home” via the Home ownership dashboard.
Alternatively, if you require further clarification on your HPS coverage details, you may write to us and select “Housing/Property” as the Subject and “General Enquiry – Home Protection Scheme” as the Category.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How is the Home Protection Scheme premium calculated?
questions.text:
The Home Protection Scheme charges a level premium rate (i.e. same amount annually throughout the policy term) and is calculated based on several factors:
Outstanding housing loan on the flat*
Loan repayment period
Type of loan (HDB concessionary or market rate)
Age and gender
Percentage share of cover of the outstanding housing loan
*The computation of the level premium takes into account the monthly reduction in the housing loan.
Premiums are generally higher for greater share of coverage, larger loan amounts, or longer repayment periods. The premiums would be lower for younger persons and females, due to lower mortality risk.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How much premium do I need to pay for my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
You can calculate your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium online using the HPS Premium Calculator.
Find out more:
Where can I check the premium payable to renew my Home Protection Scheme cover?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How long do I have to pay my Home Protection Scheme premium?
questions.text:
You will only need to pay the premium for 90% of your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover period.
For example, if your HPS cover period is 30 years, you will only need to pay premium for 27 years.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What is the priority of the Home Protection Scheme deduction if I am also using my CPF savings to pay my monthly housing instalments?
questions.text:
If you are also using your CPF savings to pay your monthly housing instalments, the payment of HPS premium takes priority. This is to ensure that you remain financially protected by HPS for your outstanding housing loan.
During the premium grace period, your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings will be reserved for the HPS premium payment. This means that you will not be able to use your OA savings for any payments, including the monthly housing instalments, until your HPS premium is paid.
We recommend that you make alternative arrangements with your mortgagee on the shortfall in your monthly housing instalments during this period.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Home Protection Scheme cover if I do not pay the annual premium?
questions.text:
If you do not pay the annual premium for your Home Protection Scheme (HPS), your coverage will lapse and you will no longer be protected by HPS. This means that in the unfortunate event of death, terminal illness, or total permanent disability, you will not be able to make a claim under HPS.
You will need to reapply for an HPS cover if you wish to be covered under HPS in future. However, please note that your eligibility for the new HPS cover will be subject to approval and you being in good health at the time of application.
It is important to ensure that your HPS premiums are paid on time to avoid any lapse in coverage.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Where can I check the premium payable to renew my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
The Home Protection Scheme (HPS) charges a level premium rate (i.e. same amount annually throughout the policy term). This means that you pay the same annual premium throughout 90% of your HPS coverage period. You can find the premium amount on your HPS certificate, which was sent to you when the HPS cover was first issued to you.
Your HPS premium is deducted from your CPF Ordinary Account every year during your policy anniversary month. You can also check the premium payable by viewing the previous premium deductions online using your Singpass or from the Yearly Statement of Account.
To find out more on how long you need to pay your HPS premium, please refer to this FAQ.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Where can I check and view my Home Protection Scheme premium deduction?
questions.text: You can check and view the Home Protection Scheme premium deduction from your CPF Ordinary Account online using your Singpass. The deduction will also be shown in your Yearly Statement of Account.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I reserve monies in my CPF Ordinary Account to pay the annual renewal premium for my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text: The monies in your CPF Ordinary Account (OA), including your incoming CPF contributions, will automatically be reserved up to a period of two months for the full Home Protection Scheme premium amount, when you do not have sufficient funds in your OA at the time of HPS cover renewal.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I use the monies in my CPF Special Account to pay the annual renewal premium for my Home Protection Scheme cover if I do not have sufficient savings in my CPF Ordinary Account?
questions.text: Home Protection Scheme premiums can only be paid from the savings in your CPF Ordinary Account, and not from your CPF Special Account (SA) savings. The SA savings are meant for retirement needs as they may be the only source of funds that members can turn to for financing their living expenses in old age.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why is the Home Protection Scheme premium not refundable if I did not make a claim?
questions.text: Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premiums paid for past policy years are not refundable. This is because you have received insurance protection during the period of cover and would have been eligible to receive the HPS benefits in the event of a claim.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why does the status of my Home Protection Scheme cover show “pending renewal” in the Home ownership dashboard when I have sufficient monies in my CPF Ordinary Account for the premium?
questions.text:
The deduction of premiums for the renewal of Home Protection Scheme (HPS) covers takes place on a weekly basis.
If your HPS cover renewal date falls between the weekly deduction runs, the status of your HPS cover will show as "pending renewal" in the Home ownership dashboard. Once the premium has been successfully deducted, the status of your HPS cover will change to "Active".
In the event that you do not have enough Ordinary Account (OA) savings to pay the premium, we will inform you to top-up the premium shortfall.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why are only certain individuals allowed to pay my Home Protection Scheme premium using their CPF Ordinary Account savings?
questions.text:
Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premiums are consumptive in nature, which means that when your family member (who is your spouse, parent, child, or sibling) uses their Ordinary Account (OA) savings to help with your HPS premium payment, they will have less CPF savings for their retirement.
This is why only certain family members, who are co-owners of the flat, are allowed to use their CPF OA savings to pay your HPS premium. By doing so, they can help to secure the family home while limiting the impact on their retirement savings.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How do I make a top up for my spouse/parent/child/sibling's outstanding Home Protection Scheme premium?
questions.text:
If you co-own the flat with your spouse/parent/child/sibling, you can authorise us to use your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings to pay the insured’s premium shortfall. You can do this online by logging in with your Singpass.
Once the application is approved by the Board, the premium will be deducted from the available balance in the insured’s CPF OA first, followed by your CPF OA.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How can my family member authorise the Board to deduct my Home Protection Scheme premium from their CPF Ordinary Account?
questions.text: Your family member (that is your spouse, parent, child or sibling) who co-owns the flat with you can authorise us to use their CPF Ordinary Account savings online using their Singpass to pay for your Home Protection Scheme premium.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I use more than one of my family members' CPF Ordinary Account savings to pay my Home Protection Scheme premium shortfall?
questions.text:
If you have a Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium shortfall, you can only use the CPF Ordinary Account savings of one family member (spouse, parent, child, or sibling), who is a co-owner, to pay the premium at any given time.
If you need help with subsequent HPS renewal premiums, you can approach another family member who is also a co-owner for assistance.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What is the priority of Home Protection Scheme deduction if my family member has authorised the Board to deduct my premium from their CPF Ordinary Account?
questions.text: The Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium will first be deducted from the available balance in your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) followed by your family member's OA.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Which CPF account would the premium be refunded to if my family member has used their CPF savings to pay for my Home Protection Scheme premium?
questions.text: If your family member (that is your spouse, parent, child or sibling) has used their CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings for your Home Protection Scheme premium, any premium refund will be paid into your OA.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I terminate my standing instruction to use my CPF Ordinary Account savings to pay for my co-owner's Home Protection Scheme premiums?
questions.text: Please write to us if you wish to revoke your standing instruction to use your CPF Ordinary Account savings to pay your co-owner's Home Protection Scheme premium shortfall.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How can I check the status of my Home Protection Scheme exemption application?
questions.text:
You can contact your insurer to confirm if they have submitted the Home Protection Scheme exemption application to the Board. You may ask them to provide you with the application number (i.e. FormSG ID number).
Once your insurer(s) have submitted your application to the Board, you will receive notification of the outcome generally within five working days from the date it was submitted. Your insurer(s) will also be notified of the outcome.
However, if you haven't received any notification after this period and have confirmed that your insurer has submitted the application, you may write to us to check on the status of your application.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If I am currently insured under the Home Protection Scheme (HPS), how much premium refund will I get if my application to be exempted from HPS is approved?
questions.text: If you are successful in the exemption application, your existing HPS cover will be terminated. You will get a full premium refund into your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) provided that the exemption application is received (by the Board) within one month from the issuance of the HPS cover. Otherwise, a pro-rated refund will be credited to your OA upon the termination of your HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I apply to be exempted from the Home Protection Scheme for my new flat with the private insurance policy that was previously used for my old flat?
questions.text:
You can use the private insurance policy to apply for a Home Protection Scheme (HPS) exemption for your new flat if you meet the following conditions:
The remaining policy sum assured and policy term are enough to cover your current outstanding housing loan, and
The policy covers you in the event of death, terminal illness and total permanent disability up to the full term of loan or age 65, whichever is earlier.
To apply for HPS exemption, you will need to approach the insurer(s) of your private insurance policies and have them submit your application to us. Please note that we will only accept applications that are submitted through insurers.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Home Protection Scheme exemption if I refinance or restructure my housing loan?
questions.text: If you have recently refinanced or restructured your housing loan, or if you have obtained a new housing loan for part-share/transfer of ownership of the flat, it is essential to review your private insurance policy(s) to ensure that the policy(s) remains sufficient to cover the newly refinanced or restructured loan. If the current policy(s) you have used for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) exemption doesn't offer sufficient coverage for your newly refinanced or restructured loan, you will need to approach your insurer(s) to purchase additional policy(s) or apply for HPS.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Home Protection Scheme exemption if my private insurance policy used for the exemption is discontinued or altered?
questions.text:
If you have been exempted from the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) using a private insurance policy, the exemption will no longer be valid once your insurer informs us that the policy has been discontinued or altered.
In such cases, we will automatically issue an HPS cover to you based on the declared percentage you are exempted for, subject to your eligibility for an HPS cover.
Once the HPS cover is issued, you will receive an HPS certificate, containing the details of your HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I apply to be partially exempted from the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
You cannot be exempted from the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) and insured under HPS at the same time. However, you may apply to be 50% exempted from HPS while your co-owner applies for a 50% HPS share of cover.
The total share of coverage for all co-owners must add up to at least 100% of the outstanding housing loan.
You are encouraged to be insured under your private insurance based on your share of responsibility to service your housing loan. This will ensure that you have sufficient coverage to settle your share of outstanding housing loan in the event of a claim.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If I am already exempted from Home Protection Scheme (HPS) with my private insurance policy, can I apply for HPS again?
questions.text:
If you are already exempted from Home Protection Scheme (HPS) with your private insurance policy, you may still apply to be covered under HPS anytime.
To apply for an HPS cover, please submit the application online, using your Singpass.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What are the common reasons for unsuccessful Home Protection Scheme exemption application?
questions.text:
Your exemption may be rejected for the following reasons:
Your share of the exemption and your co-owners’ share of the exemption/Home Protection Scheme coverage adds up to less than 100%.
You have applied for exemption using private insurance policies from multiple insurers, however we did not receive all your applications from your insurers within seven calendar days from the date of receipt of the first application submitted by one of your insurers.
Your property address provided by your insurer(s) does not tally with our records.
We do not have your housing records as you have not previously used your CPF savings for your HDB flat at the time of purchase or for your monthly housing instalments.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why is the premium for my new Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover higher than my old HPS cover even though I have made a partial repayment of my loan?
questions.text:
Your Home Protection Scheme premium is higher than before because you had extended your repayment period to a longer tenure, after you made the partial repayment of your loan.
Find out more:
How is the Home Protection Scheme premium calculated?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How can I include new co-owners for my Housing & Development Board (HDB) flat and how do they apply to be insured under the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
You would first need to contact or visit the Housing Development Board (HDB) Branch Office managing your flat to include your new co-owners.
After your new co-owners have obtained legal ownership of the flat, they may apply for a Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover. The process to apply for an HPS cover differs, depending on the type of loan that they are taking.
For Housing & Development Board (HDB) Loan
Your co-owners may apply for an HPS cover when applying to withdraw their CPF savings for the monthly housing instalments via HDB.
For Bank Loan
Your co-owners may apply for an HPS cover online using their Singpass. This can be done at the same time when they are applying to withdraw their CPF savings for the monthly housing instalments.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why does my Home Protection Scheme cover end when I have fully redeemed my housing loan?
questions.text: You will not need insurance protection if there is no outstanding housing loan. Thus, we will terminate your Home Protection Scheme cover and any pro-rated premium refund (if any) will be credited to your CPF Ordinary Account.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What happens to my Home Protection Scheme cover when I renounce my Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency?
questions.text: When you have renounced your Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency, your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will cease upon the sale of your HDB flat or at the end of the current HPS policy year, whichever is earlier. There will be no further renewal of your HPS cover, even if you are in the process of selling your HDB flat, as the scheme is only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What happens after I have terminated my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
You will get a full premium refund to your Ordinary Account (OA) if the termination application is received within one month from the issuance of your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover. Otherwise, any unused premium will be refunded back to your OA upon the termination of your HPS cover.
The monthly servicing of your housing loan instalments via CPF savings (if any) will cease upon the termination of your HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What are the claim exclusions for the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
The Home Protection Scheme (HPS) provides coverage for CPF members in the event of death, terminal illness, or total permanent disability.
However, there are certain exclusions to the coverage. If any of the following events occur within the first year of the policy, claim benefits will not be payable:
The member committed self-inflicted injury or suicide
The member committed a criminal offence punishable by death
The claim arose from the member’s own intentional criminal act
Additionally, HPS benefits will not be payable if:
The member was not in good health before the start of HPS cover
The member provided false or misleading information
The claim arose from wars or any warlike operations or participation in any riot
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What are the restrictions imposed on the sale of my flat after I have claimed the Home Protection Scheme benefits?
questions.text: There are no restrictions and you can sell your flat after claiming the benefits under the Home Protection Scheme.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Do I need to refund the sale proceeds to my CPF accounts if I sell my flat after claiming the benefits under the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text: Yes, if you sell your flat, you will need to make a refund to your CPF accounts. The refund amount and how it is handled may vary depending on your age and other factors, as detailed in the answer to How much do I need to refund to my CPF account when selling/transferring my property?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If my co-owner and I are both insured under the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) for 75% each, what will happen after my co-owner has claimed the HPS benefits?
questions.text:
Upon approval of your co-owner’s claim, we will pay the sum assured based on his/her 75% share of the HPS cover. After that, your HPS cover will be adjusted to match the remaining 25% of the outstanding housing loan and your premium will be adjusted accordingly.
This means that you will still be covered by the HPS for your share of the loan, and your premiums will be adjusted accordingly.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: My family member has passed on. How do I check if they were covered under the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
If your family member was covered under the Home Protection Scheme (HPS), his/her coverage status will be made available for viewing by his/her CPF nominee(s) on the Deceased CPF Member Dashboard.
Alternatively, you may write to us by selecting “Home ownership” as the Subject and “Protecting against losing your home” as the Category to find out more.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Do I need to inform the Board to terminate the housing monthly instalment from my CPF account if my housing loan is fully paid by the Home Protection Scheme claim?
questions.text: You do not need to do anything. If your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) sum assured has fully paid off your outstanding home loan, CPF Board will work with your mortgage provider to stop deducting money from the CPF accounts of all the joint-owner(s).
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How do I check the status of my Home Protection Scheme claim application on terminal illness or total permanent disability?
questions.text: To check the status of your Home Protection Scheme claim application on terminal illness or total permanent disability, you can login to CPF website, click on ‘my CPF’, followed by ‘Activities’.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Do I have to submit employment information for Home Protection Scheme claim?
questions.text: Yes, for claims under Home Protection Scheme, you are required to inform your employer to fill in this form as we require your employment information. The employment information will allow CPFB to accurately determine your claim event date and amount of claim benefits. Your employer would require a Corppass to login.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I choose to switch to Annual Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS) if I am currently insured under the Single Premium HPS?
questions.text: If you are currently insured under the Single Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS), you cannot choose to switch to the Annual Premium HPS. The Annual Premium HPS is only applicable to those who joined HPS on or after 1 March 2001.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: I am currently insured under the Single Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS). How can I extend my HPS cover until age 65?
questions.text:
Your Single Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will only insure you up to age 55 or 60. If your original housing loan is still outstanding by then, we will extend your HPS cover to age 65 by issuing you an Annual Premium (AP) HPS cover when your Single Premium HPS cover expires.
However, if you had restructured your housing loan and had been previously rejected by CPF Board for an increase to your HPS cover period or sum assured arising from the changes to your housing loan, you will not be eligible for the additional AP cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: I am currently insured under the Single Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS). Do I have to pay additional premiums when my HPS cover is extended to age 65?
questions.text: If you are insured under the Single Premium Home Protection Scheme and wish to extend your coverage to age 65, you will need to pay additional premiums. This premium will be paid annually.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Single Premium Home Protection Scheme cover if there are changes to my outstanding housing loan?
questions.text:
If your loan repayment period or loan amount has reduced, your Single Premium (SP) Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will be terminated. We will issue you an Annual Premium (AP) HPS cover based on your new outstanding housing loan. Any surrender value of your SP HPS cover will be paid to your CPF Ordinary Account.
However, if the changes to your housing loan result in an increase in your HPS cover, such as an increase in cover period or sum assured, obtaining an additional AP cover will be subject to you being in good health. If you are not eligible for the additional cover, you will remain insured under your SP cover.
Do I need to inform the Board to adjust my Home Protection Scheme cover if I make a partial repayment of my loan?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Single Premium Home Protection Scheme cover if I change my share of cover but there are no changes to my outstanding housing loan?
questions.text:
If you have changed your share of Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover without making any changes to your outstanding housing loan, you will remain covered under the Single Premium (SP) HPS.
Once the adjustment is approved, your SP HPS cover will be adjusted accordingly to the new percentage declared. However, please note that any increase in your HPS coverage is subject to approval and you being in good health.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If I work after age 65, do I still need to contribute to my MediSave Account?
questions.text: As long as you continue to work, you will need to contribute to your MediSave Account (MA). These contributions will accumulate up to the Basic Healthcare Sum and help cover your medical expenses during retirement.

questions.title: How is the Basic Healthcare Sum determined?
questions.text: The Basic Healthcare Sum is an estimate of your likely medical expenses from age 65 onwards. It is determined based on past trends in MediSave usage among the elderly and is intended to cover your own basic subsidised healthcare expenses, as well as health and long-term care insurance premiums during old age.

questions.title: Why is the Basic Healthcare Sum adjusted yearly?
questions.text:
The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is adjusted annually for cohorts below age 65 to ensure it remains relevant and keeps pace with rising healthcare consumption, especially with increasing healthcare costs and expansions in MediSave usage.
For each cohort, the BHS is fixed from age 65 onwards and remains the same for the rest of their lives. This helps members save adequately for their basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age, while providing certainty on the amount they need to set aside in their MediSave Account.

questions.title: As an employee, how much do I contribute to my MediSave Account (MA)?
questions.text: A portion of your monthly CPF contributions is allocated to your MediSave Account depending on your age group. You can refer to the CPF contribution and allocation rates.

questions.title: What happens if I do not have the Basic Healthcare Sum when I turn age 65?
questions.text: The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is the estimated savings you need in your MediSave Account (MA) to cover your basic subsidised healthcare expenses in old age and is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA. If your balance is less than the cohort BHS at age 65, you are not required to top up your MA. However, if you wish to build up your healthcare savings, you can choose to top up your MA with cash. You can do so via this form to make cash top-ups to your own or your loved ones’ MA.

questions.title: What is not covered under the MediSave scheme?
questions.text: MediSave generally does not cover optional and cosmetic treatments, accident and emergency (A&E) fees and non-medical treatments such as ambulance transport. Please approach the medical institution to find out whether your treatment can be covered under MediSave.

questions.title: Are there additional charges for using my MediSave to pay for my medical expenses?
questions.text: CPF Board does not impose any administrative fee for using MediSave.

questions.title: What happens to my MediSave if I do not use it?
questions.text:
Any unused MediSave savings will remain in your MediSave Account and grow with interest.
Learn more about CPF interest rates.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my siblings' insurance premiums for schemes such as MediShield Life, Integrated Shield Plans or ElderShield/ElderShield Supplement?
questions.text: Yes. Since 1 June 2019, members may use their MediSave to pay for their siblings' insurance premiums.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for my siblings' medical expenses?
questions.text: You may use your MediSave to pay for your siblings' medical expenses, as long as they are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents (SC/PR). You would have to provide proof to the medical institutions that your siblings are SC/PR (e.g. NRICs).

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay the remainder of my medical bill that is not covered under my pensioner benefits?
questions.text:
You can use your own or your immediate family members' (i.e. spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings) MediSave to pay the remainder of your medical bill that is not covered under your pensioner benefits, up to the MediSave withdrawal limits. The expenses incurred must be for medical treatments approved under the MediSave scheme.
If you would like to use your MediSave to pay the remainder of your medical bill, please inform the Medical Institution (MI). You will be required to complete the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF), which authorises the MI to use your MediSave to pay the bill. Please note that any amount above the MediSave withdrawal limits would need to be paid in cash.

questions.title: Can I choose to receive both digital notification and a hardcopy MediSave transaction statement?
questions.text: You will not be receiving hardcopies of your MediSave transaction statement once you receive notifications digitally. This will aid us in our pursuit to reduce the use of paper.

questions.title: Can I choose to receive the hardcopy MediSave transaction statement instead?
questions.text:
Notification through hardcopy statements will result in a delay in informing you of deductions made from your MediSave account. It will also contribute to the usage of paper, which is not environmentally friendly.
We encourage members to join us in our efforts to go digital and reduce our environmental footprint, while enjoying the convenience of timely notifications.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for my overseas medical treatment if I am living overseas for the long term?
questions.text:
As MediSave is primarily meant for medical treatment in Singapore, it does not cover overseas medical expenses for those residing overseas for the long term. This is a common feature of national healthcare systems in many countries.
If you are residing overseas for the long term, please consider obtaining medical coverage to meet your overseas healthcare needs.

questions.title: I have directed a medical institution to submit a claim on my behalf. However, I would like to make an amendment to that claim. What should I do?
questions.text: Please approach the medical institution that submitted the claim on your behalf for assistance.

questions.title: I do not have a Singpass account. How will I be notified of my MediSave deduction?
questions.text:
You will be notified of your MediSave deduction digitally via your contact details maintained with CPF Board.
We strongly encourage you to update your contact details with us using Singpass to obtain timely notification of your MediSave deduction.
Having a Singpass account provides added convenience and security when accessing Singapore government services. You can register a Singpass account by following the instructions on the Singpass website.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for hearing aids?
questions.text:
MediSave cannot be used for the purchase of hearing aids. This is because MediSave is primarily designed to help Singaporeans offset costly hospitalisations, day surgeries and selected outpatient treatments.
However, you may apply for the Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF) which provides subsidies to eligible seniors for a range of assistive devices, including hearing aids. You can call the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) at 1800 650 6060* or visit AIC website for more details.
* Airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: Why are MediSave withdrawal limits imposed?
questions.text:
MediSave is used to pay for a wide range of expenses, including health insurance premiums, hospitalisation, day surgery and outpatient bills like chemotherapy and dialysis.
To ensure that Singaporeans have sufficient savings in their MediSave Account for their basic healthcare needs in old age, MediSave withdrawal limits have been carefully set to strike a balance between the affordability of current treatments and future healthcare needs. These limits, after taking into account Government subsidies and applicable MediShield Life payouts, are generally adequate to cover most of the charges incurred at subsidised inpatient wards and outpatient treatments.
The Ministry of Health reviews the MediSave withdrawal limits from time to time to ensure that they remain relevant to healthcare costs and Singaporeans’ needs.

questions.title: What is the healthcare hotline?
questions.text:
For healthcare-related enquires, you may call us at 1800 222 3399* / 65 6222 3399 (overseas) from Mondays to Fridays, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT+8, excluding public holidays). Alternatively, you can also write to us.
* Airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: How much MediSave can I use to pay for my own or an approved dependant's day surgery bills?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave:
Up to $830 per day for ward charges; and
Between $240 and $5,290 for your surgical procedures, depending on the type of procedures performed.
You can use up to the same withdrawal limit for each approved dependant. Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

questions.title: I am going for a day surgery. How do I know if I can use my MediSave in that clinic/hospital?
questions.text:
You can refer to this list of medical institutions or day surgery centres participating in the MediSave scheme.
To use your MediSave, please inform the staff handling your hospital admission that you wish to do so. The staff will submit your claim for you after your authorisation.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for the removal of my wisdom tooth?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave savings to pay for the removal of your wisdom tooth incurred at a participating private dental clinic under the MediSave Scheme, provided that it is a surgical procedure. The day surgery limits are:
1) Day surgeryUp to a maximum of $830 per day for daily hospital charges, including investigations, medicines and doctor's attendance fees.
2) OperationA fixed limit for operations ranging from $240 to $5,290 depending on the type of operations performed.

questions.title: I intend to seek treatment in a hospital. How do I know if I can use my MediSave in that hospital?
questions.text:
Please refer to this list of medical institutions or day surgery centres participating in the MediSave scheme.
To use your MediSave, please inform the staff handling your hospital admission that you wish to do so. The staff will submit your claim for you after your authorisation.

questions.title: What types of hospital charges can be covered by my MediSave?
questions.text: You can use your MediSave for your hospitalisation, surgery, and rehabilitation charges.

questions.title: What happens if my employer or insurer is paying part of my hospital expenses?
questions.text:
If you have given the hospital a Letter of Guarantee or Hospitalisation Identity Card at admission, the hospital will send the bill to your employer or insurer. Your employer or insurer will then work out the part of the bill to be paid by you. They will then ask you to sign a Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF) if you wish to pay the amount from your MediSave Account (MA).
When your employer or insurer returns the MCAF to the hospital, the hospital will arrange to deduct the amount from your MA.
Some hospitals may request that you sign the MCAF at admission especially if your employer or insurer is paying only part of your hospital expenses.

questions.title: If I am hospitalised, how much MediSave can I use to pay for my hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text:
For daily hospital charges1, you can use up to $1,130 per day from MediSave for the first two days of inpatient stays, and $400 per day thereafter.
If you had undergone a surgery, you can use your MediSave to cover part of, or the whole surgery cost. The amount of MediSave you can use depends on the complexity of your surgery, as listed in the Table of Surgical Procedures. You may refer to the MOH website for more information on withdrawal limits for MediSave.
It is useful to note that you are considered hospitalised if you have been admitted for at least eight hours. This requirement does not apply to day surgeries.
1 Includes eligible Mobile Inpatient Care @ Home stays

questions.title: What if my hospital bill is more than what my MediSave can cover?
questions.text: The MediSave withdrawal limits are generally sufficient to cover bills incurred in B2 or C ward types in a public hospital. This restriction is necessary to prevent premature depletion of your MediSave, as your MediSave savings are to last through your lifetime. This is particularly important as elderly people may require more hospital stays and medical care than younger ones. If there is any part of the hospital bill that MediSave is unable to cover, you will need to pay in cash.

questions.title: My approved dependant is a foreigner, while I am a Singapore Permanent Resident. He/She has incurred medical expenses in Singapore. Can I use my MediSave to pay for his/her bills?
questions.text: You may use your MediSave to pay for your approved dependant's medical bills, if it is a MediSave-approved treatment incurred at any of the approved medical institutions in Singapore. Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that your grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my step/adopted children's hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text:
If your step children are under your custody, they are considered your approved dependants, and you can use your MediSave for their hospitalisation expenses.
To use your MediSave for your adopted children, you need to submit legal documentary proof of your relationship to the hospital. If the legal process of adoption is still underway, you should submit the following documents to the hospital:
a. A lawyer's letter stating that the legal adoption is underway, and
b. The birth certificate within one year of your child's date of birth.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for the medical treatments received by dependants other than my approved dependants (spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings)?
questions.text:
MediSave is meant to help you save for your personal or approved dependant's healthcare expenses incurred in any of the participating medical institutions (MIs) under the MediSave Scheme.
You can apply to use your MediSave for a dependant who is not your approved dependant, if the dependant is receiving treatment in a public healthcare institution or voluntary welfare organisation in Singapore. Please approach the medical institution's Business Office for more details on the eligibility criteria and the application process. Such applications will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for optional/cosmetic treatments like liposuction, orthodontics treatment or laser surgery to correct short-sightedness?
questions.text: Generally, MediSave cannot be used for optional/cosmetic treatments. Please check with your attending doctor if the cost of your treatment can be covered by your MediSave.

questions.title: As a bankrupt, can I still use my MediSave?
questions.text: You may use your MediSave to pay for your own or your approved dependants' healthcare expenses even if you have declared bankruptcy. Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

questions.title: What outpatient treatments can be paid using MediSave and what are the withdrawal limits?
questions.text: Please refer to the MOH website for the list of outpatient treatments that can be paid using MediSave and their corresponding withdrawal limits.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my approved dependant's renal dialysis?
questions.text:
You may use your MediSave to pay for approved dependent’s renal dialysis treatment costs, up to a limit of $450 per month per patient.
Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that your grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
To use your MediSave to pay for your approved dependant’s renal dialysis treatment costs, please complete a Medical Claims Authorisation Form at dialysis centres.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for Traditional Chinese Medicine?
questions.text: If you are aged 60 and above, you may withdraw up to $400 per year from your own, or your spouse’s MediSave Account under the Flexi-MediSave scheme to pay for acupuncture treatment for lower back pain and neck pain at specialist outpatient clinics in public hospitals.

questions.title: How are claim limits for MediShield Life and MediSave determined when more than one cancer drug is used in the treatment?
questions.text:
Patients who need more than one cancer drug treatment on the Cancer Drug List (CDL) in a month may claim up to the higher of the MediShield Life, MediSave and Integrated Shield Plan (IPs) claim limits applicable for the individual treatments.
For example, if a patient uses both Treatments X (MediShield Life claim limit of $2,000 & MediSave withdrawal limit of $600) and Y (MediShield Life claim limit of $1,000 & MediSave withdrawal limit of $600) in a month, the patient may claim no more than $2,000 from MediShield Life and withdraw no more than $600 from MediSave in that month.
Please consult your doctor if you wish to clarify the claim limit that will apply for your treatment.

questions.title: What is outpatient Flexi-MediSave?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave allows members aged 60 years old and above to use their MediSave or their spouse's MediSave (if the spouse is also aged 60 and above), up to $400 a year, for outpatient medical treatments at polyclinics, public hospital Specialist Outpatient Clinics and general practitioner clinics participating in the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).
Please note that the $400 is applied on a per patient basis, regardless whether you are using your MediSave or your spouse's MediSave.

questions.title: I am aged 65 years old, and I would like to use my Flexi-MediSave to pay for my father's outpatient medical treatment cost at a polyclinic. Can I do so?
questions.text: Flexi-MediSave can only be used for your own or your spouse's outpatient medical treatment expenses.

questions.title: My child is paying for my chronic disease treatment under the MediSave500/700 scheme. Can I also tap on my spouse's Flexi-MediSave to pay for the co-payment?
questions.text:
If both you and your spouse are aged 60 years old or above, you can use your spouse's Flexi-MediSave for the 15% co-payment.
Also, if you have reached the withdrawal limit for chronic disease treatment, you can tap on your own or your spouse's Flexi-MediSave to continue reducing the cash payment, provided that you have not reached the $400 withdrawal limit.

questions.title: Is there a limit to the number of times I can use Flexi-MediSave for my outpatient treatments in a year?
questions.text: There is no limit to the number of Flexi-MediSave claims you may make in a year. However, you can only use up to $400 in a calendar year.

questions.title: Is there a minimum bill amount before I can use Flexi-MediSave?
questions.text: There is no minimum bill amount before Flexi-MediSave can be used. However, as smaller amounts of cash payment are generally affordable, patients may wish to conserve the use of their Flexi-MediSave for larger outpatient bills, e.g. above $20 - $30.

questions.title: I have used my MediSave for some outpatient medical treatments this year, and would like to know how much more I can use under Flexi-MediSave. How can I do so?
questions.text:
You can check how much more you can use under Flexi-MediSave through:
a. my cpf digital services
• Log in to your Healthcare dashboard using your Singpass
• Select 'Utilisation of healthcare benefits' from the menu bar or scroll down to the 'Utilisation of healthcare benefits' section for 'Additional benefits for the elderly (Flexi-MediSave)'
b. CPF Mobile app
• Download CPF Mobile app
• Log in using your Singpass
• Select 'Healthcare' from the menu bar for 'Flexi-MediSave'

questions.title: What can I use Flexi-MediSave for?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave can be used for outpatient medical treatments (i.e. visits that do not involve a hospital stay or day surgery) received at polyclinics, public hospital Specialist Outpatient Clinics and general practitioner clinics participating in the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).
Flexi-MediSave can cover consultation fees, select restorative dental procedures, tests and drugs, and other services such as physiotherapy, if ordered by your doctor for diagnosis or treatment of your medical condition.
Please refer to this FAQ for medical expenses that Flexi-MediSave cannot be used for.

questions.title: Are there any medical expenses that Flexi-MediSave cannot be used for?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave aims to help elderly patients reduce their cash payment, with the focus on outpatient medical treatment.
It cannot be used for treatments that are for non-medical purposes, such as those for cosmetic or lifestyle purposes (e.g. hair loss, slimming, and erectile dysfunction). It also cannot be used to pay for items from the retail pharmacies, such as skincare products. Non-medical charges such as administrative fees are also not covered.
Flexi-MediSave cannot be used for admissions to the Accident and Emergency department and cancer drug treatments using cancer drugs that are not on the Cancer Drug List.

questions.title: If I have used up other MediSave limits - for example, for scans or for cancer drug treatment, can I use Flexi-MediSave to pay?
questions.text:
If you are already using MediSave to pay for outpatient treatment but have reached your withdrawal limit, you can use Flexi-MediSave to further lower your cash payment, provided that treatment was sought at a polyclinic, public specialist outpatient clinic or general practitioner clinic participating in the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).
Flexi-MediSave cannot be used for cancer drug treatments using cancer drugs that are not on the Cancer Drug List.
However, as Flexi-MediSave covers a much wider range of outpatient treatments than other limits, you may want to save the use of your Flexi-MediSave for treatments that are not already covered by MediSave so as to lower your total cash payments.

questions.title: I intend to seek treatment at a general practitioner (GP) clinic at my void deck. How do I know if I can use my Flexi-MediSave there?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave can be used at:
Polyclinics,
Specialist Outpatient Clinics in the public hospitals and national specialty centres, and
Medical general practitioner (GP) clinics participating in the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) scheme.
The list of participating CHAS medical GP clinics can be found at the following websites:
CHAS
Ministry of Health

questions.title: Is Flexi-MediSave applicable only to the Pioneer Generation or all elderly?
questions.text: Flexi-MediSave applies to all elderly aged 60 and above.

questions.title: Why is Flexi-MediSave only applicable to elderly members aged 60 years old and above?
questions.text:
MediSave is meant to help Singaporeans pay for their more costly medical expenses, especially after retirement. Older Singaporeans usually incur more healthcare expenses as outpatient medical treatments tends to be more expensive for them, while having lower or no income if they have retired. The Flexi-MediSave scheme helps them by allowing them to use MediSave more flexibly to reduce their out-of-pocket expenses for outpatient medical care.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) will regularly review Flexi-MediSave and other financing policies to ensure that outpatient care remains affordable for all Singaporeans.

questions.title: What vaccinations can MediSave be used for?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay for the following vaccinations received at any of the approved medical institutions in Singapore. Please refer to the list of approved medical institutions that provide these vaccinations.
For a list of MediSave-approved clinics under the MediSave500/700 scheme, please visit the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) webpage.

questions.title: How much MediSave can I use to pay for approved vaccinations for myself?
questions.text:
You can use up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for patients with non-complex chronic conditions) yearly per patient from your MediSave or your immediate family members' MediSave.
Your immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. To use your grandchildren's or siblings' MediSave, you must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident. The same yearly withdrawal limit applies for approved chronic disease treatments and health screening.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for outpatient treatment of chronic diseases?
questions.text:
You can use MediSave for outpatient treatments of the chronic diseases listed below.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) regularly reviews the list of conditions covered under the Chronic Disease Management Programme, to ensure that they continue to meet the needs of Singaporeans.
For more information, please visit the Ministry of Health website.

questions.title: How much MediSave can I use for my outpatient treatments of chronic diseases?
questions.text:
