You can use up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for patients with non-complex chronic conditions) yearly per patient from your MediSave or your immediate family members' MediSave.
Your immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. To use your grandchildren's or siblings' MediSave, you must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to fully pay for my chronic diseases treatment?
questions.text: You only need to co-pay 15% of the bill for your chronic diseases treatment in cash before using MediSave to pay the rest, except for treatments received at your enrolled Healthier SG clinic. You may find out more about Healthier SG and search for a clinic near you to enrol into one. This is to help you conserve some of your MediSave savings for future healthcare needs.

questions.title: How was the MediSave500/700 withdrawal limit sized?
questions.text: The MediSave withdrawal limits are generally sized to cover subsidised bills, so that the healthcare costs remain affordable.

questions.title: I have signed up for an approved chronic disease treatment package or an approved vaccination package with my healthcare provider. May I use my MediSave to pay for the package?
questions.text: You may use your MediSave for approved treatments under the MediSave500/700 withdrawal limit. Your healthcare provider will be able to help you to submit a MediSave claim for each treatment of the package. Please contact your healthcare provider for assistance.

questions.title: I was diagnosed with a complex chronic condition in the middle of the year. How does this affect my MediSave500/700 withdrawal limit?
questions.text: If you are diagnosed with a complex chronic condition in the middle of the year, your MediSave 500/700 withdrawal limit will automatically be increased from $500 to $700, and the new limit will apply for the entire year.

questions.title: I am a patient with a complex chronic condition. Will I enjoy the higher withdrawal limit of $700 under MediSave500/700 even after my condition improves?
questions.text: The MediSave500/700 withdrawal limit is a yearly limit. This means that you will continue to be able to withdraw up to $700 in the new year if you have had visits for two or more conditions listed under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP), or one CDMP condition with complications in that year.

questions.title: If I have used $500 from my MediSave account for my treatment under MediSave500, can I still withdraw from my family members' MediSave accounts to pay for my treatment?
questions.text: From 1 January 2021, each patient is eligible to withdraw up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for non-complex chronic patients) for their own treatment, regardless of how many MediSave accounts are being withdrawn from.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for my mammogram screening?
questions.text:
If you are aged 50 years old or above, you can use up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for patients with non-complex chronic conditions) yearly per patient from your MediSave or your immediate family members' MediSave for your mammogram screening.
Your immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. To use your grandchildren's or siblings' MediSave, you must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.

questions.title: I intend to send my newborn child for health screenings. Which of the health screenings for newborns can be covered by my MediSave?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave for the following health screenings for your newborn:
Hearing test
G6P deficiency screening
Metabolic screening
Thyroid function test
You can use up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for patients with non-complex chronic conditions) yearly per patient from your MediSave for your newborn's health screenings.

questions.title: What is the MediSave Maternity Package?
questions.text: The MediSave Maternity Package is a package that allows MediSave to be used to pay expenses incurred during delivery and pre-delivery medical expenses such as consultations, ultrasounds, tests, medications etc.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for my maternity expenses?
questions.text:
MediSave can be used to pay for the delivery and pre-delivery medical expenses.
Pre-delivery expenses have to be claimed under the MediSave Maternity Package. However, post-natal consultation fees cannot be claimed under MediSave.

questions.title: Am I able to use my MediSave for pre-delivery medical expenses before my delivery?
questions.text:
You can only use MediSave for pre-delivery expenses after you have delivered.
You will have to present the bills incurred for pre-delivery medical care to the hospital where you delivered. The hospital will submit these bills, together with the bill for the delivery expenses, for MediSave withdrawal under the MediSave Maternity Package on your behalf.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for the cost of terminating my pregnancy?
questions.text:
The use of MediSave for termination of pregnancy (TOP) is subject to the MediSave Maternity Package guidelines. This includes a $900 withdrawal limit for your pre-delivery expenses. In addition, if the procedure was conducted in a day surgery setting, you may claim an additional $830 per day for Daily Hospital Charges.
Please approach the medical institution where you have received or will be receiving the treatment from to check the specific value of MediSave that can be used. The medical institution is best-placed to advise you on the MediSave usage towards your specific treatment(s) and the expected expenses.

questions.title: I have used my MediSave to pay for my medical expenses. Can my employer or insurer reimburse me in cash?
questions.text: Your employer or insurer cannot reimburse you in cash for the portion of your medical expenses paid using your MediSave and/or MediShield Life. The reimbursement for the respective amount must be credited back to your MediSave Account and/or MediShield Life.

questions.title: I have just obtained my Singapore Permanent Resident status. When is the start date of my MediShield Life cover?
questions.text: Your MediShield Life cover will commence on the date that Immigration Checkpoints Authority (ICA) grants you your Permanent Residency status.

questions.title: Do I need to apply for MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are automatically covered under MediShield Life. No application is required.
You will receive a cover issuance or renewal notification about one month before the start or renewal of your MediShield Life cover. The notification will inform you of your MediShield Life premiums and subsidies. If you have children under 21 years old, you will receive their MediShield Life notifications.

questions.title: Why does my child not have a MediShield Life cover to claim for the hospitalisation bills incurred before he passed away?
questions.text:
We are sorry to hear of your child's demise. The MediShield Life claims can be submitted by the medical institution and will be processed if your child was a Singaporean/Singapore Permanent Resident.
Please contact us at 1800-222-3399 or write to us with your child's details.

questions.title: How much can I claim from MediShield Life?
questions.text:
MediShield Life has features such as claim limits, deductible and co-insurance. As such, the amount you can claim from MediShield Life for your bill can only be finalised after the Board processes the completed claim information submitted by the medical institution.
In the meantime, you can use the MediSave and MediShield Life claims calculator to estimate the maximum amount you can withdraw from your MediSave and / or claim from MediShield Life.

questions.title: I intend to visit a clinic/hospital. How do I know if I can use MediShield Life coverage in that clinic/hospital?
questions.text:
You can refer to this list of medical institutions participating in MediShield Life.
To make a claim, please inform the staff handling your hospital admission or outpatient treatment that you wish to do so. The staff will submit your claim for you after your authorisation.

questions.title: I wish to check the amount claimed from my MediShield Life coverage for my recent hospitalisation. How can I do so?
questions.text:
You can view the details of your MediShield Life claims (with transaction dates within the last 15 months from the date of enquiry) at cpf.gov.sg/healthcare:
1. Login to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass
2. Proceed to 'Latest healthcare payments and claims'
3. Select and view the details of your recent healthcare payments and claims. To view more claims, click on 'View past 15 months'.
4. Click on 'View details' under MediShield Life to view the claim details.

questions.title: For those with serious pre-existing conditions, why do they have to pay Additional Premiums for MediShield Life?
questions.text: Those with serious pre-existing conditions pay a higher MediShield Life premium as a reflection of the higher risks they pose to the pool and to fund part of their coverage. The Government will support most of the cost of extending MediShield Life coverage to all Singapore Residents.

questions.title: When will my MediShield Life coverage cease?
questions.text:
Your MediShield Life cover will be terminated when you pass away or renounce your Singapore citizenship/Permanent Residency. Premiums for the unused period will be refunded to the premium payer’s MediSave Account.
The payer may view the refunded premium (if any) at Transaction history statement under “Contributions / Government Cash Grant / Government Top-up".

questions.title: Who manages MediShield Life?
questions.text: MediShield Life is administered by the Central Provident Fund Board on behalf of the Ministry of Health.

questions.title: Will checks be conducted for new Singapore Residents who are covered under MediShield Life?
questions.text:
For new Singapore Residents who are covered under MediShield Life, we will have a range of checks, including reviewing medical records after they are covered. They are required to declare their health status upon receipt of the In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter from the Immigration Checkpoint Authority of Singapore (ICA).
If they are identified to have serious pre-existing medical conditions, they will be subjected to 30% Additional Premiums for 10 years. Those who make false health declarations will be guilty of an offence under the MediShield Life Scheme Act and will be liable to pay penalties.

questions.title: What are the hospitalisation and outpatient treatment benefits under MediShield Life?
questions.text:
MediShield Life covers expenses incurred for hospitalisations and certain approved outpatient treatments, such as kidney dialysis, cancer drugs and radiotherapy for cancer.
The benefits under MediShield Life are shown in these tables. They are designed to cover subsidised bills incurred for hospitalisations in Class B2/C wards and subsidised outpatient/day surgery treatments in public hospitals. Patients who seek non-subsidised treatments in Class A/B1 ward types in public hospitals or private hospitals will also be able to benefit from MediShield Life. However, as such non-subsidised bills are much higher, MediShield Life will cover a smaller portion of the bill.

questions.title: Why are there changes to cancer treatment financing?
questions.text:
Before 1 September 2022, MediShield Life paid up to $3,000/month for all cancer drugs, and Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) often covered costs above that on an as-charged basis (i.e. no claim limit), with a small co-payment.
Such a design meant that drug companies had no incentive to charge lower prices for drug treatments that cost less. As a result, we paid higher prices for many cancer drugs as compared to other countries such as Australia, South Korea and the United Kingdom.
The changes to cancer treatment financing allow us to negotiate lower prices for cancer drugs and ensure that cancer treatment costs and insurance premiums remain affordable for Singapore residents in the long term.

questions.title: How will the new Cancer Drug Treatment benefit under MediShield Life and MediSave impact my claims from 1 September 2022?
questions.text:
MediShield Life and MediSave will only cover treatments on the Cancer Drug List (CDL) from 1 September 2022. Each cancer drug treatment on the CDL will have its own MediShield Life claim limits and MediSave withdrawal limits.
You may refer to the CDL for the list of cancer drug treatments that are claimable under MediShield Life and MediSave, and their respective claim and withdrawal limits. Please consult your doctor if you wish to find out whether the treatment that you are currently undergoing is on the CDL.
The CDL will only come into effect for Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) on 1 April 2023, upon renewal or application. If you have an IP, you will continue to be covered under your current policy terms until it is renewed on or after 1 April 2023.

questions.title: Does the Cancer Drug List also apply to inpatient cancer drug treatments under MediShield Life and MediSave?
questions.text: Currently, the Cancer Drug List does not apply to inpatient cancer drug treatments as these are covered separately under the inpatient claim limits for MediShield Life and MediSave, together with other costs incurred during the inpatient stay.

questions.title: What are the criteria for inclusion in the Cancer Drug List?
questions.text:
Generally, the Cancer Drug List comprises of drugs that are clinically proven and more cost-effective in treating a particular cancer.
A drug is clinically proven if it is registered with the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) for the particular clinical indication and has met the required standards of safety, quality and efficacy. A drug is cost effective if it provides good value in treating the particular cancer as compared to the existing standard of care, in terms of health benefits to the patient and cost.

questions.title: Can a patient claim for cancer drug services from the Cancer Drug Services limit if he is receiving a treatment that is not on the Cancer Drug List?
questions.text: Yes, patients may claim for cancer drug services from the annual Cancer Drug Services limit even if the service was rendered for a cancer treatment not on the Cancer Drug List (CDL) (i.e. the claim limit is not specific to treatments on the CDL).

questions.title: I am prescribed a drug that is not on the Cancer Drug List. Can I claim under the Cancer Drug Services Limit?
questions.text:
The cancer drug services limit is meant to cover ancillary services that patients may require as part of their cancer drug treatment.
If the drug you are prescribed is a supportive medication to manage the symptoms and side effects of your cancer drug treatment (e.g. antibiotics to reduce risk of infection, pain medication or anti-nausea medication), it is claimable under the Cancer Drug Services limit.
However, if the drug is used for the treatment of the cancer / tumour itself (e.g. chemotherapy, immunotherapy or targeted therapy), it should be claimed under the Cancer Drug Treatment limit instead. Cancer Drug Treatments that are not listed on the Cancer Drug List are not eligible for MediShield Life, MediSave and Integrated Shield Plan claims and should not be claimed under Cancer Drug Services limit.

questions.title: What happens if I have to change treatment in the middle of the month? Does it mean that the new treatment is not claimable?
questions.text: For patients who have to switch treatment in the middle of the month, both treatments would be claimable up to the higher of the MediShield Life, MediSave and Integrated Shield Plan claim limits applicable for each individual treatment.

questions.title: My cancer drug treatment is on a 3-weekly cycle. Is the cancer drug limit sufficient for months when I need to undergo 2 rounds of treatment?
questions.text:
For cost-effective cancer drug treatments on 3-weekly cycles, the MediShield Life (MSHL) claim limits have typically been sized to cover the post-subsidy costs of two treatment courses in a month.
For other cancer drug treatments, the MSHL claim limit has been sized to cover up to the monthly cost of the cost-effective alternative.

questions.title: How do Government pensioners benefit from MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Government pensioners can use MediShield Life as a complement to their post-retirement medical benefits, to pay for overall out-of-pocket expenses for large hospitalisation bills that are incurred from:
Co-payments for large hospitalisation bills that exceed their post-retirement medical benefits
Ward upgrades beyond their eligibility in Restructured Hospitals e.g. when a pensioner eligible for Class B1 ward chooses to stay in Class A ward
Private hospital expenses, which are not covered by Civil Service medical benefits today.
The Public Service Division has sent letters to pensioners to inform them of their MediShield Life benefits in 2015.

questions.title: How can I apply for the suspension of MediShield Life premium collection?
questions.text:
The MediShield Life Council (MLC) recognises that there is a small and distinct group of Overseas Singaporeans (OS) who live outside Singapore permanently, have no intention to reside in Singapore, and feel that they will not benefit from MediShield Life.
If you belong to the OS group, you can apply for a suspension of premium collection even though you will remain covered under MediShield Life. You can refer to the Suspension of MediShield Life Premium Collection for more information on the eligibility criteria and application process.

questions.title: What should I do if my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is approved and I later decide to relocate back to Singapore?
questions.text:
If you have relocated back to Singapore, please inform us via cpf.gov.sg/writetous. We will cease the suspension of MediShield Life premium collection. The accumulated sum of premiums that were suspended from collection, with compound interest, will be payable.
We will provide you with details of the total premiums, the amount deducted from your MediSave Account and inform you if there is any outstanding balance to be paid.
You may refer to the Terms & Conditions for more information.

questions.title: Can I cancel or terminate my MediShield Life cover?
questions.text: MediShield Life provides universal healthcare coverage to Singapore Citizens (SCs) and Permanent Residents (PRs) regardless of their pre-existing medical conditions, for life. Coverage is mandatory for SCs/PRs and cannot be cancelled or terminated. With every Singapore resident collectively supporting our healthcare costs by paying premiums and pooling our healthcare risks under MediShield Life, we can keep annual premiums affordable to support payouts for those of us who incur unexpectedly large hospital bills.

questions.title: How can I find out more information about my dependants' MediShield Life covers?
questions.text:
If you are the premium payer for your dependants' MediShield Life covers, you will be notified about a month before the renewal of their covers.
You can also log in to Healthcare dashboard 'Coverage and premium details' for information on your and/or your dependants' MediShield Life premiums and subsidies.
If you are not the payer of your dependant(s)' MediShield Life cover(s), they or their payers will need to log in to Healthcare dashboard to check their coverage and premium information.

questions.title: Can you explain the various premium components and computation for my MediShield Life Cover?
questions.text: You can refer to the MediShield Life Information Booklet for more information on the premium components and computation for more information.

questions.title: What are MediShield Life premium rebates?
questions.text:
Members pay higher premiums during their working ages. In return, they enjoy premium rebates that reduce the premiums they pay after age 66.
The premium rebates you receive depend on how long you have been insured under the scheme. The earlier you join the scheme, the higher the premium rebates you will receive.
The premium rebates can be found in the following tables:
Note: Figures are indicative. Premium rebates will be adjusted from time to time in line with the experience of the scheme.

questions.title: Why have I received a notice from the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) informing me that I owe MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
IRAS is authorised under the MediShield Life Scheme Act and the CareShield Life Scheme Act to carry out enforcement actions to recover MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums.
The amount stated in IRAS' notice includes any outstanding MediShield Life premiums, interest and penalties as at the print date.
You should pay your outstanding premiums by the deadline indicated by IRAS to avoid further enforcement actions or apply for assistance to help you pay the premiums. Find out more on the payment options.

questions.title: Can the outstanding MediShield Life premiums be waived due to financial difficulty?
questions.text:
Members with financial difficulties may apply for Additional Premium Support (APS). APS helps members who cannot pay their MediShield Life premiums despite Government subsidies and have limited family support.
You can find out more on APS by calling 1800-222-3399 (or +65 6222 3399) from Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5:30pm (GMT+8).
The Ministry of Health will assess each application to ensure that assistance is provided to members who need financial support.

questions.title: I have renounced my citizenship and applied to withdraw my CPF savings. Will my application be affected if I choose not to pay the outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Your withdrawal application will be processed even if you have outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums.
However, you are advised to fully pay your outstanding premiums to avoid enforcement actions by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). To do so, please click on the link below to view the payment options.
I have renounced my citizenship/am residing overseas without local bank account. How do I pay my outstanding MediShield Life premiums?

questions.title: If I have renounced my citizenship, will interest and penalty still be imposed on my outstanding MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text: You need to pay your MediShield Life premiums incurred prior to your renouncement date of your citizenship. If your premiums remain outstanding, compounded interest of 4% and penalties of up to 17% will be imposed and enforcement actions will be taken.

questions.title: I am a bankrupt and I do not have monies to pay the MediShield Life premiums for my child/dependant and myself. Will there be interest and penalty imposed on me?
questions.text:
A claim will be filed with the Private Trustee or Official Assignee for outstanding MediShield Life premiums (including interest and penalties) incurred prior to the date of your Bankruptcy Order.
You are required to pay any MediShield Life premiums incurred after the date of your Bankruptcy Order. Bankrupt parents/guardians remain liable to pay for their child/dependant's premiums.
If you face difficulties paying the premiums, you may apply for Additional Premium Support (APS). APS helps members who cannot pay their MediShield Life premiums after Government subsidies and have limited family support. Find out more information on APS by calling 1800-222-3399 (or +65 6222 3399) from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT+8).
The Ministry of Health will assess each APS application to ensure that assistance is provided to members who need financial support. They will notify you of your APS application status.

questions.title: Can the Board refund the amount of outstanding MediShield Life premiums recovered from my/my child's MediSave if we qualify for Additional Premium Support?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) is provided to members who have insufficient MediSave and limited family support to pay their outstanding premiums.
The Government will pay your/your child's outstanding and future premiums at the point of APS qualification for the next two years. Hence, there is no refund of any outstanding premiums recovered prior to your APS qualification.

questions.title: Will premium recovery measures for MediShield Life include chasing the next of kin?
questions.text:
Premium recovery measures will not be levied on the next of kin. Members are responsible for their own MediShield Life premiums.
The Government will implement measures such as imposition of interest and penalty on outstanding premiums on members who default premium payments repeatedly.

questions.title: What does it mean to appoint agents to recover outstanding MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) will take enforcement actions against members with outstanding MediShield Life premiums. This may include appointing agents like employers, banks or tenants in member's properties to recover the outstanding premiums.
IRAS will inform members and their agents of the appointment in writing. The appointed agents will pay the premiums to the MediShield Life Fund on behalf of the member.

questions.title: Can the premium recovery measures for MediShield Life be waived?
questions.text:
Premium recovery measures cannot be waived as premiums must be paid timely. These measures are only imposed if the member defaults on premium payments repeatedly.
By paying on time, members do not cause others to shoulder their premium debts. You can write to us at www.cpf.gov.sg/writetous if you need assistance with premium payments.

questions.title: Will I be eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
You will receive MediShield Life Premium Subsidies (up to 60%) if you meet the following eligibility criteria:
Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.
Household monthly income per person of $3,600 and below
Living in a property with an Annual Value of $31,000 and below.
Those who are either older, have lower income or live in residences with lower Annual Value will enjoy higher subsidy rates. Individuals who own multiple properties will not be eligible.
Permanent Residents will receive half of the subsidy rates applicable to Singapore Citizens. This is aligned to the subsidy policy in public healthcare institutions.

questions.title: Will I receive premium subsidies if my child / payer is paying for my MediShield Life premium?
questions.text: You will receive the subsidies you are eligible for regardless of who is paying your MediShield Life premiums. You can login to Healthcare dashboard 'Coverage and premium details' to check your eligible subsidies.

questions.title: I am a Pioneer Generation member (Pioneers). How much subsidies will I receive for my MediShield Life premium?
questions.text:
Pioneers Generation Subsidies range from 40% at age 65 to 60% at age 90.
The Government is committed to helping Pioneer Generation seniors aged 80 and above in 2014 by fully covering their MediShield Life premiums. This is done through a combination of Pioneer Generation Subsidies and MediSave top-ups. For younger Pioneers, their MediShield life premiums will be about half of the MediShield premiums after Pioneer Generation Subsidies and MediSave top-ups.
You can login to Healthcare dashboard 'Coverage and premium details' to check your coverage, premiums and subsidies.

questions.title: Will I be eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies for the lower- to middle-income for the rest of my life?
questions.text:
Premium Subsidies are provided to help the lower- to middle-income households with their MediShield Life premiums as long as you meet the eligibility criteria. Pioneer Generation Subsidies are applicable for the rest of the Pioneer's life.
The Government will ensure that the process for subsidies is as simple and convenient as possible, so that those who meet the eligibility criteria can get the subsidies easily.

questions.title: Why am I receiving subsidies even though I have withdrawn from the eligibility check for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
There are different types of MediShield Life premium subsidies.
The eligibility check process was used to determine eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies for lower- to middle-income Singapore Residents.
If you did not participate in the eligibility check, the Government will still compute the MediShield Life Premium Subsidies for your household. However, it will be based on existing information in Government records, which may not be up-to-date. For individuals who miss the date to confirm their household information and wish to make changes, please call 1800-222-3399 for further assistance.
Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Merdeka Generation Subsidies are given based on your Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation statuses, and are applied automatically to your MediShield Life premium.

questions.title: How do I take over my/my dependant(s)' MediShield Life premium payment or change payer?
questions.text:
If you have a valid Singpass and sufficient funds in your MediSave Account, you can submit a Change Payer for MediShield Life request online to take over your/your dependant(s)' MediShield Life premium payment.
If you need help with the request, contact us at 1800 222 3399 or write to us.

questions.title: How often do I have to pay MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text: MediShield Life cover is renewed yearly. Payers are notified about one month before cover renewal date and premiums are collected within a month after the cover is renewed.

questions.title: How can I find out my child's outstanding MediShield Life premiums as I am unable to view it from the 'Outstanding MediShield Life Premium' section of my Healthcare dashboard?
questions.text:
You can only view the MediShield Life premiums of the dependant(s) whom you are currently paying for in your Healthcare dashboard or if the premiums are paid from your child's MediSave Account.
If your child’s MediShield Life premium is paid by the other parent or another payer, please write to us at www.cpf.gov.sg/writetous with your child’s name and birth certificate/NRIC number.

questions.title: How do I view the details of my outstanding MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
You can log in to Outstanding MediShield Life premium to view the breakdown of your outstanding premiums, interest and/or penalties.
If you do not have any outstanding premium for the previous policy years, but your dependants have, you will see a blank section below the premium summary table. Your dependants can view the breakdown of their outstanding premiums by logging into their own Healthcare dashboards.
If you and your dependants (if any) do not have outstanding premium, you will not be able to view this page.

questions.title: Why do I have to pay MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
MediShield Life provides universal coverage to Singapore residents for life, regardless of their pre-existing health condition. Members uphold their collective responsibility by paying their premiums on time to ensure that MediShield Life is able to meet its commitments and pay out claims to its members.
Defaults on premium payment will translate to bad debts to the MediShield Life Fund and result in higher premiums for all.

questions.title: How much MediSave can I use to pay for my family member's outstanding MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text: You can pay your insured family member's outstanding MediShield Life premiums in full using your MediSave.

questions.title: How do I track the status of my request to pay for my dependant's MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
You can log in to Activities to track the status of your request to pay your dependant(s)' MediShield Life premiums.
For subsequent policy renewals, you will receive a premium notification about a month before the policy is renewed. You can also log in to Healthcare dashboard 'Coverage and premium details' for information on your and/or your dependants' MediShield Life premiums and subsidies.

questions.title: Why am I identified to pay for my own MediShield Life premiums when my payer has been paying my premiums?
questions.text: You have been identified to take over paying your own premiums because there are sufficient funds in your MediSave Account. This helps to preserve your previous payer’s MediSave for his/her own healthcare needs. We have notified your previous payer. If the previous payer or a new payer wishes to help with your premium payment, he/she can submit a Change Payer for MediShield Life.

questions.title: Will my MediSave be deducted if the amount is less than my/my dependant's outstanding MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The amount deducted from your MediSave Account will be your/your dependant’s outstanding premium, or your MediSave balance, whichever is lower.
If you have insufficient MediSave for premium payment, please click on the link below to view the payment options.
How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)'s CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?

questions.title: When will the deduction from my MediSave Account take place after I submit the Change Payer request?
questions.text:
If the insured has outstanding MediShield Life premiums, the deduction will be made from your MediSave Account soon after you have submitted the request.
Thereafter, the insured(s)' MediShield Life premiums will automatically be deducted from your MediSave Account once a year, within a month after the Insured(s)’ cover renewal date.

questions.title: What is ElderShield?
questions.text:
ElderShield was first launched by the Ministry of Health in September 2002 as a severe disability insurance scheme which provides basic financial protection to those who need long-term care especially in their old age. It provides a monthly cash payout for up to 72 months to help pay out-of-pocket expenses in the event of severe disability.
ElderShield was offered to eligible Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who had a MediSave Account when they turned 40 years old in 2019 or earlier.

questions.title: Why is there an error message stating that my MediSave balance is insufficient to take over paying an insured's CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
If you received an error message stating that your MediSave balance is insufficient to take over paying an insured's CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediShield Life premiums, it could be because your MediSave balance has been reserved for upcoming premium payments for yourself and/or your dependants' healthcare insurance coverage.
If you do not have enough MediSave balance to take over paying another insured's CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediShield Life premiums, you may top up your MediSave balance or arrange for another family member to take over the insured's premiums. This will ensure that you have sufficient MediSave balance reserved for your own healthcare needs.

questions.title: Why is there an error message stating that I am not paying for my family member's CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediShield Life coverage when I tried to stop premium payment?
questions.text:
If you encountered an error message stating that you are not paying your family member's CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediShield Life premiums, it could be due to several reasons:
1. Not the Payer: The error may arise if you are not the payer for your family member's healthcare insurance.
2. Coverage Under Integrated Shield Plan (IP) or Supplement Plan: If your family member has an Integrated Shield Plan or Supplement Plan, please contact the insured's private insurer directly for payer arrangements.
3. Inactive Coverage: Your family member's healthcare coverage is inactive.

questions.title: What is a private Integrated Shield Plan (IP)?
questions.text: A private Integrated Shield Plan (IP) is an optional medical insurance plan provided by private insurance companies which offers additional benefits on top of MediShield Life. You will need to pay higher premiums using MediSave and cash when you are older.

questions.title: Do I get additional payouts from buying Integrated Shield Plan (IP)?
questions.text: In the majority of hospitalisation bills, you are unlikely to get additional payout from your Integrated Shield Plan (IP) if you stay in B2/C wards in public hospitals.

questions.title: Will I receive hospitalisation subsidies if I choose A ward type in public hospital or choose to go to a private hospital?
questions.text: You will not receive any hospitalisation subsidy in an A ward type in a public hospital or at a private hospital. Hence, if you are inclined to stay in an A ward in a public hospital or go to a private hospital for treatment, you should consider an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) that covers the cost for the particular ward/hospital type.

questions.title: How do I switch to a lower Integrated Shield Plan (IP) / terminate my existing IP?
questions.text: You can instruct your private insurer to assist you in switching or terminating your Integrated Shield Plan (IP). You will continue to be covered under MediShield Life.

questions.title: What happens if I do not pay my Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums?
questions.text: If you do not pay your Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums within your insurer’s stipulated Grace Period, your insurer will terminate your IP coverage and you would lose the additional private insurance coverage. However, you would continue to be covered under MediShield Life and pay the lower MediShield Life premiums. You may wish to refer to your IP policy contract for details on the Grace Period.

questions.title: I am an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) policyholder. Am I eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies or Additional Premium Support (APS)?
questions.text: Integrated Shield Plan (IP) policyholders will be able to receive MediShield Life premium subsidies if they meet the eligibility criteria. However, they are not eligible for Additional Premium Support (APS), as APS is targeted at those with financial difficulties. Should you have difficulty paying your premiums, you may wish to consider terminating your IP and applying for APS.

questions.title: What will happen if I have insufficient MediSave to pay for my Integrated Shield Plan?
questions.text: Your insurer will notify you of the outstanding amount payable for your Integrated Shield Plan and advise you how to make payment to the insurer. Please contact your insurer if you require further assistance.

questions.title: Do I have to pay Additional Premium (AP) for pre-existing conditions if I have an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), and would these conditions be covered after AP is paid?
questions.text:
An Integrated Shield Plan (IP) comprises two parts, namely the MediShield Life (MSL) and the additional private insurance component. MSL is sized for B2/C wards at Government hospitals, while the additional private insurance is sized for A/B1 wards at Government hospitals and private hospitals.
The 30% Additional Premium (AP) for serious pre-existing medical conditions is only applicable to the MSL component of your IP premiums.
For the additional private insurance coverage component, it will be separately assessed by your IP insurer. Generally, private insurers exclude pre-existing medical conditions from their coverage. You should contact your IP insurer to find out more.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to purchase an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) for my family member who is a foreigner?
questions.text: Integrated Shield Plan (IP) coverage for Singaporeans and Permanent Residents include the MediShield Life (MSL) component. You can use your MediSave to purchase a similar non-integrated healthcare plan for your foreign dependent. However, such plans for foreigners will not have the MSL component. Please approach your insurer to advise on the plans offered.

questions.title: My family members are covered with free Integrated Shield Plan (IPs) provided by a private insurer. Do I still need to pay MediShield Life premiums for them?
questions.text: If your family members are covered with free Integrated Shield Plans (IPs), please check directly with your insurer who is administering the IPs if you still need to pay MediShield Life premiums for them.

questions.title: How will I know the amount of premiums that I need to pay for my/ my dependents' Integrated Shield Plan (IP)?
questions.text: Your insurer administering the Integrated Shield Plan (IP) will notify you of your premium details before your policy is renewed. You can log into your insurer's web portal to check your IP premium amount or approach your insurer directly for further clarifications.

questions.title: Why was the payment for my Integrated Shield Plan (IP) / MediShield Life (MSL) unsuccessful even though there are sufficient funds in my MediSave Account (MA)?
questions.text: The funds in your MediSave Account (MA) may be reserved for other healthcare payments, such as ElderShield/CareShield Life premiums, hospitalisation bills, or premium payments for your dependents’ healthcare policies. These may have resulted in insufficient funds in your MA to pay for your Integrated Shield Plan / MediShield Life.

questions.title: How do I change the payer for my/my dependants' Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums?
questions.text: As your Integrated Shield Plan is administered by the private insurer you have chosen to cover you, please approach your insurer directly to make the change.

questions.title: Can I insure my dependent under Integrated Shield Plan (IP), but insure myself under MediShield Life and vice-versa?
questions.text: Yes, you can choose to cover yourself under MediShield Life and get Integrated Shield Plan (IP) from different private insurers for your dependents, or vice versa.

questions.title: What happens to my existing Integrated Shield Plan (IP) when I apply for a new IP?
questions.text:
Your existing Integrated Shield Plan (IP) will automatically be terminated when your new IP commences. This ensures you will only pay premiums for one IP, as medical claims can only be paid from one IP at any one time. Your insurer will refund any unused premium for the remaining cover period of the terminated IP.
Before you buy a new IP, you should check if your new insurer will cover all your pre-existing medical conditions. While the MediShield Life component of your new IP will continue to cover you for life, including any pre-existing medical conditions, private insurers generally will impose exclusions i.e. they generally do not pay claims for pre-existing medical conditions that you already suffer from before the start of your IP.

questions.title: How do I update my personal particulars (including change of address) for my Integrated Shield Plan (IP)?
questions.text: As your Integrated Shield Plan (IP) is administered by the private insurer you have chosen to cover you, please approach your insurer directly on all matters relating to your IP or by updating your particulars on your insurer’s web portal.

questions.title: As I am covered under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), why are there two transactions made in my Yearly CPF Statement of Account?
questions.text:
An Integrated Shield Plan (IP) is made up of two components, namely:
1. The MediShield Life component – reflected as MSL, and
2. The additional private medical insurance component – reflected as PMI.
Hence, there would be two transactions reflected for any deduction/refund of IP.

questions.title: I am paying the Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums for my dependants. Why is this information not reflected on my Yearly CPF Statement of Account?
questions.text: Your dependants’ details would not be reflected if you are not using your MediSave to pay for their Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums. However, you can log in to your Healthcare dashboard to view your dependants’ coverage information. The information is available under “Health insurance - Coverage and premiums details”.

questions.title: What is CPF nomination?
questions.text: A CPF nomination allows you to specify who will receive your CPF savings and the proportion of your savings each nominee will receive when you pass away. Your nominee(s) will receive your CPF savings in cash.

questions.title: Who can make a CPF nomination?
questions.text:
You can make a CPF nomination as long as you are a CPF member, at least 16 years old and must not lack mental capacity. Members who are bankrupt or have disabilities (e.g. visual impairment) can also make a CPF nomination.
If you are critically ill and want to make a CPF nomination, we would advise that a medical practitioner be present with you at the time the nomination is made. Doing so would provide better assurance that your nominees will receive the CPF savings in the manner you intended.
The medical practitioner should also provide a medical certificate stating that you possess the mental capacity to make the nomination.
Notwithstanding the above, we encourage CPF members to make their nominations as early as possible and review them regularly, and not leave nomination making until they are nearing end of life.

questions.title: Why is there a minimum age for making a CPF nomination?
questions.text: CPF members should be of sufficient maturity when they make a decision to nominate and bequeath their CPF savings. Therefore, a minimum age of 16 is set for making a nomination, in line with the minimum age to work and earn wages under the Employment Act.

questions.title: When should I make a CPF nomination?
questions.text: We encourage you to make a CPF nomination as soon as you begin to accumulate savings in your CPF account. As you progress in life, you should also review your nomination regularly, especially after major life events (marriage, childbirth, divorce etc.) so that your nomination continues to fit your intention.

questions.title: What is covered by CPF nomination?
questions.text: You can refer to the infographic below to find out what a CPF nomination covers.

questions.title: I have already made a will. Do I still need to make a CPF nomination for my CPF savings?
questions.text:
Yes, you will still need to make a CPF nomination as CPF savings are excluded from your estate and therefore cannot be covered by a will.
Excluding CPF savings from your estate protects your savings from any creditor claims on outstanding loans that you may have after your demise. This ensures that your CPF savings are fully preserved for your loved ones.
You are encouraged to make a CPF nomination to distribute your CPF savings according to your wishes.

questions.title: How should I notify the CPF Board of my overseas marriage in relation to my CPF nomination?
questions.text:
You can notify us of your overseas marriage by completing the form Notification of Marriage in relation to CPF Nomination. We may require generally up to five working days from the submission of the completed form (including all supporting documents) to act on the marriage notification. If you have a CPF nomination made before this marriage, your nomination will be revoked.
You are strongly encouraged to make a new CPF nomination after your marriage if you want your CPF savings to be distributed according to your wishes.

questions.title: I submitted a CPF nomination form under my old account. Do I need to make a new CPF nomination if I have merged my CPF accounts?
questions.text: You do not need to submit a new CPF nomination form. If you have a valid CPF nomination form under your old CPF account, the CPF nomination status will automatically be updated in your new account. Hence, you do not need to make a new CPF nomination under the new CPF account unless you wish to change your nominee(s).

questions.title: Can I make a CPF nomination if I am holding more than one CPF account?
questions.text:
If you are a Singaporean/Permanent Resident (PR) and you are holding more than one CPF account, you will need to merge your CPF accounts before making the CPF nomination.
Maintaining only one CPF account will simplify your transactions with the Board. You can make a CPF nomination once your CPF accounts are merged.
You can find out what are the documents needed to merge your accounts and how to submit them to us.

questions.title: Are my MediSave Account savings covered under CPF Nomination?
questions.text: CPF Nomination covers all savings in your MediSave Account, including those in your Ordinary, Special and Retirement Accounts.

questions.title: How would my child's CPF savings be distributed if he were to pass away?
questions.text:
The minimum age to make a CPF nomination is 16 years old.
If a member passes away before attaining 16 years of age, he/she would not have a valid CPF nomination, and as such his/her CPF savings would be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office for distribution in accordance with the Intestate Succession Act or the Administration of Muslim Law (for Muslims).

questions.title: If I have made a CPF nomination, how will my CPF savings be paid to my nominees?
questions.text:
By default, your nominee(s) will receive the CPF savings due to them in cash or GIRO.
If you have made a CPF nomination, you can check your details to find out how your CPF savings will be distributed to your nominee(s).
Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS)
If you have made a nomination under the Special Needs Savings Scheme, your children will receive your CPF savings on a monthly basis upon your demise. Find out more about SNSS Nomination.
Please contact the Board if you have any enquiries on the above.

questions.title: If I have not made a CPF nomination at the point of my passing, what will be distributed to my family under intestacy laws?
questions.text: If you have not made a CPF nomination at the point of your passing, we will pay the savings in your Ordinary, Special, MediSave and Retirement Accounts to the Public Trustee’s Office for distribution to your family member(s) in accordance with the relevant intestacy laws or inheritance certificate (for Muslims).

questions.title: How will CPF savings be distributed under the intestacy laws?
questions.text:
Member's CPF savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office for distribution in accordance with the Intestate Succession Act (Cap 146) if he did not make a CPF nomination.
For a Muslim member, his CPF savings will be distributed in accordance with the Inheritance Certificate. His family can obtain the certificate from the Syariah Court, Family Link @ Lengkok Bahru, 8 Lengkok Bahru, #03-01, Singapore 159052.

questions.title: I have bought an annuity in place of the retirement sum when I turned 55. Will my nominees receive the remaining guaranteed sum from my annuity when I pass away?
questions.text: If you had bought an annuity in place of the retirement sum when you turned 55, your nominees will receive the remaining guaranteed sum from your annuity when you pass away.

questions.title: Why are CPF Investment scheme (CPFIS) investments not distributed to nominees in the CPF nomination?
questions.text:
CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) investments are not covered under CPF nomination. When a member passes away, his CPFIS investments1 and any cash balance in his Investment Account will form part of his estate. Doing so allows beneficiaries of the estate to decide how best to manage these assets, including the preferred timing for the sale of assets such as unit trusts and stocks. These decisions should be made by the beneficiaries as the decisions could affect the value of the CPFIS investments. CPF monies covered under CPF nomination can then be disbursed quickly without having to await the beneficiaries’ decision on the CPFIS investments.
1 Except for insurance policies where the policyholder has made an insurance nomination with the respective insurance company. The nominated beneficiaries can contact the insurance company to claim the death benefits.

questions.title: Is Faraid the only way to distribute a Muslim's estate?
questions.text: Faraid is not the only way to distribute a Muslim’s estate. There are various Islamic legacy planning tools available. CPF nomination for example, is a valid form of hibah (gift), that Muslims can consider when planning for their legacy.

questions.title: If a valid CPF nomination has been made, can a Faraid heir who has not been nominated claim a portion of the deceased member's CPF savings?
questions.text: No. According to a fatwa by the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (Muis), CPF nomination is a valid form of hibah (gift). Thus, when a nomination has been made, only the nominee(s) is entitled to the CPF savings. A Faraid heir who has not been nominated does not have a legal claim over the CPF savings.

questions.title: Can Muslims nominate a non-Faraid heir to receive their CPF savings after they pass?
questions.text:
Yes. According to a fatwa by the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (Muis), CPF nomination is a valid form of hibah (gift). You may thus nominate whoever you wish, non-Faraid heirs or even legal institutions for charitable purposes.
Learn more about nominating legal institutions here.

questions.title: Do I need to make a CPF nomination if I have made my Islamic Will?
questions.text:
CPF savings do not form your estate and cannot be covered under an Islamic Will.
You are strongly encouraged to make your CPF nomination to ensure that your CPF savings are distributed swiftly and conveniently to your nominee(s) without any administrative fees.
Unnominated CPF savings will be held by the Public Trustee’s Office (PTO). Family members must initiate the claims process, retrieve the deceased’s Inheritance Certificate from the Syariah Court, and provide other necessary paperwork. The distribution process can take up to six months, and administration fees will be charged by the PTO and Syariah Court.

questions.title: Who is the Public Trustee?
questions.text:
The Public Trustee is appointed by the Minister for Law under the Public Trustee Act 1915. Among other functions, the Public Trustee may act as the trustee to administer the estates of deceased persons and distribute them to the rightful beneficiaries.
If you require further information or clarification, please contact:
The Public Trustee's Office
45 Maxwell Road
#07-11, The URA Centre (East Wing)
Singapore 069118
Tel: 1800 2255 529
Website: pto.mlaw.gov.sg

questions.title: Who can I include as my nominee?
questions.text:
You can nominate any person (regardless of age or nationality) or organisation so long as the nominee is not a witness in the nomination.
Find out what are the things you need to prepare when making a nomination.

questions.title: Can my nominee be below 18 years old?
questions.text:
Yes, your nominee can be of any age.
If your nominee is below 18 years old at the time of claim, his share will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) and held-in-trust until he reaches 18 years of age.
Visit PTO's website to find out important information (such as admin fees) related to shares belonging to a minor nominee.

questions.title: What happens to my CPF savings if my nominee is below 18 years old?
questions.text:
If your nominee is below the age of 18 at the time of claim, his share will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office and held-in-trust until he reaches 18 years of age.
Alternatively, you can nominate a trustee/trust company to receive your CPF savings on behalf of your beneficiary who is a minor.
You are advised to make arrangements with the trustee/trust company on how to channel your CPF savings to your intended beneficiaries. Please note that we are not in a position to enforce or ensure that the trustee/trust company will apply the CPF savings received for the benefit of your intended beneficiaries. This is strictly a private arrangement between you and the appointed trustee/trust company.

questions.title: Will my nominee(s) be notified when I make a nomination?
questions.text: Your nomination is confidential. We will not disclose your nomination details to anyone, including your nominee(s). We will only contact your nominee(s) regarding the distribution of your CPF savings when you pass away.

questions.title: If my nominee is a bankrupt, can he still claim my CPF savings?
questions.text: If any of your nominee is an undischarged bankrupt on and from the date of your death, the nominated monies vest in your nominee’s trustee in bankruptcy for the benefit of your nominee’s creditors. Hence, CPF Board will have to notify the Official Assignee, who maintains the Bankruptcy Estate Account on behalf of all trustees, of these assets.

questions.title: Do I need to indicate the address of my nominees, if they do not live in Singapore?
questions.text: Mailing address is required for foreigners to facilitate us in contacting them when distributing your CPF savings. Mailing address for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents will be based on the address registered with Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA).

questions.title: Is there a limit to the number of nominees I can appoint?
questions.text:
There is no limit to the number of nominees you can appoint.
If you are nominating up to 15 nominees, you can submit an online application. If you are nominating more than 15 nominees, please visit our CPF Service Centre to make a nomination.

questions.title: Why do I need to provide the NRIC or a unique identification number of my nominees in my CPF nomination form?
questions.text: The NRIC or a unique identification number of your nominees will facilitate the Board's identification of your nominees which allow them to claim your CPF savings swiftly and easily.

questions.title: Can I nominate a trust fund to receive my CPF savings for the benefit of my nominee?
questions.text: CPF members are not allowed to nominate a trust fund as it is not a legal entity which is capable of receiving monies.

questions.title: What should you do if you are going to nominate or have nominated Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC)?
questions.text:
If you are going to nominate SNTC as a nominee, you should contact SNTC to find out the procedures to observe. This is especially important if you have specific intentions as to how you want your CPF savings to be used or allocated by SNTC (e.g. to benefit a specific SNTC trust beneficiary). If you have already nominated SNTC in your nomination and have yet to inform SNTC, please contact SNTC via enquiries@sntc.org.sg or office hotline 62789598 to inform them of your nomination.
Please ensure that SNTC is kept informed of your intentions as CPF Board is not in a position to enforce or ensure that the organisation will apply the CPF savings received in the manner you intended.

questions.title: What is a legal entity?
questions.text:
A legal entity is a person or legal body capable of receiving monies, including CPF savings in its own right.
For an entity to be capable of receiving monies, it has to be recognised under the law as being capable of doing certain things in its own name and not in the name of its members, such as owning and holding property, suing others and being sued. Such entities would include societies registered under the Societies Act 1966, companies (including public companies limited by guarantee) registered under the Companies Act 1967, and limited liability partnerships (LLP) registered under the Limited Liability Partnerships Act 2005.
Businesses such as Partnerships and Limited Partnerships, are not legal entities.

questions.title: Why do I need witnesses when I make a CPF nomination?
questions.text:
Disputes on who should receive your CPF savings may sometimes arise after you have passed on. That is why you have to appoint two witnesses who can attest that you have made your nomination willingly and calmly. Your witnesses cannot be your nominee or an organisation.
Witnesses do not need to know your nominee(s)’ details to perform their roles as witnesses. Where necessary, your witnesses can help us understand how the nomination was made so that we can distribute your CPF savings according to your wishes.

questions.title: Who can be my witnesses for my CPF nomination?
questions.text:
Your witnesses must be two different individuals who:
are at least 21 years of age;
must not lack mental capacity; and
are not any of your nominee(s).
If you are making an online nomination, your witnesses must have a valid Singpass.

questions.title: Can my nominee be my witness?
questions.text: Your nominee cannot be one of your witnesses, to prevent a conflict of interest.

questions.title: My witnesses are residing in a different country from me. Can I appoint them as witnesses for my CPF nomination?
questions.text:
Yes, you can make an online nomination and appoint them as your witnesses as long as they meet the criteria to be a witness and have a valid Singpass.
Once you have decided on your witnesses, you should contact them and inform them of your intention to make a nomination. You should request that they confirm this when asked to do so by CPF Board.

questions.title: Will my witnesses know the details of my CPF nomination?
questions.text:
Your CPF nomination details will not be made known to your witnesses. Your witnesses will only need to declare that they are aware of your intention to make a nomination and specify how the witnessing request was communicated to them.
Making your nomination online provides added privacy and confidentiality, as your witnesses will not be able to see your nomination details.

questions.title: Do I need to review and update my CPF nomination after making one?
questions.text: Yes. Making a CPF nomination is not a one-time affair as your circumstances may change (e.g. marriage, childbirth, divorce etc). You are encouraged to review your CPF nomination so that it remains relevant to your latest circumstances.

questions.title: Do I have to update or change my CPF nomination record when there are changes to my circumstances (e.g. marriage, child birth, divorce, death of my nominee)?
questions.text:
You are encouraged to make a new CPF nomination to keep your nomination relevant to your latest circumstances.
See the infographic below for some examples of life milestones when you should consider reviewing your nomination.

questions.title: What happens to my CPF nomination upon divorce?
questions.text:
Divorce does not revoke a CPF nomination. This treatment is similar to that of wills (which are not revoked upon divorce).
Some members may still wish to bequeath their CPF savings to their ex-spouse and/or children via their existing nominations, and therefore, it is best for members to review their latest personal circumstances and update their nomination accordingly.
You can make a new nomination online.

questions.title: What happens if I have children after making my CPF nomination?
questions.text: Childbirth does not change your existing CPF nomination. However, you should make a new nomination if you wish to include your child as one of the beneficiaries of your CPF savings.

questions.title: Can I make a new nomination instead of notifying CPF Board of my marriage?
questions.text: You can make a new nomination if you do not wish to notify us of your marriage. The new nomination will supersede your previous nomination (if any).

questions.title: What happens if I do not inform the CPF Board of my marriage in the required manner?
questions.text: If we are not informed of the marriage in the required manner, the distribution of your CPF savings will follow your existing nomination, which may not be your latest bequeath intention to distribute your CPF savings.

questions.title: How do I cancel a CPF nomination I made earlier?
questions.text:
You can cancel your CPF nomination by making a new CPF nomination. The new nomination will supersede the nomination which you have made earlier.
To make a nomination, you can do so online using your Singpass.

questions.title: What happens to my existing CPF nomination when I make a new one?
questions.text: Your new CPF nomination will supersede any earlier CPF nomination which you have made. The Board will follow your latest instruction in your new nomination.

questions.title: Where do I submit the completed CPF nomination form?
questions.text:
We encourage you to make your CPF nomination online at my cpf Online Services.
Alternatively, you can visit any of our CPF Service Centres and complete the CPF Nomination Form in the presence of our Customer Service Executives (CSEs) who can act as your witnesses and clarify any questions you may have. You can book an appointment with us through our CPF Appointment Service at the CPF website. The appointment can be made on your preferred date and time, subject to the availability of appointment slots.

questions.title: Can a blind person make a CPF nomination?
questions.text:
A blind person can make a CPF nomination if he wants his CPF savings to be distributed according to his wishes.
If he chooses not to make a CPF nomination, his CPF savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) for distribution to his family members under the Intestate Succession Act or the Inheritance Certificate (for Muslims). This ensures that the welfare of his dependants is provided for.

questions.title: Can I indicate my nominee's share of my CPF savings as a fixed amount instead of a percentage?
questions.text:
No. In the event that your CPF savings are insufficient to meet this fixed amount you had specified in your nomination, we will not be able to distribute your CPF savings according to your wishes.
Indicating nominee(s)’ entitlement as a percentage of your CPF savings will allow us to distribute your CPF savings to your nominee(s) according to your wishes, regardless of changes to your CPF balances. The total entitlement for all nominees must sum up to 100%.

questions.title: How can I make a CPF nomination if I am overseas?
questions.text:
You can make an online nomination using your Singpass.
Your witnesses need not be physically present with you to verify your intention to nominate. However, your witnesses must have a valid Singpass to complete the witnessing for your nomination.

questions.title: Can I change my CPF nomination? Is there a limit to the number of times I can change my nomination?
questions.text:
Yes, you can change your CPF nomination by making a new nomination. Your new nomination will supersede your existing nomination.
There is no limit to the number of times you can change your nomination.

questions.title: Can I still make a CPF nomination if I am seriously ill?
questions.text:
Yes, you can do so provided you are conscious and must not lack mental capacity when making the nomination.
You can consider appointing a doctor to be one of your witnesses in your nomination. You can request your doctor to write a memo stating that you have the mental capacity to make a CPF nomination and submit it to us.

questions.title: My nominees have changed their personal particulars (e.g. names, addresses or passport numbers). Do I need to update the changes in my CPF nomination?
questions.text:
If your nominee is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
You do not need to update the changes in your CPF nomination.
For name changes, the Board will request your nominee to present document(s) e.g. Deed Poll, as proof of their name change when they apply to withdraw the CPF monies after your demise.
If your nominee is a foreigner
You should make a new CPF nomination with their latest particulars. This will help us identify and contact your nominee easily to distribute your CPF savings.
We also encourage CPF members to indicate the NRIC equivalent of their nominee’s home country in their nomination. This is because passports do expire and nominees may not retain possession of their expired passports when they apply to withdraw a deceased member’s CPF savings.

questions.title: What if I am unable to find two witnesses to witness my nomination online?
questions.text:
You can make an appointment at any of our CPF Service Centres to make a CPF Nomination if you cannot find two witnesses online. Our Customer Service Executives will assist you to complete your nomination, and also act as your witnesses. Alternatively, you may visit any of the ServiceSG Centres to make your online CPF nomination.
View the list of ServiceSG Centres locations and its operating hours.

questions.title: Can I make a CPF nomination if I am a bankrupt?
questions.text:
Even if you are bankrupt, you should make a CPF nomination if you want your CPF savings to be distributed according to your wishes.
If you do not make a CPF nomination, your CPF savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office for distribution to your family member(s) in accordance with the relevant intestacy laws or inheritance certificate (for Muslims). This ensures that the welfare of your dependants is provided for.

questions.title: What is online nomination? How is it different from submitting a hardcopy nomination?
questions.text:
Online nomination allows you to submit your CPF nomination online, anytime, anywhere, without the need for your witnesses to be physically present to sign the hardcopy form. The process is simple and takes place entirely online:
You log in with your Singpass and submit the online nomination form with the required details.
Inform your witnesses so that they are aware of your intention to make this nomination.
Your appointed witnesses are notified by email and/or SMS to perform witnessing.
The appointed witnesses log in with their Singpass and affirm your intention to make the nomination.

questions.title: Why should I make my CPF nomination online?
questions.text: Online nomination is convenient – you can make your nomination anytime, anywhere. Your personal information is protected as your witnesses will not be able to see your nomination details.

questions.title: Is it safe to make my CPF nomination online?
questions.text:
There are multiple layers of checks in place so that CPF members can make their nomination online in a safe and secure manner.
A Singpass is required to log in securely to my cpf digital services to make your online nomination. Singpass has multiple layers of security measures in place, including Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) login. We will also send SMS and email notification alerts to your registered mobile number/email address when you make your nomination online.
The combination of these measures will provide a safe and secure environment for you to make your nomination online.
You are also encouraged to adopt good security practices such as not sharing your Singpass credentials with others and changing your passwords regularly.

questions.title: How can I check the status of my nomination?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your online nomination at cpf.gov.sg/Activities using your Singpass.
We will send you an email/SMS once your nomination is routed to your witnesses. Upon the completion of witnessing by your witnesses, we will generally process your nomination within four working days. You will also receive an email/SMS of the status.
Once your online nomination has been processed, you will receive one more email/SMS notification on the final status of your nomination.
If you wish to view the details of your nomination, you can then access the information at cpf.gov.sg/viewnomdetails.

questions.title: How many nominees can I specify in my online nomination?
questions.text: You can specify up to 15 nominees. If you wish to nominate more than 15 nominees, you can make a nomination at our CPF Service Centres.

questions.title: What should I do if I wish to amend an online nomination I have submitted?
questions.text:
You can amend your nomination if either or both your witnesses have not witnessed your nomination. You can do so by withdrawing your nomination and submitting a new one.
If both your witnesses have already witnessed your nomination, you will not be able to withdraw and amend the nomination. However, you can submit a new nomination after your earlier nomination is processed. Your new nomination will supersede your earlier nomination.
You can only submit one nomination within the same day. This includes the nomination that has had its witnessing process completed that day.

questions.title: How can I withdraw my online nomination?
questions.text:
You can withdraw your application so long as at least one of your witnesses has yet to complete the witnessing:
Log in to my cpf digital services using your Singpass at cpf.gov.sg/Activities.
In transaction details, click on “withdraw this application” and confirm your intent to withdraw the application.
Please note that after you withdraw your online nomination, your existing nomination status remains unchanged. If both your witnesses have completed their witnessing and you wish to make a new nomination, you can submit one via this link.

questions.title: I am using an iOS device (iPhone or iPad) to submit my online nomination, and I was not able to submit my nominee's particulars. How can I resolve this?
questions.text: If you are using an iOS device (such as iPhone or iPad) to submit your nomination, the “Smart Punctuation” feature in iOS may prevent you from submitting your nomination. You can disable the feature by performing the following steps on your device: Settings > General > Keyboard > Turn off Smart Punctuation.

questions.title: How do I submit an organisation as my nominee in my online nomination?
questions.text: If you would like to nominate an organisation, select 'Registration No.' under the ‘Select identification type’ field and indicate the organisation’s unique corporate registration number (such as Unique Entity Number (UEN)) in the ‘Registration number of organisation’ field.

questions.title: Is there an administrative fee when I submit my nomination online?
questions.text: There is no administrative fee to make a CPF nomination.

questions.title: How long will CPF Board take to process my online nomination?
questions.text: If you submit your nomination online, the Board will process it generally within four working days from the date that both your witnesses complete the witnessing of your nomination. You can check the status of your online nomination under “Activities” by logging in to my cpf Online Services using your Singpass.

questions.title: What information relating to my witnesses do I need to provide when I make a nomination online?
questions.text:
You will need to provide the following information of your witnesses when making an online nomination:
NRIC
Full Name* as per NRIC
Email and/or Singapore registered mobile number (for receiving of SMS notification to perform witnessing)
*It is important to provide your witnesses' full name as indicated on his NRIC, including comma, hyphen and space accordingly. However, you should exclude the Hanyu Pinyin, Alias and married name. See examples of NRIC names.

questions.title: Am I allowed to submit another online nomination if my previous nomination is still pending action from my witnesses?
questions.text:
You cannot submit another nomination if you have an existing nomination pending witnessing. However, if any of your witnesses has not completed their witnessing, you can withdraw your nomination and submit a new one.
How can I withdraw my online nomination?

questions.title: Can I submit more than one nomination online within the same day?
questions.text:
You can only submit one nomination within the same day. This includes the nomination that has had its witnessing process completed that day.
If you wish to submit a new nomination, you may withdraw the current one if your witnesses have not witnessed it. If both your witnesses have already witnessed your nomination, you can submit a new nomination after your earlier nomination is processed. Your new nomination will supersede your earlier nomination.
How can I withdraw my online nomination?

questions.title: Who is eligible to make a nomination online?
questions.text: CPF members who are aged 16 and above, and have a valid Singpass, are eligible to make a nomination online.

questions.title: I have been requested to witness an online nomination. What do I need to do?
questions.text:
As a witness, you will need to declare that you are aware of the CPF member’s intention to make a nomination and specify how the request was communicated to you.
If you are ready with this information, please login with your Singpass to complete your witnessing.
You can view the video guide for more information on being a witness for a CPF nomination online.

questions.title: Why can't witnesses view the CPF member's nomination details?
questions.text: The role of a witness is to affirm the CPF member’s intention to make a CPF nomination. There is no need for witnesses to know the nomination details to perform their role as witnesses.

questions.title: Is there a deadline for me to witness an online nomination?
questions.text:
Yes, you have seven calendar days from the time you receive the SMS/email notification request to complete the witnessing.
If you cannot complete the witnessing in time, please inform the CPF member, as the nomination application will expire and the CPF member will need to submit a new application.

questions.title: Why can't I access the online nomination witnessing request that was sent to me?
questions.text:
You will not be able to access the online nomination witnessing request if:
the nomination application had expired (after seven calendar days from application date);
the member making the CPF nomination has withdrawn the nomination; or
you have already completed witnessing the nomination.

questions.title: How can I be sure that I'm witnessing a legitimate nomination?
questions.text: It is your responsibility as a witness to ensure that the CPF member making the nomination has specifically requested for you to witness his nomination. You should check with the member to affirm his intention to make a CPF nomination before proceeding to witness his nomination.

questions.title: I received a request to witness an online nomination from someone I do not know. What should I do?
questions.text: Do not complete the witnessing process. Please contact us immediately so that we can follow up with the CPF member.

questions.title: What supporting documents do I need if I am making a nomination at the CPF Service Centre?
questions.text: You are strongly encouraged to bring along photocopies of your nominee(s)’ identification documents (such as NRIC or foreign identification document) indicating their particulars.

questions.title: Do I need my own witnesses to be present if I am making my nomination at any CPF Service Centre?
questions.text: Our Customer Service Executives can act as your witnesses.

questions.title: How can I check my CPF nomination details?
questions.text:
You can view your CPF nomination details using your Singpass. However, please note that nominations made more than 30 years ago cannot be viewed online.
If your nomination is over 30 years old, we strongly recommend making a new nomination even if you wish to nominate the same nominees:
