Allow your CPF savings to be distributed in accordance with your latest wishes
Update your nominees' personal information for swift identification and contact
Enable convenient online access to your nomination details
Making a new nomination is a simple process. Find out how you can make a CPF nomination.

questions.title: Do I need to authorise specific person(s) to access my CPF account information when I pass away?
questions.text:
From 1 February 2024, nominees and eligible family members under intestacy laws will be allowed to access your CPF account information, after your passing.
With this change, there is no longer a need for you to authorise your loved ones to access your CPF account information upon demise.

questions.title: I have appointed authorised person (AP) in my nomination to access my CPF account information upon my demise, but I can no longer see the appointed AP under my nomination dashboard. Do I need to make a new nomination to appoint AP again?
questions.text:
From 1 February 2024, nominees and eligible family members under intestacy laws will be able to access your CPF account information after your passing.
This change brings greater convenience to members and makes it easier for their loved ones to settle matters relating to the deceased member’s CPF accounts.
Your appointed authorised persons will still be able to access your CPF account information upon your demise if they are your nominees or eligible family member. Else, your information will not be disclosed to them.

questions.title: What CPF account information can my nominees and eligible family members under intestacy laws access, upon my demise?
questions.text:
Your nominees and eligible family members can access the following information:
CPF account balances and past 15 months' transaction history
Nomination details
CPF schemes which you have participated in

questions.title: Can anyone access my CPF account information while I am still alive?
questions.text: No. Your CPF account information is confidential. No one will be able to access your CPF account information while you are alive.

questions.title: Can I instruct CPF Board to disallow my nominees or family members from accessing my CPF account information, upon my demise?
questions.text:
No. Allowing your nominees and family members to access your CPF account information make it easier for them to reconcile your CPF account information and settle any post-demise matters relating to your CPF account.
This practice is also aligned with industry standards on matters such as for estate distribution under wills and distribution of assets by the Public Trustee’s Office, where details of the distribution can be provided to all beneficiaries.
Please be assured that your CPF information remains confidential while you are alive. Your nominees and family members who are eligible beneficiaries under intestacy laws can only access your CPF account information after you have passed away.

questions.title: Can I instruct CPF Board to allow person(s) who are neither my nominees nor family members who are eligible beneficiaries under intestacy laws, to access my CPF account information, after my death?
questions.text: No, you cannot instruct the Board to allow any other persons other than your nominees or family members who are eligible beneficiaries under intestacy laws to access your CPF account information, upon your demise.

questions.title: Will I be able to access the CPF account information of a deceased CPF member?
questions.text:
If CPF Board is notified* of the death before 1 February 2024
If the deceased member had appointed authorised persons in his/her CPF nomination, only the authorised persons can access his/her CPF account information.
If CPF Board is notified* of the death on or after 1 February 2024
Nominees and family members who are eligible beneficiaries under intestacy laws will be able to access a deceased member's CPF account information.
*Please note that the notification date may not be the same as the actual date of death of the CPF member.

questions.title: Can I make or revoke a CPF nomination on someone's behalf?
questions.text:
A CPF nomination must be made or revoked by the CPF member personally.
However, if a CPF member lacks capacity under Section 4 of the Mental Capacity Act ("MCA"), only the Courts are allowed to make or revoke a CPF nomination on behalf of the member.
An interested party can apply to the Court to do so, and the court would decide in the interest of the member who is lacking capacity, whether to accept the application to make or revoke a CPF nomination on his behalf.

questions.title: How can a donee/deputy make or revoke a CPF nomination for members who lack mental capacity?
questions.text: For CPF members who lack capacity under Section 4 of the Mental Capacity Act ("MCA"), only the Courts can make or revoke a CPF nomination on their behalf.

questions.title: How does CPF Board ensure that changes to CPF nomination of members who lack mental capacity, are done in their best interest?
questions.text:
The treatment of CPF nominations has been aligned with that of wills under the Mental Capacity Act 2008 (MCA).
Safeguards are in place under the MCA as the Court in making decisions on behalf of a member who lacks capacity, has to take into account what is in the member's "best interests". This includes taking into consideration the member's past and present wishes and feelings, his beliefs and values that would likely influence his decision if he had the mental capacity. The Court will also have to take into account the views from persons who were close to the member.

questions.title: What happens if the CPF Board finds out that the CPF nomination was made whilst the member lacked capacity?
questions.text:
If the Board is informed of any facts or circumstances which may affect the validity of the CPF nomination and has evidence and supporting documents to ascertain the fact that the member lacked capacity at the time of making the CPF nomination, the Board will invalidate the CPF nomination made by such a member.
Anyone, who is of the view that the CPF nomination is invalid on the grounds that the member lacked capacity at the time the said CPF nomination was made, could also apply to Court to set aside the nomination.

questions.title: What happens to my CPF nomination if I lose mental capacity after making my nomination?
questions.text: Your CPF nomination will not be affected and remains valid even after you lose mental capacity.

questions.title: Can I appoint someone to make or revoke my CPF nomination on my behalf before I lose mental capacity?
questions.text: No. Only the Court is allowed to make or revoke a CPF nomination on behalf of the member, under Section 4 of the Mental Capacity Act 2008.

questions.title: What happens if the CPF Board deems that the CPF nomination was made whilst the member lacked capacity?
questions.text: If the CPF Board deems that the CPF nomination was made whilst the member lacked capacity within the meaning of section 4 of the Mental Capacity Act 2008, the Board will invalidate the nomination. The previous CPF nomination (if any) made by the member would remain valid (assuming the member did not lack capacity when he made the previous CPF nomination). The member's CPF savings would be distributed in accordance with the intention of the member in his previous valid CPF nomination. If there is no previous valid CPF nomination, the CPF savings would be paid to the Public Trustee for distribution in accordance with intestacy laws.

questions.title: Can both parents nominate the same child with disabilities?
questions.text: Both parents of an eligible child with disabilities can participate in the Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS). The child with disabilities will then receive separate streams of payout from each parent’s CPF savings upon the parent’s demise.

questions.title: Can parents cancel their Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) nomination after making one?
questions.text:
Parents can cancel their Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) nomination by making a new CPF nomination.
The new nomination will supersede the SNSS nomination which they have made earlier.
To make a nomination, you can do so online using your Singpass.

questions.title: Will there be a charge levied on members for Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS)?
questions.text: There will be no charge levied on members for making a CPF nomination under Special Needs Savings Scheme.

questions.title: Apart from Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), how else can parents set aside money for their child under the CPF system?
questions.text:
Parents can also set aside money for their child by topping up to the Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) nominee's CPF accounts based on current CPF rules. These top-up monies will enjoy CPF interest rates and will be set aside specifically for the child's retirement needs instead of being disbursed under the SNSS.
For parents who are under the CPF LIFE scheme, and have made a Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) nomination, they can opt not to receive their monthly CPF LIFE payouts, and retain the monies in their Retirement Account (RA).
To do so, members can inform the Board of their intention in writing at least 2 months before their Payout Eligibility Age (PEA) or anytime after they have reached their PEA. In the request, members should indicate their name, NRIC number, signature and their intention to retain their CPF LIFE payouts in their CPF Retirement Accounts (RA) for the benefit of their SNSS nominee(s).

questions.title: Can parents determine the amount of monthly payouts for their nominated child with disabilities?
questions.text: Parents can determine the amount of monthly payout for their nominated child with disabilities at the point of application, subject to a minimum payout of $250 per month with a minimum duration of at least one year.

questions.title: I would like to change how much my child can receive monthly under the Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), how can I make the change?
questions.text: Under the Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), parents can revise the monthly payout by submitting a new nomination indicating the new amount.

questions.title: How do I make a Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) nomination?
questions.text:
The Special Needs Saving Scheme (SNSS) caters to Persons with Special Needs (PSN) who are nominated by their parents to draw a fixed monthly payout from the parents' CPF savings upon the parents' demise.
For more details on SNSS, please visit SNTC's website.

questions.title: What is the Special Needs Savings Scheme?
questions.text:
The Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) allows parents of children with special needs to nominate their child to receive a regular stream of fixed payouts from their CPF savings in the event of the parent’s demise.
CPF members interested to nominate their children under SNSS can approach the Special Needs Trust Company for more information.

questions.title: How is Special Needs Savings Scheme different from CPF nomination?
questions.text:
Unlike a CPF nomination, where the member’s CPF savings are distributed in one lump sum, CPF savings under Special Needs Savings Scheme will be distributed to the nominee on a monthly basis, based on the amount specified by the CPF member, until the bequeathed savings run out.
This enables parents to set aside CPF savings for the long term care of children with special needs.

questions.title: Can I nominate part of my CPF balances under the Special Needs Savings Scheme, while nominating the rest under the CPF cash nomination?
questions.text: Yes. You can decide the percentage of your CPF balances to be nominated under the Special Needs Savings Scheme, and the remaining CPF savings to be nominated under the cash nomination rules for other beneficiaries.

questions.title: What interest rates will be paid on the monies for Special Needs Savings Scheme nominees?
questions.text:
The nominated monies will continue to earn the same CPF interest, including extra interest, in the SNSS nominee’s account, as the rate earned by CPF members.
Extra interest is paid on the first $60,000 of the combined balance of the parent(s) who nominated the child under SNSS and the child’s own CPF savings, with up to $20,000 from the child’s Ordinary Account.
Please refer to CPF interest rates for more information on the CPF interest rates.

questions.title: Who should I contact if I want to know more information on the Special Needs Savings Scheme?
questions.text:
You may contact the Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) who is the appointed scheme administrator.
Parents can visit SNTC’s SNSS website. Alternatively, SNTC can be contacted via phone at 6278 9598 or via email at enquiries@sntc.org.sg for more information.

questions.title: What is the sequence of disbursement for Special Needs Saving Scheme's monthly payout from CPF account? (i.e. which of the deceased's CPF account will be disbursed first?)
questions.text: The CPF savings nominated under Special Needs Savings Scheme will be paid via monthly payouts, starting from the lowest interest earning account, i.e. the Nominee Ordinary Account (NOA) first before moving to Nominee Special Account (NSA) and then Nominee Retirement Account (NRA).

questions.title: How fast can a Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) nominee receive the fund into their bank account after the death of member?
questions.text: For Special Needs Savings Scheme cases, the payment will commence in the following month upon receipt of the completed application form and supporting documents. The payment is generally processed on the 12th of every month until the monies due to the nominee are exhausted.

questions.title: What is required before making an SNSS nomination?
questions.text:
Before you apply for SNSS nomination, you are required to obtain an eligibility letter from Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC). SNTC will issue the letter to you after confirming your nominee’s eligibility for the SNSS. You may then proceed to any of our Service Centres to make the SNSS nomination.
For more details on SNSS, please visit SNTC’s website.

questions.title: Will the deceased member's CPF savings continue to earn interest after his death?
questions.text: The deceased member's CPF savings will continue to earn base interest in the respective accounts for up to six months. However, the CPF savings will not earn extra interest once we are notified of the member's death. Nominee(s) have the right to claim the nominated savings at any time but they are encouraged to submit the withdrawal application as early as possible.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What happens to the deceased member's CPF LIFE premium?
questions.text: The deceased member's CPF LIFE premium balance (if applicable) will be paid to his nominee(s) together with his CPF savings.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: Will the deceased member's CPF savings be used to pay his income tax liabilities?
questions.text: No, the deceased member’s CPF savings will not be used to pay his income tax liabilities. This is because CPF savings do not form part of the deceased member’s estate.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What happens to the deceased member's property bought using his CPF savings?
questions.text: The CPF savings used to buy the property need not be refunded to the deceased member’s CPF account. The property will form part of his estate if it is held in tenancy-in-common or passed on to the remaining surviving owner(s) if it is held in joint tenancy.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What happens to the deceased member's CPF savings used for CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: If the deceased member’s CPF savings had been used under the CPF Education Loan Scheme for himself or someone else, the withdrawn monies, including accrued interest, do not have to be refunded to his account.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: I have applied to withdraw the deceased member's CPF savings. Can I change my payment details?
questions.text:
You can change your payment details for your application to withdraw the deceased member’s CPF savings by submitting the form applicable to you:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, please update your bank account details with CPF Board via my cpf digital services - Account settings with your Singpass.
If you are not a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, please complete the form “Change payment details (for withdrawal of deceased member’s CPF savings or account closure)” (Form NAC/SUPP/F) and mail it back to us.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: Is there a deadline for me to claim the deceased member's CPF savings?
questions.text: You are encouraged to claim the deceased member's CPF savings as early as possible as the deceased member's CPF savings will cease earning base interest in the respective accounts six months after the Board is notified of the member's demise. You can do so anytime by submitting an online application.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: I am an appointed nominee. How will the deceased member's CPF savings be paid to me if I am bankrupt?
questions.text: By operation of Singapore’s bankruptcy laws, if you are an undischarged bankrupt at the time of the member’s death, the nominated monies vest in the trustee in bankruptcy, for the benefit of your creditors. We will notify the Official Assignee (OA), who maintains the Bankruptcy Estate Account on behalf of all trustees, and transfer the nominated monies to the OA upon his instructions.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What happens to the CPF savings if the nominee passed away before he could receive the CPF savings of the deceased member?
questions.text:
The CPF savings would form part of the deceased nominee's estate and would be paid to the Executor/Administrator appointed under the Grant of Probate (GP)/Letters of Administration (LA). For more information on how to apply for a GP or LA, visit Singapore Courts' website.
If there is no Executor/Administrator appointed, the CPF savings may be paid to a proper claimant if the estate does not exceed $50,000. Write to us for more details about the application via the proper claimant route.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: How will the deceased member's CPF savings be distributed to a nominee who is certified to lack mental capacity permanently?
questions.text: If the nominee has a donee appointed through a Lasting Power of Attorney or a deputy appointed via a court order under the Mental Capacity act, the donee and deputy can submit the withdrawal application and receive payment on the nominee's behalf.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: If I am currently using my Special Account (SA) for Dependants' Protection Scheme premiums, how would I be impacted by the closure of SA?
questions.text:
After your Special Account (SA) closes at age 55, your Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) premiums can only be paid from your CPF Ordinary Account (OA), subject to available balance, or in cash directly to the appointed DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life.
Transition measures are in place to provide short-term support to members immediately affected by the SA closure. These members will be notified directly and advised on the necessary steps to take.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Am I covered under the Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your Dependants' Protection Scheme coverage via:
- your yearly CPF Statement of Account
- the "Providing for your loved ones" dashboard by logging in with your Singpass
If you do not have a Singpass, you can apply for one at the Singpass website.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: What is the purpose of the Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text: CPF members who are working and earning an income may have dependants who are reliant on their income. If such CPF members suddenly meet with an accident or contract a terminal illness that results in the loss of their income, the dependants who are reliant on them may be left in the lurch. The impact is greater when the member has not yet accumulated enough CPF or other savings which could be bequeathed to their dependants to tide them over the first few years of their untimely demise. Therefore, Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) is useful to such working CPF members. This is also the reason why DPS coverage is automatically extended to members upon their first CPF contribution between age 21 and 65.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Who will be covered under Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
All Singaporeans and Permanent Residents between age 16 and 65 can be covered under Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS).
DPS coverage is automatically extended to Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents upon a valid CPF working contribution between 21 and 65 years old.
Members aged 16 and above who were not extended a DPS cover automatically but wish to be insured can apply to join DPS with Great Eastern Life directly.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Is Dependants' Protection Scheme compulsory?
questions.text:
Coverage under the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) is not compulsory. Insured members can contact their existing insurer, Great Eastern Life or NTUC Income, to terminate their DPS cover any time by completing the opt out form.
Members should consider the benefits of DPS carefully before he/she terminates his/her DPS cover. Continuing with the DPS cover will provide some financial protection for the member’s family. If members decide to rejoin DPS in the future, they will need to submit a health declaration again and the cover will be provided subject to them being in good health then.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Who do I contact for enquiries on Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text: For enquiries relating to the Dependants’ Protection Scheme, you may contact Great Eastern Life at greateasternlife.com > Contact us.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: I am a Singaporean or a Permanent Resident but I am not living in Singapore. What will happen to my Dependants' Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text: You will remain insured under the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) as long as premiums are paid. DPS coverage is worldwide and a claim can be made when a member meets the claim criteria.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: I am no longer a Singaporean or a Permanent Resident. What will happen to my Dependants' Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
Your Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) coverage will be terminated as the scheme is only available to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
Your DPS insurer will refund any unused DPS premiums for the current policy year to your CPF account. The unused DPS premiums will be paid to you together with your CPF savings when you transfer your CPF savings to your bank account.
If you wish to find out more, please contact your DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life at greateasternlife.com > Contact us.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: My family member has passed on. How do I check if he was covered under the Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
If your family member was covered under the Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS), their coverage status will be made available for viewing by their CPF nominee(s) on the Deceased CPF Member Dashboard.
Alternatively, you may contact Great Eastern Life to verify whether your family member was covered under the DPS.
Great Eastern Life can be contacted at greateasternlife.com > Contact us.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: What do I need to do to restore my Dependants' Protection Scheme cover after I have obtained Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency again?
questions.text: You may wish to contact Great Eastern Life at greateasternlife.com > Contact us for further information regarding your eligibility to re-join the Dependants’ Protection Scheme after regaining Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: I was issued a bonus sum assured in 2003 and/or 2005. Will it be carried over to my Dependants' Protection Scheme policy under the newly enhanced scheme?
questions.text:
CPF Board distributed surpluses in the form of bonus sum assured to the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) members insured before DPS was privatised in 2005. Members can contact their DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life to check if they qualified for the bonus sum assured previously.
To standardise the sum assured for all insured members to the new amount of $70,000 from 1 April 2021 under the newly enhanced DPS, existing members who were eligible for the bonus sum assured will receive a one-time premium rebate in lieu of the bonus sum assured. The one-time rebate has been credited into members’ CPF Ordinary Accounts in May 2021.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Can I terminate my Dependants' Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
Coverage under the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) is not compulsory. You can terminate your DPS cover any time by completing the opt out form. Please approach your DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life for the form.
Please consider the benefits of DPS carefully before you terminate your DPS cover. Continuing with your DPS cover will provide some financial protection for your family. If you decide to join DPS again in the future, you will need to submit a health declaration again and the cover will be provided subject to you being in good health then.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: My Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) is covered by NTUC Income prior to 1 April 2021. When my DPS cover is transferred over to Great Eastern Life from 1 April 2021, do I need to declare my health?
questions.text: No, members who are already insured under Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) prior to 1 April 2021 do not need to submit a new health declaration form for illnesses that developed on or after the commencement of their DPS covers under NTUC Income. Great Eastern Life is required to take over all obligations of DPS covers issued under NTUC Income. This means that Great Eastern Life will continue to cover any medical conditions that had developed on or after the commencement of members’ DPS covers under NTUC Income.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: My Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) cover was issued by NTUC Income. Will Great Eastern Life take over all obligations when my cover is transferred? What if I have developed medical conditions on or after the commencement of my cover under NTUC Incom
questions.text: Great Eastern Life is required to take over all obligations of Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) covers issued under NTUC Income. This means that Great Eastern Life will continue to cover any medical conditions that had developed on or after the commencement of members’ DPS covers under NTUC Income.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: How do I apply to be insured under Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text: You may do so by submitting your Dependants' Protection Scheme application to Great Eastern Life directly.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Can I get any money back after my Dependants' Protection Scheme cover ends when I reach the age limit?
questions.text:
Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) is a term-life insurance scheme which does not include any saving or investment component. Hence, there is no cash back when the member's DPS cover expires at age 65.
This is because DPS is designed to provide members with the maximum financial protection at the lowest possible premium.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Why are some funds reserved in my CPF Ordinary Account for the Dependants' Protection Scheme premium?
questions.text:
To ensure that working CPF members are financially protected by the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS), the necessary amount will be reserved in your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) during the premium payment grace period. This means that you will not be able to use or withdraw up to that amount of OA savings during this period.
If you prefer to pay your premiums in cash, contact the DPS insurer (Great Eastern Life) to top up the full premium in cash. The reserved amount in your CPF OA will be released after your cash payment is processed.
In the event that you need to use the reserved amount for other purposes, please write to us for assistance. However, please note that your DPS cover could lapse if no payment is made within the grace period stipulated by the DPS insurer.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: What is the Dependants' Protection Scheme claim criteria?
questions.text:
A Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) claim can be made when a member passes away or is certified to be suffering from terminal illness or total permanent disability.
For more information on DPS claim criteria, please refer to Great Eastern Life.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: I have already made a nomination for Dependants' Protection Scheme prior to 1 April 2021. Do I need to make a new nomination after 1 April 2021?
questions.text:
From 1 April 2021, Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) is solely administered by Great Eastern Life.
If your DPS policy was under NTUC Income, it has been automatically transferred to Great Eastern Life. As the DPS policies with NTUC Income has ceased after 31 March 2021, nominations of DPS policies previously made under NTUC Income is no longer valid. As such, if you had previously made a nomination under NTUC Income, under the Insurance Act, you will be required to make a new nomination. Your new insurer, Great Eastern Life, would have sent out the nomination forms to you.
If your DPS policy is under Great Eastern Life and you had made a nomination previously, there is no need for you to submit a new nomination, unless you wish to nominate new beneficiaries.
Please note that DPS claim benefits do not form part of CPF savings and will not be distributed based on your CPF Nomination.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: What are the claim exclusions for Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
Claim benefits under Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) will not be payable if any of the following events occur within the first policy year of the cover:
Member committed self-inflicted injury or suicide
Member committed a criminal offence punishable by death
The claim arose out of member's own intentional criminal act
DPS benefits are also not payable if:
Member was not in good health before the commencement of DPS cover
Member provided false or misleading information
The claim arose from wars or any war-like operations or participation in any riot
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: I have not made a nomination before. How do I make a nomination for my Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
If you are at least 18 years old and wish to have the death claim benefits paid to specific person/organization i.e. beneficiary(s), you are advised to make a nomination by submitting the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) nomination form (available on Great Eastern Life’s website) to the insurer. Should you wish to amend your nomination thereafter, you can do so by submitting a new nomination.
Reminder:
DPS claim benefits do not form part of CPF proceeds and will not be distributed based on your CPF Nomination.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: How do I check if I have made a Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) nomination?
questions.text:
To check if you have made a Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) nomination, please contact Great Eastern Life directly. You can reach them at greateasternlife.com > Contact us.
Reminder
DPS claim benefits do not form part of CPF proceeds and are not distributed based on your CPF Nomination.
As of 1 April 2021, DPS is solely administered by Great Eastern Life. If you previously made a nomination under NTUC Income, you need to make a new DPS nomination with Great Eastern Life.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: How will the Dependants' Protection Scheme claim benefits be distributed?
questions.text:
For claims under medical grounds, the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) benefits will be paid out to the insured member directly.
For death claims, if the insured member has made a DPS nomination, or has a will which is made known to the DPS insurer, the beneficiary(s) according to the nomination or will (whichever takes effect at the later date) will receive the benefits.
If no nomination or will is made, the benefits will be paid to proper claimant(s). A proper claimant can be the executor of the deceased's estate or family member, e.g. spouse, parent, child, or sibling.
For more details, please approach the appointed DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: How can I claim Dependants' Protection Scheme benefits under medical grounds on behalf of my next-of-kin who lacks mental capacity?
questions.text:
As an appointed donee/deputy for your next-of-kin, you can claim his insurance benefits and withdraw CPF savings due to Reduced Life Expectancy by completing this form and submitting the required documents as listed in the form. The form will allow you to concurrently apply for both Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) and Home Protection Scheme (HPS) benefits, as well as withdrawal of CPF savings.
Upon receipt of the completed form and supporting document(s), CPF Board and Great Eastern Life (for DPS) will review the application and follow up with you.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: My Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) claim has been approved. How will I receive my DPS claim payout?
questions.text: Upon approval of the Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) claim, Great Eastern Life (GEL) will disburse the DPS claim benefits to your PayNow account, which is linked to your Singapore NRIC and bank account. If you prefer not to receive your DPS claim benefits via PayNow, you may contact GEL directly. If payment made via PayNow is unsuccessful, GEL will contact you to check with you on your preferred payment mode.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: How can I check the status of my Dependants' Protection Scheme claim application?
questions.text: You may contact Great Eastern Life directly to check on the status of your Dependants' Protection Scheme claim application.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Are all non-Singapore Citizens and non-Permanent Residents eligible for account closure?
questions.text: Yes, all non-Singapore Citizens and non-Permanent Residents should close their CPF account and transfer their CPF savings to their bank account by submitting the account closure form.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to my CPF account if I am no longer a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident?
questions.text: Your CPF account will be closed, and you are required to transfer your CPF savings to your bank account. To transfer your CPF savings, please refer to the steps mentioned in this FAQ.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: How can I inform CPF Board of a change in my mailing address if I am not a Singapore Citizen (SC) /Permanent Resident (PR)?
questions.text: With the closure of your CPF account as a non-Singapore Citizen (SC)/non-Permanent Resident (PR) from 1 April 2024, you do not have to inform CPF Board of any changes in your mailing address. You may refer to our webpage for more information on account closure.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What if a non-Singapore Citizen or non-Permanent Resident with a CPF account has passed away before he had closed his account and transferred all his CPF savings?
questions.text: The next of kin will have to inform CPF Board of his passing with the original death certificate. Thereafter, the deceased’s remaining savings will be distributed to his beneficiaries, depending on whether he had made a valid CPF nomination before his passing.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: How can I get the letter from Immigration & Checkpoints Authority confirming the cancellation of my Singapore Permanent Residency?
questions.text:
To obtain the letter from Immigrations & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) confirming the cancellation of your Singapore Permanent Residency, you may submit your request via ICA | Feedback.
*If you are a Malaysian, you are not required to obtain the letter from ICA.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What is a Singapore Overseas Mission?
questions.text:
Singapore Overseas Missions located in certain countries can help CPF members residing overseas in witnessing and certification of application forms and documents.
You will need to visit the Singapore Overseas Mission in person. Find out where the overseas mission nearest to you is.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs
Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: How do I apply to be insured under the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) after I obtained Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency again?
questions.text:
You may re-apply for a Home Protection Scheme cover online, using your Singpass, if your previous HPS cover has ceased and you are the owner of a HDB flat with an outstanding housing loan.
Your eligibility for HPS coverage is subject to approval and your current health condition.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: Do I need to refund the transferred CPF savings if I decide to obtain Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency again after I have closed my account?
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: Will I be able to return to Singapore for work if I have closed my CPF account?
questions.text:
For enquiries on work permit or employment pass application, please contact Ministry of Manpower at 6438 5122 or send your enquiries to them using the online feedback service.
For enquiries on applying for Permanent Residency in Singapore, you may submit your request via ICA | Feedback.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What is the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
The CPF Education Loan Scheme is a loan scheme which allows you to use your Ordinary Account (OA) savings to pay for your own, children’s, spouse’s, siblings' or relatives' subsidised tuition fees.
Only full-time subsidised diploma​​/degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs) are covered under this loan scheme. The student would need to start repaying the principal amount withdrawn plus the accrued interest in cash, to your CPF account, one year after graduation or termination of studies, whichever is earlier.
If the institution or course does not fall under this scheme, you and the student can consider taking up a loan with the commercial banks or approaching the institution for other financial assistance options.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I apply for the use of my Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) funds?
questions.text:
For payment of approved fees and charges, you can withdraw the Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) funds by establishing a Standing Order with MOE or by submitting ad hoc withdrawal applications as and when withdrawals are to be made. The form to use will depend on the approved institution you are in. You should consult the approved institution you are studying in on which form to use.
For more information on PSEA, please visit MOE PSEA website.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: I have previously obtained government subsidies for my first diploma, hence my second diploma is not subsidised. Will I still be able to use CPF savings for my second diploma?
questions.text: As you are not eligible for government subsidies for the second diploma, CPF savings cannot be used even if it is a full-time course offered by an approved educational institution.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: I have previously obtained a degree and will study for a full-time diploma course which is not subsidised by the government at SP/NP/TP/NYP/RP/NAFA/LAS/ITE. Can CPF savings be used for the diploma course?
questions.text: As your selected diploma course is not subsidised by the government, CPF savings cannot be used even if it is a full-time course offered by an approved educational institution.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Do I have to submit supporting documents to prove the relationship if I am applying to use my parent's, spouse's, siblings' or relatives' CPF under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
Supporting documents to verify the relationship between you and the CPF lender is not required at the time of application under the CPF Education Loan Scheme. However, we may request such documents to verify the relationship for audit purposes.
If requested, please provide the required document(s) by completing the “Audit on Application for Use of CPF Savings for Education” form.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: When must the CPF lender endorse the online application submitted under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: The CPF lender must login to the link provided in the email or the Endorse CPF education loan form in the CPF website, using his/her own Singpass, within 14 days from the date the application was submitted, and click 'Yes, I agree to let the student use my CPF savings' if he/she wishes to withdraw his/her CPF savings to pay for the borrower's tuition fees. The online application will be automatically rejected if no action is taken by the lender after 14 days.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Why does the CPF lender need to login to endorse my online application under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: The CPF lender must endorse your CPF Education Loan Scheme application using his/her Singpass to consent to the withdrawal of his/her CPF savings for your tertiary education.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I check the status of my application under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: You can check the status of your CPF Education Loan Scheme application under "Activities" by logging in to CPF website using your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I check for the reasons if my application under the CPF Education Loan Scheme is rejected?
questions.text: You can check the reason for rejection of your CPF Education Loan Scheme application under "Activities" by logging in to CPF website with your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I still apply for CPF Education Loan Scheme after the application period had closed?
questions.text: All applications under the CPF Education Loan Scheme should be submitted within the application period. You may refer to the Application schedule to apply for CPF education loan for the application period of the approved educational institutions.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: When is the application period for the approved educational institutions?
questions.text: You may refer to the Application schedule to apply for CPF education loan for the application period of the approved educational institutions.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Why is there a cap on the amount of Ordinary Account savings that I can use for education purposes?
questions.text: The primary objective of CPF savings is to help members save for their retirement needs. Hence, to avoid depleting members' CPF savings, there is a limit on the amount of savings that can be used for education. The student would also have to repay in cash, the amount withdrawn plus accrued interest after he graduates or leaves the institution to fully restore the member's CPF savings.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Apart from the Ordinary Account savings, can I use my savings from other CPF Accounts under CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: Only Ordinary Account savings can be used under the CPF Education Loan Scheme.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What if I lose the endorsement email or did not receive the endorsement email for the use of my CPF savings under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
The CPF lender can log in to the CPF website using their own Singpass and endorse the application using the Endorse CPF education loan form.
A reminder email would be sent generally within the next three days if the lender has not endorsed the application.
Should you have any queries on the application process, you may reach us at cpf.gov.sg/writetous.
Note: The lender is also advised to ensure that their email settings are in place and the email address used by the borrower in the application is accurate.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: If I have already paid the tuition fees, can I be reimbursed under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: CPF savings can only be used for tuition fees that are due and payable directly to the approved educational institutions.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: When will payment be made to the institution under the CPF Education Loan scheme?
questions.text:
Payment to the institution under the CPF Education Loan Scheme is based on an agreed schedule between CPFB and the institutions. Generally, payments will be made about one to two months after the application closing date. Please note that the schedule may be changed and is indicative only.
The payment made to the institution is subject to availability of funds in the CPF member's Ordinary Account, at the point of deduction for payment to the institution.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Will I receive any notification after payment has been made to the institution under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: If you (i.e. the CPF account holder) have used your CPF savings to pay for the tuition fees, you should receive a notification generally by the following month after the payment has been made to the institution.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How will the CPF savings be deducted when more than one person's savings are used for education?
questions.text:
When more than one person's CPF savings are used, the deductions will take place in the order the application forms are received and processed.
For example, the first parent to apply to use his savings will pay first. The second parent will pay only when the first parent's savings are not enough to pay for the full tuition fees.
If there are not enough savings in the payers' CPF accounts, the student will have to pay for any shortfalls in cash, to the approved educational institution.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How will the CPF savings be deducted if I am paying for more than one student's tuition fees under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
If you are using your CPF savings to pay for the fees of more than one student under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, the deduction will take place based on the payment date to the institution. For example, if the payment date for Institution A is 1 Feb and for Institution B is 3 Feb, the savings will be used to pay Institution A first before paying Institution B.
If there are not enough savings in the CPF account, the student will have to pay for any shortfalls in cash, to the approved educational institution.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: If I have used my CPF savings to pay for my child's education, can I still use it for my other child/children?
questions.text:
You can use your CPF savings to pay the tuition fees for more than one child, as long as there is Available Withdrawal Limit (AWL) for education in your Ordinary Account.
For more information on how much of my CPF savings I can use under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, please refer to this FAQ.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What other financing options do I have if I am not allowed to use CPF savings for unsubsidised courses under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: If you are not allowed to use CPF savings for unsubsidised courses under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, you may wish to apply for a study loan with commercial banks, or approach your institution for financial assistance schemes that they can offer to you.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Is a guarantor required for borrowers under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
No, a guarantor is not required for borrowers who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents. The borrower, as the beneficiary of using their own or another CPF lender's CPF savings for their education, is responsible for the repayment of the savings used. However, the Board reserves the right to request a guarantor or other forms of guarantee on a case-by-case basis.
For borrowers who are already under the scheme but subsequently renounced their Singapore citizenship or Permanent Resident status, they will need to provide a guarantor for their applications as a foreigner. In the event of death or bankruptcy of the guarantor, or if the guarantor is physically or mentally incapacitated from continuing in any employment, the lender whose CPF savings have been used or the foreign borrower will need to notify the Board in writing and provide a new guarantor.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What is the interest rate for loans taken under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
Interest on the outstanding CPF education loan is computed based on the prevailing Ordinary Account (OA) interest rate.
You can refer to the CPF Interest Rates for more information.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How is the interest rate computed for the amount withdrawn under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: Under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, the interest will start to accrue from the time CPF savings are withdrawn from member's Ordinary Account (OA). Interest is calculated on a monthly basis and is compounded on a yearly basis, pegged at the prevailing interest rate for OA.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How long does it take to process my online application under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
Applications will only be processed based on the agreed schedule with each approved educational institution, after the application period for the approved educational institution has closed. Generally, it takes three working days from the receipt of students’ enrolment data from the approved educational institution to complete the processing.
If your institution requires proof of application for the Education Loan Scheme, please provide them with a screenshot of your application showing the status 'In-Progress'.
You can check the status of your application via ‘Activities’ section on the CPF website after logging in with your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Why do we need to use a Singpass for the online application under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: Singpass, which stands for "Singapore Personal Access", is the common password to transact with the Government online. Singpass is the online equivalent of the identity card, and is required for e-services where users must identify themselves online. Please refer to the Singpass website for more information.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What if we do not have a Singpass to submit our online application under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: You may apply for a Singpass online. After obtaining your Singpass, you may complete and submit an online application via “Apply for CPF education loan” under "Forms and e-applications", within the application period.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I amend my online application under the CPF Education Loan Scheme after submission?
questions.text: The application under the CPF Education Loan Scheme cannot be amended once it has been submitted. However, you may cancel the application and submit a new one.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I cancel my online application under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: You can cancel a pending application by accessing ‘Activities’ section on the CPF website after logging in with your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I revoke the use of CPF savings under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
You must be the CPF lender (whose CPF savings is withdrawn) in order to apply to revoke the use of CPF savings under the CPF Education Loan Scheme.
You may submit your application online to revoke the use of CPF savings for education through the "Revocation Form" using your SingPass. You will be informed through email notification on the status of the application if you have registered your email with the Board through Account services.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What should I do if I have submitted an application to use CPF savings for education under Institution A, but have now enrolled with Institution B instead?
questions.text: You can only use CPF savings to finance one course of study at any point in time. You need to cancel your existing application before you submit a new one.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: If I am a foreign student (not Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident), can I apply under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: No, you cannot apply under the CPF Education Loan Scheme if you are a foreign student (not Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident). You may wish to apply for the MOE Higher Education Student Loan or check with your educational institution for other financing options.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Why does the CPF Education Loan Scheme cover only approved full-time subsidised courses?
questions.text:
The CPF Education Loan Scheme is meant for students studying for full-time courses because these courses are subsidised by the government. Also, these students have no income and are likely to have difficulties paying their tuition fees with their own cash savings. Most of them are young adults going straight from school or national service to the universities, polytechnics or arts colleges.
Part-time courses are generally tailored for working adults who are in a better position to pay their tuition fees as they have their own income. If they do not have enough savings for a part-time course, they can defer and build up enough personal savings to pay for their course fees later. Part-time students can therefore plan ahead with greater flexibility to ensure that they can meet the tuition fees.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Why are only subsidised courses by the approved educational institutions included under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: The CPF Education Loan Scheme is a loan scheme that allows CPF members to use their CPF savings to provide their children with a basic tertiary education. Courses subsidised by Ministry of Education (MOE) generally have lower tuition fees payable, which means lesser impact on retirement savings.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Why doesn't the CPF Education Loan Scheme cover overseas studies?
questions.text: Local education at approved educational institutions is subsidised by the government so students should be able to repay the CPF savings withdrawn in cash. On the other hand, overseas education is very costly and would affect the payer's retirement savings if the student is unable to repay the CPF savings withdrawn.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Why doesn't the CPF Education Loan Scheme cover postgraduate courses?
questions.text: The CPF Education Loan Scheme was introduced to help CPF members finance basic local tertiary education. Students who have graduated with basic tertiary qualifications have earning capabilities that enable them to build-up their personal savings for further studies. Autonomous universities also offer various financing schemes, such as the MOE Higher Education Student Loan, to help students pay their tuition fees. Students may also draw on the funds in their Post-Secondary Education Account for fee payment, provided the course is eligible.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How much do I have to repay under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
You have to repay the full amount of CPF savings used and the accrued interest which is computed from the time the savings were withdrawn, until the CPF education loan is fully repaid. The amount repaid will be credited to the CPF member(s)' Ordinary Account.
You may check your outstanding loan amount by logging in to your Education dashboard with your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Why must CPF savings withdrawn for education be repaid with interest?
questions.text: The primary objective of CPF savings is to help members save for their retirement needs. The amount withdrawn for education and the accrued interest must be repaid to the CPF member's Ordinary Account. This is so that the member would not lose out on the interest that he/she would have earned had the monies not been withdrawn for education purposes.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I check the outstanding loan amount repayable under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
If you are a CPF lender whose CPF savings have been withdrawn from your Ordinary Account (OA), you can log in to your Education dashboard with your Singpass and click on "Loans by your borrowers" to view the outstanding amount to be repaid to your OA.
Please note that the outstanding loan amount includes the accrued interest that would have been earned if the monies were not withdrawn for education. The borrower needs to repay the accrued interest to fully restore the savings in your OA.
If you are a borrower making repayments, you can check your outstanding loan amount by logging in to your Education dashboard with your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: When do I need to start repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
You are required to start repaying the CPF education loan one year after graduation or leaving your course of study, whichever is earlier.
We will send a notification to you generally about three months before the repayment start date, to inform you on the repayment.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Would I receive any notification to start repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: We will send a repayment notification to you to inform you to start repayment. It will state the outstanding CPF education loan amount, the date to start repayment and the monthly instalment rate. For your convenience, you are encouraged to repay via GIRO. Refer to this FAQ on how to apply for GIRO to authorise monthly deductions from your preferred bank account for your monthly repayment to the CPF lender's Ordinary Account.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I stop the use of CPF savings for my tuition fees and make a lump sum or full repayment for the education loan before I graduate?
questions.text:
The CPF lender (whose CPF savings is used) will need to submit an online application to revoke the use of his/her CPF savings via the "Revocation Form" using his/her Singpass, if he/she no longer wishes to use his/her CPF savings to pay your tuition fees for future semesters.
After the revocation application is approved, please inform us of your intention to make a lump sum or full repayment through Write to us.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What happens if I default in my education repayment and has arrears?
questions.text: You will receive monthly arrears notifications to inform you on your repayment in arrears. You may make payment for your arrears through "Manage education loan repayments" under "Forms and e-applications". If you are facing financial difficulties in repaying the arrears, you can write in to us to discuss on a suitable payment plan.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: If I use my own CPF savings under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, why must I repay the CPF savings withdrawn?
questions.text:
CPF savings are primarily meant for your retirement needs. Any withdrawal of CPF savings will cause your retirement savings to be reduced. Hence it is important that you repay the CPF savings withdrawn under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, including the accrued interest which would otherwise have been earned.
Repayment will be credited into your Ordinary Account.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Is repayment required under the CPF Education Loan Scheme if the CPF member passes away?
questions.text: Upon the death of the member, repayments of his CPF savings including the accrued interest under the CPF Education Loan Scheme shall cease.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Is repayment required under the CPF Education Loan Scheme if the student passes away or is permanently incapacitated?
questions.text:
In the event that the student passes away or has obtained a certification from an accredited doctor* certifying that he/she is physically or mentally incapacitated from continuing in any employment, we will not recover the outstanding amount owed by the student under the CPF Education Loan Scheme.
* The list of accredited doctors are those from government restructured hospitals, polyclinics or specialists. If clarifications are needed, a detailed medical report may be required from your doctor from the accredited list. If your doctor is not from the accredited list, you would be required to obtain an independent assessment from the Board's panel of doctors.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How will the repayment be credited if I have used more than one CPF member's savings to pay my tuition fees?
questions.text:
The amount repaid will be credited proportionately to each member based on the total outstanding loan amount of each account.
Please see example below:
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I check my education loan repayment history?
questions.text:
You can check the repayment history for your education loan in the following ways:
Refer to your bank account statement, or
Check with the CPF lender(s) who had used their CPF savings for your education. They will need to log in to the CPF website with their Singpass and retrieve their "Transaction History".
You can log in to your Education dashboard with your Singpass to check for arrears if you have missed repayments. If you have arrears, refer to this FAQ on how to make the payments.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What are education loan arrears? Are there any penalties for non-payment of monthly instalments?
questions.text: Education loan arrears refer to the amount of monthly loan repayments that have not been paid on time. Arrears will form part of the total outstanding loan, which includes the principal amount and accrued interest, that is repayable to the CPF lender’s Ordinary Account. There are no penalties charged for any missed payments.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Why do I still receive notifications from CPF Board regarding my education loan arrears even though I have made repayment via PayNow?
questions.text:
You will receive notifications if there are arrears on your education loan due to missed payments for past and current months. Notifications are sent in two situations:
If you are not on GIRO or your GIRO application is still being processed, any payments made will be used to offset your current month’s payment before offsetting arrears. If the payment is insufficient to cover the total outstanding arrears, you will receive a notification for payment of the outstanding arrears.
If you are on GIRO and there are insufficient funds in your bank account to repay your current month’s instalment, the notification will nudge you to pay for your current month’s instalment and arrears (if any).
All payments received will be used to offset the outstanding education loan and there are no penalties charged for any missed payments.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What is the monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: Your monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme will be stated in the repayment notification sent to you. Generally, the monthly instalment rate will enable you to fully repay your education loan within six years.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What is the minimum monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
The minimum monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme is $100. The instalment rate stated in the repayment notification will be $100 if this rate is expected to enable you to fully repay the loan within six years. You are encouraged to fully repay the loan within six years to reduce the interest incurred for the loan.
If you have a bigger outstanding loan amount, a higher monthly instalment rate will be stated, to enable you to repay within a period of six years.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I reduce the monthly instalment for my CPF Education Loan stated in my repayment notification?
questions.text:
Reducing the monthly instalment amount will mean a longer repayment period thus incurring more interest on the loan.
Under the Terms & Conditions of the CPF Education Loan Scheme, the loan must be fully repaid within 12 years, which starts one year after you graduate or leave the course of study. Any outstanding balance has to be paid in full before the end of the 12th year. Hence, if you repay at a lower monthly instalment, not only do you incur additional interest due to the prolonged repayment period, you may have to make a lump sum repayment of your outstanding loan at the end of the 12th year.
If you would like to reduce the monthly instalment (subject to a minimum repayment of $100), you may submit your application online through "Manage education loan repayments" under "Forms and e-applications" using your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I increase the monthly instalment for my Education Loan repayment?
questions.text:
You are encouraged to increase the monthly instalment for your education loan repayment if you are financially able to do so. This will enable you to fully repay the loan within a shorter period and hence minimise the interest you have to pay.
If you would like to increase the monthly instalment, you may submit your application online through "Manage education loan repayments" under "Forms and e-applications" using your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I change my monthly instalment for my education loan repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
Students (borrowers) may submit an application online to change the monthly instalment payable through "Manage education loan repayments" using their Singpass.
The minimum monthly instalment is $100. Students are encouraged to increase their monthly instalment as this will enable them to fully repay the education loan within a shorter period and hence minimise the accrued interest payable to the member.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Is there any tool available that can help me project the monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
You may use the online CPF education loan repayment calculator to estimate your monthly instalment rate payable.
You may also check your latest outstanding loan amount by logging in to your Education dashboard with your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Is there any tool available that can help me project the repayment period under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
You may use the online CPF education loan repayment calculator to estimate how long it would take to repay your education loan.
You may also check your latest outstanding loan amount by logging in to your Education dashboard with your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: When will the change in my monthly instalment rate be effective under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
The effective date for the new monthly instalment rate depends on how you make your payments.
1. Repayment by GIRO: If you pay through GIRO, you will need to submit a request to change the instalment rate before the 15th of the month for it to take effect in the current month. It usually takes one working day to process the request. For example, if the 15th of the month falls on a Sunday, please submit the request by the 12th of the month (Thursday) if you want the new rate to be effective for the current month. Otherwise, the change will only be effective in the following month.
2. Repayment using other payment modes: If you use other payment modes, please change the instalment rate before the end of the month. Generally, it will take one working day to process the request.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Where can I check the status of my request to change monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: You may check the status of your request to change the monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme at CPF website by logging in to "Activities" using your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I use another person's bank account to repay my CPF education loan?
questions.text: You may authorise the monthly deductions from your own or another person's bank account for the loan repayments under the CPF Education Loan Scheme. Please submit a GIRO application through "Forms and e-applications" with your Singpass. You will be re-directed to the bank’s ibanking portal to complete the application.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I use different bank accounts to repay my education loans for two different courses?
questions.text: Only one bank account may be maintained for repayments under the CPF Education Loan Scheme. If you submit a GIRO form for repayment using a new account, deductions for all the courses that you are repaying will be made from the new account. Please submit a GIRO application through "Forms and e-applications" with your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Would I receive any acknowledgement after submitting my GIRO application form for the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
Generally, you will receive an acknowledgement notification within two weeks upon receipt of your GIRO application form. The notification will indicate the start date of deduction and the monthly instalment rate.
Generally, GIRO applications will be processed within 4 working days for e-application and 21 working days for hardcopy application. Upon receipt of your bank's approval of your GIRO application, we will send a notification to inform you on the approval, together with the start date of the deduction and the monthly instalment rate.
In the meantime, please repay your education loan through "Manage education loan repayments" under "Forms and e-applications".
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Where can I check the status of my GIRO application for repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: Your Direct Debit Authorisation / GIRO application for your repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme will be sent to your bank and will generally be processed within 21 working days. We will notify you of the status and effective date of the Direct Debit / GIRO arrangement upon approval.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What is the deduction date if I'm repaying my education loan by GIRO?
questions.text: The GIRO deduction date for repayments under the scheme is on the 20th of every month. If 20th of the month falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday, the deduction will be made on the next working day.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I change the bank account for my repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: Students (borrowers) will need to submit a new GIRO application through "Set up GIRO for education loan repayments" using Singpass to change the bank account for their repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme. Students will be re-directed to the bank’s ibanking portal to complete the application. Deductions will continue to be made from the existing bank account until the new account has been verified by the receiving bank.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I terminate my GIRO arrangement for my education loan repayment?
questions.text: You may approach your respective bank directly to terminate the GIRO arrangement for your education loan repayment. Please note that all requests should be submitted and approved before the 15th of each month for the termination to take effect for the current month. Upon termination, all Standing Instruction(s) for repayments will cease. You will need to submit a new GIRO application through "Forms and e-applications" if you want to repay using GIRO in future.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to repay the monies withdrawn under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: CPF savings cannot be used for repayment of amounts withdrawn under the CPF Education Loan scheme.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Why CPF savings cannot be used to repay an outstanding education loan?
questions.text: CPF savings are primarily meant for a member's retirement needs. Allowing the use of CPF savings to repay an outstanding education loan would cause a premature drawdown of your own CPF savings.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I apply to defer the repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
You may submit an application online to defer your education loan repayment through "Manage education loan repayments" under "Forms and e-applications" using your Singpass.
You must read the Terms & Conditions and declare that you have obtained consent from the CPF lender(s) whose Ordinary Account savings were used, in the online form.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: If I choose not to waive the repayment, what will happen to the repayments made to my CPF Ordinary Account under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: Under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, the repayments will be credited to your CPF Ordinary Account and form part of your CPF savings which you can withdraw if you are eligible to do so under the current CPF withdrawal rules.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can the repayment of the CPF Education Loan and interest be waived, especially during economic downturns?
questions.text:
CPF is primarily for members' retirement needs. Hence, while you can take a loan from your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) for your own or immediate family's tertiary education, the principal amount withdrawn has to be repaid to your OA, with the interest that you would otherwise have earned had the monies been left in your OA. This restores your CPF savings so that your retirement security is not worse off compared to not having taken the education loan. Retirement security remains important, if not more so, during economic downturns.
A waiver of the repayment is only allowed if you have already met your retirement needs, i.e. you are 55 years old and above and have set aside the Full Retirement Sum in your Retirement Account.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I apply to waive the repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
You may submit an application online to waive the education loan repayment through "Manage education loan repayments" under "Forms and e-applications" using your Singpass.
For more information on the waiver of education loan repayment and the conditions to meet in order to waive the repayment, please refer to this FAQ.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme
