questions.title: Can I use my Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) savings to repay my outstanding education loan?
questions.text:
Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) holders can use their PSEA funds for full or partial lump sum repayment of their own education loan taken under the CPF Education Loan Scheme. Repayments will be credited to the members’ (lenders’) CPF Ordinary Accounts (OAs).
Students (borrowers) may log in to the Ministry of Education’s Student Finance System (SFS) using their Singpass to check their available PSEA balance and submit their application to use PSEA funds for repayment. Account holders will receive an email informing them of their application outcome 30 to 60 days after submitting the form.
For more information on the usage of PSEA, please refer to the PSEA website.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I use my sibling's Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) to repay my outstanding education loan?
questions.text: You can only use your own Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) savings to repay your education loan.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Is there a minimum amount for using Post-Secondary Education Account savings to repay my outstanding education loan?
questions.text: There is no minimum amount set for using Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) savings to repay loans taken under the CPF Education Loan Scheme.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I use my Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) savings to repay multiple education loans?
questions.text: To repay more than one loan under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, please indicate details of the loan (institution name) in the order of repayment priority in the Loan Repayment Application Form. Withdrawal of Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) savings for loan repayment will be made in the order specified in the application form.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I invest under the CPF Investment Scheme if I am bankrupt?
questions.text:
If you are an undischarged bankrupt, you will not be able to use your CPF savings for investment. If you had previously used your CPF savings to invest, you can continue to hold your investments but you will not be allowed to make new investments. However, if you had previously used your CPF savings to invest in a regular premium insurance policy prior to your bankruptcy, you may continue to use your CPF savings to pay for your regular insurance premium subject to the Board's terms and conditions.
When you subsequently liquidate your investments, the sales proceeds will be credited into your CPF Investment Account or Special Account. If your Special Account is closed, the proceeds will be credited to your Retirement Account up to Full Retirement Sum, and any excess balance will be credited to your Ordinary Account.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: As a bankrupt, can I use the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) investments that I have withdrawn to settle my judgement debts?
questions.text: Once your CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) investments and cash balance in your CPF Investment Account are withdrawn, they will no longer be protected from claims by your creditors and/or the Official Assignee. Please liaise with the Official Assignee on using your withdrawn CPFIS investments to settle your debts.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: Can I invest after I am discharged from bankruptcy?
questions.text: After your discharge from bankruptcy, you can continue to invest your CPF savings if you are at least 18 years old, subject to the investment thresholds and limits set by the Board.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: Can I continue to use my CPF savings for my existing private property housing loan if I am going to be made a bankrupt?
questions.text: Yes, if you own a private property and have earlier used your CPF savings to pay for the property before being declared bankrupt, you can continue to use your CPF to service your housing loan.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: As a bankrupt, can my CPF savings be used to pay for my children's tertiary education?
questions.text: You may use your CPF savings for your children's tertiary education under the CPF Education Loan scheme as long as you have the available withdrawal limit.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: As a bankrupt, can I use my CPF savings for my own tertiary education?
questions.text: You may continue to use your CPF savings for your own tertiary education if your application has been approved before your bankruptcy.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: What should I do if I have obtained a divorce court order overseas?
questions.text:
For foreign divorce court orders, please note that the court order will only have effect in Singapore if it is recognised in Singapore either through legislation in Singapore or by Singapore Courts (which would require an application to the Singapore Courts). The Board will not be bound by orders made by foreign courts.
You may seek the advice of a law firm in Singapore on the issue of the enforcement of a foreign Order of Court in Singapore. You can obtain a list of law firms from the Law Society of Singapore’s website.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Why does the CPF Board need me to provide identification documents of the parties stated in the court orders?
questions.text: As the Board identifies CPF members by their CPF account numbers, we would not be able to verify the parties’ identities based on the passport number or driving license number or any other identities which are not their CPF account numbers, that was indicated in the court order. As such, we would require documents that can allow us to link to the identification numbers of the parties stated in the court orders. Alternatively, the parties may amend the court orders to reflect the parties’ Singapore NRIC number.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Why do I get error messages when I submit my court order?
questions.text:
If you experience any error messages when you submit your court order, please check that your attachment meets the following conditions:
The attachment is in pdf format only.
Attachment size is 5MB or less.
No special characters in the name of the attachment.
If you still encounter issue in your submission, please try again later and if the issue persists, please send us a screenshot of the error message via Write to us.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: If I do not need to submit my court order, does my conveyancing lawyer need to submit any documents to CPF Board?
questions.text:
Yes, your conveyancing lawyer will need to submit the relevant applications at our Housing Business Partner Portal, even if full refunds are to be made to the outgoing owner’s CPF account based on your court order.
If you own an HDB flat, please confirm your eligibility with HDB before proceeding with the housing transaction.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: How long will CPF Board take to give effect to the court order?
questions.text:
Upon receipt of your court order, the Board will generally take two to three weeks to give effect to the court order. As court orders differ in complexity, the CPF Board will need to review the relevant orders and will keep the lawyers and parties informed on the progress of the matter.
We will upload the replies to you and your ex-spouse via your registered email address in our record or Mailbox for members. An SMS will be sent to the Mailbox recipient's mobile number in our record. For law firms and the Legal Aid Bureau, we will reply via their registered email address.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Is my ex-spouse entitled to have a share of my CPF savings upon our divorce?
questions.text: While CPF savings may be considered as matrimonial assets and a share may be given to your ex-spouse, there is nothing in the laws that give your ex-spouse an automatic entitlement. It is up to the Court to decide whether your ex-spouse is entitled to any part of your CPF savings, taking into account the matters set out in section 112 of the Women's Charter / section 52(3)(d) of the Administration of Muslim Law Act. For more information, please visit the Family Justice Courts’ website or Syariah Court’s website.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: How can I ensure that my court order for a transfer order or charging order meets CPF legislations?
questions.text:
Your court order must contain the following information:
Legal provision of your ex-spouse’s entitlement for the CPF savings
The CPF Account that the transfer of CPF savings will be made from
The amount of CPF savings to be transferred (the “Ordered Amount”). If the amount cannot be determined yet, the court order should state which party will be notifying the CPF Board of this information
Triggering event upon which the CPF Board should transfer the Ordered Amount
In the absence of the above information, the CPF Board may not be able to comply with the provisions of the court order.
It is important to note that the use of CPF assets must be for the purpose of a division of matrimonial assets, and not for settling maintenance or personal claims or debts.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: What are your obligations after the court order is granted, before and following the transfer or payment of CPF savings to your ex-spouse in a divorce?
questions.text:
You are obliged to comply with the court order and shall not withdraw or transfer or attempt to withdraw or transfer any amount that your ex-spouse is entitled to under the court order.
In the event of a transfer or payment of CPF savings upon the making of housing refunds pursuant to a disposal of the property, loans or grants taken by you which are repayable or refundable to the Government must be repaid or refunded first before the transfer or payment of CPF savings can take place. Grants include housing grants from the Housing and Development Board (HDB) and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).
Keep in mind that transferring or paying CPF savings to your ex-spouse might impact your participation in CPF schemes. If necessary, consider making alternative financial arrangements.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: What happens if my CPF savings are not enough to fulfil my ex-spouse's entitlement as required in the court order?
questions.text:
If your CPF savings are not enough to fulfil your ex-spouse’s entitlement as required in the court order, the Board can only effect the transfer or make the payment based on the available balances in your CPF account(s) as at date of transfer or payment.
You and your ex-spouse may wish to settle the shortfall amount privately or seek legal advice on the remedies available.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: As a member or an ex-spouse, what are my options if I am an undischarged bankrupt under division of CPF savings in a divorce?
questions.text:
The Court may still grant a transfer order or a charging order; similar to a member/ or an ex-spouse who is not an undischarged bankrupt.
If you are the ex-spouse, and payment is to be made to you under a charging order, please check with the Official Assignee whether you can receive the CPF savings.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Under a transfer order, do I need to set aside my retirement sum before my ex-spouse can receive their entitlement?
questions.text:
The transfer of CPF savings to your ex-spouse can take place without you setting aside your retirement sum* first. This gives your ex-spouse certainty over the amount they can receive and they can use them immediately for approved purposes such as housing, investment and education. Your ex-spouse may also withdraw the CPF savings when they are entitled to.
In the event of a transfer of CPF savings upon the making of housing refunds pursuant to a disposal of the property, the Board will first transfer the amount to your ex-spouse. Thereafter, the remaining refunds will be used to make up your retirement sum, up to your applicable Full Retirement Sum. Any balance housing refunds will remain in your Ordinary Account, and you can decide how to manage it.
*Only applies to members aged 55 and above.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Is there a limit on the CPF transfers that can be made to my ex-spouse's CPF Accounts under the division of CPF savings in a divorce?
questions.text:
There is no limit on the CPF transfers if so ordered by the Court. It is up to the Court to decide on the division of CPF savings and how much your ex-spouse's entitlement is.
Before the Court grants the court order, you should ensure that the Court is kept informed of any changes to the amount of CPF savings available for division or any planned utilisation of your CPF savings (e.g. deductions for housing payments) that would affect the division of the same.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Can I use the CPF savings immediately upon the receipt of the transferred monies from my ex-spouse?
questions.text: Yes, you can use the CPF savings for approved purposes such as housing, investment and education. You may also withdraw the CPF savings when you are entitled to do so.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Under a transfer order, can I request the monies to be paid to me in cash, instead of transferring to my CPF account?
questions.text: Under a transfer order, the monies can only be transferred from your ex-spouse’s CPF account to your designated CPF account. If you wish to receive the monies in cash, you may consider applying to the Courts for a charging order instead.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: What do I need to do to receive payment under a charging order?
questions.text:
You will first need to submit the court order for the division of CPF assets via the online service "Submit Court Order for Division of CPF Assets". We will write to you and your ex-spouse once we have reviewed the court order.
When your ex-spouse is entitled to withdraw their CPF savings, we will write to you to inform you of the withdrawal procedure.
Once we receive your withdrawal application and the necessary documents, we will process the application and the monies will be paid to you within 10 working days through Inter-Bank GIRO and 15 working days via Telegraphic Transfer.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: After the transfer or sale of the matrimonial property has been completed pursuant to the existing court order, I reached a different agreement with my ex-spouse on the division of CPF assets. Can we undo the transfer or sale?
questions.text:
The CPF Board has no power under the relevant legislation to reverse the transfer or sale of the property.
Please seek legal advice to amend the court order.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Can the courts order the sale (as opposed to a transfer (other than by way of sale)) of my share of the matrimonial property to my ex-spouse without any CPF refund?
questions.text: Upon the sale of your share of the matrimonial property to your ex-spouse, the required CPF refund must be made to your CPF account. The Court can then order the transfer or payment of the refunded CPF savings from your CPF account to your ex-spouse’s CPF account or to you in cash if it so decides.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Do I need to make any CPF refunds if I sell my share of the property to my ex-spouse?
questions.text:
Yes, the required CPF refunds must be made in full to your CPF account upon the sale of your share of the property to your ex-spouse.
If you intend to transfer your share of the property to your ex-spouse with no or partial CPF refunds to be made to your account, you have to obtain a court order for a transfer of property instead. Please note that the relevant requirements in Part 3A of the CPF Act will apply.
View how much you need to refund on the sale of your property. For information on transferring the property, please go to the next section on Transfer of Property.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Can I transfer my share in the property to my ex-spouse?
questions.text:
Yes, you can do so if the Courts decide to make such an order. The amount of CPF refunds, who is required to make those refunds and at what point in time the refunds need to be made will depend on whether the court order provides for full, partial or no CPF refunds to your CPF account upon transfer of your share in the property to your ex-spouse.
We set out the CPF refund details in the table below:
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to make the required CPF refunds to my ex-spouse upon the transfer of property?
questions.text:
Yes, you can use your Ordinary Account savings and cash to make the required CPF refund to your ex-spouse upon the transfer of the property.
Please note that for HDB flats, your CPF usage may be subject to the applicable housing withdrawal limits, which will be determined when we receive the detailed information regarding the transaction.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to pay for the cash consideration to my ex-spouse for the transfer of property?
questions.text: No, you cannot use your CPF savings for any cash consideration to your ex-spouse in a property transfer. You may, however, use your Ordinary Account savings to make the refunds to your ex-spouse’s CPF account upon the transfer of property.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: What should I do if the Court has instructed me to use the cash consideration provided by my ex-spouse to make the required CPF refund upon the transfer of property?
questions.text:
You should check if the cash consideration is sufficient to make the required refund to your CPF account upon the transfer of property. If the cash consideration is not enough to cover the required refund, you will need to make up the difference in cash, in a lump sum, upon the completion of the transfer of the property to your ex-spouse.
On the other hand, if the cash consideration is more than enough to cover the required refund, the Board will only collect the required refund amount to your CPF account. For example, the Court has instructed your ex-spouse to pay you a cash consideration of $60,000 and you are to use this sum to make your required CPF refund amount. As at the date of transfer, your required refund is $25,000. In this case, the Board will only accept $25,000 to your CPF account.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: What are the ex-spouse's (remaining party) obligations following the transfer of the property under matrimonial proceedings?
questions.text:
If the Court so orders, the ex-spouse (remaining party) has to refund a sum (amount as decided by the Court) to the member’s (outgoing party) CPF Account(s) upon transfer.
The Court may also order the transfer of property with no refunds to the member’s CPF Account. If that is the case, upon the subsequent sale/transfer or otherwise disposal of the property, the ex-spouse would be required to refund to their own CPF Account(s), the CPF monies withdrawn (including the accrued interest) by them and the member for the purchase of the property, and any amount for which the property has been pledged to set aside their and the member’s retirement sums.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Can the cash balance in my Investment Account be transferred under the division of CPF savings in a divorce?
questions.text: Cash balances in your Investment Account can be transferred but you have to initiate the transfer of cash balance from your Investment Account to your Ordinary Account first before CPF Board can transfer the balance to your ex-spouse's Ordinary Account.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: How can I submit an application to transfer CPF Investment Scheme investments sale proceeds in a divorce?
questions.text:
You will need to submit the following:
The court order; and
An application to transfer your CPF Investment Scheme investment sale proceeds here.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: What are the criteria to be fulfilled by my ex-spouse before my investments can be transferred to them under the division of CPF savings in a divorce? What are the options if my ex-spouse cannot fulfill the criteria?
questions.text: Before your investments can be transferred to your ex-spouse, they must be a CPF member who is Singaporean or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) and 18 years old and above. If your ex-spouse is below 18 years old, they can consider requesting the Court to order your investments to be liquidated and the sale proceeds to be transferred to their CPF accounts.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: How does CPF Board protect and use my personal information? Is CPF Board bound by Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA)?
questions.text:
There are strict policies, processes, and safeguards to ensure the proper use and protection of personal data within CPF Board. While the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) does not apply to government agencies, Government's data protection standards are aligned with, if not more stringent than, the requirements of the PDPA. CPF Board also requires the same high standards in third parties’ handling of CPF data to prevent inadvertent disclosure of CPF member’s details.
CPF Board is committed in ensuring that CPF members’ data are protected, while using the data to continuously understand members’ needs to refine and develop better policies and services.
You may refer to our privacy statement for more details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: Isn't it against the law for CPF Board to reveal a member's personal details publicly?
questions.text:
Members’ data are safe with the Board and there are high standards in place to prevent its unintended disclosure.
Where it is in the public interest, the law allows the CPF Board to release a member’s personal details. For example, where misleading information is put out and widely disseminated, we must be able to provide the public with relevant facts. This approach applies to all public agencies. It helps the public gain a fuller picture of the case and counter the misinformation, both of which are necessary to maintain the trust placed in public agencies.
CPF Board is committed in ensuring your data is protected. You may refer to our privacy statement for more details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: What is the mission and vision of CPF Board?
questions.text:
The CPF Board's mission is:
"To enable Singaporeans to have a secure retirement, through lifelong income, healthcare financing and home financing."
Our vision:
"A trusted and respected social security organisation, committed to enable Singaporeans to have a secure retirement."

questions.title: What does the CPF logo represent?

The circle emphasises the completeness of the CPF system as a national social security savings scheme.
The shield represents security and protection for our members in their retirement.
The three keys represent the unity of the tripartite relationship among Employees, Employers and the Government.
Lastly, the use of the colour green in our logo highlights the need for CPF's constant growth and dynamism.

questions.title: What is Central Provident Fund (CPF)?
questions.text:
The Central Provident Fund (CPF) is a comprehensive social security system that enables working Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents to set aside funds for retirement. It also addresses healthcare, home ownership, family protection and asset enhancement.
Working Singaporeans and their employers make monthly contributions to the CPF and these contributions go into three accounts:
Ordinary Account - the savings can be used to buy a home, pay for CPF insurance, investment and education.
Special Account - for old age and investment in retirement-related financial products.
MediSave Account - the savings can be used for hospitalisation expenses and approved medical insurance.
Please refer to the CPF website for an overview of CPF.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: What is available at CPF Self-Help Lobby?

questions.text: Service Centre appointment bookings are opened 2 weeks in advance.

questions.title: Why does CPF Board refer my case to another organisation?
questions.text:
CPF Board is committed to providing the best possible assistance to those in need. To make sure you get the right kind of support, we’ll look at your situation and assess whether there are other organisation(s) with more appropriate assistance tailored to your needs. If the situation warrants, we will refer your case to our partner organisation(s) that have the right assistance programme(s) and expertise to better assist you. Please inform us explicitly if you do not want us to refer your case to our partner organisation(s).
CPF Board is committed in ensuring your data is protected. You may refer to our privacy statement for more details.

questions.title: What are CPF Online Applications for Employers?

For employer or self-employed matters, assistance is available through our digital services, hotline, Write to us or phone appointment. In-person appointments are not available for these matters.

questions.text:

If you have received your Singpass for the new account, you can continue using that Singpass.

questions.text:

questions.title: Why is the Board still sending links in SMS messages?
questions.text:
Website links remain a legitimate means for the Board to point citizens to useful services and information. To ensure that a link genuinely leads to the CPF website or another Government website, you should always check that the domain ends with “.gov.sg”.
We will not ask users to provide their credentials, such as passwords, through websites directly accessed through SMS links.
Find out how else to protect yourself from falling prey to phishing scams.

questions.title: What is E-Xperience workshop?
questions.text:
CPFB’s E-Xperience Workshop is a 30-min session conducted in a group setting where our officers/CPF volunteers will guide you on how to use your own mobile device to transact digitally with us. Please bring along your smartphone to the E-Xperience Workshop.
We will guide you on how to:
Set up and use Singpass mobile app
Set up and use CPF mobile app
View and download your CPF statements
Top-up your CPF accounts
Submit CPF withdrawal applications
Protect against scams
Book an E-Xperience Workshop slot

questions.title: I am a foreigner. I can't seem to be able to login to CPF digital services using my Singpass, why is it so?
questions.text:
With the discontinuation of the OneKey Token from 1 April 2021, foreign CPF members will no longer be able to access CPF digital services using the Singpass which was registered under their CPF issued account numbers (e.g. SA987654C or TC123456A) previously.
Foreign CPF members with CPF issued accounts and are currently holding FIN may apply for a new Singpass under the FIN to access CPF digital services for their CPF SA/SB/TC account. You may refer to the Singpass website at singpass.gov.sg for the steps to apply.
CPF members who do not meet the above criteria may Write to Us for assistance.

questions.title: What is "my cpf digital services"?
questions.text: my cpf digital services is a series of personalised online services available to help you manage your CPF savings better. questions.text: You are unable to amend/cancel any online request that has been submitted. If you wish to make any changes, please contact us.

questions.title: What is "Activities"?
questions.text:
"Activities" informs you of the latest status of all your online transactions with the Board. At one glance, you will be able to tell whether your application is received, being processed, rejected or approved.

questions.title: How can I view my online forms I have submitted and their status?
questions.text: Once you have made your selection, confirm your submission. An acknowledgement page will be displayed to confirm your submissions. You can check the status of your online submission through Activities.

questions.title: How can I save the information in Activities?

questions.title: What is responsive web design or mobile responsive website?
questions.text: Mobile responsive pages will automatically fit mobile screens, without having to pinch or zoom in/out to see contents clearly.

questions.title: Why is there a need to provide mobile number/email address to CPF Board?
questions.text:

questions.title: What is "Mailbox" and how do I access it?

questions.title: What should I do if I can no longer locate an old digital service or if service has been discontinued?
questions.text:

If you need help with the service, please write to us.

questions.title: How can I update my subscription preferences for my CPF notifications?
questions.text:
You can update your subscription preferences via the Account settings page with your Singpass. Once you have logged in with Singpass, click on the “Subscription” tab. You can choose to receive notifications on CPF educational content and events, as well as alerts on your CPF contributions, by clicking on the respective check boxes.
You can unsubscribe from such notifications anytime. Even if you unsubscribe from receiving educational content, please rest assured that you will still receive key notifications on CPF transactions and policies through your registered contact details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What is CPF Mobile?
questions.text: CPF Mobile provides you with easy access to your personal CPF information on the go and quick access to your CPF statement and services to manage your CPF. You can also receive push notification alerts and updates regarding your personal CPF matters, educational articles, CPF tips and events even when you are on the move. For more information, please see CPF Mobile services. It is available in both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: How can I download CPF Mobile?
questions.text: You can download CPF Mobile directly to your mobile phone from either the Apple App Store or the Google Play Store. Please ensure that the developer of the application is Central Provident Fund Board.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why doesn't CPF Mobile offer all the services found on CPF website?
questions.text: CPF Mobile and CPF website complement each other to serve different needs of our customers as we deliver a multi-channel digital experience. CPF Mobile provides easy access to popular services such as viewing account balances to allow one to access CPF information on the go, while the website allows customers to access the full suite of CPF digital services.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Do I have to pay to use CPF Mobile?
questions.text:
CPF Mobile is a free service provided by CPF Board. However, you would need to bear any data charges that might be charged by your service provider. Please check with your mobile service provider for details of the charges.
M1: 1627
SingTel: 1626
StarHub: 1633
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What is the minimum requirement to access CPF Mobile on my mobile device?
questions.text:
CPF Mobile is compatible with Apple iOS 15.1, Android 11 and above. Keeping your Operating System (OS) updated is crucial to maintain the security of your mobile device and ensure compatibility with our mobile app. Furthermore, up-to-date OS improves performance and offers a better user experience.
You can update your OS via the following steps:
For iPhone users: Go to Settings > General > Tap on “Software Updates”
For Android users: Go to Settings > System > Tap on “Software Update”
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What is OCBC Digital?
questions.text: OCBC Digital is a payment mobile app to allow OCBC customers to transfer funds and receive funds, as well as make payment to organisations. For more information, do visit OCBC Digital.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What are the CPF payment services available for PayNow QR and OCBC Digital?
questions.text: PayNow QR and OCBC Digital payment options are available for all payment services in CPF Mobile. You may use PayNow QR or OCBC Digital to top up Special Account/Retirement Account (SA/RA Top-Up) or refund funds used for your housing (Housing Refund).
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Where can I find the PayNow QR and OCBC Digital option?
questions.text: You will be able to select the PayNow QR or OCBC Digital option under the ‘Payment Mode’ page in CPF Mobile after confirming the transaction details. Please note that the OCBC Digital payment option will only be available if you have installed the OCBC Digital mobile app.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What is the payment limit for PayNow QR and OCBC Digital?
questions.text: The daily payment limit for PayNow QR and OCBC Digital is currently up to $200,000. Please ensure you have updated your banking transaction limits with your respective banks.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why can't I find the OCBC Digital option in CPF Mobile?
questions.text: The OCBC Digital option is only available if you have installed the OCBC Digital app on your mobile devices. You will be able to select the OCBC Digital option under the 'Payment Mode' page in CPF Mobile after confirming the transaction details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What is the difference between General and Personalised Notifications?
questions.text:
General Notifications are notifications that contain non-sensitive information such as alerts on educational articles, CPF tips and events.
Personalised Notifications are notifications that contain personal information such as alerts on CPF contributions.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: How do I enable/disable push notifications on my mobile device?
questions.text:
For General Notifications, go to your device settings to turn on notifications.
For Personalised Notifications, tap on the ‘side menu’ icon located on the top left corner of the app and select ‘Settings’. Toggle the switch to enable personalised Push Notifications.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Can I enable personalised push notifications on multiple mobile devices?
questions.text: No, you can only enable personalised push notifications on one mobile device at any time. If you had already enabled personalised push notifications on one device, enabling it on another device will disable the personalised notifications on your older device.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: How long will the message stay in the notification list?
questions.text: The content will be available for 15 months from the notification date and will be removed automatically thereafter.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: How do I delete the messages in the notification list?
questions.text: You can delete the message by tapping on the ‘Bin’ icon in the notification detail page.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: How do I read the full content of push notifications?
questions.text:
You can view the full content of the push notification via three ways:
Tap on the banner and it will bring you to view the full content of the notification.
Before logging into the app, tap on the ‘bell’ icon located at the top left corner.
After logging into the app, tap on the ‘bell’ icon located at the top left corner of the side menu.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Do I need to log in to access personalised notifications on CPF Mobile?
questions.text: Yes, Singpass login is required to view your personalised notifications.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Can I still view my past notifications if I change to a new mobile device?
questions.text: Yes, you will have access to your past personalised notifications after you have successfully enabled notifications on your new mobile device. Notifications sent in the past 15 months will be available.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: I lost my mobile device. How can I disable personalised notifications?
questions.text: In the event that you lose your mobile device, you can enable personalised notifications on your new mobile device. By doing so, there will be no personalised notifications sent to your missing mobile device.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: How do I disable personalised notifications before I sell my mobile device?
questions.text: You can disable personalised notifications at the app settings page. It is recommended that you uninstall CPF Mobile before selling your mobile device.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why is CPF Board rolling out Chinese language in CPF Mobile?
questions.text: We are introducing Chinese language in CPF Mobile as a pilot to gauge customers’ usage and interest in vernacular features.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why is some content in CPF Mobile still in English when my device language is set to Chinese?
questions.text: CPF Mobile has recently extended Chinese language to more services on the app. We are progressively extending this to more services.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why am I receiving push notifications on my mobile device when I did not enable them on CPF Mobile?
questions.text: For early detection of unauthorised changes to contact details, push notifications are enabled on CPF Mobile automatically. You can change your setting at the app settings page of your mobile device.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: I was previously able to use OCBC Pay Anyone app for payment. Can I continue to do so?
questions.text: Payment via OCBC Pay Anyone app will no longer be available on CPF Mobile from 22 Aug 2023. You can continue to make payment via OCBC Digital app. To do so, you need to download the OCBC Digital app on the Apple App Store or Google Play Store. Thereafter, you will be able to select the OCBC Digital option under the ‘Payment Mode’ page in CPF Mobile after confirming the transaction details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Do CPF Mobile's security features scan my device or collect my personal information?
questions.text: We take your privacy seriously. CPF Mobile's security features are limited to the detection of malware activity and no additional personal data from your device is collected. We seek your understanding that these features are necessary to protect CPF members from malware or suspected malicious apps. You can read up more on how to avoid falling prey to malware scams.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Can I make more than one payment using the same QR code?
questions.text: No, the QR code generated is unique to your submitted application. Should you require to make another payment, please submit another application. A new QR code with the required payment details will be generated for you to make another payment.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What if I made more than one payment using the same QR code?
questions.text: You should only use the generated QR code for one payment as the QR code generated is unique. If there is more than one payment, the subsequent payment will be refunded to you.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: How can I benefit from electronic payments?
questions.text:
You can benefit in the following ways with electronic payment modes:
Easy and convenient
Faster processing time
Secure and seamless transaction
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why is payment via eNETS discontinued with effect from 23 April 2023?
questions.text: CPF Board regularly reviews the services and payment options we provide to our customers. Payment via eNETS had been discontinued from 23 April 2023 because payments made by customers via eNETS are unable to be updated in the members’ accounts instantaneously. Customers can use PayNow QR or OCBC Digital via our digital services on CPF Mobile to make payment and these transactions will be processed instantaneously.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: How do I clear my browser's cache?
questions.text: You can clear your browser's cache after each session by following the steps on this page for major browsers.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why do I encounter a Security Warning Message when I login to my cpf Online Services or other online application?
questions.text:
The transaction you're performing makes use of a Secure Socket Layer (SSL) digital security certificate. This allows you to conduct safe e-transactions with 256-bit encrypted SSL connections.
Essentially, this digital certificate is an electronic document which your browser uses to authenticate our server and initiate the encryption processes. The certificate is like a stamp of approval that also carries the information needed to activate the SSL process.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What should I do when I see the Security Warning Message?
questions.text:
You can click "Yes" to proceed with your intended transaction. However, the message will appear when you login the next time. For a long-term solution, please do the following:
Click on the 'View Certificate' button.
Click on the 'Install Certificate' button.
Click on the 'Next' and 'Finish' buttons as required to accept and install the certificate.
Click "Yes" when you see 'Do you want to ADD the following certificate to the Root Store?'
Click 'Ok' as required.
Click 'Yes' to the Security Alert warning which may still be being displayed.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What should I do if I think the information in my CPF statement is incorrect?
questions.text: Please notify us immediately via Write to Us if you think that the information is incorrect. Please note that it is your responsibility to carefully review your CPF statements.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: I would like a hardcopy of my CPF Yearly Statement of Account (YSOA). Where can I get it?
questions.text:
As part of our efforts to go green, CPF Board has transformed the Yearly Statement of Account (YSOA) into a digital statement. We strongly encourage you to view your YSOA online to enjoy a richer and more interactive user experience.
You may log in to my cpf digital services to view, download and save/print your YSOA for the past 10 years by clicking the "PDF icon". To find your downloaded documents on mobile devices, refer to this FAQ.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: What is the total employment contribution I received for the year?
questions.text:
You can sum up the “Employee Contribution” under the “You” category and “Employer Contribution” under “Employer” category to derive the total employment contributions for the year.
For more details on the rates, see rates for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: How do I derive the interest indicated in my Yearly Statement of Account?
questions.text: Please refer to the CPF interest page for more information on CPF interest. Details on extra interest and how CPF interest rates are determined can be found in our FAQs.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: How do I save or download a copy of my Digital Yearly Statement of Account?
questions.text: On the Digital Yearly Statement of Account (YSOA) page, click on “PDF icon” to view, download and save a copy of your YSOA. To find your downloaded documents on mobile devices, refer to this FAQ.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: How do I stop receiving my hardcopy Yearly Statement of Account?
questions.text: As part of our efforts to go green, we have transformed the Yearly Statement of Account (YSOA) into a digital statement. If you wish to go green and stop receiving a hardcopy YSOA, please submit a request to us. Singpass login is required.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: If I am granted sole custody of my child following a divorce, can I request to remove my ex-spouse's access to our child's CPF statement?
questions.text: Yes, you can write to us using your Singpass and attach the Court Order as a supporting document.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: What is Singpass?
questions.text: Singpass stands for Singapore Personal Access and it is your common password to transact with the Government online. Please visit Singpass website for more information on Singpass.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on other government agencies

questions.title: How do I get a Singpass?
questions.text:
To obtain a Singpass, you can either:
visit Singpass website to apply for your Singpass online or
visit any of the Singpass counters located islandwide in-person.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on other government agencies

questions.title: Where can I find advice on tax issues?
questions.text: For tax issues, such as queries on IR8A form, please visit IRAS's website.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on other government agencies

questions.title: How do I know if I need to submit my Income Tax Return?
questions.text: You may wish to visit IRAS website for more details. Alternatively, you may wish to contact IRAS at 1800 356 8300 for further assistance.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on other government agencies

questions.title: How to make use of Edusave funds?
questions.text: For Edusave issues, please visit Ministry of Education's website.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on other government agencies

questions.title: I have issues with my Singpass. What should I do?
questions.text:
Singpass is an authentication service governed by GovTech. CPF Board is one of the government agencies using Singpass and its two-factor authentication (2FA) service.
If you have any Singpass issues (e.g. unable to login via Singpass, forgot Singpass password, unable to receive SMS OTP), please contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on other government agencies

questions.title: Why is Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) allowed to recover unpaid taxes/ MediShield Life premiums when I withdraw my CPF savings?
questions.text:
Taxes go towards funding of government expenditure; and to support the government's economic and social programme to ensure quality growth and an inclusive society. Most taxpayers pay their taxes on time. To encourage voluntary compliance where every taxpayer contributes their fair share of tax, there are penalties if taxes are not paid on time. Actions to recover the unpaid taxes may include appointment of agents such as CPF Board.
Under the law, IRAS is empowered to appoint CPF Board as an agent for the recovery of unpaid taxes/MediShield Life premiums. IRAS would have informed you that CPF Board has been appointed as agent to recover the unpaid taxes/MediShield Life premiums when you withdraw your CPF savings.
You may approach IRAS at 6356 7012 to discuss alternative arrangements to settle your unpaid taxes/MediShield Life premiums before submitting your withdrawal application.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on other government agencies

questions.title: What is Supplementary Retirement Scheme?
questions.text:
The Supplementary Retirement Scheme (SRS) is part of the Government's multi-pronged strategy to address the financial needs of a greying population. It is a voluntary scheme that complements the CPF. Participants can contribute a varying amount to SRS (subject to a cap) at their own discretion. The contributions may be used to purchase various investment instruments. The SRS offers attractive tax benefits. Contributions to SRS are eligible for tax relief, investment returns are accumulated tax-free (with the exception of Singapore dividends), and only 50% of the withdrawals from SRS are taxable at retirement.
You may wish to find out more information on SRS.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on other government agencies

questions.title: How can I provide feedback on the event?
questions.text: You may scan the survey QR code at the end of the session to share your feedback or suggestions with us.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Event

questions.title: When is the event registration deadline?
questions.text: Event registration will close one day before the event date or when the event is fully subscribed, whichever comes first. You are strongly encouraged to register early to secure your seat.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Event

questions.title: What do I need to bring to the physical event?
questions.text: You will receive an email confirmation upon successful registration of the event. Please present the email confirmation to the event personnel in order to enter the event premises. If you are unable to find your email confirmation, please provide your name so that our event personnel can assist to verify your registration status.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Event

questions.title: How do I check or register for an event?
questions.text: You may visit the CPF Events page to view and register for CPF events.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Event

questions.title: What is the definition of an employee?
questions.text:
Under the CPF Act, an employee is defined as:
A person who is employed in Singapore under a contract of service; or
A Singapore Citizen who is employed under a contract of service or other agreement entered into in Singapore as a master, seaman or apprentice in any vessel.
Find out more information on the different types of employees.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for part-time, casual or temporary employees?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable for part-time, casual or temporary employees who are:
Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents,
Engaged under a contract of service, and
Earning total wages of more than $50 per month.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: What is a contract of service?
questions.text:
A contract of service is an agreement in which one person agrees to employ another as an employee, and the other person agrees to serve the employer as an employee. The agreement can be in writing, verbal, expressed or implied.
Please refer to the Ministry of Manpower website for more information on a contract of service.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: If my foreign employees request to contribute to CPF, can I make CPF contributions for them?
questions.text:
CPF is a comprehensive social security system that is intended to support Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents (SPRs). From 1 January 2003, CPF contributions are exempted for foreign employees as they may not retire here in Singapore. Therefore, CPF contributions are only payable for Singapore Citizens and SPRs.
For foreigners who wish to save voluntarily for their own retirement, they may instead consider the Supplementary Retirement Scheme (SRS).
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: What is the minimum age for your employees to qualify for CPF contributions?
questions.text: Your employees are required to pay CPF contributions as long as they are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents, and are employed in Singapore under a contract of service.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for church workers?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable for church workers who are employed under a contract of service.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for consultants?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable for consultants who are employed under a contract of service.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for directors?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are not payable on directors' fees voted to them at General Meetings.
However, if the directors of the company are also engaged under a contract of service, CPF contributions are payable on the wages received.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for full-time National Servicemen (NSFs)?
questions.text: CPF contributions are not payable for full-time National Servicemen (NSFs) enlisted for national service under the Enlistment Act as they are not employed under a contract of service.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for my hawker assistant?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable for your hawker assistant who is employed under a contract of service.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for law pupils?
questions.text:
Based on the law practice training guidelines of the Singapore Institute of Legal Education (SILE), the factors in a Practice Training Contract do not point towards a contract of service. Generally, CPF contributions are not payable for law pupils, i.e. law graduates who are serving their practice service period.
However, if the law graduates enter into a contract of employment with the law firm, CPF contributions are payable on wages given to them.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for Limited Liability Partners (LLP)?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable for partners of Limited Liability Partners (LLP) who are employed under a contract of service.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for locum doctors?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable for locum doctors employed under a contract of service.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for partner or sole proprietor of a firm?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable for partner who is employed under a contract of service with your firm. Otherwise, he is considered as a self-employed person (SEP) and cannot receive CPF contributions from the firm as an employee.
Sole proprietor of a firm is considered as an SEP. As such, a sole proprietor cannot receive CPF contributions from the firm as an employee.
Do note that an SEP earning an annual Net Trade Income (NTI) of more than $6,000 needs to pay compulsory MediSave contribution. NTI is your gross trade income minus all allowable business expenses, capital allowances and trade losses as determined by IRAS. Please visit the IRAS website to read more on the definition of an SEP.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for students?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable for students who are employed under a contract of service and are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents earning total wages of more than $50 per month.
CPF contributions are exempted on wages (e.g. allowances, bonus, overtime pay) payable to certain classes of student employees. Find out more about who you need to pay CPF contributions for (PDF, 0.2MB) under the header “Students”.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for Shatec students engaged in trainings approved by Shatec Institutes?
questions.text: With effect from 1 March 2018, CPF contributions are payable for Shatec students employed under a contract of service.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for volunteers?
questions.text: CPF contributions are not payable if the volunteers are not employed under a contract of service.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for my employee who is on no pay leave?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on the total wages earned by your employee in each calendar month, less any no pay leave he has taken in that month.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for my employee who went on absence without leave (AWOL)?
questions.text:
CPF contribution are not payable if your employee is not entitled to any wages during the period he was absent without leave (AWOL).
CPF contributions are payable on the total wages given to him in that calendar month if he had worked certain days before AWOL.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for my employee during his overseas training?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable during overseas training if your employee is employed in Singapore but is required to go overseas for the training period.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for my employee who is seconded or transferred from overseas to work in Singapore?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable for your employee who is a citizen or permanent resident of Singapore if he is working in Singapore and earning total wages of more than $50 a month.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for my employee who is employed to work overseas?
questions.text: CPF contributions are not payable on wages given to your employee who is employed to work overseas.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for my employee who is seconded or posted to work overseas?
questions.text: CPF contributions are not payable for your employee who is seconded or posted to work overseas as wages given in respect of overseas employment do not attract CPF contributions.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for my employee, who is under overseas employment, if he returns to Singapore for personal reasons and works during the Stay Home Notice (SHN) period?
questions.text: If your employee is returning to Singapore for personal reasons, e.g. to celebrate festive holidays with his family, and will be working remotely in Singapore for you during the Stay Home Notice (SHN) period, CPF contributions are not payable for him since working during the SHN period is a temporary work arrangement due to COVID-19 restrictions.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable by the holding company or the subsidiary company if my employee is seconded from the holding company to the subsidiary company?
questions.text: The employer who had entered into an employment contract with the employee is required to pay the CPF contributions.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on Annual Wage Supplement (AWS)?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on Annual Wage Supplement (AWS) given to your employee.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on bonus?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on bonus given to your employee, e.g. retention Bonus, 13th month bonus, sign-on bonus, discretionary bonus.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: What is the definition of wages?
questions.text: Under the CPF Act, wages are defined as remuneration in money, including any bonus that is due or granted to a person in respect of his employment. CPF contributions are computed based on an employee’s wages.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on mobile phone subscription allowance or reimbursement?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable on mobile phone subscription allowance.
CPF contributions are not payable on mobile phone subscription reimbursement if your employee incurred the expenses solely for official purposes. Otherwise, CPF contributions are still payable.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on housing/rental subsidy?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on housing or rental subsidy given to your employee.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on payments given to my employee for meeting the Key Performance Indicators (KPI)?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on payments given to your employee for meeting the Key Performance Indicators.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on meal allowance or reimbursement?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable on meal allowance given to your employee.
CPF contributions are not payable on meal reimbursement given to your employee for working beyond normal working hours, e.g. overtime and on non-working days. Otherwise, CPF contributions are still payable.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on probation period pay?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on probation period pay.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on tips?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on tips that you have collected and distributed to your employees.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on bonus given to my employee by a third party e.g. my service partner?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable on bonus given to your employee by a third party, e.g. your service partner, if the bonus is a reward for work done in respect of your employee’s employment.
Example
Company A is a marketing company partnering various banks to help increase its sales for personal loans and credit cards. Upon achieving specific monthly targets, the banks will give bonuses to the employees of Company A as a reward. Company A receives these bonuses from the banks and disburses to its employees.
Company A is required to pay CPF contributions on the bonuses given to its employees as the cash payments are wages given in respect of their employment.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on benefit in kind?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are not payable on benefit given to your employee in kind, e.g. a commemorative watch or payment made directly by you to a service provider.
Such benefit in kind where no cash payment to your employee is involved would not be considered as wages because only remuneration in money granted in respect of employment attracts CPF contributions.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on monetary donations given to my employee for bereavement?
questions.text: CPF contributions are not payable on monetary donations given to your employee for bereavement.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on reimbursements?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are not payable on reimbursements incurred for official purposes. The reimbursement amount must not exceed the expenditure incurred.
Some examples are:
Transport expenses incurred by your employees to travel to a client's office for a business meeting
Meal expenses incurred by your employees for working overtime
Laundry expenses for your uniformed employees.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on monetary wedding gift given to my employee?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on monetary wedding gift given to your employee.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on insurance payout given to my employee?
questions.text: CPF contributions are not payable on insurance payout made by insurer to your employee if he is the insured person and the payout is for his benefit.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on winter wear and luggage allowances given to my employee?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable on winter wear and luggage allowances given to your employee.
However, CPF contributions are not payable on reimbursements given to your employee for expenses incurred on winter wear and luggage for official overseas trips. The reimbursement amount must not exceed the expenditure incurred.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable by the holding company or the subsidiary company if the employee is seconded from the former to latter?
questions.text: The employer who had entered into an employment contract with the employee is required to pay the CPF contributions.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on payouts from retirement savings held by a trust fund to my employee who is still in employment?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on the payouts from funds set aside for pensions or retirement given to your employee who is still in employment with you.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on cash benefits given to my employee when he leaves his employment?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable on any cash benefits given in respect of your employee’s employment as they constitute wages. As long as wages are payable to your employee who is a Singapore Citizen/Singapore Permanent Resident, even if they are payable only after your employee has left employment, CPF contributions are required. Examples are bonuses, end of contract incentives, completion of contract bonuses.
Find out more if CPF contributions are payable on Additional Wages payable to ex-employees after they have left their employer’s employment.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on cash payment given to your employee for self-improvement courses?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on cash payment given to your employee for self-improvement courses.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on cash rewards given to my employees who report on safety lapses and incidents in the workplace?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on cash rewards given to your employees who report on safety lapses and incidents in the workplace if the employees are required to do so as part of the job scope. Otherwise, CPF contributions are not payable.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on encashment of leave?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on cash payment given to your employee for encashment of his leave.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on Monthly Variable Component (MVC)?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on the monthly variable component given to your employee.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on reimbursement of examination fee incurred by my employee?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable on reimbursement of examination fees given to your employee if the examination is taken for his self-interest or personal development.
CPF contributions are not payable if the examination fees are incurred by your employee for official purposes, e.g. for employment-related training or certification. The reimbursement must not exceed the actual expenditure.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on cash payments given to my employee if they are not paid through the payroll system?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable on wages given to your employee and not payable on non-wages, e.g. reimbursements incurred for official purposes.
The CPF treatment is the same regardless whether they are paid through the payroll system.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on allowances?
questions.text: Allowances, i.e. monetary payments that increase your employee's wages, are also wages. Hence, they will attract CPF contributions. Some examples include meal and transport allowance, etc. Please refer to Types Of Payments That Attract CPF Contributions (PDF 0.2MB) for more information.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on profit sharing?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on profit sharing given to your employees.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on redundancy payment?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable on redundancy payment given to your employee who is still under your employment but not required to report to work temporarily.
CPF contributions are not payable on termination benefits given for retrenchment or loss of employment.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on wages given to my employee who has passed away?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on the wages payable to your employee who has passed away.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on ang bao/red packet?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on the cash payment given to employee in the form of ang bao/red packet.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on Restrictive Covenant payment?
questions.text: CPF contributions are not payable on Restrictive Covenant payment given to your employee to comply with specific contractual obligations after he has left your employment, e.g. to restrain him from entering into an employment with another company in the same industry or to join your competitors after he left your employment.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on cash payments given to my employee for his personal car-related expenses?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable on cash payments given for your employee’s personal car-related expenses, e.g. car loan interest, car parking fee, Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) fee, petrol, road tax, insurance, repair, servicing fee.
However, CPF contributions are not payable on reimbursement of expenses incurred by your employee for official purpose, e.g. the company’s car is used for work-related travel and you reimburse your employee the petrol expenses. The reimbursement amount must not exceed the expenditure incurred.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on encashment of flexible benefits?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on the cash payments given to your employee from unused flexible benefits.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on cash prizes given in contests?
questions.text: CPF contributions are not payable on cash prizes given to participants in contests where the cash payments are not given in respect of employment, e.g. Dinner and Dance, lucky draws, early bird draws.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on personal car loan?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are not payable on personal car loan given to your employee if it is not tied to his employment.
CPF contributions are payable if you agree that your employee need not pay back the loan or for the loan to be written off, e.g. given as a cash gift to your employee or you imposed conditions that are tied to employment (such as your employee must clinch a deal with a client or he has to work overtime for the next few months). In such cases, the cash payment is given in respect of employment.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on cash payments given to my employees for passing examinations?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on cash payments if passing examinations are part of your employee’s official duties, e.g. you sent your employee to a course as part of your training programme and he is required to pass the examinations to get the qualification to perform his job. The cash payments are akin to other awards given to recognise or incentivise employees for good performance.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on cash payment given to my employee for child care expenses incurred by his children?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable on the cash payment given to your employee for his children’s child care or school expenses.
CPF contributions are not payable if you make the payment directly to the service provider, e.g. child care centre or school, as it will be considered as benefit-in-kind.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on death benefits given to my employee's next of kin?
questions.text: CPF contributions are not payable on death benefits given to your deceased employee's next of kin.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on stocks or shares offered to my employees?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are payable if you give your employee any cash payment for them to purchase or subsidise their purchase of stocks or shares.
CPF contributions are not payable if the stocks or shares are given in kind to your employee (i.e. he receives the stocks or shares held in his name) or if the stocks or shares are discounted (i.e. he pays a lower price for the purchase but no cash payment is made to him). If the employee subsequently sells the stocks or shares which are held in his name, CPF contributions are not payable as the stocks and shares belong to him.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on donations given to my employee for bereavements?
questions.text: CPF contributions are not payable on donations given to your employees for bereavements.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions
