questions.title: Are there any changes required to the corporate service buyer's payment system/process to reconcile the payments made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text:
You may consider changing your payment system/ process to reconcile payments made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), if necessary.
If you’re using the online submission mode (DDA mode), you may download the CAYE payment file via the CAYE Digital Services to reconcile the payment made to the SEPs.
Generally, if you’re using PACE (PayNow for CAYE), you will receive a return file from CPFB within five working days from the Funds Deduction Date.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: For corporate service buyers who currently do not have an account with OCBC, are they required to open an account with the appointed bank, OCBC, if they wish to opt for bank mode payments?
questions.text: You do not need to have a bank account with OCBC for Contribute As You Earn (CAYE). However, you'II need to obtain and complete a Host-to-Host (H2H) application form from OCBC to establish a H2H file transfer link-up with the bank.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: For corporate service buyers using OCBC accounts, is there still a need to set up a Direct Debit Authorisation arrangement with OCBC to facilitate the deduction of service fee for bank mode payments?
questions.text: You’ll need to sign up for GIRO with OCBC to authorise OCBC to deduct the full service fees from your agency’s bank accounts for the purpose of Contribute As You Earn.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: How do corporate service buyers know if the payment to self-employed persons is successful?
questions.text:
Generally, for payment via PACE (PayNow for CAYE), you will receive a return file from CPF Board within five working days of the Fund Deduction Date indicated in your corporate payment file to the appointed bank, OCBC. This return file will indicate the amount of Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions and net service fee, the payment status, and rejection reason (for any unsuccessful payment).
For payment via the online submission mode, you can log into the CAYE Digital Services to view the payment status and CAYE contributions made to the self-employed person.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Under what scenarios will monies transmitted via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) bank mode be returned to the corporate service buyer?
questions.text:
An admin fee of $0.55 per transaction will be deducted from the gross service fees before the remainder is returned to the corporate service buyer if:
the self-employed person (SEP)’s bank account is closed or invalid;
the SEP’s NRIC is invalid; or
the CPF submission number in the bank file is invalid.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Would payments made via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) online submission mode be debited from the corporate service buyers' bank account?
questions.text: Yes, payments made via the Contribute As You Earn online submission mode would be debited from the corporate service buyers’ bank account via direct debit.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: How do corporate service buyers identify if the vendor is under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text:
For self-employed persons (SEPs) who submit e-invoices, Vendors@Gov will automatically identify vendors covered under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) who log in through Corppass or Singpass. These vendors will be notified of CAYE via prompts. The e-invoice file format will be modified to store two additional columns, CAYE indicator and SEPs’ NRIC, which will subsequently be loaded into NFS@Gov and interfaced to agencies.
For invoices outside of Vendors@Gov, corporate service buyers (CSBs) need to identify and tag SEPs manually via:
the NRIC used by the SEP to transact; or
the Unique Entity Number (UEN) issued by ACRA. CSBs can use the Enterprise Data Hub (EDH) to check whether the vendor’s business entity type is a sole proprietorship or partnership. If it is a sole proprietorship, CAYE will apply.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Do corporate service buyers with existing CPF Submission Number (CSN) for making CPF contributions to employees need to register for a Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) CSN?
questions.text: Corporate service buyers (CSBs) with existing CPF Submission Number (CSN) are required to register for a Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) CSN for CAYE transactions. This is because the existing CSN that CSBs have is only for the purpose of making CPF contributions to employees. A CAYE CSN will enable self-employed persons (SEPs) to identify CSBs who made CAYE contributions on their behalf. The CSN for employee transactions cannot be used for CAYE transactions, and vice versa. CSBs who need to apply for a CAYE CSN may do so via CAYE digital services.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Do corporate service buyers need to factor in an approving authority to ensure accuracy of records submitted under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: Under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), corporate service buyers are advised to factor in an approving authority within their internal processes before making payment to ensure accuracy of records submitted (i.e. no fraudulent transactions, no error in payment amount or self-employed person to be paid). Once submitted, CAYE payments are considered correctly paid.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: For PACE (PayNow for CAYE) payments, when do corporate service buyers need to submit a payment file to CPF Board to make Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions by the stipulated deadline?
questions.text: Corporate service buyers using PACE (PayNow for CAYE) need to submit the payment file to CPF Board at least five working days before the service fee payment due date to ensure timely payment to the self-employed person (SEP)’s MediSave Account.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Does CPF Board accept credit notes to offset future payments if there have been erroneous payment of Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions?
questions.text: CPF Board does not accept credit notes for the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions. If the corporate service buyer (CSB) has made an erroneous payment, the CSB can request a refund of the CAYE contribution from CPF Board within one year from the time the contribution was credited into the self-employed person (SEP)’s MediSave account. The CSB will have to seek a refund of the remaining service fee made from the SEP directly and re-transmit the CAYE contributions.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What if the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution was paid in error (i.e. paid wrong amount, or paid to the wrong self-employed person)?
questions.text: Corporate service buyers (CSBs) can request a refund of the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution from CPF Board within one year from the time the contribution was credited into the self-employed person’s MediSave account. After receiving a refund of the CAYE contribution paid in error, the CSB will be required to re-submit the correct CAYE contribution via the CAYE digital services.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What happens if payment to the self-employed person via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) bank mode is unsuccessful?
questions.text: For unsuccessful payments made via PACE (PayNow for CAYE) (e.g. due to invalid bank account number or invalid NRIC provided), the full service fee minus $0.55 per transaction (admin fee) will be returned to the corporate service buyer’s bank account via FAST. If the full service fee exceeds S$200,000, the payment will be rejected and the full service fee minus $0.55 per transaction (admin fee) will be refunded to the corporate service buyer’s bank account.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What happens if the corporate service buyer provided an invalid NRIC for crediting of the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions?
questions.text: Under Contribute As You Earn, if the NRIC provided is invalid, you will be prompted to amend the NRIC if you are using the online submission mode. If you are using PACE (PayNow for CAYE), you’ll automatically receive a refund minus $0.55 per transaction (admin fee) for that record as a rejection fee as the bank will reject the payment.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), what should corporate service buyers do to set-off monies from an upcoming payment?
questions.text: To set-off monies (e.g. due to over-payment, or excess non-revenue payment made earlier) from an upcoming payment, corporate service buyers (CSBs) need to make the transaction via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) online submission mode. This means that CSBs need to key in the full service fee payable to derive the MediSave payable via CAYE, and thereafter set-off any monies from the net service fee payable to the self-employed person.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Why are Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps reduced for CPF Investment Scheme funds?
questions.text: The purpose of CPF Investment Scheme is to provide alternative investment to help CPF members build up their retirement savings. As expenses of investment have a significant impact on returns, a regular review of the Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps is important as high expense ratio would erode investment returns for CPF members. Where feasible, TER caps should be kept low to increase the fund’s per-unit net asset value and enable CPF members to accumulate their retirement savings faster. This is in line with the efforts by regulatory authorities in other countries to reduce the cost of funds to investors.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What actions should Fund Management Companies/insurers take if their existing CPF Investment Scheme List A funds are unable to comply with the Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps?
questions.text: Fund Management Companies (FMCs)/insurers have undertaken to comply with the Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps for funds included under CPF Investment Scheme. If their List A funds are not able to comply with the new TER caps from 2016, FMCs/insurers will be required to compensate the funds for the difference between the actual expense ratios and the new TER caps. The funds would then be downgraded to List B with effect from the implementation date (see relevant reporting period, (PDF, 0.1MB)). Under List B, funds are not allowed to take in new CPF monies.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Do Fund Management Companies/insurers need to submit a new undertaking in view of the new Total Expense Ratio caps?
questions.text: There is no need to submit a new undertaking. The previous undertaking continues to be valid for existing List A funds under CPF Investment Scheme.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can a fund downgraded to List B resume accepting CPF monies once the fund's Total Expense Ratio meets the cap subsequently?
questions.text: The fund would be upgraded to List A, and can take in CPF monies if its audited Total Expense Ratio meets the cap subsequently.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How frequent will CPF Board assess whether a fund can or cannot take in CPF monies?
questions.text: CPF Board will assess whenever a fund’s audited financial statements become available (i.e. yearly basis for most funds). A company that wishes to have its fund assessed more frequently may submit to CPF Board the fund’s semi-annual audited financial statements according to its accounting period. The company must ensure that all subsequent published Total Expense Ratios (TERs) of its funds are also in line with the TER cap.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will a fund be excluded from CPF Investment Scheme due to not meeting the Total Expense Ratio cap subsequent to the inclusion?
questions.text: The fund will remain under CPF Investment Scheme (as List B fund) but it will not be allowed to take in CPF new monies. However, the company will have to provide the fund’s investors with options to hold, redeem or make free switches within 3 months from informing the CPF Board of not meeting Total Expense Ratio caps.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What are the admission criteria that fund management companies (FMCs) and insurance companies need to meet, in order to be included under CPFIS?
questions.text: Please see the admission criteria for fund management companies (FMCs) and insurance companies.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What does the Board's investment consultant look for when evaluating fund management companies (FMCs), insurance companies or their products?
questions.text: Please see the evaluation criteria provided by the Board's investment consultant.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What are the CPFIS admission criteria for funds?
questions.text: You can refer to para 5 for the admission criteria for funds.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What are the benefits of Internet Reimbursement?
questions.text:
The Internet Reimbursement (IR) service allows you to easily submit MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursements for your employees, platform workers or insureds at your convenience. Benefits of using our IR service include:
Fast service turnaround time
Accurate reimbursements
Streamlined processes
Track reimbursement status online
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: How many reimbursements can I submit via E-File at one time?
questions.text:
You can submit up to 15,000 reimbursements at a time via E-File.
Please note that all 15,000 reimbursements should be submitted in a single Excel file.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: What sources of MediSave contributions are eligible for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contribution?
questions.text:
MediSave contributions1 made by the taxi principal hirer to offset MediSave payable will qualify him for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contribution. CPF contributions received as an employee (from both employer and self) for taxi principal hirers who are concurrently employed, as well as government top-ups are excluded.
1 You may make MediSave contributions as a self-employed person via Manage your MediSave payable or GIRO.

questions.title: My current registered bank account with CPF Board is also my PayNow NRIC-linked bank account. Do I still need to update my registered bank account with CPF Board to receive my CPF withdrawals via PayNow?
questions.text: Yes, it is necessary to do a one-time update of your registered bank account to "PayNow NRIC-linked bank account" via Account settings if you wish to receive CPF payments via PayNow. If you do not update your registered bank account to PayNow, you will receive the payments within five working days of your withdrawal application via Interbank GIRO.

questions.title: Can I update my registered bank account when I have a pending withdrawal application?
questions.text: Please do not update your registered bank account until you have received your CPF savings in your bank account to avoid any delay or disruption in receiving your payment.

questions.title: I received a Final Reminder notification regarding my outstanding CareShield Life/MediShield Life premiums, will the amount payable still be increased?
questions.text:
The Final Reminder notification shows the amount of your outstanding CareShield Life/MediShield Life premiums as at the date sent.
Please pay your full outstanding premiums by the deadline indicated in the notification. Otherwise, the amount payable will increase as the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) will impose compounded interest of 4% and penalties of up to 17% on your outstanding premiums. To do so, please click on the link below for the payment options.
How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)s' CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?

questions.title: Who is a platform worker?
questions.text: You are a platform worker if you have an agreement with a platform operator to provide ride-hail or delivery services in Singapore to users for the platform operator and from this, derive any payment or benefit in kind. You are also subject to the control of platform operators, such as what tasks are assigned to you and how much you are paid. You will be given an earnings slip that specifies your status as a platform worker.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Overview of CPF contributions for platform operators
Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Who is a platform operator?
questions.text:
Platform operators are companies that:
a. have an agreement with users to provide ride-hail or delivery services to the users;
b. use data to automate decision making relating to platform workers, in areas such as task assignment and how much platform workers are paid per task; and
c. impose rules, requirements or prohibitions on platform workers.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Overview of CPF contributions for platform operators
Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: When would my platform operator submit my CPF contributions?
questions.text: Platform operators are required to submit CPF contributions on a monthly basis. The due date for CPF contribution is on the last day of the calendar month. Enforcement action would be taken against platform operators who fail to pay by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday). This includes imposing late payment interest charged at 1.5% per month commencing from the first day after the due date.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is it mandatory for platform workers born in 1995 or later to have increased CPF contributions aligned to employees, while those born before 1995 have the option to opt in?
questions.text:
Younger platform workers have a greater need for CPF contributions because of housing needs and can benefit more from the compounding interest given their longer runway for accumulation.
Older platform workers can choose to opt in to the increased CPF contributions if they wish to, as they may have existing plans to finance housing and retirement needs.
Older platform workers who do not opt in will continue to be required to make CPF MediSave contributions, and will not receive the platform operator’s share of CPF contributions.
Platform operators will deduct the CPF contributions from platform workers’ earnings as and when they earn and transmit them to CPF Board monthly for all platform workers, including the MediSave contributions for those who do not opt in.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: How will platform workers’ CPF contributions be allocated to the CPF accounts?
questions.text:
If you are born on or after 1 Jan 1995 or have opted in to increased CPF contribution rates, your CPF contributions will be allocated to your Ordinary Account, Special or Retirement Account and MediSave Account. You can view the allocation rates.
If you are born before 1 Jan 1995 and have not opted in, your CPF contributions will be allocated to your MediSave Account only.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Is there a deadline to opt in as a platform worker for increased CPF contribution?
questions.text:
There is no deadline to opt in. You can consider your decision carefully based on your personal circumstances, before opting in to the increased CPF contributions. The decision to opt in cannot be reversed.
You are encouraged to opt in early as this will allow you to have a longer time to grow your CPF savings for your house and retirement needs. If eligible, you can also benefit from the Platform Workers CPF Transition Support.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why am I not able to reverse my decision after I have opted in to increase my CPF contributions as a platform worker?
questions.text:
Opting in is a concession given to help you increase your CPF contributions. By doing so, you will receive higher overall income, considering the contributions from platform operators. Staying committed to the CPF contributions will also ensure that your CPF savings will accumulate interest over time, thereby building up your housing and retirement adequacy in the long run.
Allowing opt-outs will not help build up your housing and retirement adequacy in the long run. It is also not practical for platform operators to track the status of workers and apply the different rates of CPF contributions if workers opt in and out multiple times. This may incur additional business costs for platform operators and make implementation more complicated overall.
As there is no deadline to opt in, you can carefully consider your decision based on your personal circumstances, before opting in to increase your CPF contributions.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Do I need to inform my platform operator once I have opted in to increase my CPF contributions?
questions.text:
You do not need to inform your platform operator once you have opted in to increase your CPF contributions.
Your platform operator will confirm your opt-in status with CPF Board directly.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Can I declare actual expenses different from Fixed Expense Deduction Amount? Will my CPF contributions be adjusted?
questions.text:
For the convenience of both platform workers and platform operators, CPF contributions will be based on gross earnings less Fixed Expense Deduction Amount (FEDA), and are not based on declared expenses.
This benefits both platform workers and platform operators as you will not have to keep receipts to track and compute actual expenses for your platform work and submit them to your platform operators. Your platform operators will also not have to incur additional operating costs to re-compute the CPF contribution based on actual expenses.
FEDA is applied to all platform workers to simplify the computation of CPF contribution for both platform operators and platform workers, regardless of income levels and delivery modes. As such, we will not adjust the CPF contributions based on declared expenses.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on reimbursements to platform workers for expenses?
questions.text: CPF contributions are not payable on payments from platform operators meant to reimburse additional expenses already incurred by workers. For example, this can include reimbursements for fuel due to cancelled jobs, and cleaning expenses if customers made a mess in the vehicle.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: What happens if I have incentives accrued across a few months but only paid later? When will the payments attract CPF contribution?
questions.text:
Platform earnings and incentives attract CPF contribution when they are due and payable, not when they are accrued.
For example, the CPF contributions on an incentive payment in June that is for trips done in May will be computed together with the rest of the June earnings.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is there no monthly earnings ceiling for CPF contributions for platform workers?
questions.text:
A monthly earnings ceiling would not be as relevant for platform workers, who generally do not have a basic monthly wage and are more likely to see high month-to-month variation in earnings.
For example, take a platform worker who earns $4,000 in January and $8,000 in February. If a monthly cap of $6,000 is applied, the worker would receive CPF contributions for the full $4,000 earned in January, but would only receive CPF contributions for $6,000 out of the $8,000 earned in February. Thus, the worker would receive less CPF than an employee who has a regular monthly salary of $6,000 per month, and would have received CPF contributions on $6,000 across both months.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Does the CPF annual ceiling apply to my net earnings as a platform worker?
questions.text:
Yes, you will be subject to the same CPF annual ceiling of $102,000 as employees. You do not need to make any CPF contributions on net earnings exceeding $102,000 in a year.
As CPF contributions are computed separately for each platform operator you work with, this annual ceiling applies on a per-platform basis.
If your total net earnings for the year across all platforms have exceeded CPF annual ceiling of $102,000, you can apply for a refund on your share of the contributions.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: If I work for multiple platforms, how will CPF contributions be calculated for each platform?
questions.text:
All your platform operators will calculate and contribute CPF for you separately (i.e. per-platform basis).
For example, Mr Lim works for platform operator A having a net earning of $3,000 and platform operator B, having a net earning of $6,000. Platform operator A will contribute CPF contributions on the $3,000 while platform operator B will contribute CPF contributions on the $6,000.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Which platform operator should pay my CPF if there is a subcontracting arrangement?
questions.text:
If you are a platform worker, the company that satisfies the definition of platform operator in relation to the work you do is responsible for paying your CPF contributions.
If unsure, please write to us.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: If I am working for more than one platform operator, can I choose to contribute CPF on the earnings from only one of my platform operators?
questions.text:
No, CPF contributions will be made by all platform operators you work with (i.e. per-platform basis).
However, if your total net earnings for the year across all platforms have exceeded CPF annual ceiling of $102,000, you can apply for a refund on your share of the contributions.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Can I apply for refund on CPF contributions paid above the CPF annual ceiling of $102,000?
questions.text:
If your total net earnings under a single platform operator exceed $102,000, your platform operator will apply for a refund on the excess CPF contributions from CPF Board. After receiving the refund, your platform operator will refund your share of excess CPF contributions to you.
If your total earnings across multiple platform operators exceed $102,000, you can apply for a refund on your share of the contributions.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Can my platform operator’s contributions be used to offset outstanding MediSave contributions from my past self-employed work?
questions.text:
Your CPF contributions (including platform operator’s share, if any) are meant for platform work done from 2025.
You will need to make separate arrangements to settle any outstanding MediSave contributions on past income earned as a self-employed person.
You may reach out to CPFB to arrange affordable instalment plans on your past MediSave obligations.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: As a taxi driver who takes both ride-hail and street-hail jobs, how should I make CPF contributions for my earnings?
questions.text:
CPF contributions on your ride-hail and street-hail earnings will be made separately.
For ride-hail earnings, platform operators will deduct and make CPF contributions for you.
For street-hail earnings, you will need to contribute MediSave on your own in the following year after you have declared your Net Trade Income (NTI) to IRAS. Your MediSave payable will be computed on your NTI after excluding net earnings from your platform work as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s). CPF Board will inform you of your MediSave payable once IRAS has assessed your income.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: If I am concurrently a full-time employee doing platform work, do I still need to make CPF contributions on platform earnings?
questions.text:
Yes, your platform operator will deduct the required CPF contributions from your net earnings from platform work. There is no change to your CPF contributions as an employee. Your employer must still deduct and make CPF contributions for you.
If your combined income from employment and platform work exceeds $102,000, you can apply for a refund on your share of CPF contributions.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: If I am concurrently a full-time employee doing platform work, will my employers be notified of my platform work because of the CPF contributions?
questions.text: No. Your employers will not be notified of your CPF contributions from platform work.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I ensure that the CPF contributions I received as a platform worker is accurate?
questions.text: You can use the platform worker CPF Contribution Calculator to check if your CPF contributions are correct by keying in your net earnings.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Where can I view the CPF contributions made by my platform operator?
questions.text:
You can view details of your platform work CPF contributions within the last 15 months by following the steps below:
Log in to my cpf digital services via your Singpass
Go to “View transactions” → “View past 15 months”
Select “Filter” → “Employment and platform contributions”
Your platform worker CPF contributions will be indicated as “[Platform operator name] (Platform)”. The results page should look like this:
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Will I lose out on interest on my CPF contributions if my platform operator pays my CPF contributions late?
questions.text: You will not lose out on the interest when your platform operator pays late. The interest will be credited to you when CPF Board recovers the CPF arrears from your platform operator.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: How much voluntary contributions can I make as a platform worker?
questions.text:
The maximum amount you can voluntarily contribute is the difference between the CPF Annual Limit of $37,740 and the mandatory CPF contributions made for the calendar year.
Do remember to consider your mandatory CPF contributions which you will be receiving for the calendar year, before making voluntary contributions. If the total mandatory CPF contributions and voluntary contributions exceed the CPF Annual Limit in the calendar year, any excess voluntary contributions will be refunded without interest in the following year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why are cash top-ups beyond Full Retirement Sum not eligible for tax relief?
questions.text: Givers enjoy tax relief for cash top-ups up to the current Full Retirement Sum (FRS). This is in line with the intent of tax relief benefits to encourage cash top-ups to members with lower to average CPF retirement balances.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I transfer my top-ups made to my Special Account/ Retirement Account to other CPF accounts if I need to use them for other purposes such as housing or healthcare?
questions.text:
No, such cash top-ups and CPF transfers are meant to boost your retirement savings to enable you to receive higher payouts. Hence, they cannot be used for other purposes or transferred to other CPF accounts such as your Ordinary Account or MediSave Account.
Consider whether you would require the monies for other purposes (e.g. housing or healthcare expenses) before topping up to your Special Account/ Retirement Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: To qualify for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS), what is considered income?
questions.text:
We will automatically assess your eligibility for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) based on the latest net earnings declared by your platform operator(s) when making CPF contributions, and the latest wages declared by your employer when making CPF contributions if you also work as an employee.
Your platform operator will compute your monthly platform net earnings based on your monthly gross earnings less a Fixed Expense Deduction Amount (FEDA). The FEDA depends on the mode of transportation you use for platform work.
Your wages from your employer are the total amount of wages for any calendar month, which is the sum of your Ordinary Wages for the month and the Additional Wage paid to you in that month.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Why must I earn more than $500 from at least one platform to receive Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS)?
questions.text:
Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) is intended to offset part of the year-on-year increase in a platform worker’s own share of CPF contributions to his Ordinary and Special or Retirement accounts. How much a platform worker will contribute to his CPF will be based on his net earnings from each platform.
A platform worker whose net earnings from each platform is less than or equal to $500 does not have to make his own share of CPF contributions. Given there is no increase in the platform worker’s share of his CPF contributions, he will not be eligible for PCTS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Why are Singapore Permanent Residents not eligible for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS)?
questions.text:
The Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) scheme is for lower-income platform workers who hold SIngapore Citizenship only.
If you require financial assistance, please contact the ComCare hotline at 1800-222-0000, or email Ask_SSO@msf.gov.sg.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Why will Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) cease in 2029?
questions.text:
Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) is meant to offset the increase in the platform workers’ share of CPF contributions in the transition phase as platform workers’ CPF contributions are gradually aligned with that of employees over five years. In 2029, when platform worker’s CPF contributions are completely aligned with that of employees, PCTS will cease.
Eligible lower-income platform workers can tap on the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) instead, where platform workers will receive higher WIS payments at the same level as employees from 2029, once their CPF contribution rates fully align with that of employees. They will also receive a higher proportion of WIS payments in cash – 40% compared to 10% today.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: How do I contribute CPF as a platform operator?
questions.text: You can write to us to onboard as a platform operator. To find out more about the onboarding steps, you can refer to this guide.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Overview of CPF contributions for platform operators

questions.title: Which platform operator should contribute CPF if there is a subcontracting arrangement?
questions.text:
The company that satisfies the definition of platform operator in relation to the work done by platform workers is responsible for contributing their CPF.
If you require clarifications, you can submit an enquiry to MOM.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Overview of CPF contributions for platform operators

questions.title: What is the monthly and annual earnings ceiling for CPF contributions for platform workers?
questions.text:
There is no monthly earnings ceiling for platform workers. A monthly earnings ceiling would not be as relevant for platform workers, who generally do not have a basic monthly wage and are more likely to see high month-to-month variation in earnings.
For example, take a platform worker who earns $4,000 in January and then $8,000 in February. If we had a monthly cap of $6,000 for example, in January, he would have received CPF contribution for the full $4,000 earned but in February would only receive CPF contribution for $6,000 out of the $8,000 they earned. He would receive less CPF that an employee who has regular monthly salary of $6,000 per month (same total income of $12,000 for January and February).
The annual earnings ceiling of $102,000 will apply to platform workers, on a per platform basis. Platform operators should not contribute any CPF contributions to their platform workers for any net earnings in excess of $102,000.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: How should platform workers’ share be deducted from earnings?
questions.text:
Platform operators should generally deduct the platform workers’ share of CPF contribution as and when they earn and submit monthly CPF contributions on platform workers’ behalf.
CPF contribution rates are lower for platform workers with net earnings less than $750 per month. If you had withheld your platform workers’ earnings based on a higher CPF contribution rate (i.e. using the rate applicable to platform workers’ earning above $750), you should refund the difference to your platform workers not later than 14 days of the following month, before submitting the CPF contributions.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / How much CPF contributions to contribute

questions.title: How to calculate CPF contributions for platform workers working with multiple platform operators?
questions.text:
All platform operators will calculate and contribute CPF for platform workers separately (i.e. per-platform basis).
For example, Mr Lim works for platform operator A having a net earning of $3,000 and platform operator B, having a net earning of $6,000. Platform operator A will contribute CPF contributions on the $3,000 while platform operator B will contribute CPF contributions on the $6,000.
Note: If a platform worker provides both delivery and ride-hail services with the same platform operator (i.e. same UEN), his earnings should be combined.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / How much CPF contributions to contribute

questions.title: Will the CPF contribution rate for platform workers who are Singapore Citizens differ from platform workers who are Permanent Residents?
questions.text: No. The contribution rate for platform workers is the same for both Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents. There is also no differentiation regardless whether a platform worker is a 1st or 2nd year Permanent Resident.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / How much CPF contributions to contribute

questions.title: Is the relevant CPF contribution rate based on the month the job is placed or the month it is completed or paid for my platform workers?
questions.text:
The CPF contribution rate for your platform workers is based on the net earnings in the month in which the payment is due and payable.
For example, if the incentive payment for trips done in January 2025 are only due and payable to a platform worker in February 2025, the incentive payment should be included in the platform worker’s February 2025 earnings. Similarly, any penalties imposed in February 2025 for trips completed in January 2025 should be deducted from February 2025 earnings for the purpose of CPF computation.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / How much CPF contributions to contribute

questions.title: Will platform operators need to make additional deductions for platform workers with outstanding MediSave liability from past years?
questions.text: No, platform operators will not deduct the outstanding CPF contributions that platform workers have incurred as self-employed persons for work done in past years. Platform workers who have difficulties making these outstanding MediSave contributions can approach CPFB to arrange affordable instalment plans.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / How much CPF contributions to contribute

questions.title: How are CPF contribution rates applied when a platform worker moves to the next age group?
questions.text:
The contribution rates of your platform worker moving to the next age group shall be applied from the first day of the month after the month of his 35th, 45th, 50th, 60th, 65th and 70th birthday.
For example, for a platform worker whose 50th birthday falls in May, he is deemed to have 50 years of age in May, and we will use the contribution rate for the “Above 45-50” age group for May. As contribution rates are applicable on a monthly basis, you will apply the contribution rate for the “Above 50-55” age group from June.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / How much CPF contributions to contribute

questions.title: What is Unique Entity Number (UEN)?
questions.text: The Unique Entity Number (UEN) is the standard identification number of an entity. The UEN is for registered entities while the NRIC is for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents. The UEN uniquely identifies the entity.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number
Employer - Platform Operator / Applying for a CPF Submission Number

questions.title: What is CPF Submission Number (CSN) and how do I use it to submit my platform workers’ CPF contributions?
questions.text:
CPF Submission Number (CSN) is a unique identifier for CPF contributions and is needed for transactions with CPF Board.
Platform operators should apply for 2 CSNs, to submit contributions for the different cohorts of platform workers. For example:
123456789-PWA-02 for platform workers who are mandated or opted in to increase contributions, and will receive platform operator's share of CPF contributions
123456789-PWM-03 for platform workers who are not opted in, and contributing to their MediSave only. They will not receive platform operator's share of CPF contributions
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Applying for a CPF Submission Number

questions.title: What is the CPF Payment Code for platform operators?
questions.text:
The CPF Payment Code in your CPF Submission Number (CSN) identifies the different types of payments made by employers and platform operators to the Board such as mandatory CPF contributions, Voluntary Contributions, and MediSave contributions under the Additional MediSave Contribution Scheme.
For example, the payment codes for platform worker CSNs are:
123456789-PWA-02 for platform workers who are mandated or opted in, and the contributions will be allocated to all CPF accounts
123456789-PWM-03 for platform workers who are not opted in, and the contributions will be allocated to their MediSave only
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Applying for a CPF Submission Number

questions.title: How do I obtain my CPF Submission Number (CSN) as a new platform operator? How long does it take?
questions.text:
You can request for a CSN application form via write-to-us.
We will provide you with the application form, and your CSNs will be issued to you within five working days after submission of the form.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Applying for a CPF Submission Number

questions.title: Who are the eGIRO participating banks for the Direct Debit Authorisation (DDA) online application?
questions.text:
eGIRO (Electronic GIRO) is a joint initiative by The Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS), and participating banks, with the support of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), to digitise the GIRO application process and significantly reduce the turnaround time for setting up a GIRO arrangement.
Please refer to the list of eGIRO participating banks for DDA online application. ABS is working with the industry to onboard more banks onto eGIRO service and we will update the list accordingly.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes
Employer - Platform Operator / Setting up of Direct Debit Authorisation

questions.title: How do I check the status of my Direct Debit application?
questions.text: If you have submitted the Direct Debit Authorisation (DDA) application online, you can check your application status online. We will also notify you of the status and effective date of the Direct Debit arrangement upon approval.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes
Employer - Platform Operator / Setting up of Direct Debit Authorisation

questions.title: If I am paying via Direct Debit, when will CPF Board deduct from my bank account after my CPF submission as a platform operator?
questions.text:
Direct Debit deduction will only take place after you have submitted your CPF contribution details. After you have made your submission via CPF EZPay as a platform operator, you will see the deduction date in the "Deduction On" field below the "Direct Debit" button.
Please remember to maintain sufficient funds for successful deduction. If your deduction fails, there will be a 2nd deduction seven calendar days later (or next working day if it falls on a public holiday). This may result in late CPF submission and incur late payment interest.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Setting up of Direct Debit Authorisation

questions.title: How do I change my company's Direct Debit account to pay CPF contribution?
questions.text:
To change your Direct Debit account for CPF contributions, simply submit a new application for Direct Debit Authorisation (DDA) for your new bank account.
CPF contributions will continue to be deducted from the existing bank account until the new Direct Debit Authorisation form has been approved. Once it is approved, the previous Direct Debit arrangement will then be terminated.
Please refrain from submitting a new online DDA application to change your bank account while the deduction for your current submission is pending. This is to avoid unsuccessful deduction which may incur late payment interest. If you wish to change the bank account for Direct Debit deduction, you should only submit the new online DDA application after the deduction is successful.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes
Employer - Platform Operator / Setting up of Direct Debit Authorisation

questions.title: What if my platform worker joined after I submitted the monthly query?
questions.text: If your platform worker (born before 1995) joins after the 15th of the month, you should use the non-opt-in rate for him until you can determine his opt in status from the next month’s query.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Setting up of platform workers’ opt-in status query

questions.title: I have updated my preference via the notification preference form. Does this preference apply to other notifications sent by CPF Board?
questions.text: The notification preference only applies to the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons. Your updated notification preference will take effect for any subsequent notice of CPF contributions thereafter.

questions.title: I have previously chosen to receive my notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons in hardcopy. Can I still change my preference?
questions.text:
Yes. Regardless of your current preference, you can update your preference anytime by completing the notification preference form.
Your updated notification preference will take effect for any subsequent notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons thereafter.

questions.title: What should I do if I wish to receive the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons in hardcopy?
questions.text:
If you wish to receive your notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons via hardcopy instead, you may update your notification preference via the notification preference form using your Singpass. The hardcopy notice will be mailed to you at your residential address.
Your updated notification preference will take effect for any subsequent notice of CPF contributions thereafter.

questions.title: How will I know when my digital notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons is ready for viewing?
questions.text:
You will receive an email notification to view your digital notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons via the self-employment dashboard when it is ready. If you do not have a registered email with CPF Board, you will receive an SMS notification instead. If you do not have a registered email address or mobile number, your notice will be sent to you in hardcopy at your residential address.
To ensure you receive prompt alerts when your notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons is ready, please update your contact details via the account services page after logging in with your Singpass.

questions.title: Can I attend the Home Protection Scheme medical examination if I am currently pregnant?
questions.text:
You can proceed with the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) medical examination even if you are currently pregnant. Please notify the clinic staff and doctor that you are pregnant so that chest X-ray will not be conducted.
Find out more:
What tests am I required to undergo for the Home Protection Scheme medical examination?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What should I do if I am currently overseas and unable to attend the Home Protection Scheme medical examination appointment?
questions.text:
We are unable to assess your eligibility for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) and process your application, if you are unable to attend the HPS medical examination.
You can submit a new HPS application online, using your Singpass, when you have returned to Singapore. A medical examination would be arranged for you thereafter.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: My witnesses did not receive an SMS or email notification to witness my nomination. What should I do?
questions.text:
You can inform your witnesses to visit cpf.gov.sg/witnessNOM to witness an online nomination. The SMS or email notification is not needed for witnesses to proceed with their declaration on cpf.gov.sg/witnessNOM.
You and your witnesses can also refer to the video guide for more information on making an online CPF nomination.

questions.title: Do I need to apply for a new CPF Submission Number (CSN) if my platform is a subsidiary company with a different Unique Entity Number (UEN) from the parent company?
questions.text: Yes, you are required to apply for a new CPF Submission Number (CSN) if your platform is a subsidiary company with a different Unique Entity Number (UEN) from the parent company. To apply for a CSN, please refer to How do i obtain my CSN as a new platform operator?
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Applying for a CPF Submission Number

questions.title: How do I calculate the Additional Wage (AW) ceiling and the amount that attracts CPF contributions?
questions.text:
The Additional Wage (AW) ceiling sets the maximum amount of AW on which CPF contributions are payable per year. An employee's AW ceiling is computed on a per employee, per employer, per calendar year basis.
You can access the following resources to help you with the computation:
AW ceiling Calculator
Examples on the Computation of the AW ceiling (PDF, 0.5MB)
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: Where can I find the list of e-services available in Corppass?
questions.text: You may find the list of digital services here.

questions.title: What is a UEN and who issues it?
questions.text:
UEN stands for Unique Entity Number, which is a standard identification number used by entities to interact with government agencies in Singapore. It uniquely identifies an entity, similar to how the NRIC is used for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
A UEN is issued by government agencies, known as UEN-issuance agencies, when an entity is officially registered. Some examples of these agencies include the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA), Registry of Societies (ROS), and Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

questions.title: What does the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) do?
questions.text:
NCSS is the umbrella body for over 500-member social service agencies in Singapore. It's mission is to provide leadership and direction in enhancing the capabilities and capacity of our members, advocating for social service needs and strengthening strategic partnerships, for an effective social service ecosystem. Community Chest is the philanthropy and engagement arm of NCSS and Social Service Institute (SSI) is the sector capability and transformation arm of NCSS.
Find out more about NCSS.

questions.title: Can I still make payment for my outstanding MediShield Life/ CareShield Life premiums after the deadline stated in the Final Reminder notification?
questions.text:
We advise you to pay your outstanding MediShield Life/ CareShield Life premiums before the due date to avoid enforcement actions.
Please click on the link below for the payment options.
How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)'s CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?

questions.title: Why does my Healthcare dashboard state that my MediShield Life/ CareShield Life premiums may be recovered from my bankruptcy estate?
questions.text:
Outstanding MediShield Life/ CareShield Life premiums incurred prior to your bankruptcy date may be recovered from your bankruptcy estate. These premiums will therefore not be reflected as outstanding premiums payable in your Healthcare dashboard.
To pay your outstanding premiums incurred prior to the date of your Bankruptcy Order, please obtain approval from the Private Trustee or Official Assignee. You can contact them at 1800 225 5529 (during office hours) or visit www.mlaw.gov.sg.

questions.title: Can I opt out of the upcoming enhanced benefits and increased premiums?
questions.text:
MediShield Life is a national health insurance scheme that covers all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents for life. As coverage is mandatory, the benefits and premiums apply to all policyholders and there is no opting out of this scheme.
With rising healthcare costs and changes in the healthcare landscape, MediShield Life benefits and premiums have to be reviewed periodically and updated to ensure the scheme remains sustainable and relevant to the needs of Singaporeans.
The Government will continue to ensure that premiums are kept affordable for all Singaporeans and no one will lose coverage due to an inability to pay their premiums.

questions.title: What are the options for me if I am the 1 in 10 whose subsidised bill is not fully covered by MediShield Life and MediSave?
questions.text:
MediShield Life is designed to fully cover nine in ten subsidised bills, with the deductible and co-insurance covered by MediSave. This strikes a balance between protecting Singaporeans against the vast majority of healthcare bills, while keeping premiums affordable.
Singaporeans can be assured that more people will see their subsidised bills fully covered by MediShield Life and MediSave. For the minority of patients whose subsidised bills exceed the claim limit, they will still receive payouts from MediShield Life up to the relevant claim limit. Those who have difficulty affording their bills after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave can also apply for financial assistance such as MediFund, or appeal to MOH for MediSave use beyond limits.

questions.title: How much is the outpatient deductible? Will I need to pay more out of pocket for outpatient consultation?
questions.text:
The outpatient deductible is set at $500 to strike a balance between ensuring that it can sieve out smaller bills meaningfully and moderate the extent to which premiums need to increase by, whilst not overly affecting affordability for patients. It applies for all admissions on or after 1 Jan 2026 and is fully payable by MediSave. There should generally be no increase in out-of-pocket payable as long as you have sufficient MediSave.
For those with insufficient MediSave, the Government will provide additional support such as MediSave top-ups. There is also MediFund to help those who are unable to afford their bills even after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave.

questions.title: What is the difference between the inpatient and outpatient deductible? Do I have to pay both the inpatient and outpatient deductible if I seek treatments in both settings?
questions.text:
The inpatient deductible is applicable for inpatient treatments, while the outpatient deductible will only apply for outpatient treatments.
The deductible paid for inpatient treatments in a policy year would also count towards the outpatient deductible and vice versa.
For example, if a patient has paid at least $500 towards their deductible in the inpatient setting in a policy year, they would have fulfilled the outpatient deductible for the same policy year.

questions.title: What happens to the deductible that I have paid for during my policy year prior to 1 Apr 2025?
questions.text:
The first phase of the increase in inpatient deductible, together with the refresh of existing MediShield Life claim limits, will take effect on 1 Apr 2025. These revised parameters will apply for all admissions on or after 1 Apr 2025.
Any deductible that you have paid for during your policy year prior to 1 Apr 2025 will be counted towards the new deductible. Assuming the same policy year, this means that if you have paid $1,500 in deductible before 1 Apr 2025, it would continue to count towards the new deductible that you have to pay for your admission on or after 1 Apr 2025.

questions.title: How did the Government decide which treatments, conditions, and care settings should be covered under MediShield Life in this review?
Why is MediShield Life covering treatments such as CTGTPs and high-cost drugs that only benefit a small number of patients?
questions.text:
CTGTPs and high-cost drugs have significant potential to treat rare diseases and conditions. However, they can be expensive. Without any financing, Singaporeans will not be able to access these potentially effective treatments.
This is where MediShield Life and risk-pooling can play a useful role. Instead of having every individual save for a CTGTP, which only some may require, MediShield Life works by collecting smaller, annual premiums from individuals, and paying out when one requires high-cost, low-incidence treatments such as CTGTPs. To ensure the scheme remains affordable and sustainable, coverage will only be extended to treatments that are assessed by MOH to be clinically and cost-effective.

questions.title: How much will my premiums be once the premium changes take effect, and how much would it increase by?
questions.text:
You may refer to the premium & subsidy table here for the premium schedule for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
The extent of premium increases will vary across policyholders depending on age group. Information on your MediShield Life premium and applicable subsidies will be sent in writing to the payer of your premium about 1-2 months before your policy renewal date, by the Central Provident Fund Board or your Integrated Shield Plan (IP) insurer (if you are insured under an IP).
To help Singaporeans manage the premium increases, the Government will provide an additional $4.1 billion in premium support measures over the next three years. With this, more than nine in 10 Singaporeans will be able to more than offset their net increase in premiums for the next three years.

questions.title: How can I participate in the programme and earn premium discount?
questions.text:
A person, who on average, does 30 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) almost daily, could earn a total of 6,000 Healthpoints in a year if he clocks these activities on his Healthy 365 app. He can then redeem these Healthpoints for $80 worth of MediShield Life premium discounts.
For residents aged 40 and above who enrol in Healthier SG and complete their first Health Plan consultation, they would be able to redeem $40 worth of MediShield Life premium discounts.
Please refer to the HPB rewards programme FAQs for more information on Healthpoints.

questions.title: Will my Integrated Shield Plan (IP) benefits be affected by the MediShield Life review?
questions.text: Whether your IP benefits will be affected will depend on your insurer, as the IP benefits are set, reviewed and adjusted by insurers based on their own commercial and actuarial considerations.

questions.title: How will my Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premium be affected by the MediShield Life review?
questions.text:
Your IP premium is made up of two components – the MediShield Life premium and the premium for the additional private insurance component.
Your MediShield Life premium component will increase.
Revisions to the private insurance component of your IP premium will depend on your insurer, who may make changes based on their own actuarial and commercial considerations, and after accounting for any changes in their product features, if any.

questions.title: How can I update my contact details to receive notification on my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payments?
questions.text: To receive notification via SMS or email on your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment, you may update your mobile number via my cpf digital services - Account Settings with your Singpass.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: I am under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme, what happens to my CPF savings when I turn 55?
questions.text:
When you turn 55, if you have savings in your Special Account (SA), it will be transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) up to your Reduced Retirement Sum (RRS) and your SA will be closed.
Once you have set aside your RRS in RA, any remaining SA savings will be transferred to your Ordinary Account and can be withdrawn at any time.

questions.title: When will the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) be expanded to cover more members with certain pre-existing health conditions to obtain HPS coverage at a higher premium rate (i.e. with premium loading)?
questions.text: From 26 May 2025, the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) expands to cover members with certain pre-existing health conditions that are not so severe, such as certain types of stroke and heart disorder, who are currently not offered coverage. CPF Board will assess each application and offer eligible members an HPS cover with premium loading.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What are some examples of pre-existing health conditions that are not so severe, which may now be eligible for Home Protection Scheme coverage, subject to premium loading?
questions.text:
Examples of pre-existing health conditions that may now be considered for coverage with premium loading include certain types of stroke and heart disorder.
A member’s eligibility for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will still be assessed based on overall severity, prognosis, control of the health condition, and the member’s health risk profile.
However, members with more severe health conditions, such as those currently receiving treatment for cancer and kidney failure are not eligible for HPS coverage, even with premium loading.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If my health condition is such that I am offered a Home Protection Scheme cover with premium loading, is it compulsory to take up this cover?
questions.text: Members who are offered Home Protection Scheme (HPS) covers with premium loading can decide whether or not to take up the HPS cover. Participation in this scheme will be on an opt-in basis for them.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If I am offered a Home Protection Scheme cover with premium loading, what will be my premium payable?
questions.text:
Home Protection Scheme premiums are calculated based on several factors:
Outstanding housing loan on the flat
Loan repayment period
Type of loan (HDB concessionary or market rate)
Age and gender
Percentage share of cover of the outstanding housing loan
The amount of premium loading depends on the seriousness of your pre-existing health condition. If you are offered cover with premium loading, the Board will inform you of the total premium amount payable and you may decide whether to take it up.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Will I continue to be covered under the same premium rates for my existing Home Protection Scheme cover if I have developed new health condition(s) after my cover has been issued to me?
questions.text: If you have developed new health condition(s) after your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover has been issued, you will continue to be covered at the same premium rate under your existing HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How did the Government decide what should be covered under MediShield Life in this review?
questions.text:
In MediShield Life Council’s review, there were a few considerations:
First, MediShield Life was created as a national health insurance scheme to fully cover majority of the subsidised bills in public hospitals. Patients use their MediSave savings to pay the deductible and co-insurance. However, as medical bills have increased over the years, this coverage has dropped.
Second, the Government recognises that healthcare is now being provided outside of hospitals — like in outpatient, community, and home settings — areas that MediShield Life mostly doesn’t cover.
Lastly, new medical technologies have introduced life-saving treatments, like Cell, Tissue, and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTPs), which are also not covered by MediShield Life.
The recommended approach balances enhancing affordability for patients while keeping premiums manageable for everyone.

questions.title: What happens to the deductible that I have paid during my policy year prior to 1 Apr 2025?
questions.text:
The first phase of the increase in inpatient deductible, together with the refresh of existing MediShield Life claim limits, will take effect on 1 Apr 2025. These revised parameters will apply for all admissions on or after 1 Apr 2025.
Any deductible that you have paid during your policy year prior to 1 Apr 2025 will be counted towards the new deductible.
Assuming the same policy year, this means that if you have paid $1,500 in deductible before 1 Apr 2025, it would continue to count towards the new deductible that you have to pay for your admission on or after 1 Apr 2025.

questions.title: What is the difference between the inpatient and outpatient deductible? Do I have to pay both deductibles if I seek treatments in both settings?
questions.text:
The inpatient deductible applies to inpatient treatments, and the outpatient deductible applies to outpatient treatments.
Please note that the deductible paid for inpatient treatments in a policy year will also count towards the outpatient deductible, and vice versa.
For example, if a patient has paid at least $500 towards their deductible in the inpatient setting in a policy year, they would have fulfilled the outpatient deductible for the same policy year.

questions.title: What are the options for me if my subsidised bill is not fully covered by MediShield Life and MediSave?
questions.text:
For the minority of patients whose subsidised bills exceed the claim limit, they will still receive payouts from MediShield Life up to the relevant claim limit.
Examples of the claim limits that will be increased:
Intensive Care Unit ward from $2,200 to $5,140
Policy year claim limit from $150,000 to $200,000
Those who have difficulty affording their bills after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave can also apply for financial assistance such as MediFund by approaching the Medical Social Workers at the MediFund-approved institution at which the treatment is received, or appeal to MOH at 1800 222 3399 or write to them at moh_qsm@moh.gov.sg for MediSave use beyond limits.

questions.title: Which vaccines are approved for use in Singapore? Which of these vaccines are included in the National Vaccination Programme (NVP)?
questions.text:
Pfizer-BioNTech/Comirnaty, Moderna/Spikevax and Novavax/Nuvaxovid* are vaccines that are authorised by the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) for use in Singapore.
* Current stock of JN.1 Novavax/Nuvaxovid vaccine has expired since 31 May 2026 and no longer available under the NVP.
Under the NVP, vaccines authorised by the HSA for use in Singapore are free for all eligible Singaporean Citizens, Permanent Residents, Long Term Pass holders and certain Short Term Pass holders.

questions.title: How do mRNA vaccines work?
questions.text:
The COVID-19 mRNA vaccine consists of messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) that carry instructions to make the spike protein of the virus. The mRNA used in the vaccine is synthesised and not extracted from actual viruses.
After being given by intramuscular injection, the vaccine mRNA is taken up by cells which then produce the spike protein. This stimulates the production of a good antibody and cellular immune response to the spike protein that protects the vaccinated person because the spike protein is an important part of the SARS CoV-2 virus.
The spike proteins are however incapable of forming SARS CoV-2 viruses or causing COVID-19 infection. The vaccine mRNA only persists for two days before it is naturally broken down by the body. It does not enter the nucleus of cells and hence cannot interfere with the DNA of the vaccine recipient.

questions.title: Are mRNA vaccines a form of genetic modification?
questions.text:
No, they are not a form of genetic modification. The mRNA vaccine is in a form that is cannot be converted back to DNA. Since our human genome is made up of DNA, there is no possibility that the COVID-19 mRNA will interfere with or modify human DNA. The mRNA is completely degraded within 48 hours of introduction to the human body.
The spike protein generated through the introduction of the COVID-19 mRNA is recognised by the body’s immune system to develop an immune response (e.g. generation of antibodies), similar to what happens in a natural infection against COVID-19.

questions.title: Are the COVID-19 vaccines halal?
questions.text: The Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS)’s position is that COVID-19 vaccines are permissible for Muslim use. Please refer to MUIS’ religious position on the COVID-19 vaccine by using this link.

questions.title: What are the differences between the updated vaccines (e.g. updated Moderna/Spikevax or Pfizer BioNTech/Comirnaty) and the previous vaccines?
questions.text: The updated COVID-19 vaccines target newer strains of virus compared to the older versions of vaccines, can provide a stronger immune response against emerging strains, and therefore may confer better protection against COVID-19. The safety profiles of the updated vaccines are comparable to that of previous versions.

questions.title: What is myocarditis and pericarditis? Can the vaccine lead to myocarditis and pericarditis?
questions.text:
Myocarditis and pericarditis are inflammatory conditions affecting the heart muscles and the outer lining of the heart, respectively. Patients may present with symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath or abnormal heartbeats. Local incidence rates remain low and the cases are usually mild and recover well. This rare risk is predominantly observed in men aged 12-29 years and largely occurs within the first week after vaccination.
Male vaccinees aged 12-29 years who are receiving any dose of Moderna/Spikevax or Pfizer-BioNTech/Comirnaty COVID-19 vaccines are advised to refrain from participating in strenuous physical activities for one week after vaccination. During this period, vaccinees should promptly seek medical attention if they experience chest pain, shortness of breath, or abnormal heartbeats.

questions.title: Is COVID-19 vaccination safe for those with chronic illness such as hypertension, high cholesterol and diabetes?
questions.text: Persons with chronic illnesses are recommended to receive the vaccine for personal protection. The participants of Pfizer-BioNTech/Comirnaty’s and Moderna/Spikevax's clinical trials and other studies included persons with medical comorbidities, who were at risk of serious, life-threatening disease and death from COVID-19 infection, and demonstrated effectiveness with no safety concerns reported in this group.

questions.title: Will the COVID-19 vaccine cause infertility?
questions.text: There is currently no evidence that the COVID-19 vaccines can cause infertility in vaccine recipients.

questions.title: What happens if I develop an allergic reaction to my first dose?
questions.text:
You should seek medical attention, if you experience a possible allergic reaction to the vaccine (e.g. eye or lip swelling, hives, generalised skin rashes, breathlessness). Fever, chills, muscle pain, headaches, injection site pain are not allergic reactions.
You should discuss your suitability for subsequent COVID-19 vaccinations with your doctor. Persons with an allergic reaction assessed to be caused by the vaccine and who are advised by a doctor that they should not take subsequent doses of the vaccine, should adhere to the advice of the doctor.

questions.title: How effective is the vaccine?
questions.text: Vaccinated persons can be infected. However, vaccination offers good protection from severe disease and hospitalisation.

questions.title: Can the vaccines protect me against all strains of COVID-19?
questions.text: The updated COVID-19 vaccines can provide better protection against current and emerging strains compared to previous versions of the vaccines.

questions.title: I have recovered from COVID-19. How soon can I receive my next vaccination dose?
questions.text: Recently recovered persons being vaccinated should receive a vaccine dose at the recommended interval after any previous dose(s), and at least 28 days after the infection although an interval of three months from the infection is recommended for better effectiveness.

questions.title: Do all vaccine doses need to be of the same brand?
questions.text:
For those who are taking more than one initial dose of the vaccine*, the initial doses should be of the same brand. Additional doses of the COVID-19 vaccine can be of different brands, where applicable.
From time to time, the composition of a COVID-19 vaccine may be updated to target more recent virus variants. If you are due for a vaccine dose, you are recommended to receive the updated version of the vaccine. There is no need for your vaccine doses to be of the same composition.
*Persons who should take more than one initial dose include:
Immunocompromised persons (three initial vaccine doses)
Children aged 6 months to 4 years (two initial doses)

questions.title: Can I receive other non-COVID-19 vaccines at the same time as the COVID-19 vaccine? How long do I have to wait before getting other vaccines?
questions.text: The vaccines can be administered together with other non-COVID-19 vaccines across all ages.

questions.title: Can individuals with a history of allergies or anaphylaxis to other medications, drugs, food, insect stings, or unknown triggers (idiopathic) take COVID-19 vaccine?
questions.text:
Individuals with a history of anaphylaxis to other medications, drugs, food, insect stings, or unknown triggers (idiopathic) CAN be vaccinated.
There is no evidence to suggest that individuals with a history of anaphylaxis to non-vaccine related triggers are at higher risk of anaphylaxis to the COVID-19 vaccines.

questions.title: Medically vulnerable persons are recommended for COVID-19 vaccination in 2025/2026. Who are considered medically vulnerable persons?
questions.text:
Medically vulnerable persons are individuals who are at increased risk of severe COVID-19 due to significant medical risk factors. These include persons with chronic diseases of the heart, lungs, kidneys, liver and other organ systems.
A list of specific health conditions that will classify one as medically vulnerable can be found by using this link. If you are unsure, you should consult your doctor.

questions.title: Are there any children who should not get vaccinated?
questions.text:
There is no category of children or teens who absolutely should not get the vaccine, unless they have a known allergy to other vaccines or one of the vaccine’s components.
People with weakened immune systems, either from illness or medication, may still receive the vaccine because it is not a live vaccine i.e. a vaccine that uses a weakened form of a germ to prompt an immune response.
If your child has any medical condition that is not stable or is getting worse, he or she should postpone the vaccination until the medical condition is better controlled.
Parents are always encouraged to speak with their teen’s or child’s doctor/paediatrician if they have any questions or concerns.
topics: Covid-19 / Vaccine recommendations specific for children

questions.title: If my child/ward was recently infected with COVID-19, when should he/she take the vaccine?
