questions.text: The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme is targeted at Singaporeans with lower retirement savings to help them save more for retirement. As member’s circumstances such as income and housing can change over time, the annual cap ensures that the scheme will help seniors who require the support over a longer period.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Can I make the top-up by cash or NETS under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.text:
No, you can use PayNow or GIRO instead to make a cash top-up to yourself or your loved ones’ Retirement or Special Account.
For PayNow, your cash top-up will generally be credited almost instantly upon successful payment.
Consider making regular monthly or yearly cash top-ups conveniently via GIRO, without the hassle of completing the application form every time you top up.
You may refer to this FAQ “How do I make a cash top-up to receive the matching grant under Matched Retirement Savings Scheme" for the guide on how to top up.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: How can I check my existing recurring cash top-up arrangements for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.text: You can check your existing recurring cash top-up arrangements, including the recipients, amount of cash top-ups, and frequency (monthly or yearly) by accessing the Manage recurring cash top-ups for retirement form, under “Who you are making recurring top-ups to”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Will I still receive the full matching grant of $2,000 if my retirement savings exceed the current Basic Retirement Sum after topping up?
questions.text: Yes, you will receive the full matching grant of $2,000 as long as you are eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme for the year, and the total amount of cash top-ups you received was at least $2,000.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I received Matched Retirement Savings Scheme matching grants in the past, before the $20,000 lifetime cap took effect in 2025. Will the past matching grants count towards this $20,000 lifetime cap?
questions.text: The lifetime cap will only be applied from 2025 onwards. Matching grants received in the past for cash top-ups made prior to 2025, will not count towards the $20,000 lifetime cap.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: How do I check the amount of matching grant that I will receive?
questions.text:
To find out the grant amount that you will receive at the beginning of the next year on the cash top-ups which you had received, you can log in to your Retirement Dashboard.
In addition, the Dashboard will provide you with the remaining grant amount, if any, which you can receive if you make further top-ups.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Who can make cash top-ups to recipients who are eligible for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.text:
Anyone, including yourself, loved ones, employers or members of the community, can help members who are eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme to receive the matching grant by making cash top-ups to their Retirement or Special Account.
Learn more on how to make a cash top-up.
You may refer to this FAQ for more information on how to check your eligibility for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I missed the deadline to top up for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme grant last year. Can I make a top-up this year for last year's grant?
questions.text:
No, to qualify for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) grant, the PayNow cash top-up must be made by 31 December or the cash top-up via GIRO must be submitted by 31 October in the year of eligibility. This is stated in the eligibility notification sent at the beginning of the year of eligibility, and on the website.
You can still make a top-up to earn interest rates* of up to 6% per annum and boost your monthly payouts. You can also enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 for cash top-ups made to yourself and your loved ones in each calendar year. Please note that cash top-ups which attract MRSS grant will not qualify for tax relief.
*Based on the current 4% interest rate floor on Special and Retirement Account monies.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: As a platform worker, if I make a top-up to my three CPF accounts, how will my top-up be allocated to the respective accounts?
questions.text: As a platform worker, your top-up will be allocated to your Ordinary, Special/Retirement and MediSave account according to this allocation table.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: What are the benefits of using Direct Debit to pay for my CPF contributions?
questions.text:
You will enjoy the following benefits if you pay CPF contributions via Direct Debit:
You do not need to provide your payment details each time you pay CPF contributions.
You may set the payment deduction date when you submit your CPF contribution details.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes
Employer - Platform Operator / Setting up of Direct Debit Authorisation

questions.title: How do I update CPF Board of changes to my platform company’s particulars?
questions.text:
Write to us to update your platform company’s particulars (e.g. principal place of business, contact details, name of platform company).
The normal processing time is within three working days. An email notification will be sent to both the platform operator representative and the persons in charge of CPF contribution matters for platform workers once the particulars have been updated.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Updating platform operator’s particulars

questions.title: What is CPF EZPay File Transfer Protocol?
questions.text:
The CPF EZPay File Transfer Protocol (FTP) enables platform operators to prepare CPF submission details offline, and only log in to CPF EZPay when platform operators are ready to make the submission.
The file should be prepared according to these specifications. The file size for uploading is limited to 2 mega bytes and the file extension should end with "dtl", ".txt" or ".dat". If you require assistance to clarify or verify the file you have prepared, you can write-to-us.
To know more about CPF EZPay (FTP), you can refer to our user guide.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I use CPF EZPay as I have more than one CPF Submission Number (CSN) as a platform operator?
questions.text:
When using CPF EZPay, you can change your CSN without logging out, by clicking “Switch” at the top of the webpage. You may refer to this guide for visual references.
Do note that you must apply for Direct Debit for each CSN separately.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: Can I use the same CPF EZPay (FTP) file format that I currently use for my employees to make contributions for my platform workers?
questions.text: No. You will need to use the CPF EZPay (FTP) file format for platform workers to make contributions for your platform workers.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: What are Advice Codes and how do I, as a platform operator, use them when I upload my submission file via CPF EZPay (FTP)?
questions.text:
If you are submitting more than one file within the same day for the same CPF Submission Number (CSN), you will need to assign a different Advice Code for each file. Advice Codes act as a file numbering system to differentiate files created for different groups of platform workers belonging to the same CSN.
To know more about CPF EZPay (FTP), you can refer to our user guide.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: Which code should I use for the employment status field in my CPF EZPay FTP file submission?
questions.text: Employment status N is to be used for platform operators making CPF contributions to the platform worker for the first time. This is regardless of which platform operator CPF Submission Number is used. If not, employment status E is to be used.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How should I indicate contributions details for platform workers when making ad hoc CPF submissions?
questions.text:
When submitting CPF contributions for platform workers using CPF EZPay, you should:
Input platform workers’ net earnings (after FEDA) in the “Ordinary Wages” field.
Leave the “Additional Wages” blank as these do not apply to platform workers.
Input the total CPF contributions payable.
For details, please refer to CPF EZPay user guide for platform operators.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I know if I have completed my CPF submission?
questions.text:
Once you have completed your submission, you will see an acknowledgement page called “CPF EZPay Acknowledgment”. You can view or save this page by clicking on the printer icon which you will be prompted to download a PDF. You will not be able to save or print this acknowledgment page if you closed your internet browser.
You will also receive an email acknowledgement if your email address is registered in 'Account settings'.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay
Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How can I view my submission history in CPF EZPay as a platform operator?
questions.text:
You can view and save a copy of your CPF contribution details as a platform operator by following these steps:
Log in to CPF EZPay
Select “For UEN-registered entities” and login with your Singpass.
Key in your CPF Submission Number (CSN).
At Manage Records & Preferences, select “View / Amend / Delete Submission”.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How long does CPF Board takes to credit payments for CPF contributions and late CPF interest?
questions.text:
The service standards for crediting of payment for CPF contributions and late CPF interest are:
ServiceNormal Processing Time
CPF contributions submissionWithin three working days
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay
Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I apply for Corppass access to submit CPF contributions?
questions.text:
A UEN-registered entity can apply for Corppass access at the Corppass portal.
Before using CPF EZPay for the first time, you will need to perform a one-time setup in Corppass portal after you have obtained Corppass access. You can refer to this guide on how to set up and assign CPF EZPay in Corppass portal.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay
Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How can I grant my staff access to 'Other services'?
questions.text:
For UEN registered entity, your Corppass Admin or Sub-Admin will need to grant your authorised users access to “CPF SERVICES FOR EMPLOYERS AND BUSINESS PARTNERS” e-Service in the Corppass portal, before they can log in to the CPF website “Other services” using their Singpass.
Please refer to the step-by-step guide (PDF, 1.1MB) to assign the access rights.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number
Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I appoint or change Administrator for CPF EZPay as a platform operator?
questions.text: Your Corppass Admin or Sub-Admin can appoint or change your Administrator by assigning the “CPF EZPay” e-service to another authorised officer within Corppass portal. Please refer to this guide for more information.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: I have made errors in my CPF submission. How can I rectify them?
questions.text: If there are errors in your CPF submission, you should apply to make adjustment to the submission online immediately and no later than one year from the date of payment.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for adjustment of CPF contributions
Employer - Platform Operator / Adjustment/Refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: I have made duplicate CPF submissions for the same month in error. Can I request refund of the payment made for the incorrect submission?
questions.text: You should apply for a refund by selecting ‘Refund of payment made for entire submission’ in the online application. The application has to be made immediately and no later than one year from the date of payment.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions
Employer - Platform Operator / Adjustment/Refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: Why am I, as a platform operator, only allowed to request refunds or adjustments of CPF contributions within one year from the date of payment of the CPF contributions?
questions.text: Any errors in CPF contributions should be rectified early while the documentary evidence is fresh. To encourage platform operators and platform workers to check their CPF contributions and come forward to rectify errors as soon as possible, any request for refund and adjustment of CPF contributions paid in error must be made immediately and no later than one year from the date of payment of the CPF contributions.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Adjustment/Refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How long does it take for CPF Board to process my application for refund or adjustment of contributions paid to my platform workers?
questions.text:
Please refer to the table for the service standards in processing your application for refund or adjustment of contributions paid to your platform workers.
Service
Normal processing time
Refund and adjustment of contributions paid
Within one month upon receipt of the necessary information*
*This excludes the two working days that banks require to credit the monies to your bank account.

questions.title: How do I check the status of my application for refund and adjustment of contributions paid?
questions.text: You can check the status of your application for refund and adjustment of contributions paid online.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions
Employer - Platform Operator / Adjustment/Refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: When am I required to refund the platform worker’s share of excess CPF contributions?
questions.text: You are required to refund the platform worker’s share of excess CPF contributions to the platform worker once you receive the refund from the CPF Board.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Adjustment/Refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How do I refund the platform worker’s share of excess CPF contributions if the platform worker has stopped working with the platform?
questions.text: You may wish to liaise directly with the ex-platform worker on his/her preferred mode of payment for his/her share of excess CPF contributions.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Adjustment/Refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is the amount refunded for excess CPF contributions less than the total excess CPF contributions made to the platform worker for the year?
questions.text: The refunded amount for excess CPF contributions is based on the available balances in your platform worker’s CPF account(s). If there are insufficient funds for the full refund, you will receive a partial refund instead.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Adjustment/Refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: I overpaid the late payment interest. Must I apply for a refund of the excess amount?
questions.text:
CPF Board will automatically refund the excess late payment interest to:
Your bank account maintained with the Board if you have an existing Direct Debit arrangement with the Board; OR
Your Corporate PayNow bank account.
You will receive a letter informing you of the outcome of the refund.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions
Employer - Platform Operator / Adjustment/Refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: When is the due date to submit CPF contributions?
questions.text: The due date for CPF contributions is on the last day of the calendar month. Enforcement action would be taken if CPF contributions are not paid by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday). This includes imposing late payment interest charged at 1.5% per month commencing from the first day after the due date.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay
Employer - Platform Operator / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: Why is composition amount imposed on employers or platform operators?
questions.text:
It is an offence under the CPF Act for late and/or non-payment of CPF contributions and late payment interest. The composition amount is offered to allow defaulting employers or platform operators to settle their CPF offences out of court, after settling the CPF arrears.
Prosecution actions will be taken against employers or platform operators who do not settle the CPF arrears and compound the offence out of court, before the deadline given.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance
Employer - Platform Operator / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: My platform worker owes me money. Can I use the amount owed to me to offset the platform operator's share of CPF contributions that is payable on his net earnings?
questions.text: You are required to pay both the platform operator and platform worker’s share of CPF contributions based on the monthly net earnings payable to your platform worker at the prevailing CPF contribution rates.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: Can I agree to my platform worker’s request not to be paid CPF contributions so that he can get higher take-home pay?
questions.text: You should not agree to your platform worker’s request not to be paid CPF contributions so that he can get higher take-home pay. Failure to pay CPF contributions to a platform worker (i.e. Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident who is providing ride-hail or delivery services under a platform work agreement) is an offence under the CPF Act.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: If I am 55 and would like to make a CPF transfer to my loved ones, in what order will my savings be transferred?
questions.text:
If you are 55 or above, your CPF savings will be transferred to your loved ones in the following order:
OA
RA*
*If you use your RA savings for the transfer, you may no longer have enough savings to meet your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). In that case, the next time you apply for a withdrawal from your OA, a portion or all of the savings will be used to meet your FRS in the RA.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: If there are adjustments under CPF Investment Scheme in my Ordinary, Special or Retirement Account, what interest rate will be used?
questions.text: Any adjustments under the CPF Investment Scheme in your Ordinary, Special or Retirement Account will be based on the CPF interest rates for the respective account. The interest rate will not include the extra 1% interest that is paid on the first $60,000 of your combined balances.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will I receive notification in advance about my Ordinary Account savings being annuitised and streamed out as higher monthly CPF LIFE payouts?
questions.text: If you are among those whose Ordinary Account savings will be annuitised, we will send you a notification about one month before the annuitisation.

questions.title: Why is there a need to annuitise the non-withdrawable Ordinary Account savings as CPF LIFE monthly payout?
questions.text:
If you have not met your Full Retirement Sum, your Ordinary Account (OA) savings may not be withdrawn as a lump sum and are meant to be streamed out as monthly payouts.
Currently, if you are an existing CPF LIFE member, you need to instruct us to annuitise your OA savings to receive higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts.
With the changes from October 2023, we will automate this process and make it easier for you to enjoy higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts.

questions.title: How will the annuitisation of the non-withdrawable Ordinary Account (OA) savings as CPF LIFE monthly payout affect my eligibility to withdraw or service the housing commitments that are financed by my OA savings?
questions.text:
Your eligibility to make lump sum withdrawals from your Ordinary Account (OA) will not be affected. This is because only the OA savings that cannot be withdrawn in a lump sum will be annuitised to provide you with higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts.
The purpose of your CPF savings is to provide you with a stream of retirement income. If you still have housing obligations after starting your monthly payouts, you can use your monthly payouts or monies in excess of your Full Retirement Sum after this transfer to meet your housing needs.

questions.title: How much will my CPF LIFE monthly payouts increase after my non-withdrawable Ordinary Account savings are annuitised?
questions.text: After your non-withdrawable Ordinary Account savings are successfully annuitised, we will send you a notification to inform you of the revised CPF LIFE monthly payout.

questions.title: I do not wish to wait for the next automatic transfer of non-withdrawable monies from my Ordinary Account to my Retirement Account. Can I perform the transfer manually and boost my CPF LIFE payouts?
questions.text:
Yes, you can. Here are the steps to perform the transfer of your non-withdrawable monies from your Ordinary Account (OA) to your Retirement Account:
1) Access the Plan my monthly payouts service.
2) Under ‘Use more CPF savings to increase payouts’ in the second page, select the OA amount to be transferred to increase your CPF LIFE payout.
You may perform the above any time, as long as you have monies in your OA.

questions.title: How will I be eligible for the automatic transfer of non-withdrawable monies from my Ordinary Account to my Retirement Account?
questions.text: To be eligible for the automatic transfer, your non-withdrawable monies in your Ordinary Account must be sufficient to increase your CPF LIFE monthly payouts by at least $10.

questions.title: When will the automatic transfer of non-withdrawable monies from my Ordinary Account to my Retirement Account take place?
questions.text: For members who are eligible, the automatic transfer will take place once a year. You will receive a notification one month before the transfer occurs.

questions.title: I was a foreigner who was on CPF LIFE. What happened to my CPF LIFE plan?
questions.text:
The purpose of the CPF system is to help Singapore Citizens (SC) and Permanent Residents (PR) retire with peace of mind. In line with this, CPF members who are not SC or PR will have to close their CPF accounts and their participation in CPF schemes such as CPF LIFE will cease.
Find out more about closing your CPF accounts.

questions.title: Can I choose to retain my Ordinary Account savings instead of automatically disbursing them as payouts when my Retirement Account is depleted?
questions.text:
No, you cannot choose to retain your Ordinary Account (OA) savings. CPF is designed to provide you with an income in retirement. The auto-disbursement of your OA savings ensures that you continue to receive a steady stream of retirement income even when your Retirement Account has been depleted.
With the monthly payouts, you also have greater flexibility for your daily living expenses or your monthly housing instalments (if applicable).
If you wish to retain the monies in your CPF accounts to earn higher interest, you should consider options outside of CPF.

questions.title: Can I continue to use my CPF savings for the property or withdraw my Retirement Account savings above the Basic Retirement Sum in cash after discharging the CPF charge?
questions.text: No, after the CPF charge is discharged, no further CPF savings can be used for the property. If you are above 55, the property cannot be pledged for the withdrawal of your Retirement Account savings above the Basic Retirement Sum. If you wish to do so, a new CPF charge is required, and legal costs will be incurred in the creation and lodgement of the new CPF charge.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Voluntary Housing Refund

questions.title: Can I select my preferred deduction date instead of the default direct deduction date, which is set at two working days after the submission date?
questions.text: You can select your preferred deduction date. Please click on the calendar icon under the Direct Debit option to change the date before submitting the contributions.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay
Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I appeal for Home Protection Scheme coverage if my health condition has improved?
questions.text:
If your health condition has improved and you would like to be considered for Home Protection Scheme coverage, please submit a new application along with an up-to-date medical report detailing all your medical conditions. Please note that the cost of the medical report will be borne by you.
Find out more:
I would like to submit a medical report to support my Home Protection Scheme application. What is the information required in the medical report?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: I just received my CareShield Life (CSHL) renewal letter. I do not remember receiving any notifications about being enrolled into CSHL and note that my free-look-period (FLP) has ended. Can I still opt out of the scheme?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born between 1970 and 1979 who was covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme, you would have been enrolled in CareShield Life from 1 December 2021. A welcome notification package would have been sent to you in November 2021, informing you of your coverage and that after the end of the free-look-period (FLP) on 31 December 2023, you would continue to be covered under the scheme. We are unable to accede to opt-out requests for members whose FLP had ended on 31 December 2023.
CareShield Life offers lifelong protection against the costs of long-term care in the event of severe disability. Find out how CareShield Life protects you for life.

questions.title: What is Baby Bonus?
questions.text: The Baby Bonus Scheme supports parents in their decision to have more children by helping to manage the costs of raising children. It was introduced on 1 April 2001 and continuously enhanced to better support families. For more information on Baby Bonus Scheme and the application, please visit LifeSG or LifeSG mobile app.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on other government agencies

questions.title: How is the platform worker's share of CPF contributions on my CPF Contribution Alert derived?
questions.text:
Your platform worker’s share of CPF contributions on the CPF Contribution Alert is derived by applying the applicable CPF contribution rate to the total CPF contributions made by your platform operator.
You will receive one Contribution Alert for each contribution made by your platform operator(s). As the platform worker’s share of CPF contributions indicated on the CPF Contribution Alert is meant to be indicative, please use the platform worker CPF Contribution Calculator to determine the exact breakdown of your platform worker's share of CPF contributions based on your net earnings per month.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: What happens if I am not provided a Letter of Guarantee (LOG) from my employer for my medical treatment?
questions.text:
If you are a Work Permit holder, your employer should bear the costs of providing medical treatment (inpatient and outpatient), regardless of whether the conditions are work-related.
If you are denied from having medical treatment, you should contact MOM immediately.
MOM will take appropriate enforcement actions against errant employers who fail to provide medical treatment.

questions.title: I have been approved to be a Asbestos-removal Contractor. When will I receive the certificate?
questions.text:
The approval letter and certificate will be emailed to the email address indicated in your online application upon approval of your Asbestos-removal Contractor application.
If you have not received it after 7 working days, the appointed eService User of your company would have to send us an official request letter using your company letterhead, stating that you have not received the certificate.
topics: Workplace safety and health / Notify for asbestos work

questions.title: Must I reimburse my employee if their medical expenses were paid out of their MediSave or MediShield?
questions.text:
If medical costs were paid by your employee using cash, MediSave or MediShield, you must reimburse payment in the following order:
Reimburse the cash portion.
Reimburse the MediSave portion directly into your employee’s MediSave account.
Reimburse the MediShield portion directly to the MediShield insurer.
topics: Workplace safety and health / Work injury compensation

questions.title: I received a notification on the refund of CPF contributions paid in excess of the CPF Annual Limit for platform workers but I have yet to receive my share of the excess contributions from my (ex-)Platform Operator, what should I do?
questions.text: Your (ex-)Platform Operator has been notified to refund your share of excess CPF contributions to you, if any. You should contact your (ex-)Platform Operator directly regarding the refund.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I would like to terminate my GIRO arrangement as I will be selling my property. What should I do?
questions.text:
You may terminate your GIRO payment plan by contacting your bank directly. However, if you have an existing GIRO arrangement that allows you to make payment for more than 1 of your own taxes (e.g. Income Tax, Property Tax or GST) or for property tax for more than 1 of your properties, please call IRAS on 1800 356 8300 or email us to terminate the relevant GIRO arrangement pertaining to the property that you have just sold/ in the process of selling.
Please ensure that all outstanding taxes are settled in full, before you terminate the GIRO arrangement.

questions.title: How can I verify the amount of my share for the excess CPF contributions refunded by my employer?
questions.text: You can use the Additional Wage ceiling calculator to verify the amount of your share for the excess CPF contributions refunded by your employer.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is the amount refunded to me by my employer less than the amount deducted from my CPF account(s) for the refund of excess CPF contributions?
questions.text: Generally, the amount deducted from the employee’s CPF account(s) for the refund of excess contributions above the CPF Annual Limit comprises both the employer and employee’s shares of the excess. As your employer is required to refund you the employee’s share, the refund you received from your employer may be lower than that deducted from your CPF account(s). You can use the Additional Wage ceiling calculator to verify the amount of your share.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is the amount deducted from my CPF account(s) for the refund less than the excess CPF contributions made for the year?
questions.text: The final refunded amount is based on the available balances in your CPF account(s). If there are insufficient funds in your account(s) for full refund of the excess contributions, the excess will be partially refunded.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I check if my employer has correctly capped the CPF contributions on the Additional Wages (AW) payable at the AW ceiling and/or CPF Annual Limit?
questions.text: You can use the Additional Wage ceiling calculator to check the CPF contributions payable on the Additional Wages paid.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Can I request CPF Board to refund the employee's share of excess CPF contributions directly to my employee?
questions.text:
The full excess CPF contributions will be refunded to the employer. The employer is required to refund the employee’s share of excess CPF contributions, if any, directly to the employee.
You can use the Additional Wage ceiling calculator to calculate the excess contributions. The calculator will help you determine the total excess amount, and the breakdown for employer and employee’s shares.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: What is the CPF Annual Limit?
questions.text: The CPF Annual Limit sets the total mandatory and voluntary CPF contributions that can be made to an employee’s CPF accounts in a calendar year; the current CPF Annual Limit is $37,740.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I find out if my Large Family MediSave Grant is successfully credited?
questions.text: You can log in to your CPF account using your Singpass to view your Transaction history to check if the Large Family MediSave Grant has been credited into your MediSave Account.
topics: Large Families Scheme / Large Family MediSave Grant (LFMG)

questions.title: What happens if the child's mother passes away after receiving the Large Family MediSave Grant payment?
questions.text: For persons who have passed away after receiving the Large Family MediSave Grant payment, their Central Provident Fund (CPF) savings, including MediSave balance, will be distributed to their beneficiaries in cash according to their CPF nomination or through the Public Trustee's Office if no CPF nominations were made.
topics: Large Families Scheme / Large Family MediSave Grant (LFMG)

questions.title: Why is the QR code unsupported when I tried to make payment with my LifeSG credits?
questions.text: Only NETS QR and PayNow UEN QR codes from supported merchants will be accepted. Please check that it’s a QR code that can be recognised by the LifeSG app.
topics: Large Families Scheme / Technical queries relating to the usage of Credits

questions.title: Why am I not able to spend my credits even though the merchant accepts PayNow QR?
questions.text: The credits in the LifeSG application can only be spent at merchants who accept payment by “Scan and Pay” via PayNow UEN QR or NETS QR. PayNow QRs registered to their personal mobile numbers or NRIC instead of a company UEN are not accepted.
topics: Large Families Scheme / Technical queries relating to the usage of Credits

questions.title: Who can make cash top-ups to persons with disabilities to qualify for the matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?
questions.text: Anyone such as the person with disability, their loved ones, employers or members of the community, can make the cash top-ups to qualify for the matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Do employers / platform operators enjoy tax benefits if they top up to their employees / platform workers' CPF accounts?
questions.text: Employers / platform operators will enjoy 1:1 corporate tax deduction, which will be deductible against their taxable income. This encourages employers to make cash top-ups to their employees' retirement accounts, thereby helping to build retirement adequacy.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: For persons with disabilities below age 55, where will the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) grant be credited?
questions.text: For persons with disabilities below age 55, the matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) will be credited into their Special Account (SA), to grow their retirement savings as per the policy objective of MRSS. This is credited at the beginning of the following year. For persons who have a Retirement Account (RA) such as those who are under the Reduced Life Expectancy (RLE) scheme, the matching grant will be credited into their RA.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I am a person with disability aged 55 and above and had received Matched Retirement Savings Scheme matching grants before its expansion to include persons with disabilities of all ages. Will my past grants count towards the $20,000 lifetime limit?
questions.text: Matching grants received for cash top-ups made prior to 2025 will not count towards the $20,000 lifetime limit. Matching grants received for cash top-ups made in 2025 or after will count towards the same $20,000 lifetime limit. This aligns with the intent of Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) to help those with lower retirement savings save more and boost their retirement payouts, which remains relevant regardless of whether these members have benefited from MRSS in the past.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Do I enjoy tax relief for cash top-ups made to persons with disabilities?
questions.text:
If you are making a cash top-up to a member eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS), including persons with disabilities, the first $2,000 of your cash top-up will enable your recipient to enjoy the matching grant of up to $2,000 per year from the Government and will thus not be eligible for tax relief.
You can continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year for your cash top-ups that do not attract the MRSS matching grant ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones).
Find out more on the conditions to qualify for tax relief.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: What is the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
The Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) aims to help Singapore Citizens aged 55 to 70 (inclusive) with lower MediSave savings to boost their healthcare savings by matching voluntary cash top-ups made to their MediSave Account (MA). The scheme is implemented in 2026 for a period of five years.
Under the MMSS, the Government will match every dollar of cash top-up to the MA of eligible members up to $1,000 per year. The matching grant by the Government will be disbursed to eligible members in the following year.
The scheme helps eligible members pay for approved healthcare insurance premiums and approved medical treatments.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: When will my eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme be assessed and do I need to apply?
questions.text:
Members’ eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) will be automatically assessed annually. You do not need to apply for the scheme.
MMSS is implemented in January 2026 for five years. You will be notified at the beginning of each year if you are eligible for the scheme for the year via email or post. Eligibility information will be available around the 2nd or 3rd week of January of each year and notifications to eligible members will be sent out around end January.
You can also check your eligibility for the MMSS via the Healthcare dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Who can make cash top-ups to recipients who are eligible to receive the matching grant under Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
Anyone, including the member himself/herself, his/her loved ones, employers or members of the community, can help the eligible member receive the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme by making cash top-ups to the member’s MediSave Account.
For more information on how to make a cash top-up to MediSave Account, you may refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What should I do if I have already submitted a refund application prior to the refund initiated by the CPF Board?
questions.text: No further action is required by you. The CPF Board will consider the total contributions paid for the year and automatically refund any excess contributions paid above the CPF Annual Limit and/or Additional Wage ceiling.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How do I check if I have paid excess CPF contributions for my employee?
questions.text:
You can refer to the monthly CPF Record of Payment at CPF EZPay to check the total CPF contributions paid for your employee. Your employee would have exceeded the CPF Annual Limit if the total amount contributed for the year is more than $37,740.
To calculate the share of excess CPF contributions paid by the employer and employee respectively, you can use the Additional Wage ceiling calculator.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How will the employer be notified about the auto refund of excess CPF contributions, and what information will be provided?
questions.text:
Employers will receive two notifications regarding the auto-refund of excess CPF contributions. In the first notification, employers will be notified on the impending refund of the excess CPF contributions paid for the relevant year. After the refund is successfully processed, employers will receive a second notification with the refund details such as the affected employee’s details, refund month(s) and refunded amount.
The affected employee(s) will also receive two similar notifications.
It is important to note that refund details are only available in the second notification, as the refund is subject to the availability of funds in the employee’s CPF account(s).
To ensure notifications are received, employer particulars must be up-to-date. Employers can update their contact details under “Account settings”.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: I was notified that the total CPF contributions received have exceeded the CPF Annual Limit of $37,740, and the excess CPF contributions will be refunded to my employer. When should my employer return my share of excess CPF contributions?
questions.text:
Generally, the refund of the excess contributions will be processed and paid to your employer within 10 days after you are first notified of the impending refund unless further assessment is required.
We will notify you and your employer after the refund is successfully processed. Your employer is required to compute and return your share of the excess CPF contributions, if any, after receiving the notification.
You should contact your employer directly regarding the refund.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: As a work pass holder, how do i get a Singpass?
questions.text:
To obtain a Singpass, you can either:
Visit Singpass website to apply for your Singpass online
Visit any of the Singpass counters located islandwide in-person.
topics: Work passes and permits / Work passes

questions.title: How long does it take to process my report on late, non-payment or underpayment of CPF contributions?
questions.text:
Please refer to the table for our service standards for processing your report on late, non-payment or underpayment of CPF contributions:
ServiceNormal Processing Time
Report on late/non/underpayment of CPF contributions from employers.You will receive an acknowledgement of your report within five working days. A case officer will be assigned to assist you thereafter.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Will I still be considered opted-in if I stop doing platform work for a while or change platform operator after opting in?
questions.text: Yes, your opt-in status is permanent after opting in and applies to all platform operators you work with.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is my final MediSave deduction amount different from the amount provided to me before my hospital admission/in my care cost form?
questions.text:
The final MediSave deduction amount may differ from the estimated amount provided during financial counselling at the medical institution due to various reasons, such as changes to the treatment, longer than expected stay etc.
For clarifications on your final medical bill, please approach the medical institution where you received treatment at for assistance.

questions.title: Why are my MediSave and MediShield Life claims not processed after my visit/hospital discharge?
questions.text:
Medical institutions may take up to about two weeks from the date of your visit/hospital discharge to submit your MediShield Life and MediSave claims. If you are on an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), it may take longer than two weeks as your claim(s) will first be submitted to your IP insurer for assessment.
Please refer to the table of processing time from the day CPFB receives the claims from your Medical Institution or insurer.

questions.title: I have a Letter of Guarantee (LOG) from my employer/insurer. How do I use it to pay for my medical expenses?
questions.text:
You may provide the Letter of Guarantee (LOG) to the hospital at admission. The hospital will be able to advise you on the billing arrangements and send the bill to your employer/insurer. If your employer/insurer is paying only part of your hospital expenses, the hospital will also assist you to submit the MediShield and MediSave claims on your behalf.
Please review the terms of your LOG carefully. For clarifications about your LOG or payment arrangements, please approach the hospital and/or employer/insurer directly.

questions.title: How do I know if my MediSave can be used for the medical treatment that I have received or will be receiving?
questions.text: Please approach the medical institution where you have received or will be receiving medical treatments from to check if MediSave can be used to pay for the expenses. Please refer to the list of medical institutions participating in the MediSave scheme. The medical institution is best-placed to advise you whether MediSave can be used for the specific medical treatment it is providing and the expected expenses.

questions.title: I paid my medical bill in full using cash, but my employer or insurer has since made a payment to the medical institution for the same bill. How can I be reimbursed for the cash I paid?
questions.text:
Cash reimbursements for medical claims are handled between the patients and their employers or insurers.
You may wish to contact your Medical Institution and/or employer or insurer for assistance in processing the reimbursement for the cash you paid.

questions.title: Where can I get the Medical Claims Authorisation Form Single Institution - MCAF(S)?
questions.text:
You may submit via this link https://for.sg/skh-bo-mcaf.
Completion guide for MCAF(S) FormSG:
For Patient's signing only: https://for.sg/mcaf-guide-patient
For Additional MediSave Payer: https://for.sg/mcaf-guide-amp
For Individuals Signing on Behalf of Others: https://for.sg/mcaf-guide-onbehalf

questions.title: How do I find out about the various healthcare financing schemes and subsidies in Singapore?
questions.text: You may refer to the Ministry of Health website Schemes and subsidies | Ministry of Health (moh.gov.sg) for more information on MediSave, MediShield Life, and many other schemes and subsidies.

questions.title: How do I view and/or pay my bills?
questions.text:
In line with our commitment towards conserving the environment, we are going digital and would like to encourage all patients to go paperless.
You may view and/or pay your bills via Health Buddy*, HealthHub, or https://for.sg/mpay (with or without SingPass).
*Bills are available up to twelve months from your visit/discharge date. Bills that has been paid can be viewed under the ‘History’ tab and any outstanding bills will be under ‘Current’ tab on Health Buddy App.
For other payment modes, you may refer here https://www.skh.com.sg/patient-care/inpatient-day-surgery/Pages/hospital-bill-payments.aspx

questions.title: How much interest would I save if I start my education loan repayment early?
questions.text:
Based on a principal amount of $12,000, interest per month is $25 (based on 2.5% p.a1). If you were to repay the education loan upon graduation or leaving your course of study instead of over 10 years, you would have saved $4,010.
1Interest is calculated monthly and compounded (i.e. added to principal amount and accrued interest) on a yearly basis, pegged at the prevailing CPF Ordinary Account interest rate of 2.5%.
Please inform us of your intention to start early repayment of your education loan through this form and we will process your request accordingly.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: My education loan repayment is deferred. Would the interest on the outstanding loan amount continue to accrue during the deferment period?
questions.text:
Yes, interest will continue to accrue until the education loan is fully repaid. The amount withdrawn for education, plus the accrued interest must be repaid using cash, to fully restore your lending member’s CPF savings. This ensures that the member would not lose out on the interest they would have earned had the money not been withdrawn for education purposes.
To reduce the interest payable, you can still make repayment during the deferment period through the "Manage education loan repayments" form and check the latest outstanding amount by accessing your Education Dashboard.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What should the Sender ID of the CDC Vouchers link be? Is it gov.sg or RedeemSG?
questions.text:
From 1 July 2024, the Singapore government has launched a new security measure - gov.sg, a single SMS Sender ID to be used across government agencies. This whole-of-government effort to transition to a single SMS Sender ID will make it easier for the public to verify authentic government communications, with greater confidence and accuracy. Moving forward, the public can expect SMSes from government agencies to come from the gov.sg SMS Sender ID, and not from individual government agencies' Sender IDs.
PA/CDC aligns with this national effort to help residents access and respond to legitimate communications from the government, such as the CDC Vouchers Scheme.
topics: CDC Vouchers (Residents) / Claiming of CDC Vouchers

questions.title: What other moves are the Government making to ensure Assistive Technology (AT) remains affordable?
questions.text:
The Assistive Technology Fund (ATF) provides subsidies of up to 90% for PwDs who require AT devices. Subsidy rates are regularly reviewed to ensure that AT remains affordable.
Open Door Programme (ODP)-registered employers can also apply for grants and employment support services such as the Job Redesign Grant to support redesigning of jobs such as purchases of equipment (including AT devices) and workplace modification.
PwDs who require more financial support in purchasing AT devices may approach SG Enable for further assistance.

questions.title: Why is the Government expanding the coverage of the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) to Singaporeans with disabilities below age 55?
questions.text:
From 1 January 2026, MRSS will be expanded to include younger Singaporeans with disabilities to give them a greater boost for retirement by helping them to start building up their retirement savings earlier via cash top-ups to the CPF Special Account (SA).
Eligible persons with disabilities can receive a dollar-for-dollar matching grant of up to $2,000/year, with a lifetime limit of $20,000 from the Government on cash top-ups received in their CPF SA. Persons with disabilities will need to register as a person with disability and will still be subject to other MRSS eligibility criteria such as CPF balances, monthly income and Annual Value of their residential property. More details on how to register as a person with disability will be released in the second half of 2025.

questions.title: Will I get into trouble if my actual income declared to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) in the following year is different from the estimated income which I provided via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) digital services?
questions.text: No, as the revenue and expenses information you provided via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) digital services is only an estimate of your business outlook for the year. You are still required to separately declare to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) your actual net trade income (NTI), which may differ from the estimated revenue and expenses provided for the purposes of CAYE.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Why do I still need to declare my income to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) when I have already provided my estimated income via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) digital services?
questions.text: The revenue and expenses information you provided via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) digital services is only an estimate of your business outlook for the year and is only used to compute your CAYE contribution rate. You are still required to separately declare your actual net trade income (NTI) in the following year to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Can I receive my net service fee payments through methods other than PayNow?
questions.text:
You will only be able to use the bank account registered to your PayNow to receive service fee payments.
Please ensure that you have registered for PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address) so that you receive your service fee payments promptly.
You may approach your bank if you need more information on how to sign up.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What happens to my recurring CPF transfer arrangement if I have reached my top-up limit or have insufficient Ordinary Account savings?
questions.text: If you have insufficient top-up limit or Ordinary Account (OA) savings, we will transfer up to your remaining top-up limit or available OA savings. Please note that your recurring arrangement will be stopped after two consecutive unsuccessful transfers (where no amount is transferred).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I am below 55 years old. Can I set up recurring CPF transfers from my Ordinary Account to Special Account?
questions.text: The recurring CPF transfer e-Service is currently only available for members aged 55 and above. If you are below 55 years old, you may wish to make a one-time CPF transfer from your Ordinary Account to Special Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I check my existing recurring CPF transfers arrangements?
questions.text: You can check your existing recurring CPF transfer arrangement by accessing the Manage recurring cash top-ups and CPF transfers for retirement form, under “Who you are making recurring top-ups to”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I make monthly transfers of my CPF employment contributions from my Ordinary Account to Retirement Account?
questions.text:
If you are aged 55 and above and would like to transfer your monthly CPF employment contributions regularly from your Ordinary Account (OA) to Retirement Account (RA), you can do so by setting up recurring CPF transfers . With this recurring transfer service, you can conveniently earn higher interest on your CPF employment contributions credited to your OA and build up your retirement savings in your RA.
Upon successful application, your recurring transfer will take effect from the following month on the 18th.
Please note that CPF transfers are irreversible. The savings are set aside to boost your monthly payouts in retirement and cannot be withdrawn for other purposes.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I make recurring CPF transfers to my loved ones?
questions.text: The recurring CPF transfer e-Service is currently only available for members aged 55 and above to make CPF transfers to their own Retirement Account. If you wish to make CPF transfer to your loved ones, you may make a one-time CPF transfer instead.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I set up yearly CPF transfers from my Ordinary Account to Retirement Account?
questions.text:
The recurring CPF transfer e-Service currently allows monthly CPF transfers only. By setting up recurring CPF transfers, you can easily transfer your monthly CPF working contributions received in your Ordinary Account to your Retirement Account.
If you intend to make a CPF transfer once a year, you may wish to do so via the one-time CPF transfer form.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: When does my recurring CPF transfer take place?
questions.text:
The transfer from your Ordinary Account (OA) to Retirement Account (RA) takes place on the 18th of each month.
If you set up a new recurring CPF transfer, the transfer will take effect from the following month upon successful application.
Note: Please ensure that you maintain sufficient funds in your OA for the transfer. The recurring CPF transfer arrangement will be stopped if there are two consecutive unsuccessful transfers. There is no penalty for unsuccessful transfers.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can someone else withdraw my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) which has been credited via GovCash, if they know my Payment Reference Number (PRN)?
questions.text:
It is not possible to withdraw your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) benefits credited into GovCash using just the Payment Reference Number as GovCash uses the Singpass facial verification technology to authenticate users during the withdrawal of Government cash benefits from OCBC ATMs. The facial verification technology incorporates a liveness-detection capability that blocks the use of photographs, videos or masks during the verification process.
This security feature prevents any fraudulent withdrawal of Government benefits by third parties using photographs or videos belonging to the beneficiary. This ensures that only the eligible Singaporean can perform the withdrawal of his or her government benefits.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Where can I obtain my Payment Reference Number (PRN) for my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) which was paid to me via GovCash?
questions.text: If you are eligible for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS), and received payment via GovCash, you will receive an 8-digit Payment Reference Number (PRN) via an email or SMS after the PCTS payment has been credited.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Can you re-send my Payment Reference Number (PRN) to me?
questions.text: You can retrieve your Payment Reference Number (PRN) via logging on to the govbenefits website using your Singpass. You can find your PRN by selecting “GovCash PRN” that is found at the menu on the left. You will be directed to the page where your PRN will be displayed.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Will notifications be sent to all platform workers on their Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payments?
questions.text:
Only eligible platform workers will receive notifications on their Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) benefits if they have an email address or mobile number registered with CPF Board, and after the payment has been credited.
Platform workers who are not eligible for PCTS will not receive notifications on PCTS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Why is the option to withdraw GovCash only available in $10 denominations and what can I do with my balance GovCash?
questions.text:
The minimum withdrawal amount at the ATMs is $10, so GovCash withdrawals are made in $10 denominations. If your GovCash balance is less than $10, you can accumulate funds for your next withdrawal.
Alternatively, you can transfer the balance to your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account, use it to make payments at merchants with PayNow/NETS QR codes, or transfer it to your family/friends by scanning the PayNow QR code using the LifeSG mobile app.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme
Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Where can I seek help regarding my GovCash withdrawal?
questions.text: If you are unable to verify your identity via Singpass Face Verification at an OCBC ATM after several attempts or if you require assistance with your GovCash withdrawals, you can visit a NEW ATM located at selected OCBC branches (refer to OCBC website for latest list of New ATMs) during the branch operating hours. OCBC Digital Ambassadors will be available to assist you.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme
Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: How do I check my GovCash balance?
questions.text: To check your GovCash balance, visit any OCBC ATMs with your 8-digit Payment Reference Number (PRN). Upon successful authentication, you will be able to view your GovCash balance. Alternatively, you can log in to the LifeSG mobile app using your Singpass to view your balance and transaction history.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme
Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: What is the bank account that is linked to PayNow with my NRIC number?
questions.text:
The information about your bank account that is linked to PayNow with your NRIC number is maintained with the bank and not known to CPF Board. Check with your bank directly on the specific bank account that is linked to PayNow with your NRIC number.
CPF Board only needs your NRIC number to make CPF payments to your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support
Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Will I still get my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) if I do not use PayNow-NRIC?
questions.text: Platform workers who do not register for PayNow-NRIC will still receive Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment based on existing modes of payment, i.e. through your bank account registered to receive Government benefits or through GovCash. You may check and update your bank account information via the govbenefits website.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Can the Government credit my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) to me via PayNow-Mobile? Why do I need to register my NRIC with PayNow to receive government payments?
questions.text: We can only credit your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) to you via PayNow-NRIC as NRIC is an unchanged proxy issued by the Government that serves as a unique identifier for each individual. Unlike the NRIC, mobile numbers are not unique to the individual and may be subject to change. To ensure that the money is credited to the correct recipient, we are using NRIC as the proxy for government payments via PayNow.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Where can I view details of my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment?
questions.text: Eligible platform workers will receive notifications for their Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment via email or SMS, after the PCTS is disbursed every month. Please refer to your bank statement of your PayNow-NRIC linked bank account or the bank account that you have registered to receive Government benefits.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Why have I not received any notification about my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment even though I am eligible, and the payment has been credited?
questions.text: You will not receive any notifications on your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment if you have not registered your email address or mobile number with CPF Board. To receive notifications, you may update your mobile number or email address via my cpf digital services - Account Settings with your Singpass.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Where can I view details of my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) eligibility?
questions.text: Eligible platform workers will receive notifications sent via email/SMS, after Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payments are made in each month. You can also refer to your bank statement of the PayNow-NRIC linked bank account or the bank account that you have registered to receive Government benefits. The crediting to your bank account will be reflected as “OTHR GOV GOV”. You can use the PCTS calculator to estimate the amount of PCTS you may be eligible to receive.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: If I work for multiple platforms, how will my eligibility for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) be assessed?
questions.text:
To qualify for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS), your total income for the month must not exceed $3,000. This includes your net earnings (gross earnings minus the Fixed Expense Deduction Amount) from each platform operator you work for, along with any income from other employment sources, which will all be summed up to determine whether your income exceeds $3,000.
If your total income does not exceed $3,000:
Your PCTS amount will be computed based on net earnings from each platform operator separately (i.e. per-platform basis), and then summed up. This is in view that all your platform operators will calculate and contribute CPF for you separately (i.e. per-platform basis), and PCTS is intended to offset part of the increase in CPF contributions made.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: What is the Retirement Account for?
questions.text:
The savings in your Retirement Account (RA) is meant to provide you with payouts in retirement. You can start your payouts anytime from your payout eligibility age of 65.
Find out how your RA is created when you turn 55.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: In setting aside the Full Retirement Sum in my Retirement Account, why are my Special Account savings transferred before my Ordinary Account savings?
questions.text: The savings in your Special Account (SA) are meant for your retirement needs, while your Ordinary Account (OA) savings can be used to meet shorter-term expenditure needs such as housing. Hence, when you turn 55, SA savings are first transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) to help you set aside the retirement sum, which will eventually be streamed out as monthly payouts when you reach your payout eligibility age.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Can I choose to transfer more savings from the Special Account to the Ordinary Account since I am still servicing my housing loan/education loan etc.?
questions.text:
When your Special Account (SA) is closed after your Retirement Account (RA) is created, any remaining savings in your SA that are withdrawable on demand will be transferred to your Ordinary Account (OA).
You may use the portion transferred to your OA for your housing loan/education loan (subject to applicable limits) or choose to withdraw them anytime for your immediate needs. You cannot choose to allocate more SA savings or your future RA contributions to your OA to service your housing/education loan, etc.
If you are using your OA savings to service your housing loan, you may apply to reserve your OA savings prior to turning 55 years old for housing payments beyond age 55. The amount reserved in your OA will not be transferred to your RA.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: I belong to the generation born before 1958 and can withdraw a portion of my Special Account (SA) savings even though I have not set aside my Full Retirement Sum. Will I continue to be able to withdraw after my SA is closed?
questions.text:
When your Special Account (SA) is closed, the amount you could have withdrawn from your SA will be transferred to your Ordinary Account, and you can continue to withdraw this amount anytime.
If you continue to work after your SA is closed, any new contributions that used to be allocated to your SA will instead be allocated to your Retirement Account (RA), up to your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). This will go towards meeting your long-term retirement needs, by allowing you to receive higher monthly payouts from your Payout Eligibility Age. If you have immediate needs, you can choose to set aside up to half the FRS using your property and withdraw your savings above the Basic Retirement Sum in your RA.
If you require further assistance, you may write to us.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Does the interest earned on my retirement savings form part of the retirement sum that I am required to set aside at age 55?
questions.text: No, the interest earned on your retirement savings does not form part of the retirement sum that you are required to set aside at 55.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Which accounts will my CPF contributions be allocated to after I turn age 55 and my Special Account is closed?
questions.text:
After you turn 55, CPF contributions allocated to your Special Account will be fully allocated to your Retirement Account (RA) instead, up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS), to boost retirement payouts.
If you have set aside the FRS in the RA, these contributions will be channelled to your Ordinary Account (OA).
To build up your retirement savings, you can now conveniently set up monthly recurring CPF transfers from your OA to your RA, allowing you to continue earning higher interest rates on your contributions.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Which CPF accounts will my voluntary top-ups be allocated to after I turn 55 and my Special Account is closed?
questions.text: If you are aged 55 and above, the portion of voluntary top-ups that goes to your Special Account (SA) currently will be allocated to your Retirement Account (RA) up to the Full Retirement Sum. Once you have set aside the Full Retirement Sum in your RA, it will be allocated to your Ordinary Account.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Why am I not eligible for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) if I do not opt in to the increased CPF contributions?
questions.text: Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) is intended to offset part of the year-on-year increase in contribution rates to platform workers’ Ordinary Account (OA) and Special Account (SA) or Retirement Account (RA) for lower-income platform workers (i.e. earning $3,000 or less per month). Platform workers who do not opt in to the increased CPF contributions will not experience increases in OA, SA, RA contributions, and are thus not eligible for PCTS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Why is the MediShield Life claim limit for a particular combination treatment not the sum of all the claim limits for individual cancer drugs in that combination?
questions.text:
If a particular combination treatment is cost-effective, the MediShield Life (MSHL) claim limit is sized to be sufficient to cover the post-subsidy cost of the entire combination in Public Healthcare Institutions (PHIs). In some cases, the claim limit for the entire combination is the same as the highest-cost drug in that combination because the cost of the other drugs in the PHIs are low and can therefore be adequately covered by the same claim limit.
If a particular combination treatment is not cost-effective, the MSHL claim limit is pegged to the highest individual claim limit of the drugs in the combination. Doctors and patients are encouraged to use treatments that have been assessed to be cost-effective, for which MSHL claim limits have been sized for.

questions.title: I have substantial balances in my Ordinary and Special or Retirement Accounts. Can I use the available funds to offset my MediSave payable?
questions.text: The Ordinary, Special, or Retirement Accounts, serve different purposes from the MediSave Account. While the Ordinary and Special or Retirement Account savings are meant for retirement or housing needs, your MediSave Account savings are for your healthcare needs. Thus, the balances in your Ordinary and Special or Retirement Accounts cannot be used to settle your MediSave payable, so as not to affect your retirement adequacy.

questions.title: Can I provide for alternate nominee(s) who will receive my CPF monies only if my sole nominee passed away before me?
questions.text:
Under the current CPF laws, making such a nomination is not possible.
If your sole nominee had passed on before you, you can make a new nomination and nominate alternate nominee(s). We encourage CPF members to review their nominations regularly and make a new nomination whenever required.
Alternatively, to give effect to your intent, instead of nominating an individual to receive your CPF, you may wish to nominate a trust company or a trustee and set up a trust agreement to control how your CPF savings should be distributed. For more information, you can read about nominating a trust company or a trustee via this link.

questions.title: How do I select the correct employment status when submitting CPF contributions for my employees?
questions.text:
Select the employment status based on your employee's situation when submitting CPF contributions:
New (N)
For submitting the first CPF contribution when an employee joins your company
Existing (E)
For submitting monthly CPF contributions for current employees who have completed at least one month of employment
Left (L)
For submitting the final CPF contribution when employment ends
New & Leaving (O)
For submitting CPF contributions when employment begins and ends in the same month
Example: Employee starts on 1 March and resigns on 15 March
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I check for ongoing CPE events?
questions.text: For details on upcoming CPE events, please refer to the Event Calendar.
topics: Continuing Professional Education (CPE) / For OOB Practitioners

questions.title: How do I update changes to my particulars?
questions.text: For any change to your personal particulars, please refer to "Update particulars" page for more information on the relevant documents and processes.

questions.title: How long will it take to process my application? Can I request for my application to be expedited?
questions.text: The average processing time is 8 to 10 weeks from the date of receipt of your application and payment of the application fee. This excludes the time required for mailing (if applicable).
topics: Verification of Registration/ Enrolment/ Certificate of Good Standing (CGS)

questions.title: How do I find a registered Allied Health Professional?
questions.text:
You can search and view the register online via “Search for Allied Health Professionals and Providers” at AHPC’s website. Allied health professionals who are registered with the AHPC are listed online as long as they have a valid practising certificate.
A search may be done by either (i) entering the full or partial name of the allied health professional or (ii) entering his/her registration number under ‘More Search Options’.

questions.title: My PC application has been approved. How do I view and download the e-Certs?
questions.text:
You will be able to view and download the e-PC that is current and valid. Once the e-PC is no longer valid, e.g. validity of e-PC has expired, you will no longer be able to view/download it.
To view and download your valid e-PC, please follow the steps below:
Log in to the Professional Registration System (PRS)
At the left menu, click "Administration" followed by "View Certificates"
Click on the hyperlink under "PC Period"
The e-PC would then display in a pop-up window:
For most mobile device users, the e-PC should download and display automatically;
For laptop/computer uses, please follow instructions on your internet browser to view and download a copy of the e-PC.

questions.title: How long will it take for my appeal to be processed?
questions.text: Your appeal will be processed within 15 working days.

questions.title: Will the Act provide any protection for SRH staff, such as care staff and social workers who are abused by clients?
questions.text:
MSF takes the safety and well-being of our social service professionals very seriously, and we do not tolerate any forms of abuse. When our professionals face threats or harassment from clients, they should promptly report the matter to the police, MSF, as well as their employers. MSF will provide guidance and support to the affected social worker while police investigations are ongoing. If a police investigation is not initiated, MSF will provide guidance to the affected social worker on lodging a magistrate’s complaint.
