Individuals will also have different financing sources. For instance, Singaporeans with higher incomes will qualify for a lower level of subsidies for their care, and will need to draw more from other financing sources. In addition to existing Government subsidies and assistance schemes, those who require additional funding can also make monthly cash withdrawals of up to $200 from their MediSave from 1 October 2020. You can also consider supplementing your basic CareShield Life/ElderShield insurance with private savings or Supplements from the private insurers.
You are strongly encouraged to plan early and consider your future income, long term care arrangement preferences and how much insurance coverage and personal savings will be needed to finance these arrangements.

questions.title: How do I access long-term care services?
questions.text:
If you have long-term care needs assessed by qualified healthcare professionals, medical social workers and/or administrative staff at public hospitals and/or Government-funded long-term care service providers can assist you with your referral to long-term care services. They can also assist with your application for Government subsidies for long-term care services, and advise on the subsidy quantum you are eligible for.
You can also contact the Agency for Integrated Care at 1800-650-6060 or via the AIC website to find out more about long-term care services.

questions.title: Do I need to pay for the CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care disability assessment?
questions.text:
The fees for clinic-based and non-clinic-based severe disability assessments are $100 and $250 respectively.
If you are applying for CareShield Life:
The fee for your first severe disability assessment will be waived, regardless of the outcome. For any subsequent assessments, you will only be reimbursed if you are assessed to have a severe disability.
If you are applying for other severe disability schemes (i.e., ElderShield or MediSave Care):
You will need to pay the assessment fee upfront to the MOH-accredited assessor. The fee will be reimbursed if you are assessed to have a severe disability.

questions.title: Can an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor certify the applicant’s mental capacity for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claims?
questions.text:
A mental capacity assessment can be carried out by any doctor registered with the Singapore Medical Council for the purpose of claiming under CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care. If you require a mental capacity assessment, it is advisable to check with your assessor beforehand to confirm whether they are able to perform it, before booking a disability assessment appointment.
Depending on the applicant’s condition and needs, some cases may require a more detailed or complex mental capacity assessment that could take more time. In such cases, the assessor may charge an additional fee on top of the disability assessment fee.

questions.title: I am the family member or caregiver of a Mentally Incapacitated (MI) Patient. Can I receive CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts on their behalf?
questions.text:
You may nominate your own bank account to receive monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts on behalf of a Mentally Incapacitated (MI) patient. However, if the payout is not made to the patient or their nursing home, the family member or caregiver must obtain a deputyship within 12 months to prevent the suspension of payouts. This measure is in place to safeguard the patient’s interests.
For more details, please refer to the Frequently Asked Questions on AIC’s website.

questions.title: Can I withdraw more than $200 per month under MediSave Care?
questions.text:
MediSave is a personal savings Account without risk-pooling benefits, and withdrawals are limited to the amount saved during your working years. The $200 monthly withdrawal limit under MediSave Care was set to ensure that sufficient MediSave is set aside for other medical purposes such as hospitalisation expenses and selected outpatient treatments. Hence, you will not be able to withdraw more than $200 per month under MediSave Care.
If you are unable to pay for your care even after Government subsidies and other means of support, additional assistance is available through Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare.
The Government also regularly reviews the MediSave Care withdrawal limits to ensure that basic long-term care costs remain affordable for Singaporeans.

questions.title: Are there alternative documents I can submit for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claims in place of a severe disability assessment?
questions.text:
The Government is exploring the recognition of equivalent assessments conducted by qualified healthcare professionals such as doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses who provide care to the patient. In such cases, patients need not undergo a separate severe disability assessment. Today, patients staying in a nursing home can already seek assistance from their nursing home to submit the Resident’s Assessment Form in place of the severe disability assessment.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) and Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) will progressively roll out the use of such equivalent assessments and will publish more information on their respective websites.

questions.title: Can I be assessed by my own doctor or therapist for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claim eligibility?
questions.text: To apply for any of the severe disability schemes, you need to undergo a disability assessment by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor. You can check whether your family doctor (GP)/own doctor/healthcare professional is on the list of MOH-accredited severe disability assessors available on the AIC website. If they are not, you will need to make an appointment with one of the assessors on the list for the assessment.

questions.title: Why is the ElderFund payout ($250) higher than the MediSave Care withdrawal amount ($200)?
questions.text:
MediSave Care is designed to complement insurance schemes such as CareShield Life/ElderShield/Supplement payouts, Government subsidies, Government assistance schemes, community support, personal savings and family support, to help individuals better meet their long-term care financing needs. The Government determined the MediSave Care withdrawal amount by considering the basic long-term care costs across various services and settings, other available sources of long-term care funding, and the need to maintain MediSave adequacy.
In contrast, ElderFund is targeted at helping lower-income Singaporeans who are unable to benefit from CareShield Life or ElderShield and have low MediSave balances for their long-term care needs.
That explains why the ElderFund payout of $250 is higher than the MediSave Care withdrawal amount of $200.

questions.title: What if I have insufficient MediSave balances for my healthcare and long-term care expenses?
questions.text:
If your MediSave Account is depleted, you may tap on your spouse's MediSave for MediSave Care withdrawals, and use your family members' MediSave for other healthcare treatments.
You may also apply for additional support through means-tested Government assistance schemes such as ElderFund and Home Caregiving Grant to cover your long-term care costs. If you are still unable to afford your care even after Government subsidies and other means of support, further assistance are available through schemes such as MediFund and ComCare.

questions.title: Why is the withdrawal quantum under MediSave Care based on my MediSave Account balance?
questions.text:
MediSave is used to cover a wide range of expenses, including health insurance premiums, hospitalisation, day surgery and outpatient bills such as chemotherapy and dialysis.
The withdrawal quantum under MediSave Care is carefully calibrated to ensure that Singaporeans have sufficient savings in their MediSave Account to meet their basic healthcare needs.

questions.title: Why am I unable to undergo a severe disability assessment for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care during my hospitalisation?
questions.text:
While you are receiving treatment at the hospital, your disability condition may still be changing, which can affect the outcome of your long-term care scheme application. As such, severe disability assessments are not recommended while you are hospitalised.
Instead, our focus is on accrediting healthcare professionals in the community, such as the GPs, and clinicians within the long-term care sector who can assess your disability status once your condition has stabilised.

questions.title: If I have developed severe disability, can I make MediSave Care withdrawals from my spouse's MediSave Account?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen (SC) or Permanent Resident (PR) with severe disability, you can make MediSave Care withdrawals from your own and your spouse’s MediSave.
Non-SC or PR who wish to make MediSave Care withdrawals from your SC or PR spouse's MediSave may be assessed on a case-by-case basis and are subject to approval.

questions.title: Why is MediSave Care restricted to individuals aged 30 and above?
questions.text:
MediSave Care is not applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents below the age of 30 as they are significantly less likely to develop severe disability and need long-term care. They also tend to have lower MediSave balances based on employment history.
Those under the age of 30 who require assistance can tap on various support schemes such as subsidies for early intervention programmes under the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), subsidies for therapy services at the KK Women's and Children's Hospital and National University Hospital, and means-tested Government assistance schemes such as the Home Caregiving Grant (HCG), in meeting their long-term care needs.
For Singaporeans who are unable to afford care even after receiving Government subsidies and support from other schemes, additional help is available through Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare.

questions.title: Will I continue getting ElderShield premium rebates in the future?
questions.text: This will depend on the claims experience of the ElderShield scheme. Premium rebates are only given if subsequent ElderShield claims are lower than projected.

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. If I join CareShield Life, will I get premium rebates?
questions.text:
Premium rebates are dependent on the recommendations of the CareShield Life Council. The independent council has been set up to regularly review and recommend premium and payout adjustments for CareShield Life, in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework.
If there are fewer claims than expected, you might receive premium rebates or have your future premiums adjusted lower. However, if there are more claims than expected, your premiums might need to increase to keep the scheme sustainable.

questions.title: How long do I have to pay for CareShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
If you are age 59 and above when you join CareShield Life, you will not have to pay premiums after 10 years.
If you are age 58 and below when you join CareShield Life, you will have to pay premiums until you reach age 67 (inclusive of the year you turn age 67). Thereafter, you will no longer need to pay for CareShield Life premiums.

questions.title: Why did the CareShield Life Welcome Package state that I was previously invited to apply for Additional Premium Support?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) is designed to help members who are unable to afford their MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums after Government subsidies and have limited family support. As you have an outstanding MediShield Life premium, a letter (Ref: APCINV) was sent earlier to invite you to apply for APS if you need assistance to pay your outstanding premiums. Alternatively, you may visit cpf.gov.sg/APSapplication to apply for APS online. This link does not require Singpass login.
For more information on APS, please visit the MediShield Life website or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 for assistance.

questions.title: Why is the premium information shown on the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service different from details in my welcome letter?
questions.text: The CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service is based on the latest information available when you log in while your welcome letter is accurate as of the date shown on the first page. The information may differ if you have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, and the appeal was successful. For further enquiries, please contact us at Write to us or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399.

questions.title: Why am I not allowed to make MediSave Care withdrawals to cover my parent or children’s long-term care needs?
questions.text:
The duration of severe disability can vary significantly, potentially leading to substantial withdrawals over a long period. Allowing individuals with severe disability to tap into their parent or children’s MediSave for withdrawals could potentially impact their parent or children’s MediSave adequacy and compromise their ability to afford their own healthcare needs.
Singaporeans who need financial assistance and have low MediSave balances may apply for ElderFund. If they are still unable to afford their long-term care costs, additional assistance is available through schemes such as MediFund and ComCare.

questions.title: If I nominatd an organisation, what would happen to my CPF savings if the organisation no longer exists or is no longer a legal entity?
questions.text:
If the organisation no longer exists or is no longer considered a legal entity at the point of your passing, your CPF savings will be redistributed to surviving nominees in the same proportion you have specified for them. If there are no surviving nominee(s), your nomination is considered revoked, and your savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee for distribution under the relevant intestacy laws or inheritance certificate (for Muslims).
We encourage CPF members who had nominated organisations, to review their nominations regularly. If an organisation had ceased to exist or is no longer a legal entity, members should make a new nomination to decide how their CPF savings should be distributed.

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. If I paid ElderShield 300/400 premiums previously but my policy lapsed due to non-payment of premiums, how will my CareShield Life premiums be affected?
questions.text:
As your ElderShield 300/400 policies have lapsed due to non-payment of premiums, you are no longer covered under ElderShield 300/400. Your premiums for CareShield Life will be based on the premiums for an uninsured individual.
Those who need assistance with their premium payment after subsidies and incentives will receive Additional Premium Support, and no one who joins CareShield Life will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.

questions.title: Can I sign up for CareShield Life on behalf of my parent/spouse/sibling?
questions.text:
Your family member’s Singpass will be required to sign up for CareShield Life.
You can guide your family member to use his/her Singpass to apply for CareShield Life via the Application to join CareShield Life form. Some applicants may need to undergo a disability assessment. Your family member will be informed by Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) if a disability assessment is required, after his/her application.
If they are facing difficulties, you can accompany them to the Community Clubs/Centres to sign up.

questions.title: How will topping up my Special or Retirement Account boost my monthly payouts if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
If you are not on CPF LIFE* in retirement, topping up your Special or Retirement Account will generally increase your monthly payouts. However, if your remaining payout duration is short, the top-up will extend your payout duration instead so that your Retirement Account can continue to provide you with monthly payouts during your retirement.
For more personalised estimates, use the CPF Monthly Payout Estimator. This tool helps you project your monthly CPF payouts in retirement and simulate the effect of different top-up amounts on your monthly payout.
*Members born in 1958 or later will be placed on CPF LIFE if they have at least $60,000 in their Retirement Account when they commence their monthly payouts.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What information can I find in each section of my Home ownership dashboard?
questions.text: Your Home ownership dashboard summarises your personalised CPF housing information to help you make informed decisions. Here's what each section contains:

questions.title: What are the GST Voucher, 2025 MediSave Bonus, and Assurance Package payouts that the Government is giving out?
questions.text: Please visit the govbenefits website for more information on the GST Voucher, 2025 MediSave Bonus and Assurance Package payouts.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on other government agencies

questions.title: Do I have to update my CPF Nomination record when there are changes to my circumstances (e.g. recent marriage, child birth, death of nominee)?
questions.text: If your circumstances have changed (e.g. recent marriage, child birth, death of nominee), your current CPF nomination may no longer meet your wishes. You are encouraged to update your CPF nomination to keep it relevant with your current circumstances.

questions.title: Can I complete an Advance Medical Directive (AMD) Form 1 before I see a doctor?
questions.text: You can fill in your details on the Advance Medical Directive (AMD) Form 1 before seeing a doctor. However, your two witnesses and you must sign the form at the same sitting.

questions.title: Is there any cost involved in making an Advance Medical Directive (AMD)?
questions.text: To make an AMD, you will have to consult a doctor who, as a witness, is required to explain the AMD. You may have to pay the doctor for the services rendered. However, the AMD form itself is free.

questions.title: Can family members overrule or object my Advance Medical Directive (AMD) from being carried out?
questions.text: If you have made an AMD, regardless of objections from members of your family, the doctors will have to respect your AMD. Hence, while making an AMD is a very personal decision, we encourage you to discuss it with your family members and loved ones. This will help them to understand and respect your wishes should you become terminally ill.

questions.title: I'm having trouble using Text Us. Where can I find help?
questions.text:
You can refer to the Text Us Flow Chart to understand how our chat service works and how to navigate through each step.
Click the link below to see our detailed Text Us guide for solutions to common issues and tips for the best experience.
Learn more (PDF, 3MB)
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: I am a self-employed person. Can I contribute to my MediSave together with my employees' CPF using CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
As self-employed person, you are required to make your MediSave payable separately from your employees' CPF. This is because payments made using CPF EZPay will be credited as employer contributions and will not be recognized as self-employed payments.
If you would like to make CPF contributions as a self-employed person, there are various ways to do so.

questions.title: How can I view or download my CPF LIFE monthly payout statement?
questions.text:
You can access your CPF LIFE monthly payout information through these steps:
Log in to cpf.gov.sg with your Singpass
Click on "my cpf" at the top navigation bar
Under "My dashboards", select the Retirement dashboard
Scroll to the 'Monthly payouts' section
Click on “Monthly payout history”
Select your preferred period to view the payout history
You may click the “PDF icon” to download your monthly payout statement for your selected period.

questions.title: Who can use PLAN with CPF?
questions.text:
PLAN with CPF is available to all Singaporeans aged 16 and above. They can log in via Singpass to access their personalised PLAN with CPF dashboard.
As the contents of PLAN with CPF are less relevant for those aged below 16 or non-Singaporeans, it is not available to these CPF members. They can view other contents in the CPF website that do not require Singpass login.
topics: PLAN with CPF / General information on PLAN with CPF

questions.title: Why do I need to log in with my Singpass to access my PLAN with CPF dashboard?
questions.text: You will need to log in using Singpass to access your PLAN with CPF dashboard because the contents are personalised based on your profile and planning progress. In addition, your previous inputs and plans will be saved for your future visits to your PLAN with CPF dashboard, making it easier for you to review your plans and track your planning progress over time.
topics: PLAN with CPF / General information on PLAN with CPF

questions.title: How do I use the PLAN with CPF dashboard?
questions.text: The PLAN with CPF dashboard helps you track your planning progress across five financial planning areas. You can easily take actions within each planning area, such as accessing relevant planners or viewing curated educational resources.
topics: PLAN with CPF / General information on PLAN with CPF

questions.title: What is the Financial fitness beyond CPF questionnaire?
questions.text:
The Financial fitness beyond CPF questionnaire enhances members’ awareness of common financial planning rules of thumb that go beyond CPF matters. It was developed in collaboration with MoneySense, based on the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s (MAS) Basic Financial Planning Guide.
You can access the questionnaire by clicking the “Financial fitness beyond CPF” icon in your PLAN with CPF dashboard.
topics: PLAN with CPF / General information on PLAN with CPF

questions.title: Do I need to log in to CPF with my Singpass to access the Home Purchase Planner?
questions.text:
It is recommended to log in to CPF using Singpass to use the Home Purchase Planner as:
your CPF information will be automatically filled, which helps save time and allows you to obtain a more accurate estimate of your home purchase budget; and
your latest CPF account balances will be used to project your retirement savings and monthly payouts.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Home Purchase Planner

questions.title: Do I need to log in to SGFinDex to access the Home Purchase Planner?
questions.text: It is recommended to log in to SGFinDex using Singpass to use the Home Purchase Planner as your financial data will be automatically filled, which helps save time and allows you to obtain a more accurate estimate of your home purchase budget.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Home Purchase Planner

questions.title: What is the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner (HIP) is an online tool that helps you make informed decisions about your health insurance coverage in about 15 minutes. Through a four-step process, HIP will allow you to:
have personalised projections of your long-term MediSave savings and health insurance premiums;
compare benefits, features, and premiums across Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) for your preferred ward type; and
have long-term premium projections for your selected IP and its rider.
These features provide you with a consolidated view to better review and plan your healthcare coverage.
To use the HIP, members will need to prepare the name of their IP and rider, as well as the number of years left to pay for their CareShield Life and ElderShield Supplements, if applicable.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Why do I need to log in with my Singpass to access the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text: Singpass login is required for the Health Insurance Planner to access your personal information, including your MediSave Account balance, MediShield Life and CareShield Life or ElderShield premiums, and details about your dependants. This information is needed to be used for projections. Through the Singpass login feature, the planner can also save your personalised inputs for future sessions, making it more convenient when you return.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: What are the assumptions used in the projections within the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text: For more information on assumptions used within the Health Insurance Planner (HIP), refer to our detailed notes.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: How accurate are the projections within the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner provides illustrative estimates to help with your financial planning. Your actual premiums and coverage may vary if you have special circumstances such as exclusions, premium loading, discounts, or claims-based pricing from your insurer. The projections also may not reflect costs of additional riders beyond co-payment riders, such as deductible cover, cancer coverage, daily cash, or global riders.
Please note that these projections should not replace professional financial advice. For specific guidance about your situation, please consult a financial advisor.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: If I am not the payer for my health insurance policies, will I be able to use the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text: Yes, you can use the Health Insurance Planner even if someone else pays for your policies. The planner will create projections as if you were the payer, allowing you to compare your current plan with other available options in the market.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Does the Health Insurance Planner account for the cost of dependants’ premiums?
questions.text: The Health Insurance Planner includes premium costs for dependants you currently pay for, based on CPF Board’s records. You can specify how many years you plan to continue paying premiums for each dependant.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Why are my future MediShield Life premiums so high?
questions.text:
The projected MediShield Life premiums you see reflect expected medical inflation over time and increases with age. Your actual future premiums may differ based on factors like real medical inflation, how much people claim, and any changes in coverage benefits.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) works with the MediShield Life Council to actively review MediShield Life coverage and premiums to ensure that healthcare remains accessible and affordable.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: The Health Insurance Planner shows that I may have insufficient MediSave for my healthcare expenses and insurance premiums. Will I lose my insurance coverage?
questions.text:
No one will lose coverage to MediShield Life, our national health insurance scheme, due to an inability to pay their premiums.
If you face difficulty paying for MediShield Life premiums even after subsidies and MediSave, help is available through schemes like Additional Premium Support.
When choosing or renewing Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders, consider both your coverage needs and long-term financial ability. Think about whether you have enough income and cash savings to cover expenses beyond what MediSave can pay.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Where does the Health Insurance Planner obtain information on Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders?
questions.text: The information on Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders is provided by the insurers and is updated annually in January. For a comparison of IPs across all insurers, you may refer to Ministry of Health (MOH)’s website.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Some riders have claims-based pricing, where premiums are adjusted based on claims made by the policyholder in the preceding year. Is this considered in the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text: The Health Insurance Planner does not account for claims-based pricing in riders. For specific information about how your claims history might affect your rider premiums, please contact your insurer or financial advisor.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Why does the Health Insurance Planner not display all benefits in the Integrated Shield Plan (IP) comparison?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner focuses on the most commonly used benefits to make comparisons simpler and more user-friendly. For a complete comparison of all Integrated Shield Plan (IP) benefits across insurers, please visit Ministry of Health (MOH)'s website.
The list of key benefits are:
Inpatient benefits
Daily ward and treatment charges (Normal ward)
Daily ward and treatment charges (ICU)
Outpatient benefits
Cancer drug treatment
Cancer drug services
Kidney dialysis
Pre-hospitalisation
Post-hospitalisation
Co-payment and other features
Deductible
Co-insurance
Pro-ration factors
Pre-authorisation
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Can the Government allow us to use more of our MediSave to pay for our Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums? Why aren’t withdrawal limits sized such that IP policyholders do not have to pay cash for their IP premiums?
questions.text: MediSave's main purpose is to help you save enough for basic healthcare needs, particularly after retirement. While Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) provide additional coverage, they are optional commercial products beyond MediShield Life. The MediSave Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs) are carefully balanced to help make IPs more affordable while ensuring you have enough savings for both current and future healthcare needs.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Are Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders which are closed to new business included in the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
If you currently have a closed Integrated Shield Plan (IP) or rider, you can select it in the "Current Plan" section and compare it with other available options.
However, if you are not already covered under a closed plan, these plans will not appear in the IP comparison since they are not open to new subscribers.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: What should I do if I want to get advice or make changes to my coverage (e.g. Integrated Shield Plan (IP) and rider) after using the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
After using the Health Insurance Planner, you can download a report containing your personalised projections and Integrated Shield Plan (IP) comparisons for reference during discussions with your insurer or financial advisor.
Please note that the planner's projections are for illustration only and should not be taken as financial advice from CPF Board or Ministry of Health. To make changes to your coverage:
If you are staying with your current insurer but want to downgrade to a lower ward class IP, no new premium loading or exclusions will apply.
If you are switching insurers, you may need new medical underwriting, which could result in premium loading, new exclusions, or application rejection.
Before making any changes, please consult your financial advisor to understand all implications.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Can I bring my pet to the event?
questions.text: Pets, except for service animals, are not allowed at the event venue due to safety and hygiene considerations.

questions.title: Will military assets be showcased for Heartlands?
questions.text: The Mobile Column to the Heartlands, comprising of 12 assets from SAF, SPF and SCDF, will be making their way from the city centre and travel along five different routes to reach the Heartland sites. The convoys will form up as static displays at each site. There are limited assets that can travel on the road, and we evaluate the capacity that each site can hold them.

questions.title: How do I cancel my Permanent Resident status if I intend to close my CPF account upon leaving Singapore?
questions.text: As cancellation of Permanent Resident status is administered by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA), you may submit your request via ICA | Feedback.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What are some good practices to follow when contributing CPF to my platform workers?
questions.text: For more details regarding good practices to follow, and common mistakes to avoid when contributing CPF to your platform workers, please refer to this document.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / How much CPF contributions to contribute

questions.title: My mobile number/email address is outdated. How can I update my records in Singpass?
questions.text:
To update your mobile number/email address with Singpass, please complete the following steps:
Login to the Singpass website
Select ‘Menu’ > ‘Update profile’ (under the ‘My Account’ tab) and follow the instructions on the website to complete the updating of your mobile number/email address
Please ensure that you have access to your mobile phone/email as a One-Time Password (OTP) will be sent to your updated mobile number/email address for verification.
If you require further assistance, please contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly. The operating hours are from 8am to 8pm (Mondays to Fridays) and from 8am to 2pm (Saturdays) excluding Sundays and public holidays.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: I am not a self-employed person. Why did I receive a notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons from CPF Board?
questions.text:
You will receive a notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons if you had declared a net trade income (NTI) to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) and your NTI1 exceeds $6,000. The notice of CPF contributions will inform you of your mandatory MediSave contributions.
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards.
If you disagree with the assessed income by IRAS, you may approach IRAS for further clarifications.

questions.title: What happens if I have used my CPF savings to pay for my home and do not have enough CPF savings left to set aside Full Retirement Sum when I turn 55?
questions.text:
You can set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) with a mixture of CPF savings in your Retirement Account (RA) and CPF savings used for your property. At age 55, if your RA savings is less than your FRS, the CPF savings used for your property (including accrued interest) will automatically be counted towards meeting up to half of your FRS.
For example: John turns 55 in 2025 and has $113,000 in his RA. He had used $200,000 of his CPF for his property (including accrued interest). His FRS of $213,000 would be set aside with the $113,000 in his RA and $100,000 of the CPF used for his property.
When you sell your property, you will need to refund the CPF savings (including accrued interest) used for your property to your CPF accounts. This will be used to set aside your FRS in cash.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Will my CPF savings withdrawn under the CPF Investment Scheme be used to make up my Full Retirement Sum when I turn 55?
questions.text:
No, your CPF savings withdrawn under the CPF Investment Scheme will not be used to make up your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). Your FRS is made up using your Special Account (SA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings.
Find out how your FRS is set aside when you turn 55.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Can I choose to receive my CPF savings partially when my CPF account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore citizenship/ permanent residency?
questions.text: No, your CPF savings will be paid to you in full.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: When should I receive my CPF contributions?
questions.text:
Your employer must pay your CPF contributions for each month's wages by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday).
Enforcement action will be taken against employers who fail to pay CPF contributions by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday).
Once CPFB has received the payment, the contributions will be credited to your CPF accounts within three working days, and you will be able to view the amounts through the CPF transaction history using your Singpass.
If you notice that your CPF contributions are not paid accurately or timely, you should check with your employer immediately.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is a conveyancing lawyer required when using CPF savings to purchase a private property?
questions.text: A conveyancing lawyer is required when you would like to use your CPF savings for purchase of a private property for the first time. The lawyers would typically manage all legal aspects of your transaction, including preparing and submitting required documents needed by the Singapore Land Authority (SLA), creating and lodging a CPF charge. This legal representation protects both your CPF savings and your interests in the property, which is critical in high-value transactions such as buying a property.

questions.title: Is my voluntary top-up to the 3 CPF accounts reversible?
questions.text:
Voluntary top-ups made are irreversible.
However, if the total mandatory CPF contributions and voluntary top-ups exceed the CPF Annual Limit in the calendar year, any excess voluntary top-ups will be refunded without interest. Therefore, do remember to consider your mandatory CPF contributions which you will be receiving for the calendar year, before making voluntary top-ups.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Why is there a limit set for top-up to my 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text: There is a limit set as the CPF system is generally meant to cater to the needs of up to 80th percentile of workers in Singapore. Higher income earners would have other means to supplement their retirement income.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: How long does it take to process voluntary top-ups applications to my 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text:
The application relating to voluntary top-ups to your 3 CPF accounts will be processed as stated in the table below.
Service
Processing Time
Top up your 3 CPF accounts
Almost immediately
If the top-up amount is not reflected in your CPF accounts, please check your CPF account balance after five working days as more time may be needed to process the transaction. Such cases may arise due to intermittent network connectivity issues beyond CPF Board's control.
Please alert us immediately if your payment is still not updated in your CPF account balance after five working days.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Why are the excess voluntary top-ups only refunded in the following year?
questions.text:
The CPF Annual Limit (AL) consists of both the Mandatory Contribution (MC) from your employer and Voluntary Contributions (VC) paid by you, if any. You are allowed to top up VC up to the CPF Annual Limit (AL) of the year.
As the MC for December can be paid by January of the following year, any excess VC top-ups made for the preceding year can only be finalized and refunded in the following year.
If your mandatory and voluntary CPF contributions have exceeded the CPF Annual Limit during the year, you can write to us to request for refund of the excess voluntary top-ups.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Why are the excess voluntary top-ups refunded with no interest?
questions.text: The excess voluntary top-ups can only be determined after all your mandatory contributions have been received for the year. This is usually after the month of January in the following year. The interest on the excess voluntary top-ups which should not be earned by the member will be returned to the Board.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: How can I check the status of my top-up application?
questions.text:
You may login to your CPF account and check the status of your online application under “Activities”. If your top-up application is successful, it will be reflected in your CPF accounts.
If you have made multiple top-up applications, do check the status of all your applications to see which transactions have been successfully processed and make a new application if necessary.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account
Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: My top-up via PayNow QR is not reflected in my CPF account. Why is my CPF account balance(s) not updated immediately?
questions.text:
Your top-up via PayNow QR will generally be processed immediately upon successful deduction from your bank account.
If your top-up is not reflected in your CPF accounts, please check your CPF account balance after five working days as more time may be needed to process the transaction. Such cases may arise due to intermittent network connectivity issues beyond CPF Board's control.
Please alert us immediately if your payment is still not updated in your CPF account balance after five working days.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account
Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: With the closure of my Special Account, how will the top-up to my 3 CPF accounts be allocated?
questions.text:
For CPF members aged 55 and above, the voluntary top-up to your 3 CPF accounts after the closure of the Special Account will be made to your Ordinary Account (OA), Retirement Account (RA) and MediSave Account.
The CPF contributions allocated to the RA will be up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS). For members who have set aside the FRS in the RA, these contributions will be channelled to the OA.
You may refer to the CPF allocation rate table (PDF, 0.1MB) for more details.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: How do I find my downloaded CPF documents on my mobile phone or tablet?
questions.text:
When you download your CPF documents (e.g. statements) your device saves it automatically. Here's how to find it:
For iPhone or iPad:
Look for the blue "Files" app on your screen
Tap on "Files"
Tap on "Downloads"
Your CPF documents will be there
For Android phones or tablets:
Look for "My Files" or "File Manager" app
Tap to open it
Look for "Downloads"
Your CPF documents will be there
For more information, please see:
Where to find downloads on your iPhone or iPad
Where to find downloads on Android devices
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What is the CPF EZPay Submission Mode Recommender?
questions.text:
The CPF EZPay Submission Mode Recommender is a tool designed to assist employers to easily identify a CPF EZPay submission mode that is assessed to be suitable for them.
The Recommender would recommend one of the available submission mode (i.e. CPF EZPay (Employee Database), CPF EZPay (FTP), CPF EZPay (ESI), and CPF EZPay Mobile) based on information the employer provides. Employer may find out more on the submission mode recommended to see if it meets their needs.
Regardless of the recommendation by the Recommender, employers may continue to use any of the CPF EZPay submission mode they prefer.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: Can my employer update my employment details with the Board on my behalf?
questions.text: No. You must submit an Update Particulars application through the Professional Registration System using your Singpass credentials to update your employment details.

questions.title: Can I pay my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium by instalments?
questions.text:
Home Protection Scheme premiums cannot be paid by instalments. The premium is structured to be paid in full at the beginning of each policy year so that the scheme remains viable and the premiums kept affordable for all insured members.
You can find out more on the available payment options.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I request an extension for my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium payment if I am facing financial difficulties?
questions.text: If you are unable to pay the outstanding Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium within the given two months grace period due to financial difficulties and need more time for payment, you may request to extend the HPS premium payment deadline online. Your request is subject to approval.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why are platform workers not counted towards my Work Permit and S Pass quota?
questions.text:
Only Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents who are employed under a contract of service and are paid at least the Local Qualifying Salary will count towards your foreign worker quota.
Platform workers are not employees under a contract of service and are therefore not counted towards your foreign worker quota.
topics: Work passes and permits / Work passes

questions.title: Can I download or print the results from the KETs verification tool?
questions.text: You can save the results by selecting the “Save as PDF” option under Print.

questions.title: What should I do if I do not trust the doctors appointed by my employer?
questions.text: If you have a valid concern, you should lodge a case with MOM or raise this issue to the case officer who is assisting with your claims.

questions.title: My employee is currently covered under MediShield Life. What will happen to their MediShield Life cover if I buy an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) for them?
questions.text: All Integrated Shield Plans (IP) have a MediShield Life component and an additional private insurance component. Hence, your employee’s MediShield Life cover will continue when you buy them an IP. In addition, they will not have exclusions for their MediShield Life cover, even if there are exclusions for the additional private insurance component of their IP.

questions.title: Is salary during an employee's notice period subject to CPF deductions?
questions.text:
Yes, Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions must be made by both employer and employee if:
The employee is working during the notice period.
The employee hasn't yet joined their new company.

questions.title: My employer hasn't paid my salary, or has made an unauthorised deduction. What can I do?
questions.text:
You should make a claim as early as possible as this will give you a higher chance of recovering the salary owed to you.
To be eligible to file a claim, you need to:
Be covered by the Employment Act.
File the claim within 1 year of the non-payment.

questions.title: I have outstanding MediSave payable but I am unable to contribute the full amount. Can I make a partial contribution using the Manage your MediSave Payable form (MMSP)?
questions.text: You can make contributions of any amount using the Manage your MediSave Payable (MMSP) form, if you are contributing to your MediSave monthly via an instalment plan. This enables you to shorten your instalment duration and fulfil your MediSave payable sooner by making additional contributions as and when you wish to.

questions.title: How will the GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) and GRIT@Gov Programmes help fresh graduates? What are the expected outcomes of GRIT?
questions.text:
GRIT and GRIT@Gov are initiatives by Workforce Singapore (WSG) and Public Service Division (PSD) respectively that offers fresh graduates with traineeship opportunities for a period of 6 months across various sectors.
The programme supports structured traineeships for trainees to gain hands-on industry-relevant experience and skills, preparing them for successful transition into full-time employment.

questions.title: How will I receive my monthly payouts if my combined Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings are less than the minimum sum of $350?
questions.text: You will receive monthly payouts as long as you have at least $350 in your combined Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings. If your combined RA and OA savings are less than $350, the balance will be paid to you next January (e.g., if your balance falls below $350 in August, you will receive your payout next January).

questions.title: What happens if my Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings are depleted and I receive new inflows in my RA and OA?
questions.text: If you are not on CPF LIFE, your monthly payouts will stop when your combined Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings are depleted. When you receive any new inflows in your RA or OA, your monthly payouts will automatically resume from the following month. However, if your combined RA and OA savings are less than $350, the balance will be paid to you next January (e.g., if your account balance falls below $350 in August, you will receive your payout next January).

questions.title: How do I make payment after MRI Scan?
questions.text:
You may check if your bill is ready for payment by logging into Health Buddy, Health Hub or the SGH Online Payment portal www.sgh.com.sg with your SingPass.
You will receive an SMS notifying you of your final bill 1 to 7 days after your appointment.
Visit the following URL to find out more about the different payment modes offered: https://for.sg/sgh-payment

questions.title: What are the signs of infection?
questions.text: Redness, Swelling, pain, warm to touch, pus

questions.title: Why is there a need to double CareShield Life payout growth rate?
questions.text: CareShield Life works alongside other Government subsidies and grants to support long-term care costs. With rising long-term care costs, the enhancements in the payout growth rate are necessary to ensure that CareShield Life continues to meaningfully support the varied care needs of those with severe disability.

questions.title: What happens to my CareShield Life payout if I have been receiving payouts prior to 1 January 2026?
questions.text: Existing CareShield Life claimants will not be affected by the enhanced CareShield Life benefits and increased premiums, and will continue to receive their existing CareShield Life payouts for the duration of severe disability.

questions.title: How much will my CareShield Life premiums be after the premium changes take place, and how much would it increase by?
questions.text:
With the CareShield Life premium support measures, annual CareShield Life premium increases from 2026 to 2030 will be moderated to about $38 on average, and no more than $75.
CareShield Life premiums will continue to be fully payable via MediSave, which will minimise out-of-pocket payments for policyholders.
Lower- and middle-income policyholders will have smaller CareShield Life premium increases, as they will receive means-tested premium subsidies.
Individuals may check their personalised premiums through the CareShield Life premium checker from November 2025 onwards.

questions.title: How is the Government Transitional support different from the CareShield Life premium subsidy?
questions.text: Unlike CareShield Life premium subsidies, which are means-tested and targeted at the lower- and middle-income policyholders, all policyholders who see an increase in their gross premiums will benefit from the transitional support to help manage the premium increases from the CareShield Life 2025 Review.

questions.title: Where can I get help if I cannot afford my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The Government provides means-tested premium subsidies targeted at the lower- and middle-income individuals.
Policyholders’ loved ones may also help with premium payment for policyholders through their MediSave or by topping up to the MediSave accounts of their loved ones.
For those who are unable to pay for their CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies and family support, the Government will provide Additional Premium Support, so that no one loses CareShield Life coverage due to an inability to pay their premiums.

questions.title: How will my CareShield Life Supplement premiums be affected by the CareShield Life changes?
questions.text:
CareShield Life Supplements are offered by private insurers, and CareShield Life Supplement premiums are independent of CareShield Life.
Most Supplement benefits also stack independently on top of CareShield Life benefits, and would not be affected.
Supplement policyholders may wish to contact their insurers to enquire about any potential changes or impact to their Supplement policies.

questions.title: Can I opt out of the upcoming CareShield Life enhancement?
questions.text:
Maintaining the enhancement as a standard feature for all policyholders helps keep the scheme fair and sustainable, and premiums affordable. This helps to:
Reduce adverse selection risk, where those who are more likely to claim are more likely to opt into the scheme.
Keep administrative processes simple and efficient.
Hence, the CareShield Life Council has recommended to apply the enhancements to all policyholders, striking a fair balance between stronger protection and premium affordability for all.

questions.title: Who can still enroll in CareShield Life after 1 January 2026?
questions.text:
After 1 January 2026, individuals born in 1979 or earlier can still enrol into CareShield Life if they do not have any pre-existing disabilities.
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later will continue to be automatically enrolled when they turn age 30.

questions.title: What is the CareShield Life 2025 Review about?
questions.text: On 27 August 2025, Ministry of Health announced the changes related to the CareShield Life 2025 Review. You can read more about the changes by clicking on this link.

questions.title: When will the enhancements to CareShield Life take effect?
questions.text:
The revised payouts and premiums under the CareShield Life 2025 Review will take effect from 1 January 2026.
Changes to other aspects of the scheme such as improvements in scheme administration will take place progressively.

questions.text: Existing CareShield Life claimants will not be affected by the enhanced CareShield Life benefits and increased premiums, and will continue to receive their existing CareShield Life payouts for the duration of severe disability.

questions.title: Why does the CareShield Life claim threshold remain at severe disability?
questions.text:
Expanding CareShield Life coverage to those with milder forms of disability would require premiums to at least double, due to the longer claim duration and higher claim incidences for these individuals. As this would have come at the expense of premium affordability for more policyholders, the CareShield Life Council has recommended not to vary the scheme’s scope of coverage.
Importantly, the CareShield Life Council notes that those with mild/moderate disability can continue to access Government subsidies and grants that have been designed with them in mind. These include long-term care subsidies and grants such as Home Caregiving Grant that the Government will enhance progressively from 2026.
Those who wish for additional insurance coverage can also consider Supplements offered by private insurers.

questions.text:

questions.title: Why is the enrolment criterion being reinstated for CareShield Life application?
questions.text:
When CareShield Life was launched, older Singaporeans with less severe disability were allowed to join as a time-limited concession, so that more seniors could enrol in and benefit from CareShield Life.
However, this also meant that premiums for all older Singaporeans had to be priced higher, to account for the possibility that those with milder forms of disability were more likely to join the scheme.
This concession period lasted 4 years, over twice as long as what MOH had announced when the concession was rolled out. In this time, application rates have also decreased over time.
Thus, the CareShield Life Council views that this is an appropriate juncture to reinstate the underwriting criteria, which will moderate the extent of premium increases for all older policyholders, keeping the scheme fair and sustainable.

questions.title: I am paying the premium for my family member's CareShield Life policy. How can I find out more information about their policy?
questions.text: If you are paying for your family members' CareShield Life premiums, you can log in to Healthcare dashboard 'CareShield Life/ElderShield' section for information on your and/or your dependants' CareShield Life premiums and subsidies.

questions.title: Won't natural immunity be better than getting vaccinated?
questions.text:
Our immune system produces immunity following vaccination, similar to how it would after a "natural" infection.
The difference is that you do not get sick first when you get the vaccination. Vaccines help strengthen your immune system and protect you from potentially life-threatening complications.
Hence, it is highly recommended that you and your loved ones get vaccinated according to the national immunisation schedules.

questions.title: What does the Varicella vaccine do?
questions.text:
The Varicella vaccine helps prevent chickenpox, a highly infectious disease caused by the Varicella-Zoster Virus (VZV).
Chickenpox is a highly contagious viral disease that spreads through direct contact, respiratory droplets, or contaminated items. It causes an itchy rash across the body (except palms and soles), fever, fatigue, loss of appetite and headache. While typically lasting a week, it can also lead to serious complications including skin, lung, blood, bone and joint infections, as well as inflammation of blood vessels and neurological tissues such as brain and spinal cord coverings.

questions.title: How many varicella vaccine doses are required, and what are the intervals?
questions.text: Two doses are recommended, given 4 to 8 weeks apart.

questions.title: How do I reschedule my appointment?
questions.text:
To cancel or reschedule your appointment, please use the unique booking link in your confirmation SMS.
There are no penalties for missing an appointment, but please inform the clinic in advance if you need to cancel or reschedule.
If you have deleted the previous appointment's confirmation SMS, you can reach out here - https://go.gov.sg/has-support to share your details so we can provide better help.

questions.title: Can I apply for loans or credit facilities after being discharged from bankruptcy?
questions.text: Yes, you can apply for loans or credit facilities after you are discharged from bankruptcy. However, you may wish to note that this is subject to the financial institution's approval.

questions.title: Where can I find a list of all law practices and lawyers in Singapore?
questions.text:
Please refer to the Legal Services Regulatory Authority's ("LSRA") integrated online search function, which lists all Singapore solicitors with a current practising certificate from the Supreme Court of Singapore, as well as all foreign lawyers, individuals and law practice entities registered with the LSRA.
Please note that search results are based on the data available at the time of the search.
topics: Licensing or Registration of Law Practice Entities/Individuals
Licensing or Registration of Law Practice Entities/Individuals / General

questions.title: How do I terminate my moneylending licence?
questions.text: You may submit your application here to terminate your moneylending licence.

questions.title: I have a query on CPF matters.
questions.text: Please refer to https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member for information on CPF-related matters.

questions.title: CPF Board has notified me that the deceased's un-nominated CPF monies will be forwarded to the Public Trustee but a check with the Public Trustee reveals that there are no CPF monies in the case account.
questions.text:
Upon receiving notification of the death of the CPF member, the CPF Board typically requires 17 working days to transfer the moneys to the Public Trustee.
You will only be able to submit an online application for the administration of the Deceased’s un-nominated CPF moneys after we have received the CPF moneys from the CPF Board.
Once we have received the moneys from the CPF Board, we will write to the person who had notified the CPF Board of the death of the CPF member or his next of kin, to make an online application to us to distribute the un-nominated CPF moneys.

questions.title: When will the estate monies be paid out?
questions.text: As a general rule, the monies will be distributed within 4 weeks from the date of receipt of the full set of documentation or the date of receipt of the deceased's monies, whichever is later.

questions.title: What is the meaning of tenants in common?
questions.text: When a property is owned under tenants in common, the deceased's share does not automatically pass on to the surviving owner(s). The deceased's share is distributed according to the terms of the will. Where there is no will, the deceased's share will be distributed according to intestacy laws.

questions.title: Does the Public Trustee assist in the administration of a deceased's share in a HDB flat?
questions.text: On a case-by-case basis, the Public Trustee does administer a deceased's share in a HDB flat if it is of small value (≤ $50,000). You will first have to submit an online application at https://go.gov.sg/pto (Deceased's Assets other than Un-nominated CPF Monies / Baby Bonus / Edusave / PSEA) for the Public Trustee to administer the deceased's estate so that we may consider your request.

questions.title: Minor's CPF monies held in trust.
questions.text:
The Public Trustee will hold in trust, monies of minors who have yet to attain the age of majority.
The monies that is held in trust will be invested in safe financial instruments such as fixed deposits and bonds. The monies with interest earned (after deduction of the Public Trustee's administration fees) will be distributed to the minor when he / she reaches the age of majority (either 18 or 21).
Statement of Accounts for the monies held in trust by the Public trustee can be viewed online through https://go.gov.sg/pto.

questions.title: Are Podiatrists doctors?
questions.text: Podiatrists are trained foot and ankle specialists. In Singapore, we are allied health professionals, not medical doctors.

questions.title: I encountered problems with accessing my Singpass account or I have forgotten my Singpass password. What can I do?
questions.text:
If you have forgotten your Singpass password, you may reset your password online by following these steps here: https://go.gov.sg/singpass-password-reset-guide.
If you require further assistance with your Singpass account, please contact the Singpass Helpdesk by filling out this form: https://go.gov.sg/singpass-feedback-issue , and a helpdesk officer will get in touch with you.
You may refer to the link for Frequently Asked Questions on Singpass

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on traineeship allowance given to your trainee under the GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) Programme if you are the host company?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are not payable on traineeship allowance for your trainee under the GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) Programme so long as the trainee is not employed under a contract of service.
You and your trainee may enter into an employer-employee relationship at any time, including upon completion of the GRIT programme, in which case, CPF contributions would be payable on wages given to your employee.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: What happens to the Silver Support paid via GovCash if the beneficiary passes away?
questions.text: If the beneficiary passes away before fully using their GovCash, the remaining balance will be credited to their CPF Ordinary Account. This amount will form part of their CPF monies and will be distributed according to their CPF Nomination. If there is no CPF nomination, the CPF monies will be forwarded to the Public Trustee’s Office for distribution in accordance to the intestacy or Muslim inheritance laws.

questions.title: How are Healthier SG vaccinations selected for inclusion under NAIS?
questions.text:
Healthier SG vaccinations listed under NAIS are selected based on recommendations by the Drug Advisory Committee and Expert Committee on Immunisation which takes into consideration public health needs, local disease burden, vaccine efficacy and safety and cost-effectiveness. If the vaccine effectively prevents vaccinated individuals from infection or minimises complications if infected and is found to be cost-effective for its intended target population, the vaccine will be considered for inclusion under the NAIS.
MOH, in consultation with the Expert Committee on Immunisation, also monitors newly registered vaccines or those in the development pipeline to assess their relevance for Singapore, taking reference from international guidelines.

questions.title: What are the common side effects for PCV20?
questions.text: The vaccine has been assessed to be safe for use. However, similar to other vaccines, individuals may experience common side effects which include injection site reactions (e.g., pain, redness, swelling), headache, body aches, fatigue and fever. While most side effects are mild or moderate and usually resolve within a few days, individuals should consult a doctor if the side effects persist or worsen.

questions.title: Will I need to verify my disability status every year to qualify for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?
questions.text: No, verification of your disability status will be a one-time process. If you are a person with disability below 55 and are verified with MSF, we will automatically assess your eligibility for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) at the beginning of each year. If you are eligible, we will notify you via email or post at the beginning of each year. You can also check your eligibility via the Retirement Dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I have just been verified as a person with disability. As my medical condition existed way earlier, do I also qualify for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) for my cash top-ups made in previous years?
questions.text:
The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) has been expanded to include verified Singaporeans with disabilities below age 55 who meet the eligibility criteria from 2026.
This does not change your MRSS eligibility in previous years. No back-payments will be made as newly eligible persons with disabilities below 55 would still be able to make cash top-ups and receive MRSS matching grants up to the same $20,000 lifetime limit as those who are currently eligible for MRSS. Cash top-ups made in the previous years would have enjoyed tax relief and continue to benefit from the stable interest rate in the Retirement or Special Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: When will the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) be expanded to include Singaporeans with disabilities below age 55?
questions.text:
From 1 January 2026, the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) will be expanded to include verified persons with disabilities below age 55 who meet the other MRSS eligibility criteria such as Singapore Citizenship status, residing in Singapore, CPF balances, monthly income and Annual Value of their residential property.
Cash top-ups made in 2025 to the CPF Special Account of persons with disabilities under the age of 55 will not enjoy the matching grant but will continue to benefit from the stable interest rate.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: What is the maximum number of records I can enter in the Submit Employment Income Records digital service?
questions.text:
You can enter up to 200 records per submission.
If you have more than 200 records to submit, you can make more than one submission, with each submission limited to 200 records.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Submit employment income records

questions.title: Why am I asked to attend Home Protection Scheme medical examination but not my co-owner?
questions.text: Each Home Protection Scheme (HPS) application is assessed individually. The medical examination will allow us to assess your eligibility for HPS coverage.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What does the CPF Volunteering (CPFV) mobile app offer?
questions.text:
Our CPF Volunteering (CPFV) app serves as a one-stop platform for volunteers and partners of CPF Board to:
Register with us as a volunteer of CPF Board
Receive CPF updates and access onboarding and training resources on CPF
Network with other like-minded individuals
Be guided on how they can pay it forward through various opportunities to do good
View personal achievements and impact of one’s contributions
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Will the “Referrer Name” field affect my CPF application or request in any way?
questions.text: The “Referrer Name” field will not affect your application nor request.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: How can I show my appreciation to the CPF Board staff who recommended this e-service to me?
questions.text: You may provide the referrer’s details of the staff in your application form. Alternatively, you can also express your appreciation for our CPF officer by submitting a compliment through our website. Simply visit cpf.gov.sg/writetous and select "Compliments/Feedback" from the drop-down list of options.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Will I be paid for my efforts as a CPF volunteer?
questions.text: In the spirit of the Community Paying it Forward movement, CPF volunteers are not paid when they do good by helping others within their social circles better understand CPF schemes and make informed decisions on the use of their CPF savings. Nevertheless, the CPF Board acknowledges the efforts of volunteers and show appreciation to them in many other ways, such as digital rewards, seasonal sponsored prizes and appreciation event.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: How did the “Community Paying it Forward” movement come about?
questions.text:
This movement rides on a widely popular concept known as “Pay it Forward”. A simple way of explanation is that by helping three people, who in turn each help three more people and so on, we can help many more people collectively.
As CPF is an essential component in planning for our retirement, it is important for us to understand how we can maximise our CPF savings. Therefore, after benefitting from this information ourselves, we can also pay it forward by sharing it with others, so that they too, can make the most of what the CPF system has to offer.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Where can I find out more about this CPF Volunteering initiative?
questions.text:
To learn more about the purpose of CPF Volunteering initiative, watch why and how our volunteers have been paying it forward.
Alternatively, you can also read our infographic for more information on Community Paying it Forward.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: What is a Self-Help Lobby Guide and how do I register to be one?
questions.text:
CPF Board has introduced the Self-Help Lobby and E-Xperience Space at the service centres for members to learn and conveniently access the Board’s digital services. The Self-Help Lobby is equipped with self-service kiosks where members can perform tasks such as making CPF withdrawals and updating of personal information independently. The E-Xperience workshops are held at Bishan Service Centre, Tampines Service Centre and Woodlands Service Centre to guide and empower members to effectively utilise CPF’s digital services and online tools.
The role of a Self-Help Lobby Guide is to assist members with their inquiries at the Self-Help Lobby and conduct the E-Xperience workshop. Volunteers who are keen in this role should download the CPFV mobile app and complete the E-Xperience Training topics (Beginner and Advanced) in the Learn Module.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: How can I request for a CPF volunteer's contact details after an event if I have further queries?
questions.text: Our volunteers are not allowed to share their contact details. If you have further queries, please contact us via our customer service channels.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: If I discover any wrongdoing by a CPF volunteer, what action should I take?
questions.text:
We do not tolerate any wrongdoings by volunteers in their course of advocating for CPF. If you come across any wrongdoings, it is important that you report so that appropriate action can be taken.
By reporting the wrongdoing, you can help to ensure that our volunteers are held accountable for their actions and that steps are taken to prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future.
All reports should be made in good faith, without any personal agenda, or ulterior motive, and when there are reasonable grounds to suspect that an incident of wrongful practice has occurred.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: What are the types of wrongful practices?
questions.text:
Examples of wrongful practices include, but not limited to the following:
Violation of CPFV’s code of ethics (PDF, 0.1MB),
Fraud or deliberately providing false or incorrect information,
Violation of intellectual property rights,
Financial and non-financial malpractices
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: How can I provide new information or make changes to a previous report on wrongdoing?
questions.text:
To provide us with new information or make changes to a previous report on wrongdoing, please email us at volunteer@cpf.gov.sg and include the following information:
1. Your name
2. Contact number
3. FormSG response ID that you submitted previously
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Will I be further involved after making a report on wrongdoing?
questions.text: We may contact you for more information after you made a report on wrongdoing. Please ensure that you have the necessary evidence or supporting documents if you are being contacted.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Why do I need to update the CPFV app?
questions.text: We have upgraded the CPFV app and volunteers can expect exciting new features. Updating the app will ensure that you stay on top of app updates so that you have the best possible experience with the app. We appreciate your patience and understanding as we strive to improve your volunteering journey.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: When will the CPFV app update be available for download?
questions.text: On 14 July 2023, there will be a CPFV app update for you to download through your Mobile Devices’ App Store.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Will my data from the previous version of the CPFV app be carried over to the new update?
questions.text: Yes, your profile and data will be migrated to the new CPFV app. Any badges and points earned before 30 June 2023 will be recorded and reflected there. Do note that some data and progress information (e.g. challenges and topic completions) may not be compatible or relevant to the new app's features or functions. Hence, these will not be available in the new app.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Will my login credentials remain the same after the transition to the new CPFV app?
questions.text: You do not need to re-submit your user information. However, when you download and enter the updated CPFV app, you are required to enter your mobile number and email address that were used in the app’s previous version. OTPs will be used in place of passwords moving forward. All past and present password data are not stored in the CPFV app nor able to be accessed by us.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: What do I need to do on 14 July 2023 for my CPFV app?
questions.text: You will need to update the CPFV app from 14 July 2023 to keep up with the latest happenings and updates in the app. If you do not update the app, you will not be able to access its latest content.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Is support available if I encounter problems with the new release of the CPFV app?
questions.text: If you experience any technical difficulties using the new CPFV mobile app, please refer to the error pop-up in-app and follow the FAQ guide displayed to troubleshoot. Alternatively, if you have questions on the Community Paying it Forward movement, please email us at volunteer@cpf.gov.sg.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: What should I do if I can't connect to the CPFV app?
questions.text:
You can try the following methods:
Check that your internet connection is stable
Relaunch the CPFV app and try to login again
Make sure your device operating system and CPFV app are updated to the latest version
Restart your mobile device
Delete and reinstall the CPFV app
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Why are the deductible and co-insurance features necessary under the MediShield Life scheme?
questions.text:
The deductible sieves out smaller medical bills that can be paid via MediSave or cash, and focuses MediShield Life coverage on larger, catastrophic medical bills to keep premiums sustainable and affordable. The co-insurance encourages responsible and appropriate consumption of healthcare services, while managing the financial burden on the patient. Both the deductible and co-insurance can also be covered by MediSave, up to respective withdrawal limits.
