This strikes a balance between protecting Singaporeans against the vast majority of healthcare bills, while keeping premiums affordable.
Those who have difficulty affording their bills after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave can also apply for financial assistance such as MediFund.

questions.title: Can I use my redeemed premium discounts for my Integrated Shield Plan premiums?
questions.text:
You can redeem MediShield Life (MSHL) premium discounts if you are covered under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP). Your IP premiums are made up of two components – the MSHL portion and the additional private insurance coverage. The premium discounts you redeemed will be applied to the MSHL premiums of your IP policy.
IP policyholders may check with their IP insurers if they separately offer premium discounts or rewards which incentivise healthier behaviours.

questions.title: When will the pilot end?
questions.text: The three-year pilot programme will start on 18 September 2025 and end on 17 September 2028. This means that the last day to redeem Healthpoints for MediShield Life premium discounts would be 17 September 2028. Premium discounts redeemed on and before 17 September 2028 will still be valid for 12 months from redemption, even after the pilot ends.
topics: MediShield Life / MediShield Life Premium Discount

questions.title: What is the maximum amount of premium discounts that could be redeemed?
questions.text:
Under the regular conversion rate of 150 Healthpoints to $1, the maximum value of cumulative Healthpoints that an individual can earn in a calendar year is worth $270.
As the MediShield Life premium discounts have a higher conversion rate of 150 Healthpoints to $2, the maximum value of premium discounts that could be redeemed per calendar year is $540. Please refer to this webpage for more details.
topics: MediShield Life / MediShield Life Premium Discount

questions.title: Why is the validity period of the premium discounts capped at 12 months?
questions.text: Once the premium discounts have been redeemed, they are valid for a period of 12 months. The discounts will automatically apply to the policyholder’s premium payment at the next MediShield Life policy renewal, which takes place every 12 months.
topics: MediShield Life / MediShield Life Premium Discount

questions.title: Can I use my MediShield Life premium discount to pay for my outstanding MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text: Premium discounts can only be used for your next MediShield Life premium payments from 18 September 2025 onwards. They cannot be applied to any outstanding premiums from previous policy years.

questions.title: Why is there a difference between the premium discounts shown on my MediShield Life/ Integrated Shield Plan Premium Notice Letter and the amount I redeemed?
questions.text: The premium discount shown on the Premium Notice Letter reflects the amount you had redeemed as of the letter printing date. If you had redeemed more premium discounts after receiving the Premium Notice Letter, these will be reflected in your Healthcare Dashboard. Please log in for more details. The information is available under “Health insurance – MediShield Life premium discount”.

questions.title: I have redeemed my Healthpoints on the Healthy 365 app for MediShield Life premium discounts. Can I use it to pay for my dependant’s MediShield Life or Integrated Shield Plan premiums?
questions.text:
The premium discounts you earn are designated for your own personal MediShield Life (MSHL) premiums and cannot be used to pay for your dependant’s MSHL or Integrated Shield Plan premiums.
Similarly, the premium discounts redeemed by your family members can only be applied to their respective MSHL premiums, regardless of who their premium payer is.

questions.title: I only turn 40 in December, but my policy year renewal is in November, will I be able to redeem premium discounts before that?
questions.text: You will be able to redeem MediShield Life premium discounts in the year that you turn 40, regardless of when your birthday is.

questions.title: What happens to my premium discounts if I switch my Integrated Shield Plan (IP) or terminate my existing IP?
questions.text: If your redeemed premium discounts have already been used for your MediShield Life (MSHL) premiums before you switched Integrated Shield Plan (IP), no further action would be required. Any unused premium discounts or premium discounts redeemed after you switched IP, will be carried forward and used for your MSHL premiums at your next policy renewal, so long as they remain valid (premium discounts are valid for one year from the date of redemption).

questions.title: I have redeemed $70 worth of premium discount but only $50 was used for my MediShield Life premiums. What happens to the remaining $20 of premium discount?
questions.text:
Any unused premium discounts will be carried forward and used for your MediShield Life premium at your next policy renewal, so long as these remain valid (premium discounts are valid for one year from the date of redemption).
For information on your premium discount, you may login to your Healthcare Dashboard.

questions.title: I am a nominee. How do I apply to withdraw the deceased member's CPF savings?
questions.text:
We will contact the nominee(s) within 10 working days after the Board is notified of the member’s demise.
The CPF savings will be automatically paid to the nominee(s) (i.e. you do not need to submit a withdrawal application), if you meet the following criteria, subject to additional eligibility requirements:
are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
aged 18 and above
have a local residential address
have a registered bank account with CPF Board
If you do not qualify for automatic disbursement, you will receive instructions on how to submit the withdrawal application in our notification to you.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: Why is the pilot only open to individuals who are 40 years old and above? Are there plans for the programme to be rolled out to younger individuals in the future?
questions.text:
This pilot programme is introduced in support of Healthier SG. As such, for a start, the pilot will focus on those aged 40 and above, which is the age criteria for the Healthier SG enrolment programme.
We will study the outcomes of the pilot before deciding whether premium discounts should be made a permanent feature of the MediShield Life scheme, and whether the discounts should be extended to younger individuals.
Under Healthier SG, all Singapore residents are encouraged to stay active and live healthily, such as by participating in programmes offered by the People’s Association (PA), Sport SG and the Health Promotion Board (HPB). All Singapore residents can participate in Healthy 365 programmes and challenges, to earn and redeem Healthpoints. Regardless of age, healthier lifestyles generally lead to better health outcomes and reduced healthcare utilisation.

questions.title: When will I receive my monthly payouts?
questions.text: The monthly payouts of all members are deducted on the 2nd of the month, and the crediting of the monthly payouts to members’ bank accounts will depend on the bank's processing time. You will receive the monthly payouts in your bank account generally by the 4th working day of the month. You will generally receive your payouts earlier if your bank supports Fast And Secure Transfer (FAST).

questions.title: What will cause my CPF LIFE monthly payouts to be adjusted and when will payout adjustments be effected?
questions.text:
We want to ensure that your CPF LIFE monthly payouts are sustainable over the long term. As such, our actuarial consultant reviews them yearly and take into account the following:
Deviations in mortality experience. If more people live longer than expected in the long term, the monthly payouts might be lower, and vice versa.
Deviations in interest rates. If interest rates are higher than expected, the monthly payouts might be higher, and vice versa.
The revised payout, if any, will take effect every July of the year. We will notify you if there is an adjustment in your monthly payouts. Rest assured that any changes are expected to be small and gradual.

questions.title: When can I apply to start my monthly payouts?
questions.text: You can submit your instructions to start your monthly payouts anytime from three months before the month you turn 65, up to age 70. We will notify you three months before you turn 65 to guide you in exploring the options for your monthly payouts.

questions.title: Why do I need to log in with my Singpass to access the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text:
You must log in with Singpass to use the Retirement Payout Planner as it enables the planner to personalise your experience.
Once logged in, the planner will
use your CPF balances to project your retirement savings and monthly payouts,
save your goals and details so you can continue from where you left off on future visits.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Who can use the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text: The Retirement Payout Planner is available for members from age 16, up to 4 months before 65. Members who are reaching or have reached 65 can use the Plan my monthly payouts service to make key decisions related to their payouts.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: What is the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text:
The Retirement Payout Planner is a digital tool that helps you plan for your retirement in three ways:
Set your retirement payout goal
Project your retirement savings and payouts, and
Explore how different actions could bring you closer to your goal.
Did you know? The Retirement Payout Planner was enhanced in September 2026. Find out what’s new in the Retirement Payout Planner.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: How accurate are the projections within the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text:
The results provided in the Retirement Payout Planner are estimates, based on various assumptions and your inputs. They are meant to facilitate your planning of your CPF retirement savings and payouts, and should not be regarded as advice by CPF Board.
For more information on assumptions used within the Retirement Payout Planner, refer to our detailed notes.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Can I use the Retirement Payout Planner if I am self-employed?
questions.text: Yes, you can. The Retirement Payout Planner is accessible by members from age 16, up to 4 months before turning 65. Self-employed members can input their monthly net taxable income (NTI) under the monthly salary field. As the projections are based on working contributions from employment calculated using the salary figures provided, they may not fully reflect the circumstances of self-employed members.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: What are the assumptions used in the projections within the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text: For more information on assumptions used within the Retirement Payout Planner, refer to our detailed notes.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: I am below 55. Can I use this Monthly Payout Estimator to estimate my monthly payout?
questions.text:
The Monthly Payout Estimator is designed to help members between the ages of 55 and 79 to estimate their monthly payout based on their desired retirement lifestyle.
If you are below 55, you can log in with your Singpass and try out the Retirement Payout Planner. This online tool can help you in setting your retirement income goal, visualising your projected retirement savings and payouts, and simulating the impact of actions you can take to achieve your goal. You may also perform selected transactions such as making retirement top-ups.
With the planner, retirement planning is easy with just a few steps and takes only 15 minutes to complete.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Why do I need to log in using my Singpass to access the Monthly Payout Estimator to estimate my CPF LIFE monthly payouts now?
questions.text: From July 2024, you will have to log in using Singpass when using the Monthly Payout Estimator. By logging in, your CPF account details, such as birth year and CPF balances, will automatically be retrieved to estimate your monthly payouts, providing you with a more seamless experience when using the estimator. You can still adjust the CPF details.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: What is the Monthly Payout Estimator?
questions.text:
The Monthly Payout Estimator is an online tool designed to help CPF members aged 55 to 79 plan their monthly payouts. It allows you to estimate your monthly payouts based on your Retirement Account balances and desired retirement lifestyle.
Key Features:
Estimate Monthly Payouts:
Calculate your monthly payouts based on your current Retirement Account balance.
Choose from different CPF LIFE plans to see how they impact your payouts.
Simulate Deferred Payouts:
Explore how different payout start ages could impact your monthly payouts.
Top-Up Calculator:
Simulate the amount you need to top up to achieve your desired monthly payout.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: I previously received CPF savings as a nominee of a deceased member. I notice there are new balances in the deceased member’s CPF account. How do I receive these additional funds?
questions.text: We will disburse any new balances in the deceased member's CPF account to your bank account registered with CPF Board. You will receive a notification if you are eligible for the supplementary payment. You do not need to submit a new application for withdrawal.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What is the CPF Retirement Planning Service about?
questions.text:
The CPF Retirement Planning Service (CRPS) is part of the Board’s efforts to help CPF members understand our policies and enable them to make informed decisions about their CPF savings in retirement.
Find out if you are eligible and how you can make an appointment.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Who is eligible for the CPF Retirement Planning Service and how do I make an appointment?
questions.text: CPF members who are reaching 55, as well as members approaching their payout eligibility age (currently age 65), can make an appointment via cpf.gov.sg/CRPSAppt to attend the CPF Retirement Planning Service.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Who can use the Plan my monthly payouts service?
questions.text:
You can use the Plan my monthly payouts service if you are turning 65 within the next three months, or if you are currently 65 years old or older. It allows you to customise your monthly payouts to suit your desired retirement lifestyle.
If you are younger, you can use the Retirement Payout Planner to set your retirement payout goal, project your payouts, and explore personalised actions to help you reach your goal.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Where can I find a list of Commissioners for Oath and Notaries Public?
questions.text: Please refer to the Singapore Academy of Law's directory of Commissioners for Oath and Notaries Public.

questions.title: My GIRO deduction for MediSave contributions has been stopped due to two unsuccessful deductions. How do I reinstate my GIRO deductions using my existing bank account registered with the Board?
questions.text:
To reinstate your MediSave GIRO deduction using your existing bank account, you can submit the “Reinstate GIRO deductions for MediSave contributions” form within 14 days from our notification. If we do not receive your application by the deadline, your current instalment plan will be terminated.
Your monthly deductions will resume once your application to reinstate your MediSave GIRO deductions has been processed. To avoid future interruption, please maintain sufficient funds in your bank account for the deductions.

questions.title: I've used up my Flexi-MediSave limit of $400, but my spouse needs medical treatment too. Can I use my MediSave for his/her medical bills?
questions.text:
Seniors aged 60 and older can use up to $400 per year under Flexi-MediSave for their own outpatient treatments, using their own MediSave or their spouse’s MediSave (spouse has to be aged 60 and older too).
If a senior has already used up their own $400 limit for outpatient treatments, they may still use their MediSave savings to pay for their spouse’s outpatient treatments, subject to the spouse’s $400 limit.
The $400 withdrawal limit applies to each patient per year, regardless whose MediSave account is used.

questions.title: Why did my GIRO monthly MediSave instalment amount change?
questions.text:
The monthly instalment amount for your self-employed MediSave contributions may change when there are changes to your outstanding MediSave contributions, which could be due to:
Assessment or reassessment of your net trade income by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore
Previous unsuccessful GIRO deductions
Refunds of MediSave contributions
Additional MediSave contributions made or received

questions.title: What are the penalties for failing to report a work-related accident, Dangerous Occurrence or Occupational Disease under the Workplace Safety and Health (Incident Reporting) Regulations?
questions.text: Any employer who fails to make an incident report may be fined up to $10,000 for a first offence. For repeated offence, the penalty will be up to $20,000 or 6 months' jail, or both.
topics: Workplace safety and health / Reporting work-related accidents

questions.title: What happens to my CPF when I turn 65?
questions.text:
You can start to receive monthly CPF payouts from age 65.
Three months before your 65th birthday, we will notify you about your monthly payouts options. You will be guided to the personalised Plan my monthly payouts (PMP) service where you can:
1. choose to start or defer your payouts
2. view your estimated payouts
3. explore ways to increase your payouts using available CPF savings.
Find out more about what happens when you are reaching age 65.

questions.title: What will happen if I do not instruct CPF Board to start my monthly payouts?
questions.text:
If you do not provide instructions to the CPF Board using the "Plan my monthly payouts" service, your monthly payouts will start automatically when you reach age 70. These payouts will be paid to the registered bank account provided in your Account settings.
Find out more on what happens to your CPF savings when your monthly payout starts.

questions.title: Why is there another transfer of monies from my Ordinary Account (OA) to my Retirement Account (RA) before I start my monthly payouts?
questions.text:
As Singaporeans are now working longer, CPF contributions made after age 55 become an essential part of their retirement savings. The increase in senior worker CPF contribution rates further reinforces this. This additional transfer will help to boost your retirement savings and provide you with higher monthly payouts.
If you have already set aside your Full Retirement Sum in cash in your Retirement Account, the transfer will not occur.

questions.title: What are some common causes of dysphagia?
questions.text:
Dysphagia can result from various conditions including:
Stroke Neurological conditions (like Parkinson's disease)
Head and neck cancer or its treatment
Age-related changes
Brain injury
Muscle weakness

questions.title: How long does it take to recover from facial palsy?
questions.text: Recovery time varies greatly depending on the extent of nerve damage and type of diagnosis. It can take anywhere from days to 4 months or even longer. Each person's recovery journey is unique, so patience is essential during this process.

questions.title: How do regular MediSave co-contributions received under the Drive and Save Scheme benefit me?
questions.text:
Under the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme, the regular MediSave co-contributions from your taxi operator can:
Offset your mandatory MediSave contributions under the Self-Employed Scheme
Earn up to 6% interest per annum on your MediSave savings
Use of MediSave savings to pay for medical expenses and healthcare insurance
Qualify for Workfare Income Supplement scheme for lower-wage workers

questions.title: My family member is covered under the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS). Can I pay their DPS premium using my CPF savings?
questions.text:
No, your CPF savings cannot be used to pay your family member's Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) premium. This is to ensure that your CPF savings, which are generally meant to meet your retirement needs, are not depleted prematurely.
However, if you wish to help your family member, you may do so by paying their premium in cash directly to the appointed DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life (GEL). Visit GEL’s website for detailed instructions and forms.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Other than clinics, are there any other heartland locations that provide Covid-19 vaccination?
questions.text:
Mobile Vaccination Teams (MVT) are deployed to serve selected heartland locations, making vaccination more accessible for seniors. Each MVT will be deployed at a designated site for a few days to conveniently serve residents in their neighbourhoods.
Please visit go.gov.sg/mvt-s for the latest MVT deployment schedules and locations.

questions.title: Where can I get vaccinated?
questions.text:
Adult COVID-19 vaccines are available at participating General Practitioner (GP) clinics and polyclinics under the COVID-19 National Vaccination Programme. If you are eligible to be vaccinated under the National Vaccination Programme, please check https://www.gowhere.gov.sg/vaccine for the nearest vaccination sites and their operating hours.
You may book an appointment at participating General Practitioner (GP) clinics through vaccine.gov.sg/covid, or polyclinics through the HealthHub booking system under the National Vaccination Programme.

questions.title: Why is my polyclinic only offering one type of vaccine?
questions.text:
The polyclinics generally only carry one brand per vaccine type. If you are keen to receive a vaccine not offered by your polyclinic, you may visit a participating GP clinic offering the vaccine of your choice.
Please visit vaccine.gov.sg/covid to book an appointment at a participating GP clinic under the National Vaccination Programme.

questions.title: How do I make back-payments for Skills Development Levy (SDL)?
questions.text: You can make back-payment for Skills Development Levy (SDL) by logging into GoBusiness, and go to Levy > Skills Development Levy (SDL). For detailed step-by-step instructions, refer to "How do I make my SDL payment on GoBusiness?"
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Skills Development Levy (SDL)

questions.title: Why did CPF Board and MOH launch the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner (HIP) is a joint initiative by CPF Board (CPFB) and Ministry of Health (MOH) under PLAN with CPF, our one-stop guidance service for financial and retirement planning.
Making decisions about health insurance coverage and comparing Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) can be challenging due to the complexity of information. As healthcare costs rise, members need to ensure their coverage matches both their care preferences and financial circumstances.
The HIP uses members' personal data to generate long-term projections of their MediSave savings, healthcare expenses, and insurance premiums. Working alongside existing information on MOH, CPFB and insurers' websites, the planner helps members make better-informed decisions about their health insurance coverage.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Do I need to pay my NSmen employees' CPF contributions?
questions.text: You should continue to pay your employees' CPF contributions based on their usual remuneration, as though they are not away for their ORNS/SV activity. The CPF contributions payable by both employer and employee remain the same and are based on prevailing CPF Board guidelines.

questions.title: How will I know that I have successfully spent the cash credits in the LifeSG application?
questions.text: You will see a payment success screen at the end of each transaction if your payment has been successful. You will also be able to view your credit balance and past transactions on the LifeSG mobile application.

questions.title: Can I cancel my payment after I have confirmed the payment on the LifeSG application?
questions.text: No, your credits will be deducted once the payment is successful.

questions.title: I am on the contract service and I understand that my CPF contribution rates are different from the Full CPF rates. How is the CPF contribution computed for both employee's and employer's portion?
questions.text: Pensionable components like Basic Rank Pay, Basic Pay Supplement (if any), MVC, etc attract a lower CPF rate while Non-Pensionable Components like NPVP and NPC, etc attract the full CPF rates. These rates are subject to changes from time to time.

questions.title: Can I use my property or CPF money to furnish the Banker's Guarantee?
questions.text: CPF funds or properties cannot be used to furnish a Banker's Guarantee.

questions.title: I am residing overseas and when do I need to register for National Service (NS)?
questions.text: Overseas pre-enlistees will receive a NS Registration Notice upon reaching 16.5 years old. This notice will provide you with the necessary information and instructions on how to proceed with your NS registration.

questions.title: There is an error when I tried submitting my Deferment application.
questions.text: Please save the screenshot of the error message and email it to contact@ns.gov.sg for further assistance.

questions.title: Why do I need to link my NRIC number to my PayNow registered bank account to receive my IPPT incentive award? Can I link my mobile number instead?
questions.text: NRIC/FIN is the only accepted proxy for Government disbursements via PayNow. Unlike mobile numbers which are subject to change, the NRIC/FIN is an unchanging identifier assigned by the Government. Linking your NRIC/FIN to your PayNow account will ensure that Government disbursements are sent to the correct payee.

questions.title: I have multiple bank accounts. How do I know which bank account I have linked PayNow to?
questions.text: To check which bank account(s) you have linked PayNow to, you may approach your bank for assistance, or go to the PayNow interface on the internet banking platform or mobile banking app for any bank that you are registered with. The bank account(s) that is linked to your NRIC number and/or mobile number will be displayed. Your NRIC number and mobile numbers can be linked to different bank accounts.Please note that your NRIC number can only be linked to one bank account for PayNow at any one time.

questions.title: I'm experiencing problems registering for PayNow, how do I resolve this?
questions.text: If you are experiencing problems registering for PayNow or linking your NRIC number to your PayNow account, please approach your bank for assistance.

questions.title: Can I be assured that the personal data provided to MINDEF via Form.SG will be secured?
questions.text: The care and protection of information, including the personal data of servicemen, is of utmost importance to MINDEF. Servicemen are regularly educated on the guidelines on personal data protection, and the need to handle personal data carefully and sensitively. These include the requirement to seek proper approval for the collection, use, and disclosure of personal data.

questions.title: What should I do if I am using one of the recommended browsers but the site is not displaying correctly?
questions.text:
Please clear your browser cache. This simple step can often resolve display issues. If you are accessing the site via Proxy or Firewall, contact your IT department regarding available proxy ports. If the problem persists, please report your issue here and provide the following details:
Browser information
Details of error messages
Screenshots of the issue

questions.title: Who contributes the employers CPF during training?
questions.text: Under the Enlistment Act 1970, when the employee is away from work performing training, his employer is required to continue paying CPF contributions based on his usual civilian remuneration. The employer has to pay the CPF contributions on the wages given by the employer and the payments given by MINDEF/SPF/SCDF as though the employee has not been away from work. The CPF contributions payable by the employer and the amount which the employer can recover from the employee's wages are based on the CPF Board's guidelines.

questions.title: What is HOMES?
questions.text:
HOMES is the Household Means Eligibility System, a Government system that supports public schemes in conducting means tests as part of their assessment to determine the level of assistance for applicants. HOMES officers will contact parents to request supporting documents or information needed to determine means test eligibility. Parents must respond to contact made by HOMES officers for HOMES to assess eligibility for Student Care Financial Assistance (SCFA).
HOMES outbound calls are made from 6015 5700. An SMS from gov.sg will be sent requesting for follow up/callback in the event, applicant is uncontactable.

questions.title: How is income calculated for Student Care Financial Assistance (SCFA) subsidy?
questions.text:
For salaried employees:
Based on average gross monthly income derived from the CPF contributions made over the last 12 months or the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 calendar years).Includes: basic salary, bonuses, commissions, overtime pay, allowances, cash rewards, and employee CPF contributions.
For self-employed individuals:
Based on average trade income over 12 months from the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 calendar years), or income declared to CPF Board.

questions.title: What happens to my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover when my account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text: When you have renounced your Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency, your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will cease upon the sale of your HDB flat or at the end of the current HPS policy year, whichever is earlier. There will be no further renewal of your HPS cover, even if you are in the process of selling your HDB flat, as the scheme is only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to my CPF savings if I have an outstanding CPF education loan when my account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text:
If you have used another CPF member’s CPF savings for your education and have an outstanding CPF education loan owed to him, your CPF savings may be used to pay the education loan before the remaining CPF savings are transferred to your bank account. In the event that your CPF savings are not sufficient to cover your full education loan, your repayment liability remains even after your CPF account is closed.
If you have used your CPF savings for your education or your child/spouse/siblings/relative’s education, the repayment of all such outstanding CPF Education Loans to you will be waived.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to the top-ups I had received in my Special or Retirement Account when my account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text: Any remaining monies which you have received through CPF transfers and cash top-ups will be paid to you, along with your CPF savings, when you transfer your savings to your bank account. This is subject to safeguards to prevent premature withdrawals.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to my CPF LIFE plan when my CPF account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text: Your CPF LIFE plan will be terminated, and you will receive your CPF LIFE premium balance (if any) together with your CPF savings when you transfer your savings to your bank account.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: Do I have to refund the sale proceeds when I sell my property after my CPF account is closed upon my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text: Yes, you must refund your CPF principal amount withdrawn with accrued interest or amount you have pledged to refund if you have not transferred your CPF savings to your bank account upon renunciation, by the time you sell your property.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to my CPF savings if I have unpaid taxes, MediShield Life premiums, CareShield Life premiums or outstanding education loan owed to a CPF member when my account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore citizenship/ permanent residency?
questions.text:
If you have unpaid taxes/MediShield Life premiums/CareShield Life premiums/outstanding education loan owed to a CPF member, we may recover the unpaid amount from your CPF savings when your CPF account is closed.
You are encouraged to settle any outstanding liabilities (e.g. insurance, tax and housing liabilities) before your CPF account is closed.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: Can I use CPF savings to buy a property?
questions.text:
Yes, you can use your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings to purchase residential properties in Singapore under the CPF Housing Scheme. Under this scheme, you can use your OA savings to:
Buy Housing & Development Board (HDB) flats
Buy or build private residential properties in Singapore
It's important to keep in mind that your Special Account (SA) and Retirement Account (RA) savings cannot be used for property purchases as these accounts are specifically meant to provide you with retirement income.
For comprehensive information about using your CPF savings for property purchase, please refer to the Terms and Conditions.

questions.title: I am planning to buy a property, but will be overseas and unable to handle the transactions. What should I do?
questions.text: If you are unable to handle property transactions in person due to overseas commitments, you can appoint a trusted person to act on your behalf through a Power of Attorney. This legal document gives your appointed representative the authority to manage your CPF savings and handle property-related matters in your absence. This ensures your property purchase can proceed smoothly even when you are not physically present in Singapore.

questions.title: Do I need a valuation report to use my CPF savings for property purchase if I am not taking a loan?
questions.text:
Yes, a valuation report is mandatory when using CPF savings for property purchase, regardless of whether you are taking a loan. This report determines the maximum amount of CPF savings you can use for your property purchase.
For HDB flats: Only HDB's valuation will be accepted, and it must be dated within three months from your application date.
For private properties: The valuation report must be:
Conducted by a licensed valuer, which can be your bank’s valuer
Dated within three months from your property purchase date

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to buy properties overseas?
questions.text:
CPF savings can only be used to buy properties in Singapore.
If you are looking to buy a property in another country, you will not be able to use your CPF savings to fund the purchase. It is important to keep this in mind when planning your property purchase and to ensure you have enough savings or financing options available for a property purchase outside of Singapore.

questions.title: What are the terms and conditions to use my CPF savings to buy an HDB flat or a private property?
questions.text: You can refer to the Terms and Conditions to use your CPF savings to buy a property.

questions.title: What is Edusave and can I use Edusave to pay for school fees?
questions.text: You may find out more details here - https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/edusave-account

questions.title: Why am I not eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme if my monthly income is above $4,000?
questions.text: The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme is designed to help senior Singapore Citizens with lower retirement savings save more and boost their retirement payouts. The average monthly income of $4,000 will cover most senior workers. If your average monthly income is above $4,000, you will not be eligible for the scheme as it is intended to provide additional support to those who need it the most.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Do the claim limits for High-Cost Drugs (HCD) and Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTP) apply if these treatments are administered during an inpatient stay or day surgery?
questions.text: Yes, if a patient receives High-Cost Drugs (HCD) or Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTP) treatment during an inpatient or day surgery admission, the respective HCD/CTGTP claim limit will apply to these treatments, while the daily inpatient hospital limit will apply to the room and board charges. This ensures adequate healthcare financing support by MediShield Life and MediSave for patients who receive HCD or CTGTP treatment in inpatient or day surgery settings.

questions.title: How can I check for healthcare GIRO deductions on my bank statement?
questions.text: You can check your online banking, mobile banking app, or bank statement for transactions showing 'IBG CPF MSL MSL'. This code appears for all healthcare premium GIRO deductions (MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield).

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on payments under the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA) if the claim is eventually rejected, unsuccessful or withdrawn?
questions.text:
When a WICA claim is rejected, unsuccessful, or withdrawn, employees may need to use their existing medical or hospitalisation leave entitlements for the absence period.
Any payments which the employee may receive under the Employment Act or employment contract (such as medical leave, hospitalisation leave, or continued wages during the period of incapacity) would be subject to CPF contributions. These are considered as regular employment remuneration, not WICA compensation.
topics: Workplace safety and health / Work injury compensation

questions.title: Will there be any fees for unsuccessful GIRO deduction of MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield premiums?
questions.text: CPF Board (Billing Organization) will not impose any charges for unsuccessful deductions of MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums. However, some banks will impose service charges as an unsuccessful deduction may be treated like a bounced cheque. Please contact your bank for further details on the fees and charges (if applicable).

questions.title: Will my new CPF working contribution partially pay off my outstanding MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums if I am on a monthly GIRO instalment plan?
questions.text:
Yes, your new CPF working contributions will be used to pay your outstanding MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums. This helps to reduce the outstanding amount and avoid enforcement actions.
If you are currently on a monthly GIRO payment arrangement, your monthly GIRO deduction amount will remain unchanged, but the payment plan will end earlier once outstanding premiums are fully paid.

questions.title: Can I change the bank account to pay for my MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life/ElderShield premiums?
questions.text: Yes. You will need to submit a new GIRO application with the new bank account details. The new application will generally be processed within 21 working days. We will continue to deduct your healthcare premiums from the current bank account until the new GIRO application is approved.

questions.title: How do I apply for GIRO for my/my dependant's MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums?
questions.text:
You can use your own or a third party's bank account to apply for GIRO for your/your dependant's MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums by clicking on Set up GIRO for healthcare premiums.
Upon approval of your GIRO application, your healthcare renewal premiums will be deducted from your bank account every year, within a month after the cover is renewed. If you/your dependant has outstanding healthcare premiums, it will be paid in monthly instalments from the GIRO bank account.

questions.title: What happens if my Healthcare GIRO application is rejected or my MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield GIRO deductions was unsuccessful for two or more consecutive months?
questions.text:
If your Healthcare GIRO application is rejected, you may re-apply by clicking on Setting up GIRO arrangement.
In the event of unsuccessful GIRO payment for your renewal premiums, the premiums will be deducted from MediSave. If your monthly GIRO deductions fail for two consecutive months, your payment plan will be suspended and you will need to write to us to request reactivation, which will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.
We will impose new interest and penalties on your outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums if your GIRO application is rejected or GIRO deductions are suspended.

questions.title: How do I terminate my/my dependant's GIRO arrangement for MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life/ElderShield premiums?
questions.text: You can approach your bank to terminate your GIRO arrangement for healthcare premiums.

questions.title: How do I make an ElderShield claim?
questions.text:
If you are covered under ElderShield and would like to make a claim, you can arrange for a severe disability assessment with an MOH-accredited assessor and submit your application through the AIC’s eService portal (eFASS) using your Singpass.
If you are a caregiver submitting a claim for a mentally incapacitated ElderShield insured, you can log in eFASS using your Singpass to submit the application on his/her behalf.

questions.title: My employer has not paid me my salary and/or has dismissed me unfairly. What should I do?
questions.text: Educators who require help in managing employment disputes (e.g. salary, wrongful dismissal) may wish to tap on the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM)’s support services at https://www.tal.sg/tadm/about.

questions.title: Why are my full healthcare renewal premiums deducted from my GIRO bank account when I have set up monthly GIRO instalments?
questions.text:
If you have set up GIRO for healthcare renewal premiums, your MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield renewal premiums will be deducted from your GIRO bank account every year. Monthly GIRO instalments are only for payment of past policy year’s outstanding premiums (excluding renewal premiums).
This arrangement was outlined in your GIRO application form.

questions.title: I am using a GIRO arrangement to pay my MediShield Life premiums. What happens to my GIRO when I upgrade to an Integrated Shield Plan?
questions.text:
If you have applied for GIRO arrangement for your MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield premiums and upgrade to an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) subsequently, the GIRO arrangement for your MediShield Life premiums will cease. Your existing GIRO arrangement for CareShield Life/ ElderShield premiums (if any) will remain unchanged. You will need to have a separate premium payment arrangement with the IP insurer.
If you switch back to MediShield Life subsequently and would like to use GIRO for your MediShield Life premiums, you must re-apply.

questions.title: I am using GIRO for my MediShield Life and/or ElderShield premiums. Do I need to re-apply when joining CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Yes, you must re-apply for GIRO when joining CareShield Life. Your current MediShield Life and/or ElderShield GIRO arrangement will not automatically extend to cover CareShield Life premiums.
If you opt out of CareShield Life and return to ElderShield, you do not need to re-apply as your earlier GIRO application was extended to ElderShield.

questions.title: I have an ongoing monthly GIRO instalment plan. My MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life cover has been renewed and has incurred new outstanding premiums. Will interest be imposed on me?
questions.text: Interest will not be imposed on the new outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums while you have an ongoing monthly GIRO instalment arrangement. Your existing GIRO payment plan will be revised to include the new outstanding premiums. You will be notified of the revised instalment to be paid.

questions.title: Where can I view the status of my GIRO application for my Healthcare premiums payment?
questions.text:
You can log in to Activities to track the status of your GIRO payment arrangement request for your healthcare premiums.
Please refer to the following FAQ for guidance on termination of GIRO arrangement for your/your dependants' MediShield Life, CareShield Life, and ElderShield premiums:
How do I terminate my/my dependant's GIRO arrangement for MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life/ElderShield premiums?

questions.title: What if my GIRO account does not have sufficient funds to pay for my MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield premiums?
questions.text:
If you do not have sufficient funds in your GIRO account to pay your MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield premiums, the GIRO deduction will be unsuccessful and a second GIRO deduction attempt will be made.
The GIRO arrangement will be suspended if there are two consecutive unsuccessful deductions.
To avoid unsuccessful deductions, please maintain enough balance in your GIRO bank account. If you have set a payment limit on GIRO deductions, please ensure that the limit takes into account the total premium amount to be deducted. Note that some banks may charge administrative fees for unsuccessful deductions.

questions.title: I have received an Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore's (IRAS) notice and applied for GIRO payment arrangement for my healthcare premiums. Will interest be imposed on me?
questions.text: Interest and penalties will not be imposed on your outstanding MediShield Life and/ or CareShield Life premiums if CPF Board receives your GIRO application before the due date stated in IRAS' notice.

questions.title: What is Silver Housing Bonus?
questions.text:
The Silver Housing Bonus (SHB) enables you to supplement your retirement income if you're moving to a 3-room or smaller flat.
By committing your housing refunds towards your retirement payouts, you can enjoy lifelong income through CPF LIFE and receive a cash bonus of up to $40,000.
Find out more about SHB.
You may also use HDB’s Enquire Housing Monetisation Options e-Service to check your eligible Housing Monetisation options.

questions.title: How do I apply for Lease Buyback Scheme or Silver Housing Bonus?
questions.text:
You can apply for the Lease Buyback Scheme or Silver Housing Bonus through HDB:
Silver Housing Bonus
Lease Buyback Scheme

questions.title: Can I retain my Ordinary Account savings instead of having them transferred to my Retirement Account to increase my CPF LIFE payouts?
questions.text:
You can retain your Ordinary Account (OA) savings for immediate withdrawal needs if you have set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in your Retirement Account (RA).
If you have not set aside your FRS, your OA savings will be automatically transferred to your RA to provide you with higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts.
If you have housing obligations, you can use your CPF LIFE monthly payouts or any CPF savings in excess of your FRS to meet these needs.

questions.title: How can I prolong my monthly payouts if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
You can consider the following options to prolong your monthly payouts:
Join CPF LIFE: CPF LIFE provides lifelong monthly payouts, unlike payouts that stop when your retirement savings are depleted if you are not on CPF LIFE. You can join CPF LIFE anytime from age 65 to one month before turning 80 via the Plan my monthly payouts service.
Reduce your monthly payouts: You can reduce your monthly payouts to extend the duration of your retirement income up to age 90. Submit your request via 'Write-to-us' with your Singpass.

questions.title: Do I have to top up my MediSave Account to the Basic Healthcare Sum if I start withdrawing my CPF savings from age 55?
questions.text: You do not need to top up your MediSave Account (MA) when you begin withdrawing your CPF savings from age 55. The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is the estimated savings you need in your MA to cover your basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age and is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA.

questions.title: What is the minimum balance I need to set aside in my MediSave Account?
questions.text: There is no minimum amount required to set aside in your MediSave Account (MA). A portion of your working contributions will be allocated to your MA until your balance reaches the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS). The BHS is the estimated savings you need in your MA to cover your basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age and is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA. Any amount above the BHS will be channelled to your other CPF accounts, depending on your age. You can find out how MediSave contributions above the BHS are channelled to other CPF accounts via this link.

questions.title: If I am 66 years old in 2026 and my applicable Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is $75,500, am I allowed to maintain a balance greater than my applicable BHS in my MediSave Account?
questions.text: You can only save up to your applicable Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) in your MediSave Account (MA), which is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA. The BHS is designed to cover your basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age and to prevent the excessive accumulation of funds in your MA.

questions.title: How do I find out the Annual Value (AV) of a property?
questions.text:
The owner of a property can check the current AV of his or her property at no cost by using our 'View Property Summary' digital service. All AVs shown are as at current date.
Please note that if there is any change to the AV stated in your 2026 Property Tax bill, it will only be reflected on the digital service from the effective date of change.
If you are not the owner of the property, you can use the 'Check Annual Value of Property' digital service to search the AV of a property at a fee of $2.50 per search. You can retrieve the AV of the current year and up to past five years. This digital service only provides information on AV, other information on the property is not made available.

questions.title: Can the AV be reduced to take into account the owner’s expenses such as interest cost, utilities, insurance and taxes?
questions.text: No, such expenses cannot be deducted for property tax purpose. AV is defined as the estimated gross annual rent at which the property can be let out on a yearly basis, with the landlord paying the expenses of repairs, insurance, maintenance and upkeep of the property.

questions.title: Where can I find more information on other Government support available for persons with disabilities?
questions.text: For comprehensive information about disability support schemes and services, you may refer to the SG Enabling Guide at enablingguide.sg/schemes-grants-support or contact SG Enable at 1800-8585-885.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I am a parent of a child with disabilities. How can I check the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) eligibility for my child?
questions.text:
If you are a parent of a child below 21 years old, you can access the Child Dashboard using your own CPF account to check the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) eligibility status of your child.
If your child is a verified person with disabilities, you will see a section on MRSS on the child dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I am eligible for both the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme and Matched MediSave Scheme but I have limited funds. Should I top up the Retirement / Special Account or MediSave Account?
questions.text:
If you and your loved ones have limited funds available for CPF top-ups and are eligible for both Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) and Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS), you can consider which scheme better meets your needs. You may also wish to consider portioning your funds and top up to both your Retirement / Special Account (RA / SA) and MediSave Account (MA) to benefit from both schemes.
If you want to increase your retirement payout, you may consider topping up your RA / SA to benefit from MRSS. If you anticipate higher healthcare spending given your health circumstances, you may consider topping up your MA to benefit from MMSS.
You can refer to this comparison table to learn the key differences between the two schemes.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am eligible for both the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme and Matched MediSave Scheme. Can I participate in both schemes to receive the maximum Government grants?
questions.text: Yes, if you are eligible for both schemes, you can top up in cash to your Retirement / Special Account to qualify for the matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) of up to $2,000 per year, as well as to your MediSave Account to qualify for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) of up to $1,000 per year. You can top up to these accounts, anytime throughout the year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What can I use the Matched MediSave Scheme matching grant for?
questions.text: Matching grants granted under the Matched MediSave Scheme are credited to your MediSave Account (MA). You can use your MediSave savings to pay for approved healthcare insurance premiums (e.g. MediShield Life, CareShield Life) and approved medical treatments.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Can I still receive Matched MediSave Scheme grants if I am a recipient of Silver Housing Bonus (SHB) or Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS)?
questions.text: If you are a recipient of either the Silver Housing Bonus (SHB) or Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS), the cash top-ups used to qualify you for SHB or LBS will not be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) grant. Any voluntary cash top-ups to the MediSave Account that do not qualify for LBS or SHB may attract MMSS grant.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How do I appeal if I believe I qualify all criteria but was deemed ineligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: Please refer to the eligibility criteria under the Matched MediSave Scheme and assess if you qualify every criterion. You can submit an appeal via Write-To-Us.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How do I check the amount of matching grant that I will receive under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
To find out the grant amount that you will receive under the Matched MediSave Scheme at the beginning of the following year based on this year’s cash top-ups, you can log in to your Healthcare dashboard.
In addition, the dashboard will provide you with the remaining grant amount, if any, that you can receive if you make further top-ups.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am a self-employed person. How do I ensure that I have fully settled or are on a monthly instalment plan for my MediSave payable, so I can benefit from the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
You may check if you have fully settled or are on an active GIRO arrangement with CPF Board for your MediSave payable by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass.
If you have not made any arrangements to settle your MediSave payable, you may make full payment for your MediSave payable or request an instalment plan via the Manage your MediSave payable form.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme at the beginning of the year. Will I still be eligible if there are changes to my circumstances during the year?
questions.text:
Your eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) for the year is first determined at the beginning of the year. Changes to your financial circumstances (e.g. increase in monthly income) will not affect your eligibility for that year. Your eligibility for MMSS will be reassessed next year based on your new circumstances.
However, you will no longer be eligible for MMSS if:
You are no longer a Singapore Citizen within the year; or
You are a self-employed person (SEP) who has not fully settled or are not on a monthly instalment plan for your MediSave payable
Find out more information on the conditions you need to meet to receive and keep the matching grant.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am self-employed and have outstanding MediSave payable. Why am I not eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme grant?
questions.text:
It is a statutory requirement for self-employed persons (SEPs) to make their mandatory MediSave contributions*. Hence, SEPs who have not fully settled or are not on a monthly instalment plan for their MediSave payable will not be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) grant.
*For platform workers, this also applies if you have outstanding MediSave payable from your platform work prior to 2025.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: If I am eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme this year, will I be automatically eligible in the following years?
questions.text: No, your eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) is assessed annually. We will inform you at the beginning of the year if you are eligible. You can also check your eligibility for MMSS via Healthcare dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Will I be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme if I am turning 55 later this year?
questions.text:
Yes, you will be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) as long as you are 55 years old at the end of the assessment year and you meet the eligibility criteria.
You can check your eligibility for MMSS via Healthcare dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Can I transfer my cash top-up to MediSave Account for Matched MediSave Scheme to be used for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme instead?
questions.text:
Cash top-ups to MediSave Account made for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) cannot be transferred to Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) as the top-ups are irreversible. If you prefer to receive matching grants for retirement savings, you may consider making cash top-ups via this link for MRSS instead.
If you qualify for both MMSS and MRSS, but have limited funds to top up, you may refer to this FAQ for useful pointers.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How do I reverse the cash top up to my own MediSave Account?
questions.text: Voluntary top-ups made are irreversible.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Is there a minimum amount I need to top up to be eligible for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: There is no minimum amount of cash top-up needed to be eligible for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme. However, the more you top up, the more matching grants you can receive, up to $1,000 per year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What are the payment options to do the top-up to MediSave under Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
Currently, members can use PayNow to make a cash top-up to yourself or your loved ones’ MediSave Account. Your cash top-up will be credited upon successful payment.
For more information on how to make cash top-up to receive the matching grant under Matched MediSave Scheme, you may refer to how to make a cash top-up to MediSave Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Why are mandatory MediSave contributions made by Self-Employed Persons that can be used to offset MediSave payable not counted towards the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
Contributions made through the Manage your MediSave payable (MMSP) form are specifically designated to fulfil your mandatory MediSave contributions as a Self-Employed Person (SEP), which is a statutory requirement that must be met first.
The Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) is designed to encourage additional voluntary cash top-ups to MediSave beyond these mandatory obligations. Hence, any contributions made through the MMSP form will not count towards MMSS.
Only voluntary cash top-ups made via the Top up MediSave Account (VCMA) form will be considered for MMSS, provided that SEPs have met the other eligibility criteria for MMSS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Why is my voluntary cash top-up to my MediSave Account not updated in my healthcare dashboard under "Matching Grant Received This Year" for Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: Voluntary cash top-ups to your MediSave Account for Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) require up to three working days to be processed and reflected in your healthcare dashboard. If you have recently made a top-up, the system may not have updated your matching grant status yet. We recommend checking your account after this processing period. Please note that top-ups eligible for MMSS cannot be claimed for tax relief purposes.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am a taxi driver receiving contributions under the Drive and Save Scheme. Will these contributions be counted towards the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: Contributions made under the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme are specifically designated to fulfil your mandatory MediSave contributions as a Self-Employed Person (SEP). Hence, any contributions made under the DAS Scheme will not count towards the Matched MediSave Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Do I have to top up in a lump sum to be eligible for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: No, you can make multiple cash top-ups throughout the year. The matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme is based on the total amount of top-ups you have received throughout the year, up to $1,000 per year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What conditions must I meet in order to receive and retain the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
To receive and retain the matching grant, you must:
Be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) for the year; and
Have received cash top-ups to MediSave Account (MA) during the year; and
Still be a Singapore Citizen when the matching grant is credited to your MA at the beginning of the following year.
If you are self-employed, have fully settled your MediSave payable or be on a monthly instalment plan for your MediSave payable.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What happens if I make multiple top-ups and exceed the annual matching cap of $1,000 for Matched MediSave Scheme? Will the excess top-ups be eligible for tax relief?
questions.text:
Givers of cash top-ups that attract the matching grant (up to $1,000 per year) under the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) will not receive tax relief.
However, you may continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year for eligible cash top-ups that do not attract matching grants from MMSS and Matched Retirement Savings Scheme ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones). For more information on how to compute my tax relief for voluntary cash top-ups to MediSave Account, you may refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What if I pass away before receiving the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: If you pass away, your matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme will still be credited to your CPF account and paid out to your beneficiaries together with any remaining CPF savings.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What incentives are there for me to top up to my loved ones under the Matched MediSave Scheme given that there is no tax relief for me?
questions.text:
Topping up to your loved ones’ MediSave accounts helps them to grow their healthcare savings and provide them with greater peace of mind.
Recipients of cash top-ups who are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) can also receive a matching grant of up to $1,000 per year from the Government, which further boosts their MediSave savings.
You may continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year for eligible cash top-ups that do not attract matching grants from MMSS and Matched Retirement Savings Scheme ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: When will I receive the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: If you are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) and have received cash top-ups in that year, you can expect to receive the matching grant in your MediSave Account at the beginning of the following year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Why are CPF transfers not eligible for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: The Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) is designed to encourage cash top-ups to senior Singapore Citizens with lower healthcare savings to help them save more. Thus, only cash top-ups to eligible members will be matched.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Will I still receive the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme if my healthcare savings exceed 50% of the current Basic Healthcare Sum after topping up?
questions.text: Yes, you will receive the matching grant for the amount you received in cash top-up to your MediSave account as long as you are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) for the year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Why is there no information about Singtel Special Discounted Shares (SDS) on my CPF Investment Dashboard?
questions.text: There is no information about SDS on your CPF Investment Dashboard because you do not have SDS shares. For members who successfully applied for and were allotted SDS shares during the original offering periods in 1993 and 1996, information about SDS shares will appear on their CPF Investment Dashboard. Please refer to this link for more details regarding the SDS scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Do I have to top up in a single sum to be eligible for the matching grant?
questions.text: No, you can also make multiple smaller cash top-ups throughout the year. The matching grant is based on the total amount of top-ups you have received in the year, up to $2,000 per year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: How can I check the amount that I can top up to my Retirement Account to reach the raised Enhanced Retirement Sum in 2026?
questions.text:
You may check your top-up limit on your Retirement Dashboard on 1 January 2026 once the Enhanced Retirement Sum is raised.
Find out how the top-up limit is computed.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: When will I receive the grant for current year’s cash top-ups made?
questions.text:
If you have received cash top-ups this year, the matching grant will generally be credited to your Retirement or Special Account by end February of the following year. You will be notified via email or post when the grant has been credited. You may also check your Transaction history. Please note the matching grant is capped at $2,000 a year, with a lifetime limit of $20,000.
For example, if you receive cash top-ups in 2026, the matching grant will generally be credited to your Retirement or Special Account by end February 2027.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I am below age 55 and my disability status has not yet been verified with MSF. Once it is verified, will I become immediately eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?
questions.text:
If you are below age 55 and complete your verification of disability status with MSF before 1 November of the current year, it will be used to assess your Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) eligibility annually from the following year.
For example, a member age below 55 who had verified his disability status with MSF before 1 November 2025 will have his MRSS eligibility automatically assessed annually from the following year (2026) onwards.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: After my disability status is verified with MSF, how do I apply for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?
questions.text:
You do not need to apply for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) after your disability status is verified. We will automatically assess your eligibility yearly at the beginning of each year. If you are below age 55, you will need to have your disability status verified with Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) before 1 November of the current year to be assessed for MRSS eligibility for the next year onwards.
For example, a member age below 55 who had verified his disability status with MSF before 1 November 2025 will have his MRSS eligibility automatically assessed annually from the following year (2026) onwards.
If you are eligible, we will notify you via email or post at the beginning of each year. You can also check your MRSS eligibility via the Retirement Dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Why is my CareShield Life premiums payable until age 67?
questions.text:
Starting the CareShield Life premium payment duration at age 30, and ending at age 67 gives you a longer period to spread your premium payments, hence reducing the annual premiums payable.
The age at which premium payments end may be subsequently reviewed to take into consideration the changes in the re-employment age.

questions.title: Where can I find my CareShield Life premiums information?
questions.text: You may refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support.

questions.title: What are the CPF allocation rates for 2026?
questions.text:
From 1 January 2026, the CPF contribution rates for employees aged above 55 to 65 are increased to strengthen their retirement adequacy.
Upon the closure of the Special Account (SA) for CPF members aged 55 and above, the CPF contributions allocated to SA will be fully allocated to the member’s Retirement Account (RA), up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS). For members who have set aside the FRS in the RA, these contributions will be channelled to the Ordinary Account.
You may refer to the CPF allocation rate table (PDF, 0.1 MB) for more details.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Can anyone, including entities, make voluntary top ups to my MediSave Account? How do I check if anyone has topped up for me?
questions.text:
Anyone, including entities (Community Partners, NGO, etc.) can make voluntary top-ups to your MediSave Account (MA). Entities will need to submit their intention to make voluntary top-ups to your MA. See more here.
If you are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS), you can check if anyone has topped up to your MA on your Healthcare dashboard. The estimated cash top-ups you have received this year which will qualify you for the matching grant will be reflected.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: If I am a non-profit organisation and want to top up to a specific member, how can my organisation make such top-up and how do I know if the recipient of the top up will benefit from Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: You can submit your request to make voluntary top-ups to specific members here and we will assess if the member is eligible and inform you accordingly.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How can I check my Government cash grants or benefits received for the year?
questions.text: We have moved records of CPF-administered cash grants from the Yearly Statement of Account to YourBenefits@LifeSG, as it provides a more comprehensive view of common Government-provided benefits you have received, covering schemes from multiple agencies including CPF Board. You would require Singpass to login. Please refer to the FAQ for more details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: When will I receive my monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts?
questions.text: You can expect to receive your monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts by the middle of each month.

questions.title: Where can I access subsidised referrals to public specialist outpatient clinics (SOCs)?
questions.text:
Eligible individuals can access subsidised referrals to public specialist outpatient clinics (SOCs) regardless of their Healthier SG enrolment status, as follows:
Singapore Citizens: You can get subsidised referrals at polyclinics. If you hold a CHAS, Merdeka Generation (MG), or Pioneer Generation (PG) card, you can also get subsidised referrals at CHAS clinics.
Permanent Residents: You can get subsidised referrals at polyclinics.
Enrolment in Healthier SG is not required for subsidised referrals.

questions.title: I am a senior and have received a letter on Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) eligibility. I do not understand the content in English. Is there a translated version?
questions.text:
If you have received a letter on your Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) eligibility and would like to view the translated contents, please refer to the following:
有关退休户头配对填补计划的中文信件, 请参阅 -> Mandarin
Bagi surat kelayakan MRSS versi Bahasa Melayu, anda boleh merujuk kepada-> Malay
MRSS தகுதி கடிதங்களின் தமிழ் பதிப்பை நீங்கள் இங்கே பெறலாம் -> Tamil
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I am eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme this year. Will I still be eligible if there are changes to my circumstances during the year?
questions.text:
Yes, you will still be eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) for the year even if your circumstances change (e.g. increase in monthly income) during the year. Your eligibility for MRSS will be assessed next year based on your new circumstances.
However, do note that renouncing your Singapore citizenship during the year will make you ineligible for the scheme and matching grant.
Find out about the conditions which you need to meet to receive and keep the matching grant.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I am a person with disability below 55. How can I check if I am verified as a person with disability and what should I do if I am not yet verified?
questions.text: The disability verification process is managed by SG Enable on behalf of MSF. To check whether you are verified or how to be verified, or to find out more information on the disability verification process, please refer to the Enabling Guide. For any further queries, please contact SG Enable at contactus@sgenable.sg or the hotline at 1800-8585-885.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Within how many days must all co-owners submit our Home Protection Scheme applications to meet the 100% coverage requirement?
questions.text: All co-owners must submit their Home Protection Scheme applications within the next three calendar days of the first application being received. Please note that your application would be rejected if the household 100% coverage is not met as we did not receive all your applications within the next three calendar days.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How long does it take to process my MediShield Life Suspension application?
questions.text:
As relevant agencies may take some time to verify your permanent residency or other status, the processing of MediShield Life Suspension application may take up to three months or longer, depending on its complexity. We will inform you of the outcome once we have assessed your application.
Please visit our website at cpf.gov.sg/HealthcareFinancing if you need more information or write to us at cpf.gov.sg/writetous.

questions.title: I have already submitted my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection. It is pending approval. Why am I still receiving reminder letters to pay my MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The premiums for your MediShield Life cover are still payable while your application is being processed. If your application is successful, premium collection will be suspended prospectively from the next policy year based on the date of receipt of your application.
Any outstanding premiums prior to the start of the Suspension Period remain payable. Please make payment promptly with the payment modes available to avoid any further enforcement action.

questions.title: I have applied for CareShield Life and my application has been approved. Why is the coverage status reflected as ‘Waiting for Cover’ on my Healthcare dashboard?
questions.text:
