In the event of your death, any benefits payable will be paid to your beneficiary in accordance with the terms and conditions of the annuity policy by the insurer.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: Where can I check the status of my voluntary housing refund application?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your voluntary housing refund application online via Activities.
Once your application has been successfully processed, the refunded amount will be credited to your CPF account. You can then view the details in your 15-months Transaction History by logging in to my cpf digital services or CPF Mobile app using your Singpass. You will also receive an email notification once your application has been processed.
Please note that the amount refunded will be used to reduce the principal amount withdrawn for your property, followed by its accrued interest.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Voluntary Housing Refund

questions.title: Am I eligible for CPF Housing Grants?
questions.text: CPF Housing Grants (CHG) are administered by HDB. Please visit HDB’s website for the detailed eligibility criteria and application information.

questions.title: What is the difference between joint-tenancy and tenancy-in-common?
questions.text:
The key differences lie in how ownership shares are held and what happens to a co-owner's share when they pass away.
Joint-tenancy
All co-owners have equal interest in the property, regardless of how much each person paid towards the purchase. When a joint tenant dies, their share automatically goes to the remaining co-owner(s), even if they have made a will stating otherwise.
Tenancy-in-common
Each co-owner holds a separate and definite share in the property while having rights to use the entire property. Unlike joint tenancy, owners can hold different ownership percentages. For example, one owner may hold 50% while two others hold 25% each.
When a tenant-in-common passes away, their share does not automatically transfer to the other owners. Instead, it will be distributed on according to their will. If no will exists, the share will be distributed according to the Intestate Succession Act.

questions.title: How can I get my title deed for my property?
questions.text:
You can obtain your title deed after fully paying off your housing loan. The process varies depending on your property type and earlier loan arrangement.
If you own an HDB flat with HDB loan
Contact HDB directly to retrieve your title deed.
If you own an HDB flat with a bank loan
Contact your bank to retrieve your title deed.
If you own a private property
When you use CPF savings to purchase a private property, a CPF charge is created on your property to secure repayment of the amount used plus accrued interest when the property is sold. This CPF charge may remain on the property even after your housing loan is fully paid off.
Once your mortgage and all other charges (including the CPF charge and other registered charges) are fully discharged, please contact SLA to issue your title deed.

questions.title: I plan to purchase my next property before receiving the CPF refunds from the sale of my current property. How can I proceed if I do not have enough cash or CPF savings to cover the purchase?
questions.text:
You can consider taking a bridging loan from any bank, provided that HDB and/or the bank approve the arrangement.
Important condition to note
The total amount of CPF savings withdrawn plus all loans (including the bridging loan) cannot exceed the lower of the purchase price or the valuation price of the property at the time of purchase.
After selling your existing property
Your CPF savings will be refunded to your CPF accounts. You can then use these funds to pay off the bridging loan once you have completed the legal documentation and settled any outstanding cash amount.

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to buy a Small Office Home Office unit?
questions.text:
You can use your CPF savings to purchase a Small Office Home Office (SOHO) unit only if the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) has approved it for residential use. If the unit is approved for office use, you cannot use your CPF savings for the purchase.
SOHO developments are approved by the URA for either office or residential use, but not for both. It is important to verify the approved use of the property before committing to any purchase.

questions.title: What should I do if I would like to use the CPF Housing Top-Up Grant for my HDB flat?
questions.text:
The process depends on your loan type:
If you have an HDB loan
In-person at HDB Branch
Complete the CPF withdrawal form (PHS9)
Book an appointment via the e-Appointment system before visiting
Processing time: generally within three to five working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
If you have a bank loan
Submit an online application with your Singpass
Processing time: generally within five working days

questions.title: If someone who had used CPF savings for a property passes away, must we repay the CPF housing refund to the late owner’s CPF account when the property is sold?
questions.text: No, you do not have to refund the CPF savings used by the late owner’s CPF account when the property is sold.

questions.title: I am a bankrupt. Can I use my CPF savings to buy a property or to pay for the housing loan of my existing property?
questions.text:
If you are buying an HDB flat
You can use your CPF savings to buy an HDB flat or pay the housing loan of your existing HDB flat, provided you are the owner of the HDB flat. You will need to contact HDB directly regarding this matter.
If you are buying a private property
You will need to obtain consent from the Official Assignee before you can use your CPF savings to buy a private property or pay the housing loan of your existing property.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: I am a bankrupt. Can I request to make a partial repayment and leave some monies in my CPF Account for my housing loan?
questions.text: Yes, you can request to make a partial repayment of your housing loan from your CPF account even if you are a bankrupt. This arrangement allows you to retain some funds in your account to continue servicing for your housing loan.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: Where can I check the number of discounted Singtel shares I have?
questions.text: You can login to my cpf Online Services with your Singpass and check the "Discounted Singtel shares" section in the Investment dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How will the Ordinary Wages (OW) and Additional Wages (AW) that I have submitted to CPF Board be shown at the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service?
questions.text: OW and AW will be shown as 'Salary' and 'Bonus' respectively.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: If the contribution details were not e-Submitted to CPF Board by 14 Jan, will the information be pre-filled at the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service?
questions.text:
Submissions made after 14 Jan will not be pre-filled and employers will have to manually add the income information which have been submitted to CPF Board after 14 Jan at IRAS' digital service.
For example
If the CPF contribution for the month of Dec 2025 is submitted after 14 Jan 2026, the data for Dec 2025 will not be pre-filled for the YA 2026 submission. You will have to manually add the income information for Dec 2025 at IRAS' digital service.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: 1. There is a change in my personal particulars. How do I update IRAS?
questions.text:
Find out how to update your personal particulars (e.g. name, marital status,
contact details, residential/mailing address).
topics: Individual Income Tax / Tax Season 2026 - About your tax bill

questions.title: Where can I find information regarding the exercise to transfer Singtel Special Discounted Shares (SDS) to SDS holders?
questions.text: You may refer to sds.singtel.com for information on the exercise to transfer Singtel SDS from CPF Board to SDS holders.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will my discounted Singtel shares be sold or liquidated when I apply to transfer my discounted Singtel shares upon meeting CPF withdrawal conditions?
questions.text: Transferring your discounted Singtel shares will not result in liquidation of your shares. It is a request to the Board to transfer the discounted Singtel shares to your Central Depository Pte ltd (CDP) securities account. Once the shares have been transferred, you will receive a statement from CDP and the Board.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will I be notified if my application is unsuccessful?
questions.text:
We aim to update applicants on the outcome of their application where possible.
Shortlisted candidates will be contacted with further details on the next steps.

questions.title: Can I get the Public Trustee’s assistance in resealing in Singapore, Letters of Administration / Grant of Probate that was obtained overseas
questions.text:
The Public Trustee does not assist in resealing in the Singapore Courts for Letters of Administration / Grant of Probate that were obtained overseas. You will have to engage a Singapore lawyer to assist you.
You can search for a Singapore law practice or lawyer using the Legal Services Regulatory Authority's online search function athttps://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/lsra/search-lawyer-or-law-firm/. Please note that the search results are based on information provided by law practices and lawyers. The Ministry of Law does not make any warranty or representation as to their accuracy, completeness or reliability.

questions.title: Can I nominate a foreign person?
questions.text:
If you are nominating someone who is not a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, please provide the nominee’s full name, foreign identification number and mailing address in your nomination form so that the Board can contact him swiftly when distributing your CPF savings.
Please note that if you are nominating a foreigner or a Singapore Citizen / Permanent Resident residing overseas, there may be inheritance tax implications in the country of residence. You are advised to seek your own legal or tax advice in the country of residence before making your nomination.

questions.title: How often should I review or update my nomination?
questions.text: Members are encouraged to review their nomination annually or more regularly if experiencing key life milestones, such as marriage, childbirth, divorce, death of a nominee, or entering their golden years. Reviewing and updating CPF nominations allows their CPF savings to be distributed according to their latest bequeath intentions.

questions.title: I made my CPF nomination many years ago. Why can't I view it online?
questions.text:
CPF nominations made many years ago were typically handwritten on hardcopy forms. Such old nominations may contain illegible handwriting, and this makes accurate transcription of the details for online viewing challenging. As such, these old nomination details cannot be made available online.
You are encouraged to make a new CPF nomination. Once you make a new nomination, you will be able to view your latest nomination details online.

questions.title: How can I get a referral for subsidised care at public SOCs?
questions.text: A referral for subsidised care at public SOCs can be obtained from either CHAS clinics or polyclinics. Do note that you will need to be a PG/MG/CHAS cardholder to obtain subsidised SOC referrals from CHAS clinics.

questions.title: Can I take a vaccination if I am currently unwell, such as having the flu?
questions.text:
It is generally recommended to postpone vaccinations if you are experiencing moderate to severe illness, such as a high fever or significant flu symptoms. However, if your symptoms are mild, you may still be able to take the vaccination.
To ensure your safety, consult your doctor or healthcare provider for advice tailored to your specific health condition before proceeding with the vaccination.

questions.title: I’m allergic to the flu vaccine but received a push notification from the HealthHub app. Does this mean I can now take the vaccine?
questions.text: Receiving a push notification from the HealthHub app does not necessarily mean that you are now suitable to take the flu vaccine if you are allergic to it. The notification is a general reminder for flu vaccination. If you have a known allergy to the flu vaccine, consult your healthcare provider before proceeding. They can assess your medical history and advise if the vaccination is suitable for you or whether alternative flu vaccine options are available.

questions.title: When will I know if my proposal will be supported?
questions.text: Evaluation outcome letters will be sent out to operators who have submitted proposals by Oct 2026. Operators are expected to implement proposals from Nov 2026 onwards and complete them within a year. Final reports will need to be submitted by Jan 2028.

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to buy a property with a lease of less than 20 years?
questions.text: No. To use your CPF savings for property purchase, the property must have a remaining lease of more than 20 years. This requirement ensures the prudent use of your CPF savings and aligns with HDB loan eligibility criteria.

questions.title: Who is responsible for reimbursing my MediSave Account for hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text: Third parties with a contractual obligation (e.g. your employer or insurer) are required to reimburse your MediSave Account for your hospitalisation expenses.

questions.title: How can I check the status of my reimbursement if I have already submitted a claim to my insurer after using my MediSave and/or MediShield Life for medical expenses?
questions.text:
You can check your reimbursement status on cpf.gov.sg/healthcare.
Simply login to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass, and go to 'Latest healthcare payments and claims' to view the recent transactions. You can also click on 'View past 15 months' to see additional transactions.
For reimbursed claims, you will see the message "You have been reimbursed for this claim. View details". Click 'View details' to see the reimbursement details.

questions.title: Can an overseas insurance company disburse the approved reimbursement to my MediSave Account via telegraphic transfer, or is it only by cheque?
questions.text: Your insurer may submit reimbursements to MediSave and/or MediShield Life electronically via the MediSave/MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement service.

questions.title: If I used cash, MediSave and MediShield Life for my medical bill, is there a specific order in which my employer or insurer should perform the reimbursement?
questions.text:
Subject to contractual obligations, your employer or insurer should reimburse you in the following order:
i. Cash reimbursement - For the amount you paid in cash.
ii. MediSave reimbursement - For the amount utilised from your payer's or your MediSave Account.
iii. MediShield Life reimbursement - For the amount utilised from your MediSave-approved Integrated Shield Plan or MediShield Life.
This order minimises your cash outlay and restores the balances in your MediSave Account.

questions.title: I am making a reimbursement claim from my employer or insurer for my medical bills. Is it compulsory to provide a hardcopy Healthcare payments and claims statement?
questions.text: CPF Board does not require any documents from your employer or insurer to process the reimbursement. You are not required to provide a hardcopy Healthcare payments and claims statement when making a reimbursement claim. If your employer or insurer requests a statement, they should accept a digital copy.

questions.title: When do I need to apply for reimbursement to my MediSave and/or MediShield Life from my third-party-payers for my healthcare expense?
questions.text:
Please submit your reimbursement request to your employer or insurer once your MediSave and/or MediShield Life claims have been processed and reflected in your Healthcare payments and claims statement. Your employer or insurer may need your Healthcare payments and claim statement to assess your request. Find out more on how to retrieve your Healthcare payments and claims statements and apply for reimbursement.
Please note that your Healthcare payments and claims statement will no longer be available for retrieval once it is older than 15 months.

questions.title: How do I apply to use Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) funds to repay my outstanding CPF education loan?
questions.text:
You may log in to the Student Finance System (SFS) via the Ministry of Education (MOE) website using your Singpass and apply for the use of your Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) funds to repay your outstanding CPF education loan.
Please note that your request will be submitted directly to MOE for processing.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Who can I contact if I have further enquiries about MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement?
questions.text: For any further enquiries about MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement, please write to us and we will assist you with your enquiries.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Are there any charges for the MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement service?
questions.text: The MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement service is provided free of charge.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: In what order should I reimburse my employees, platform workers or insureds if they have paid for medical expenses using cash, MediSave and MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Subject to contractual obligations, the reimbursement order should be as follows:
Amount paid in cash
Amount utilised from your employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave
Amount utilised from your employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave-approved Integrated Shield Plan or MediShield Life
This order minimises your employees, platform workers or insureds' cash outlay, and preserves their MediSave for future use.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I was notified by the Medical Institution that my employee, platform worker or insured's medical bill was cancelled or amended. How can I make changes to the reimbursement I submitted earlier?
questions.text: If you need to amend the MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursement you previously submitted, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I need to submit a reimbursement to my employee, platform worker or insured's MediSave and/or MediShield Life. How do I go about doing it?
questions.text:
You can submit MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursements to your employee, platform worker or insured quickly and easily via CPF's online reimbursement system, also known as the Internet Reimbursement (IR) service.
Learn more about how to submit a reimbursement via the IR service.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Do I need to reimburse my employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave and/or MediShield Life within a specific time period?
questions.text: We strongly encourage you to reimburse your employees, platform workers or insureds promptly. Timely reimbursement is particularly helpful if they need their MediSave and/or MediShield Life for further treatments.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Can I reimburse my employees, platform workers or insureds in cash for a medical bill paid using their MediSave and/or MediShield Life?
questions.text: You cannot reimburse your employees, platform workers or insureds in cash if the medical bill was paid using their MediSave and/or MediShield Life. The reimbursement for the utilised amount must be made directly to the employees, platform workers or insureds’ MediSave and/or MediShield Life.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Apart from the Internet Reimbursement service, are there other ways to submit MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursements?
questions.text:
To support our go green program and the Smart Nation initiative, we only accept reimbursements via our Internet Reimbursement (IR) service.
If you encounter any difficulties while submitting reimbursements via this IR service, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: If my employees, platform workers or insureds have used their MediSave and/or MediShield Life for medical expenses, do I need to reimburse them?
questions.text: As an employer, platform operator or insurer, you are required to reimburse your employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave and/or MediShield Life if you have a contractual obligation to cover their medical expenses.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: How do I know if my refund for PayNow QR, Apple Pay or Google Pay has been completed?
questions.text:
Refunds will be credited back to the original payment method used:
PayNow QR: refunded to the bank account linked to the PayNow transaction
Apple Pay / Google Pay: refunded to the underlying card linked to the digital wallet
A separate notification may not be sent when the refund is processed. We recommend checking your bank or card statement to confirm.
To check whether your refund has been completed, please refer to:
Your bank account statement or banking app transaction history (for PayNow QR refunds), or
Your credit or debit card statement linked to Apple Pay or Google Pay
Refund processing time may vary depending on your bank or card issuer.

questions.title: Why is there no breakdown of the deceased member’s CPF balances in the Deceased CPF Member Dashboard?
questions.text:
You can view the overall amount left in the deceased member’s CPF account under “Outstanding CPF balance”. This shows the combined total of all monies across the deceased member’s CPF accounts.
You may click on "View Transactions" to see a more detailed transaction history of the deceased's CPF accounts.

questions.title: How can I access my next-of-kin's CPF account information if I cannot obtain their legal authorisation to receive it?
questions.text:
The Board, as a trustee of CPF monies belonging to CPF account holders, has a legal duty to maintain the confidentiality of their account information.
CPF Board will release account details — such as transaction history or a Yearly Statement of Account — only if one of the following applies:
The CPF member makes the request themselves
You have a Court Order authorising you to receive the information
You hold an activated Lasting Power of Attorney that covers this
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: Is mediation compulsory before I am able commence a claim at the Employment Claims Tribunals?
questions.text:
Mediation at the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) is compulsory before claims can be filed at the Employment Claims Tribunals (ECT).
Additionally, you may only file a claim at the ECT if both of the following applies:
(a) Your dispute is unresolved after mediation at TADM.
(b) You have been issued a Claim Referral Certificate by an approved TADM mediator.
If you have yet to file a mediation request, you may do so at this link: https://www.tal.sg/tadm/eservices
topics: Employment Claims Tribunals / Commencing an Employment Claim: Prerequisities

questions.title: What is Service? / What does Service mean?
questions.text:
"Service" refers to the delivering of the document to the Respondent. This can be done by Personal Service (delivering hard copies of the document physically to the Respondent), by Registered Post to their last known residential or registered address or ACRA registered address (for businesses), or by any other means as directed by the ECT.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-file-serve-employment-claim - under the "How to file and serve" section.
topics: Employment Claims Tribunals / Commencing an Employment Claim: Service

questions.title: Why are platform workers who have not opted in to the increased CPF contributions ineligible to receive Workfare Income Supplement aligned to that of employees from 2029?
questions.text: Platform workers who have not opted in to increased CPF contributions will continue to contribute to their Medisave Account only, like self-employed persons (SEPs). Thus, the Workfare Income Supplement for these eligible platform workers are aligned with SEPs.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How is the Annual Value (AV) requirement for Workfare Income Supplement scheme determined and which address is used to calculate it?
questions.text:
The Annual Value (AV) threshold for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) covers all HDB flats and some smaller private residences. In general, Singaporeans staying in larger properties with an AV above the threshold tend to have greater access to household wealth, making them ineligible for WIS.
The AV of a property is the estimated market rental of similar properties in the area, as determined by IRAS.
To assess your WIS eligibility, we use your NRIC address to check the AV of your place of residence. For accurate assessment, please ensure your NRIC reflects your current place of residence.
Under the National Registration Act, you are required to report any change of address within 28 days at the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) website.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Why is my spouse's Assessable Income for the previous Year of Assessment used to determine my Workfare Income Supplement in the current work year?
questions.text:
This is to allow for quicker assessment of Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) eligibility. As Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) needs time to process Income data for the current work year, we use the latest Assessable Income (AI) data to determine eligibility.
The AI for the previous Year of Assessment (YOA) is used to assess one's WIS eligibility for the current year. For example, we will use your spouse's AI for YOA 2025 to assess your eligibility for 2026 WIS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Why will the Workfare Income Supplement for platform workers be aligned with that of employees only in 2029, when their increased CPF contributions were implemented in 2025?
questions.text:
CPF contributions rates for platform workers will gradually increase from 2025 to 2028, and will fully align with those of employees in 2029. Correspondingly, the Workfare Income Supplement will be aligned with employee rates only from 2029, for platform workers who are mandated or have opted in to the increased CPF contributions.
During this period, the Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) will provide monthly cash payments to support lower-income platform workers who make increased CPF contributions. The PCTS will fully cover the increase in CPF contributions in 2025 and will gradually taper off before ending in 2029.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Why is my Workfare Income Supplement amount different from previous months?
questions.text:
For employees and platform workers, your Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) amount may differ monthly as it depends on your income. It is assessed monthly based on your total gross income as declared by your employer or platform operator in the CPF submissions. If you have more than one source of income, income from all sources will be considered. Any change in your total income can result in a different WIS payment.
You can use the online WIS calculator to estimate your payment.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Why is monthly per capita household income used as an indication of my family support for the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text:
The Silver Support (SS) Scheme is targeted at seniors who had low incomes during their working years and now have little or no family support and resources in their retirement.
To automatically identify seniors who are eligible for SS, the Government has to rely on available data as broad indicators of an individual’s ability to save for retirement, access to resources and family support.
We have relied on the monthly per capita household income as a broad indicator of the level of family support available.

questions.title: Can I use CPF savings for my full-time subsidised local degree course if I have previously used CPF savings for my first subsidised diploma course?
questions.text: You can use CPF savings for your degree course as long as it is an approved full-time subsidised course under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, subject to the available withdrawal limit.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What is the SGSHARE Programme?
questions.text:
SGSHARE is the national regular-giving programme that supports communities in need. It is an initiative by Community Chest, the philanthropic arm of the National Council of Social Service, to provide sustained funding for programmes and capability-building for social service agencies serving communities in need.
The CPF Board collects your employees’ SGSHARE donations on behalf of Community Chest, from the employees’ wages made through the company payroll.

questions.title: How do I pay my employees' SGSHARE donations?
questions.text: You are expected to deduct the SGSHARE donations from your employees’ wages and pay the SGSHARE donations together with the CPF contributions.

questions.title: My employees do not wish to contribute to the SGSHARE programme. What can they do?
questions.text: Your employees can contact the HR department to cease the payroll deduction if they do not wish to contribute to SGSHARE programme.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for dental treatments?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave for selected complex dental procedures that involve surgery and are performed for medical reasons, subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits applicable for day surgeries.
If you are aged 60 or older, you can also use your available withdrawal limit under Flexi-MediSave for selected non-surgical dental procedures such as permanent crowns and root canal treatments.
Please check with your dentist whether your dental treatments are MediSave-claimable.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay the MediShield Life deductible for outpatient treatment?
questions.text: Yes, you can use your MediSave to pay for your MediShield Life outpatient deductible. There is also MediFund to help those who are unable to afford their bills even after subsidies, MediShield Life, and MediSave. Nobody will be denied appropriate care due to an inability to pay.

questions.title: I was told by my dentist that Flexi-MediSave does not cover all dental treatments. Why is that so?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave is meant to help with recurrent outpatient medical expenses, which many older Singaporeans have raised as a key concern due to significant accumulated bill sizes over the longer term.
Flexi-MediSave can be used for select restorative dental procedures, i.e. permanent crowns and root canal treatments which can be relatively more costly. Other dental expenses are not covered under Flexi-MediSave and patients can benefit from generous government subsidies to cover costs – for example, at CHAS dental clinics and public institutions such as the polyclinics and National Dental Centre.
Nevertheless, you can use MediSave under the MediSave withdrawal limits applicable for day surgeries for selected complex dental procedures.

questions.title: I can't find my Year-in-Review. How do I access it?
questions.text:
As part of our ongoing efforts to improve our services and better engage our members, we have heard your feedback for more forward-planning tools and have recently launched PLAN with CPF – your one-stop financial guidance platform that helps you make informed financial decisions as you navigate through life. We have discontinued the Year-in-Review pilot from June 2026.
You may continue to view your annual CPF balances, inflow and outflow using the Yearly Statement of Account (YSOA) or check Transaction history for recent activities.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: Why is making MediSave contributions important for self-employed persons?
questions.text:
As a self-employed person, it is important to set aside a portion of your income to build up your MediSave savings. These savings can be used for your healthcare needs such as MediShield Life premiums or hospitalisation costs, helping to safeguard your healthcare expenses especially when you are older or no longer working.
If you are having difficulties making your MediSave contributions, you can request an instalment plan1 for your MediSave contributions via the Manage your MediSave payable form.
1Please note that your request is subject to the Board’s approval. You may be required to provide additional information or supporting documents, if necessary.

questions.title: Why do I need to make MediSave contributions as a self-employed person?
questions.text:
You are required to make mandatory MediSave contributions as a self-employed person if you earn a total net trade income of more than $6,000.
These MediSave contributions helps you to build up savings for your healthcare needs, especially in the absence of regular MediSave contributions from an employer.

questions.title: I am unable to make my MediSave contributions in full. What should I do?
questions.text:
If you are having difficulties making your MediSave contributions in full, you can request an instalment plan1 for your MediSave contributions via the Manage your MediSave payable form. This allows you to make your contributions conveniently in more manageable monthly instalments, with automatic deductions from your bank account.
1Please note that your request is subject to the Board’s approval. You may be required to provide additional information or supporting documents, if necessary.

questions.title: Can I bring in pets during visits?
questions.text:
Pets are not allowed during visits.
For more information, visit: https://www.sps.gov.sg/visit-matters/visit-information/how-to-visit/

questions.title: What can I do if I have not received my Cashier’s Order or my Cashier’s Order has expired?
questions.text:
We typically dispatch the Cashier's Order within five working days of completion of processing. Time taken for the Cashier’s Order to reach you will depend on your country’s postal services.
If you have not received your Cashier's Order within two months of submitting your online application form or your Cashier’s Order has expired, please contact the Board through Write to Us.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: How do I make payment?
questions.text:
Payment is required upon registration. You can pay by:
NETS
Medisave (up to $300 per patient per year)
Major credit cards
If your payment is covered by your company or another payment scheme, please provide a Letter of Guarantee (LOG) and any supporting documents during registration.

questions.title: Should I inform my employees when making Voluntary Contributions (VC) for them?
questions.text: Yes, please keep your employees informed about any Voluntary Contributions (VC) you intend to make. This will help your employees take into account any VC you make for them, if they are also making VC for themselves.
topics: Employer - Making Voluntary CPF Contributions / Voluntary contributions

questions.title: Why is MediShield Life applying a differentiated pro-ration factor for ward charges and surgical fees?
questions.text: As ward charges and surgical fees can differ, having a single pro-ration factor could result in over- or under-proration of individual bills. Having a differentiated pro-ration factor will allow private and unsubsidised bills to be better normalise to the subsidised equivalent.

questions.title: I was admitted to a Class A/B1 ward. Why are the pro-ration factors lowered from 1 April 2025 and how will this affect my MediShield Life claim?
questions.text:
As private hospital bills and Class A/B1 bills in public hospitals are generally higher than the Class B2/C bills that MediShield Life is designed for, they are pro-rated or normalised to the equivalent level of a Class B2/C bill before MediShield Life payouts are computed to ensure payouts are comparable.
With private and unsubsidised bills growing faster than subsidised bills, the pro-ration factors have been reduced to ensure MediShield Life payouts are comparable across different settings and to reduce cross-subsidisation .
Patients who seek private or unsubsidised care should now see comparable payouts to subsidised patients.

questions.title: How do I check my Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) balance if I wish to repay my education loan using my PSEA funds?
questions.text:
You may log in to the Ministry of Education’s Student Finance System (SFS) using your Singpass to check your account balance.
For more information on how to check the outstanding loan amount repayable under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, please refer to this FAQ.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What are the CPF contribution rates for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents?
questions.text:
For more details on the CPF contribution rates, see rates for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents.
You can use our CPF Contribution Calculator to calculate the CPF contributions applicable to your employees.
For past rates, see past CPF contribution and allocation rates.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: Where do I find the Memorandum of Consent form to fill in?
questions.text: You can find the sample form for a Memorandum of Consent under the "Claim Limit" portion of the "Key Facts" section in this link: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-file-serve-small-claim

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable if I am on an overseas-based contract and working in Singapore temporarily?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are not payable if you are on an overseas-based contract and working in Singapore on a temporary basis. Examples of temporary work arrangements include attending meetings, conferences, or training, or working remotely in Singapore temporarily for personal reasons.
Please note that while your employer is still obligated to make CPF contributions for non-temporary stints in Singapore, enforcement may be limited where your employer is based overseas with no presence in Singapore and is not registered with ACRA. In such cases, CPFB may have limited ability to assist with your claims.
If you and your employer are unsure of your CPF obligations, you may write to us with the relevant facts of your case for assessment.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable if I am on a Singapore-based contract and working overseas temporarily?
questions.text:
CPF contributions remain payable if you are on a Singapore-based contract and working overseas on a temporary basis. Examples of temporary work arrangements include attending meetings, conferences, or training, or working remotely overseas temporarily for personal reasons.
If you and your employer are unsure of your CPF obligations, you may write to us with the relevant facts of your case for assessment.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: I did not use CPF savings for the matrimonial property but pledged the property to set aside my retirement sum. Can the Court order a transfer of this property to my ex-spouse
questions.text: Yes, the Court can still order the transfer of the property to your ex-spouse upon the refund of your pledged amount to your CPF account. The Court may also order for the transfer with a partial refund or without a refund. For such orders, upon the subsequent disposal of the property by your ex-spouse, the unrefunded pledged amount will have to be refunded to your ex-spouse’s CPF account (since it was not earlier refunded to your CPF account).
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: The courts ordered my ex-spouse and me to make our CPF refunds from our respective shares of sale proceeds. My share is insufficient to make the full refund. Can I waive the shortfall in refund?
questions.text:
No, full requisite CPF refunds must be made in accordance with CPF legislation upon the sale of the property in a divorce. If your (or your ex-spouse’s) respective share of sale proceeds are not enough to cover the required refunds to your CPF account, you will need to make up the shortfall in cash.
If you and your ex-spouse are unable to proceed with the sale of the property, please seek legal advice on how your proprietary share in the matrimonial asset can be satisfied.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for my employee on an overseas-based contract who is working in Singapore temporarily?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are not payable for an employee on an overseas-based contract who is working in Singapore on a temporary basis. Examples of temporary work arrangements include attending meetings, conferences, or training, or working remotely in Singapore temporarily for personal reasons.
If you are unsure of your CPF obligations, you may write to us with the relevant facts of your case for assessment.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for my employee on a Singapore-based contract who is working overseas temporarily?
questions.text:
CPF contributions remain payable for an employee on a Singapore-based contract who is working overseas on a temporary basis. Examples of temporary work arrangements include attending meetings, conferences, or training, or working remotely overseas temporarily for personal reasons.
If you are unsure of your CPF obligations, you may write to us with the relevant facts of your case for assessment.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Can I use the same CPF Submission Number (CSN) to make both mandatory and voluntary CPF contributions for my employees?
questions.text:
No. A separate CPF Submission Number (CSN) is required for voluntary contributions (VC) - the CSN for mandatory contributions should not be used for this purpose.
To make VC to your employee's three CPF accounts, use your existing CSN with the payment code "VCT" (eg. 123456789-VCT-01). To make Additional MediSave Contributions Scheme (AMCS) contributions to your employee's MediSave Account, use your existing CSN with the payment code "AMS" (eg. 123456789-AMS-01).
Submission and payment of VC for your employees can be done the same way as mandatory CPF contributions via CPF EZPay. If you do not have a CSN with the "VCT" or "AMS" payment code, you may apply for one.
topics: Employer - Making Voluntary CPF Contributions / Voluntary contributions

questions.title: Why do I need to fill in the policy number and claim number of my employee, platform worker or insured in the E-File Excel for MediSave/MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement?
questions.text: The policy number and claim number fields were added based on requests from companies to help track their MediSave/MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement submissions and match them with their records. These fields are optional and not compulsory.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Will I be notified about the status of my Direct Debit Authorisation application?
questions.text: You will be notified once the bank has approved your Direct Debit Authorisation (DDA) application, which generally takes four to six weeks. Once your DDA is approved, you can begin submitting reimbursements online.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I realised that I submitted the same reimbursement multiple times via E-File. What should I do?
questions.text:
If you submit duplicate reimbursements on the same day before 5:30pm, the most recent submission will override the previous one, and only the latest file will be processed.
If you have submitted duplicate reimbursements on different days, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: My reimbursement submission via E-File is unsuccessful, and I received a rejection reason. How should I correct my submission?
questions.text: Please refer to the common rejected reasons and their corresponding corrective actions before resubmitting.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I submitted reimbursements via E-File today, but realised there was a mistake in my submission after submitting the Excel file. What should I do?
questions.text:
You can override your previous submission by resubmitting the corrected file before 5:30pm on the same day.
For further clarification, please write to us.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I noticed that I need to fill in the Hospital Registration Number (HRN) for submitting reimbursement via E-File. How do I obtain the HRN?
questions.text:
The Hospital Registration Number (HRN) can be found in the following documents:
Your employee, platform worker or insured’s final medical bill
Your employee, platform worker or insured’s Healthcare Payments and Claims Statement
Your employee, platform worker or insured’s MediSave Transaction Statement
Please refer to this guide for more information on where to find the HRN.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Do I need to attach the employee, platform worker or insured's hardcopy healthcare payments and claims statement for submitting MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursement?
questions.text:
CPF Board does not require any documents from employers, platform operators or insurers to process the MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursement.
You should not request a hardcopy Healthcare Payments and Claims Statement from your employee, platform worker or insured. Employers, platform operators or insurers should accept a digital copy of the Healthcare Payments and Claims Statement from your employee, platform worker or insured if required.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Who are considered as immediate family members under the Student Care Fee Assistance (SCFA)?
questions.text:
Ø Immediate family members are the child’s grandparents, or any other siblings below 21 years old who meet the following criteria:
(1) Live at the same address as the applicant,
(2) Not working, or do not have any source of income
(3) Singaporean, PR or Foreigners with valid passes (e.g. LTVP, LTVP+, Student Pass, Employment Pass, Dependent Pass, Work Permit, other passes of duration more than or equal to 2 years, etc.).

questions.title: Where can I find the press releases by MHA?
questions.text: You can visit the following url - Newsroom | Ministry of Home Affairs for press releases issued by MHA

questions.title: I applied for financial assistance at the Social Service Office (SSO), but my application was rejected. How do I appeal?
questions.text: You may approach your officer directly, preparing any relevant supporting documents (e.g. updated payslips, medical certificates).

questions.title: Is Long-Term Assistance (LTA) a permanent scheme, or is it only provided for a limited period?
questions.text: ComCare Long Term Assistance (LTA) provides long-term support to those permanently unable to work due to old age, illness or disability, and have inadequate family support or savings to rely on for daily needs. Eligibility and duration of support are subject to periodic review based on the individual's circumstances.

questions.title: How can I check the status of my Trusted Contact appointment request?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your Trusted Contact appointment request via your Activities page using your Singpass.
You may also view your appointed Trusted Contacts at the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings. Only Trusted Contacts who have accepted your appointment request will be listed under “Your Trusted Contacts”.

questions.title: How does diversification help to limit my risk in investing?
questions.text:
Diversification, or spreading your assets among several investments, helps you smooth out potential ups and downs of your investment returns. Even if one investment does poorly, the others may do better, thereby potentially improving your overall return.
You can diversify your investments at two distinct levels by spreading your investments among:
different asset classes - cash equivalents (e.g., fixed deposits),bonds and stocks and/or
different markets - geographic regions, foreign countries, foreign currencies, industries and companies.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What is the processing time for an application once I have submitted all the required documents?
questions.text: Applications are processed within 15 working days from the date of receipt of all required documents, subject to the complexity of individual cases.

questions.title: What are the signs of infection?
questions.text:
Fever or chills
Feeling unwell or lethargic
Cough, breathlessness, or chest pain
Burning sensation or pain when passing urine
Redness, swelling, or discharge from wounds
New pain anywhere in the body
👉 Key message: If you notice any of these, seek medical advice early—infections can worsen quickly after transplant. Do note that because immunosuppressive drugs weaken the immune system, fever and redness may be absent or mild, even when an infection is present.

questions.title: I want to use my CPF savings to fully redeem my housing loan. Where can I find the Principal Outstanding and Accrued Interest in my redemption statement?
questions.text: You may refer to this guide to fill in the Principal Outstanding and Accrued Interest fields when making a full housing loan payment.

questions.title: What do I need to do before submitting my notice of revocation to OPG?
questions.text:
Before submitting your notice of revocation to OPG, you must inform all your Donees in writing that you have revoked your LPA.
You may do so in any of the following ways:
In person, by delivering a written notice directly to them
By post
By email
topics: Office of the Public Guardian / Revoking an LPA

questions.title: Does submitting a notice of revocation online via OPGO require a witness?
questions.text: No, the online submission via OPGO does not require a witness.
topics: Office of the Public Guardian / Revoking an LPA

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for Accident and Emergency (A&E) expenses?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay for Accident and Emergency (A&E) expenses if you are subsequently admitted to the hospital after seeking care at the A&E department, subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits applicable to your inpatient or day surgery bill.
If you are not admitted, you cannot use MediSave to pay for standalone A&E expenses. However, if you have incurred A&E expenses for a CT scan performed for traumatic brain injury at the A&E department of an approved medical institution in Singapore, you can withdraw from your MediSave through the medical institution under the MediSave withdrawal limit for outpatient scans.

questions.title: I am an Indian Muslim/Chinese Muslim. Must I contribute to MBMF as well as SINDA/CDAC? Can I opt out from MBMF?
questions.text: Yes, Chinese Muslims and Indian Muslims are required to contribute to both MBMF and CDAC/SINDA respectively, as each organisation’s fund supports the development of their respective communities. To opt out of any fund, you may submit a request directly to the relevant organisation or through your employer.

questions.title: What about Non-Malay Muslims contributing to both MBMF and CDAC/SINDA/EA who are not receiving assistance from any SHGs?
questions.text: Non-Malay Muslims are eligible to benefit from programmes offered by both MENDAKI/MUIS and their respective SHG (CDAC/SINDA/EA), subject to each programme's eligibility criteria. If you are unsure of what assistance is available to you, we encourage you to reach out directly to MENDAKI, MUIS, or your respective SHG for guidance.

questions.title: What is the MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL)?
questions.text:
Students taking MOE-subsidised diploma, undergraduate or postgraduate programmes in the following Post-Secondary Education Institutions (PSEIs) can apply for the MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL):
Institute of Technical Education (ITE)
Polytechnics
Arts institutions - LASALLE College of the Arts (LASALLE), Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA), University of the Arts Singapore (UAS)
Autonomous Universities
The MOE HESL is interest-free during the student’s course of study.
Click on the image below for a quick guide on the MOE HESL.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: I intend to take a loan to finance my tertiary education and I will repay it promptly upon graduation. Which would be a better option for me - the MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL) or the CPF Education Loan?
questions.text:
The MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL) is a better option as it is interest-free during the course of study, unlike the CPF Education loan where interest starts to accrue from the time of withdrawal. This means that if you repay the MOE HESL fully right after graduation, you will not incur any interest at all.
If you are unable to repay your MOE HESL due to further studies or financial difficulties due to unemployment or medical condition, you may appeal to defer repayment and interest. Your appeal will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
While CPF may also allow for deferment during challenging times, interest continues to accrue as it is essential to fully restore the savings intended primarily for retirement. For more information on the MOE HESL, please refer to this link.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I apply for the MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL)?
questions.text:
To apply for MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL), please apply through the StudentLoan (SLSG) portal using your Singpass account.
For more information on MOE HESL, please visit MOE HESL website or approach your institution.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How much of tuition fees can be paid using CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings?
questions.text:
The savings in the CPF Ordinary Account (OA) can be used to pay up to 100% of your own, your spouse’s, your children’s, or your siblings’ tuition fees. However, if you are paying for your relatives’ tuition fees, the percentage of tuition fees that can be paid using your OA savings is:
10% if your relative(s) is studying at a university;
25% if your relative(s) is studying at a polytechnic or pursuing an approved Technical Engineer Diploma (TED) or a Technical Diploma at Institute of Technical Education (ITE); or
50% if your relative(s) is studying at an art institution.
To pay the remaining tuition fees, the student may consider using the Post- Secondary Education Account funds or applying for the MOE Higher Education Student Loan, subject to eligibility.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Does MediShield Life or MediSave cover the GST charged on my medical bill?
questions.text: Yes, MediShield Life claim payouts and MediSave withdrawals are based on the bill amounts submitted by the medical institution, subject to the applicable limits under the respective schemes. If the bill includes GST, the GST amount will be included in the payout.

questions.title: Can I enjoy tax relief for topping up my MediSave Account to pay my MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums?
questions.text:
Top-ups to MediSave Account to pay MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums are considered voluntary contributions.
Eligible members will enjoy tax relief for these top-ups. You can refer to the IRAS website for details on the eligibility criteria and amount of tax relief for voluntary MediSave contributions.

questions.title: How do I top up my MediSave for MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums, and how can I check if it has been successfully processed?
questions.text:
You can make a top-up to your MediSave for MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premium payments via the Top up MediSave Account online form. MediSave top-ups are generally reflected immediately and will be deducted for premium payment.
You can view your MediSave top-ups by logging in to cpf.gov.sg with your Singpass. The top-up will be shown as "VOLUNTARY CON TO MEDISAVE A/C" or "HEALTHCARE TOP-UP" in your transaction records. If the top-up amount is not immediately reflected in your MediSave Account, check your MediSave Account balance after five working days, as some transactions may take longer to process.

questions.title: Can I upgrade or downgrade between ElderShield 300 and ElderShield 400?
questions.text: Switching between ElderShield plans is not possible. ElderShield 300 insureds were given a one-time option to upgrade to ElderShield 400 in 2007, and this option is no longer available. Downgrading from ElderShield 400 to ElderShield 300 is also not allowed.

questions.title: Am I still eligible to be covered under CareShield Life if I have pre-existing disabilities?
questions.text:
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later, including those with pre-existing severe disabilities, are covered under CareShield Life from 1 October 2020 or when they turn 30, whichever is later.
As part of collective responsibility, those with pre-existing severe disabilities are required to pay one year premium to join the scheme. This payment amount is less than the first monthly CareShield Life payout they will receive. Upon joining the scheme, they will continue to receive monthly payouts for as long as they are unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living. The Government will provide means-tested premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support to help those who are still unable to afford premiums even after subsidies.

questions.title: Will ElderShield 300 or 400 insureds receive premium subsidies if they upgrade to CareShield Life?
questions.text: CareShield Life premium subsidies will be extended to eligible Singaporeans, including those currently on ElderShield 300 or 400 (born in 1979 or earlier), if they upgrade to CareShield Life. These subsidies are intended to support the increased benefits under CareShield Life and ensure that CareShield Life premiums remain affordable. You can refer to the types of premium support available for more information.

questions.title: I have recovered from a severe disability. Can I join CareShield Life, even if I was previously receiving payouts from ElderShield?
questions.text:
You can join CareShield Life if you have recovered from your severe disability and are able to perform all Activities of Daily Living1 independently, regardless of whether you previously received payouts from ElderShield. You may need to undergo a disability assessment, and will be informed by the Agency of Integrated Care if this is required.
1 Activities of Daily Living refers to feeding, dressing, toileting, washing, walking or moving around, and transferring from bed to chair and vice versa.

questions.title: I was born in 1979 or earlier. Will the ElderShield premiums I have already paid be taken into account when I join CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you were continuously insured under ElderShield before joining CareShield Life, your past ElderShield premiums will be taken into account when computing your CareShield Life premiums, resulting in lower premiums. Your premiums will be lower compared to those in the same cohort who were not insured under ElderShield.

questions.title: How long will it take to receive the outcome of my Home Protection Scheme application after my medical examination?
questions.text:
Processing time for your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) application depends on your individual circumstances.
After your medical examination, CPF Board will review the results and assess your eligibility. In some cases, additional information may be required before an outcome can be determined, and this may result in a longer processing time.
If you have not received an update on your application three weeks after your medical examination, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Would I have duplicate coverage or pay double premiums if I buy an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) when I am already covered under MediShield Life?
questions.text: There is no duplication in coverage and you are not paying double premiums. Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are automatically covered under MediShield Life for life. When you buy an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) through a private insurer, the IP consists of two components: your existing MediShield Life component and an additional private insurance coverage component. You will continue to be able to enjoy MediShield Life benefits when you buy an IP.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums for my family members, and is there a limit?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums for your family members, including your spouse, parents, children, grandparents and siblings. There is no limit to the number of family members you can help pay for.
However, you should consider the long-term affordability of IP premiums for your family members and whether you will have enough MediSave savings for your own healthcare needs, including during your retirement years.

questions.title: How do Supplement plans and other private insurance plans for disability differ from CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Supplement plans and other private insurance plans for disability differ from CareShield Life in several ways.
Most private insurance plans for disability cover total and permanent disability, or are meant to insure against loss of income when one develops a disability and is unable to work. This is why they typically cease coverage between ages 60 and 70, when most insureds retire. CareShield Life, however, provides lifetime coverage and continues to cover you even if you develop severe disability in your later years.
Unlike private insurance plans, which cease coverage if insureds are unable to pay premiums, CareShield Life coverage will not lapse if you are unable to pay premiums due to financial difficulties. The Government will provide premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support.
